## Summary

Fixes the false **PLACEMENT MISMATCH** warning that every multi-GPU launch with `--gpus` printed (reported by xandrman in #1620).

`gpu_select_container_uuids` (`scripts/lib/gpu-select.sh`) reads `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid` inside the container, which prints one UUID per line, then ran `tr -d '[:space:]'`. That also deleted the newlines, so a TP=2 container's two UUIDs became one glued token. No requested UUID ever matched it, and launch.sh warned:

```
[launch] ⚠ PLACEMENT MISMATCH: requested GPU(s) not running the model — GPU-ed50… GPU-6d7f…
[launch]   requested: GPU-ed50…,GPU-6d7f…
[launch]   actual:    GPU-ed50…GPU-6d7f…
```

The fix strips spaces, tabs and CRs only (`tr -d ' \t\r'`), so the `grep | sort -u | paste -sd,` that follows sees one UUID per line again. Single-GPU launches were never affected.

## Verification

- **Live, real docker + nvidia-smi:** a throwaway `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` container holding a tensor on both GPUs, pinned by UUID the way `--gpus` pins it. Master prints the MISMATCH above; this branch prints `✓ placement verified — model running on the requested GPU(s)`.
- **`test-gpu-select.sh` §5** (stubbed `docker`, runs anywhere):
  - a two-GPU list with a repeat and a trailing space reads back as `U0,U3` and verifies;
  - a requested card the model isn't on is still a MISMATCH (positive control);
  - the one-GPU case is unchanged;
  - bash and python agree. The estate path's twin `container_placement_uuids` in `estate_cli.py` splits by line and was always right.

  Failed on master with the glued string.
- The tests that reference gpu-select (`test-gpu-select`, `test-switch-gpu-pin`, `test-compose-gpu-mask-passthrough`, `test-report-gpu-attribution`) plus all Tier 0 guards: **30/30 pass**.

body:
## Summary

Two fixes to the interconnect probes, plus one `docker logs` check with the same bug.

### 1. `grep -q` SIGPIPE turned found matches into misses (`b5576c14`)

`nvidia-smi … | grep -q` exits on the first match. nvidia-smi then takes a SIGPIPE on its next write, and under `pipefail` the pipeline returns 141, so a **found** match reads as a miss. bench.sh, report.sh, launch.sh and verify-full.sh all run with `pipefail`.

Seen in the wild in alexanderjacuna's NVLink reports (#1574 and siblings): on a 4× 3090 rig serving on its bridged pair, bench's interconnect block printed `layer 1 driver P2P grant : REFUSED` in 7 of 8 reports while layer 3 said `ENGAGED`. It's a race: on the reference rig `set -o pipefail; nvidia-smi topo -m | grep -q GPU0` returned 141 on 300 of 300 runs, but a short output sometimes wins (#1609 got it right).

| Site | Effect under pipefail |
|---|---|
| `p2p-state.sh` `p2p_host_capability` | NVLink rig read as `none` → bench layer 1 "REFUSED"; report.sh verdict lost its NVLink case |
| `p2p-state.sh` `p2p_reports_cns` | CNS probe could miss |
| `detect_nvlink.sh` auto path, >2 GPUs | sourced **host-side** by `launch.sh` under pipefail; in-container it has no pipefail and was unaffected |
| `report.sh` NVLink section | bridge could read as "No NVLink detected" |
| `verify-full.sh` vision "intended" check (`docker logs`) | 0/20 matches on a long log with `grep -q`, 20/20 with `grep -c` → an mmproj-loaded server with a broken image path became a skip, not a fail |

Fix: capture, then match in-shell (the idiom `offload-matrix.sh` already documents), or count with `grep -c`, which reads to EOF.

Not changed: the `grep -m1` sites on the same producers (`preflight.sh:2175-2176`, `thinking-budget.sh:387`) keep the value they print and only lose the exit status, and each one is behind `|| true` or a `|| rc=$?` caller. `docker ps`, `docker info` and `benchlocal-cli --help` pipes returned 0 on every run (one write, smaller than the pipe buffer).

### 2. `p2p_reports_cns` matched the legend (`ae0cedb7`)

Found while live-checking #1: on the reference rig (P2P granted, all-OK matrix) `p2p_reports_cns` returned **true**, on master too. The legend nvidia-smi prints under the matrix always contains `CNS  = Chipset not supported`. Its one consumer, report.sh's opportunity hint, could tell a same-root-complex rig whose cells read GNS/TNS/NS that "topo -p2p reports CNS". It now matches only matrix rows, as `_p2p_pairs_ok` already does.

## Tests

- `test-p2p-state.sh` §3b: a slow-writing nvidia-smi stub (it pauses after the matching line, the way the real one writes in pieces). The existing stubs print in one write and can never SIGPIPE. It asserts the capability probe, the decider under `bash -o pipefail` and the CNS probe. **Failed on master** with `pipefail: bridged 4-GPU rig -> nvlink (got none)`; the decider printed "no NVLink, no P2P" under pipefail and the right answer without it.
- `test-p2p-state.sh` §3c: the real legend appended to the matrix fixtures. **Failed on master** (all-OK matrix + legend → true).
- New tree-wide guard `test-no-grep-q-sigpipe.sh`: forbids piping `nvidia-smi` / `docker logs` into `grep -q` / `--quiet` / `--silent`, with a positive control (both producers planted) and a negative control (captured shape, `grep -c`, `grep -m1`, comments, `scripts/tests/`). Against master it lists exactly the five sites above. It greps the tree, so it joins the Tier 0 set automatically.
- 21 tests touching the changed scripts (`test-p2p-state`, `test-detect-nvlink-*`, `test-custom-ar-knob`, `test-compose-nvlink-escape`, `test-switch-custom-ar-warning`, all 10 `test-report-*`, `test-bench-capture`, `test-verify-full-thinking-check`, `test-verify-vision`, …): **21/21 pass**. Tier 0 guards: all pass.
- Live on the reference rig: `p2p_host_capability` under pipefail → `pcie_p2p` (unchanged, correct); `p2p_reports_cns` → false (was true).

Not live-tested on an NVLink rig: there's no bridge here. The slow stub reproduces the race deterministically.

## Not in this PR

- #1561: in-container auto-detect logged "no NVLink, no P2P" on a bridged rig. That path has no `pipefail`, so it's a different cause, still unknown.
- From #1620 (confirmed on master, separate fixes): `p2p_collective_check.py` `peer_bandwidth()` ignores `--gpus` (always `cuda:0`↔`cuda:1`), and `gpu-select.sh` `gpu_select_container_uuids` strips the newlines between UUIDs (`tr -d '[:space:]'`), so a TP=2 container reports a false PLACEMENT MISMATCH.

body:
## Why

`quality-test.sh` reads the server's reasoning budget back, so it can size the client thinking cap and record the budget. It only understood the vLLM / SGLang `[effort-budget] v1` boot line. On a llama.cpp slug it reported **"server budget: unknown"**, so:

- **The answer could be cut off.** The thinking cap stayed at **16384** while the server's budget is **32768** (the qwen3.8 llama.cpp default since #1617). Reasoning past 16384 was cut by the client cap (`token_limit`) instead of the server closing it gracefully with room for the answer.
- **The budget went unrecorded.** The `Quality:` line and benchlocal's `server_thinking_budget` never recorded it.

## What

When the readback finds no line (exit 2) and the container is llama.cpp, the wrapper reads the `--reasoning-budget` the container **booted with**, from `docker inspect`. It goes through `thinking-budget.sh`'s existing resolver, which resolves `${REASONING_BUDGET:-N}` the way the shell does. That is the same evidence `--thinking-budget` already verifies against, so a raw `docker run`, an override and a compose default all read alike.

| `--reasoning-budget` resolves to | Result |
|---|---|
| N | Existing path: the cap rises to N + `THINKING_BUDGET_HEADROOM`, the `Quality:` line stamps `budget=server N` (**no effort**, since llama.cpp's budget is the same for every effort), and benchlocal gets `--server-thinking-budget N` |
| `-1` or no flag | `off` (unrestricted): cap unchanged, stamps `budget=server off` |
| unresolvable | `unknown`, with a llama.cpp-specific message: cap unchanged, nothing stamped |

**`--thinking-budget N` on llama.cpp** was already verified to equal the boot value. The message now says the server carries it, instead of "sent per request and wins over it", which isn't how llama.cpp works there.

**Docs:** the `--help` text, `docs/QUALITY_TEST.md` (the readback section, its table and the `Quality:` legend), and the `quality_line.py` docstring now cover llama.cpp.

**Behaviour change to expect:** thinking-on quality runs on the four qwen3.8 llama.cpp-family slugs now run with a **36864** thinking cap instead of 16384. benchlocal scales per-case timeouts with the budget, so those runs can take longer. vLLM / SGLang runs are unchanged.

## Verified

- **`test-quality-server-budget`, new section 8:** a llama.cpp container mock whose `docker inspect` matches what the composes boot (`bash -c` script, `"${REASONING_BUDGET:-32768}"`). It covers the default (cap 36864, recorded, stamped with no effort), an effort set, an override to 8192, `-1`, no flag, an unresolvable value, and `--thinking-budget 8192`.
  - **Negative control:** against master's `quality-test.sh`, exactly these **14** assertions fail and nothing else does.
- **Live, against a real compose-launched container** (`llama-cpp-prism/qwen38-27b-single-ternary-pq2` via `switch.sh`, only `benchlocal-cli` stubbed): autodetects the container, reads `32768` from the real `docker inspect`, cap **36864**, `--server-thinking-budget 32768`, and `Quality: … budget=server 32768 …`. I deleted the stub's fake results file afterwards.
- **Tests:** `test-quality-thinking-budget`, `test-quality-passthrough`, `test-effort-budget`, `test-quality-sampling-stamp` and all Tier 0 guards pass.

body:
Two commits: bump the PrismML llama.cpp engine to `prism-b10770-6684606`, then give the four llama.cpp-family Qwen3.8 slugs a reasoning-budget default that requests can override.

## 1. `llama-cpp-prism` → `prism-b10770-6684606`

- **Built from the checked-in recipe** (`models/qwen3.8-27b/llama-cpp-prism/image/Dockerfile`) around PrismML's Linux CUDA 12.8 release tarball. The tarball's sha256 `98410e52…1d5651` equals the release asset's published digest.
- **Pushed** as `ghcr.io/noonghunna/llamacpp-prism:b10770-6684606` and **pinned by digest** `sha256:8dbbd2a6…cddf90ef`, via `engine-pin-bump.sh`. No fixtures carried the old pin.
- **What's in it:** the release is 16 commits past `b10754`, including **PrismML #318**, the GDN state-gather fix noted as missing from the old pin. `docs/UPSTREAM.md` now has #318 in the pin and the pin row updated.
- **No vendored patches**, so there is nothing to re-validate.
- **Boot-tested:**
  - `-ternary-pq2` and `-ternary-mtp` both boot on the new build (`build 10770, commit 6684606ac`);
  - MTP n=4 drafts (50 of 64 accepted on a short prompt);
  - `-pq2` booted through the **pinned registry digest** (`docker inspect` shows the `@sha256:8dbbd2a6…` ref), served 3 warm-ups, then answered correctly.

## 2. Reasoning-budget default for the llama.cpp-family Qwen3.8 slugs

**Budget semantics, measured on both engine builds.** Each was booted with `REASONING_BUDGET=64`, and reasoning tokens were counted with the server's own `/tokenize`:

| Request | prism `b10770` | mainline build 11429 |
|---|---|---|
| no budget field | 68 tokens + `[reasoning budget exhausted]` | 70 + marker |
| `reasoning_budget_tokens: 512` | **446**, ended on its own | **490**, ended on its own |
| `reasoning_budget_tokens: 16` | 21 + marker | 22 + marker |

So `--reasoning-budget` is the **server default, not a ceiling**: a request's own `reasoning_budget_tokens` (or `thinking_budget_tokens`) wins in either direction. Unlike our vLLM and SGLang patches, llama.cpp does not choose the budget from `reasoning_effort`.

**The defaults:**

| Slug | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs` | −1 (unrestricted) | **32768** |
| `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-dual-q8kxl` | −1 (unrestricted) | **32768** |
| `llama-cpp-prism/…-ternary-pq2` / `…-ternary-mtp` | 32768 | 32768 (unchanged; documented as overridable) |

**Why 32768 and not 16384:** the prism compose's measurements show this model's `medium` traces can reach ~19K tokens on one prompt (13,013 and 18,895 on two runs of the same prompt). 16384 would cut some runs of a prompt and not others. `REASONING_BUDGET=-1` restores unrestricted.

**Boots at the new default:** both mainline slugs log `[reasoning] budget=32768` and answer correctly. `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-dual-q8kxl` booted at about 22.6 GB per card with MTP n=2 drafting (36 of 38 accepted). *(Corrected: this said "for the first time", which was wrong. It has booted since 2026-08-15 with verify-full passing; its stale "never booted" note misled this description and is fixed in #1619.)*

**Preserve thinking:** all four slugs leave `--reasoning-preserve` at the template default. Every Qwen3.8 GGUF on the rig embeds `preserve_thinking is undefined or preserve_thinking is true`, so prior-turn reasoning is preserved by default, as on the vLLM and SGLang slugs.

## Not changed (noted)

- **The `dual-q8kxl` registry note** still says "NOTHING HAS BOOTED … never launched", and names `server-cuda-b10236` while the engine runs build 11429. *(Corrected: it has booted and passed verify-full since 2026-08-15; the note was simply stale. Fixed in #1619.)*
- **`quality-test.sh`'s server-budget readback** only reads the vLLM/SGLang `[effort-budget] v1` line, so on these slugs it doesn't see the llama.cpp budget. Its client thinking cap stays at the 16384 default, below the server's 32768, as before when the server was unrestricted. The `Quality:` line won't stamp the llama.cpp budget.

## Tests

- `test-compose-status-drift`, `test-compose-registry-disk`, `test-profiles-compat`, `test-launch-compat`, `test-diagnose-profile`, `test-patch-attribution`, `test-launch-knobs` and `test-compose-mounts-resolve` pass.
- `test-engine-pin-bump`, `test-compose-flags-accepted`, `test-compose-env-declared-unused`, `test-catalog-baseline`, `test-model-default-resolver` and `test-model-weights-registry` pass.
- All Tier 0 guards pass.

## Why

benchlocal-cli now requires **Python 3.11+**: noonghunna/benchlocal-cli#200, fixed by noonghunna/benchlocal-cli#201. Its StructOutput SO-04 scorer parses TOML with the standard library's `tomllib`, so on 3.10 the same pack version scored that scenario differently: a valid answer passed at 100 on 3.11+ and failed at 25 on 3.10.

On a rig whose system `python3` is 3.10, which includes stock Ubuntu 22.04, the `pip install git+…` that club-3090 tells users to run is now refused:

```
ERROR: Package 'benchlocal-cli' requires a different Python: 3.10.20 not in '>=3.11'
```

## What

The install hints now say Python 3.11+, and point an older system Python at uv, which brings its own interpreter and puts `benchlocal-cli` in `~/.local/bin`:

```bash
uv tool install --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/noonghunna/benchlocal-cli.git
```

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/quality-test.sh` | The help text's INSTALL block and the "benchlocal-cli not found" message: Python 3.11+ plus the uv command. |
| `docs/QUALITY_TEST.md` | The Install section explains why 3.11, what pip prints on 3.10, and gives `uv tool install …` / `uv tool upgrade benchlocal-cli`. |
| `scripts/report.sh`, `docs/ANNOUNCEMENT_TEMPLATE.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Short "Python 3.11+" notes on the existing install lines. |

Unchanged: the `pip install --upgrade` hints. On 3.10, pip's own error already says the Python is too old.

Wording only; no behaviour changes.

## Verified

- `uv tool install --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/noonghunna/benchlocal-cli.git`, then `uv tool upgrade benchlocal-cli` and `benchlocal-cli list`: all exit 0. I ran them in scratch `UV_TOOL_DIR` / `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, so the rig's own install wasn't touched.
- `bash -n` passes on both scripts.
- `test-quality-passthrough` (the test that covers these files) and every Tier 0 guard pass.

Merge after, or together with, noonghunna/benchlocal-cli#201. Before that, the hints are still correct: they only add a requirement that is about to apply.

body:
Follow-up to #1612.

## What was wrong

When a chat template is selected for a profile but not delivered (a declared delivery gap, or a failed drift guard), the generator removes its wiring lines. It found them with substring markers:

- the bare `--chat-template` flag
- the generic filename `chat_template.jinja`
- qwen38's `mounted_at`, which is just the suffix `/chat_template.jinja`

Each of those also matches **another** template's mount and flag. `--chat-template` is also a prefix of llama.cpp's `--chat-template-kwargs`, so the strip would leave that flag's JSON value behind as a stray argument. The comment said the strip stayed in lock-step with `reaches()`, which #1612 changed.

## The fix

`_strip_chat_template()` removes what `patch_attribution._chat_template_wired()` checks for, and nothing else:

- **the mount line** whose source is the patch's own template (the same needle);
- **the flag naming that mount's target**, in any of three forms: `- <flag>` followed by `- <target>`; `- <flag>=<target>`; or a line holding just `<flag> <target>` (the llama.cpp folded-command style).

`_patch_wiring_markers()` now returns only the mount needle for chat templates. Every other delivery mechanism keeps the marker strip unchanged.

## Impact: none on current output

- Every vLLM profile the generator handles carries exactly one template. Forcing that template out gives **byte-identical output before and after** in all 8 such profiles. A ninth is refused before the strip.
- Across all 112 composes that load-bear a template, the new strip leaves valid YAML that no longer reaches the patch:
  - 3 lines removed: gemma, froggeric, glm53, and qwen38 on vLLM;
  - 1 line removed (the mount): qwen38 on SGLang;
  - 2 lines removed: apex.
- The old strip's only real over-strip among those composes is GLM's `- '--chat-template-kwargs'`. GLM is llama.cpp, which the generator refuses, so this is hardening.

## Tests (`test-generate-compose`)

- **Forced-out froggeric on `vllm/minimal`:** removes exactly its mount, `- --chat-template` and `- /etc/qwen-froggeric-chat-template.jinja`, and the result no longer counts as wired.
- **Two-template fixture:** the fixture also holds the lines the substring strip used to catch: Gemma's mount and flag, `--chat-template-kwargs` with its value, and an apex `--chat-template-file` line in a bash script.
  - Stripping froggeric, qwen38 or apex removes only that template's lines.
  - Master's strip on the same fixture removes **9 / 8 / 6** lines; the fix removes **3 / 2 / 2**.

`test-generate-compose`, `test-patch-attribution`, `test-pull` and the Tier 0 guards all pass.

Follow-up to #1611 / #1612.

## What was wrong

`glm53-minja-numeric-index` declared `load_bearing_when: composes: null`. All 18 `llamacpp-club3090/glm53-flash-*` composes do mount its `chat_template.jinja` and pass `--chat-template-file /etc/glm53-chat-template.jinja`, the dual / multi4 / multi8 × six quant variants.

Because none of them were listed, `test-patch-attribution` never checked that wiring. A GLM compose could lose the template and stay green. Without the template, every request that carries `tools` returns HTTP 400 (#1250).

## Changes

- **`patches.yml`:** list the 18 slugs. They are the same 18 that `reaches()` finds, and the same 18 compose files that reference the template.
- **`test-patch-attribution`:** the guard that requires every slug mounting a template to be listed now also builds its needle from `delivery_spec.jinja`. It used only `files`, and glm53's `files` entry is the template's directory, which yields no needle. That is how this gap got past the guard.

## Effect

Only `generate_compose.py` and the tests read `load_bearing_when`. The generator is vLLM-only and refuses llama.cpp slugs, so no generated output changes. What changes is coverage: the coverage loop now asserts the template reaches all 18 GLM composes.

## Tests

- **The guard against master's `patches.yml` fails:** `glm53-minja-numeric-index: 18 slug(s) mount its template but are missing from load_bearing_when`. With this PR's list, it passes.

body:
Fixes #1611.

## What was wrong

`reaches()` said a chat-template patch was wired into composes that run a *different* template:

- **The bare `--chat-template` flag counted on its own.** It appears in every vLLM compose that passes any template, and it is a prefix of llama.cpp's `--chat-template-file`.
- **`wired_at: [volumes, command]` wasn't recognised** (apex, glm53), so those patches fell to the "any marker" branch.
- **qwen38's `mounted_at: /chat_template.jinja` is a suffix** that every template mounted over a model dir ends with.

## The fix

Chat templates now go through `_chat_template_wired()`, which reads the merged service instead of grepping lines. Docker renders volumes in long form (`source` and `target` on separate keys), while the offline merge keeps `src:target:ro` strings. Both parse to the same pairs.

A template counts as wired only when **one service** has both of these:

1. **A mount of the patch's own template:** the source ends with `<dir>/<file>` from `delivery_spec.jinja`, and the target is `mounted_at`.
2. **A flag that selects it:** `--chat-template-file` if `invoke` names it, otherwise `--chat-template`. The flag must be followed by that same mount target, or written as `flag=target`. Comments inside an entrypoint script don't count.

No flag is needed for `wired_at: [volumes]` (carnice), or when `mounted_at` has a single path component (qwen38). That template is mounted over the model dir's own file, whose path differs per weights variant, and SGLang loads it without a flag. `command` and `entrypoint` are treated alike.

`generate_compose.py` is unchanged: it keeps its own marker list. The chat_template block in `_spec_wiring_markers` only fed `reaches()`, so it is removed.

## Measured (registry slugs, 170)

| patch | reaches before | reaches after | load-bearing |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `qwen38-reasoning-effort-template` | 108 | **62** | 62 |
| `apex-qwen-chat-template` | 92 | **4** | 4 |
| `glm53-minja-numeric-index` | 92 | **18** | 0 (`composes: null`) |
| `gemma-google-canonical-chat-template` | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| `qwen-froggeric-chat-template` | 16 | 16 | 16 |
| `qwen-carnice-chat-template` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- The "after" counts are identical with `docker compose config` and with the offline merge.
- **The 18 glm53 reaches are real wiring.** All 18 GLM composes mount `glm53-minja-numeric-index/chat_template.jinja` and pass `--chat-template-file /etc/glm53-chat-template.jinja`. The patch declares `load_bearing_when: composes: null`, so they show up as "not load-bearing".

body:
Fixes #1597.

## What was wrong

`patch_attribution.reaches()`, which `test-patch-attribution`, `generate_compose` and the pull gate rely on, reported install-script patches as wired on composes that never mount them. On `master`:

- **911** (patch, compose) pairs passed **only** through the legacy `delivery:` fallback. Its markers were a directory's parent name (`patches`, present in every compose that mounts any patch) and generic script names (`install.sh`).
- Stripping a patch's own mount and invoke from its own compose still passed.
- Inside the spec check itself:
  - the vLLM and SGLang W4A8 patches share the mount target `/etc/club3090/w4a8`, so each "reached" the other's composes;
  - entrypoint-only and unknown-`wired_at` specs accepted a bare `install.sh`;
  - three specs (Gemma #42006, #40391, #40886) had prose in `invoke` and no `mounted_at`, so they could only ever pass through the fallback.

## Fix

- **A patch with a `delivery_spec` is judged by the spec check alone.** The legacy fallback stays for spec-less entries (none are install-script entries today), without the parent-dir marker and without generic script names.
- **Source-aware volume marker:** the patch's own directory, or its file's directory, must sit on the same line as the mount target.
- **Specific invoke markers win** where the invoke decides on its own; a generic `install.sh` counts only when nothing more specific is declared. The volumes + entrypoint branch is unchanged: its volume check is now precise, and the SGLang W4A8 composes invoke indirectly (`_p=/etc/club3090/w4a8; bash "$_p/install.sh"`).
- **The three prose specs** now name the real mount and command; the prose moved to `note`.

## Result

Reach counts now match the real mounts:

| patch | reaches (before → after) | composes that actually mount it |
|---|--:|--:|
| `fa2-fp8kv-sm86` | 76 → **12** | 12 |
| `vllm-51581-dflash-dense-kv` | 76 → **24** | 24 |
| `gemma-a4b-vllm-pr40886-awq-moe-keys` | 76 → **0** | 0 (only an archived compose) |
| `qwen-w4a8-int8-act` (vLLM) | 48 → **23** | its own vLLM composes |
| `qwen38-sglang-autoround-w4a8-v0519` | 48 → **25** | its own SGLang composes |
| `vllm-pr48375-…`, `vllm-flashinfer-decode-pin` | unchanged (46, 37) | 46, 37 |

Every declared load-bearing compose still reaches: `test-patch-attribution` passes, 79 entries.

## Verified

- **Five negative controls added to `test-patch-attribution`.** Three composes have one patch's mount and invoke stripped (flashinfer pin on vLLM dual-fast, SGLang W4A8 on SGLang dual-fast, Gemma #40391 on gemma-int8-mtp). Two are cross-patch pairs: each W4A8 patch must not reach the other engine's compose. **All five fail on `master`'s `patch_attribution.py` and pass here.**
- Tier 0 plus every test that reads `patches.yml` or calls `reaches()`: 30 / 30, including `test-generate-compose`, `test-pull` and `test-caveat-patch-ambiguity`.

## Not in this PR

The **chat-template** class still over-reports: `qwen38-reasoning-effort-template` reaches 109 composes against 62 load-bearing. Its volume marker is the generic `<model dir>/chat_template.jinja`, which other models' templates also mount over. It runs on a separate path (the effective-merge check), so I've left it for its own change.

body:
## What

A **server-side reasoning budget chosen by effort** on every Qwen3.8-27B and ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B vLLM and SGLang compose:

| effort | budget (reasoning tokens) |
|---|--:|
| `low` (and `minimal`) | 4,096 |
| `medium` | 16,384 |
| `xhigh` (and `high`, `max`) | 32,768 |

The budget closes the reasoning and hands over to the answer, rather than cutting the answer off at `max_tokens`.

**Precedence, both engines:** an explicit per-request budget > the map for the effort in use > a floor (the budget of the compose's default effort, `low` → 4,096).

**The effort in use:** the request's top-level `reasoning_effort`, then `chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort`, then the server's default. Thinking-off requests get no budget.

**Knobs:** `THINKING_BUDGET_LOW` / `_MEDIUM` / `_XHIGH`, and `THINKING_BUDGETS=off` (catalogued in `launch-knobs.json`, so `switch.sh --set` / `settings.sh` / c3 see them).

Most coding agents can only express *effort*, because the OpenAI API has no budget field, so the effort map is what actually bounds them. Through the LiteLLM gateway (v1.100.3, real route shape, measured against a capture backend):
- `thinking_token_budget`, `custom_params`, `chat_template_kwargs`, `reasoning_effort` and `/v1/messages` `budget_tokens` arrive unchanged;
- `output_config.effort` and adaptive thinking are stripped;
- a Responses-API budget field is dropped, so those clients get the floor.

## How

| Piece | Engine | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/effort_budget.py` | both | All the policy, engine-neutral, stdlib only. The compose entrypoint runs `shell-env` (validates knobs: a bad value refuses the boot, empty = unset) and prints one readback line: `[effort-budget] v1 map=… default_effort=… floor=…` |
| patch **B** `vllm-effort-budget` | vLLM | One inserted call before `request.to_sampling_params(` in `_create_chat_completion` (chat + `/v1/messages`) |
| patch **D** `vllm-default-thinking-budget` | vLLM | The floor in `SamplingParams.__post_init__` (Responses API, completions, batch) — the validated bucko local patch, moved in |
| `--enable-strict-thinking` + `SGLANG_MAX_THINK_TOKENS` | SGLang | Stock enforcement + floor. Think-end ids come from the tokenizer, so they're right for Qwen3.8 |
| patch **C** `sglang-effort-thinking-budget` | SGLang | One call in `_convert_to_internal_request`, `/v1/messages` `budget_tokens` → `custom_params.thinking_budget`, and a `thinking_token_budget` protocol field (one budget field works on both engines) |

**Built to survive engine upgrades:**
- Each hook is one call into the shared module.
- Install scripts are idempotent and use strict anchors: a moved anchor refuses the boot and names the README's re-anchor steps.
- Each patch has `selftest.sh <image>`, which is its `drift_guard.check` in `patches.yml`.
- `scripts/probe-effort-budget.sh <url>` is the live check at every pin bump, with built-in negative (`--expect-off`) and positive (`--positive`) controls.

**Provenance (AGENTS.md "upstream first"):** B, C and D are exception-class `ours` entries, each with a criticality line and a drop trigger. Runaway reasoning is a measured defect, and the shipped SGLang budget path was broken (next section). vllm#55432 (top-level effort only) is the upstream equivalent. It isn't vendored: it touches 5 files and is already behind `main`.

## Fixes along the way

- **SGLang budgets were silently inert.**
  - `thinking-budget.sh` sent SGLang's `Qwen3ThinkingBudgetLogitProcessor`, which hard-codes Qwen3's ids (151667/151668); Qwen3.8 uses 248068/248069 (sglang#20029 closed unmerged).
  - Custom processors are also bypassed under NEXTN/EAGLE-v2 spec decode (sglang#26330).
  - It now uses strict thinking + `custom_params`, and refuses when strict thinking is off.
- **vllm#58231 reproduced live** on v0.31.0 dual-fast (MTP): with `top_k=-1`, `top_p=0.95`, a fired budget produced token 0 (`!!!!`) until `max_tokens`. Because D budgets every request, B and D **skip the default budget for sampled top-k-off rows**, which stay unbounded as on stock vLLM. Drop the guard when the fix is in the pin.
- **The quality wrapper reads the server's budget** from the boot log (the last v1 line), raises the thinking cap to max(16384, budget + 4096), and stamps it on the Quality: line. It passes `--server-thinking-budget` to benchlocal when supported (benchlocal-cli #193).
- **Stale claims corrected:**
  - the AutoRound W4A8 patch is on by default (since c18c8a48);
  - the DFlash2 activation-equivalence note;
  - `sglang-stable` is wired and booted.
- **SGLang compose headers** now name their vendored patches.

## Validated (reference rig, 2× 3090, 2026-10-09)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live probe, tiny budgets (64/128/256, set through the real `switch.sh` env path; the boot line proved they arrived) | ✅ vLLM dual-fast, SGLang dual-fast, ThinkingCap vLLM + SGLang. Every leg: each effort, kwargs-only, explicit budget, both explicit shapes on SGLang, thinking off, `/v1/messages` with/without `budget_tokens`, Responses → floor, two concurrent efforts, the #58231 leg |
| Negative control `THINKING_BUDGETS=off` / positive control (real budgets) | ✅ both engines |
| Thinking-off output, budgets on vs off | ✅ identical greedy output on both engines |
| Wrapper readback against real boots | ✅ "server budget 4096 (the server's default effort, low)" on both engines |
| SGLang strict thinking, S1 (EAGLE/MTP + DFLASH) | ✅ budget 128 → 129 reasoning tokens then the answer; tool calls parse; **no measurable decode cost** (dual-fast 102.2 / 142.4, superfast 129.0 / 219.1 vs pin-bump rows, mixed signs within ±3%) |
| vLLM floor A-B-A-B (dual-fast) | ✅ **no measurable decode cost**: off 89.5 / 124.0 · 81.6 / 113.6 vs on 83.8 / 115.6 · 89.5 / 122.2. The sign flips; means are within ~1% |
| D4 gate: SGLang strict thinking must not regress tool use (`sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`, thinking on, one pass each, this branch vs master) | ✅ **directional**: toolcall-15 12 vs 13 / 15, hermesagent-20 13 vs 14 / 20 — inside single-draw noise (±2/pack). Both differing scenarios inspected: TC-06 — the model *chose* to answer from knowledge ("without needing any tools"), short reasoning, no budget hit, no tool call attempted in `<think>`; HA-05 — agentic verification miss. No sign of strict thinking swallowing a tool call. Not a pass@3 result. |
| Patch selftests on the pinned images | ✅ B and D on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` (incl. 5 #58231-guard cases each), C on `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` (53 ✓) |
| Guards | full sweep 250 / 254. Three of the four failures also fail on master: #1598, #1599 and `test-weights-revision`. The fourth, `test-compose-env-declared-unused`, was introduced by this branch (the knobs are read by the mounted module) and is fixed here. Final tree, gitignored state removed: **50 / 50** (Tier 0 + every touched guard). **c3: 1209 passed, 1 skipped** |

⚠️ After this, benchlocal's `budget_mismatch` flags older thinking baselines (no recorded server budget) as not comparable. That's intended.

Plan and decision log are maintainer-private. Learnings: Qwen3.8-27B 2026-10-09. Follow-ups: #1597 (patch-attribution can't see an unwired install-script patch).

body:
Closes the open question from #1579: **a quality number measures the model as served.**

`quality-test.sh` and `rebench-full.sh` now default to the **server's sampler**: requests carry no sampling params, so the compose's model-card sampler applies. The packs' fixed sampler (greedy with thinking off, benchlocal's generic sampler with it on) becomes the opt-in **reproducible baseline**: `--pack-sampling` / `SAMPLING_FROM_SERVER=0`.

Until now the plain default was the pack sampler, while the documented "⭐ canonical two-leg run" and `--both-modes` used the server's. So the same model scored under different samplers depending on how it was invoked, and "canonical" meant two things.

## What the default does and doesn't override

| You pass | Sampler |
|---|---|
| nothing | the server's (`sampling=server`) |
| `--pack-sampling` / `SAMPLING_FROM_SERVER=0` | the packs' fixed one |
| `-- --temperature …` (and the other sampler flags) | yours; server sampling is switched off, since benchlocal refuses the mix |
| `-- --exit-on-regression` | the packs' fixed one; a regression gate needs reproducible runs, and benchlocal refuses it on server sampling |
| `-- --retry-failed` | its baseline's (benchlocal restores it) |
| `--resume` | the original run's |

**`--resume` needed care.** The old conflict check rejected `--sampling-from-server` whenever `SAMPLING_FROM_SERVER == 1`, so flipping the default naively would have broken **every** resume. The script now records whether the sampling was chosen explicitly. An explicit sampling flag with `--resume` is still refused, as before.

## Callers

- **`rebench-full.sh`:** both 8-pack legs default `SAMPLING_FROM_SERVER` to 1. ⚠️ `=both` runs both legs against **one boot**, so under server sampling each leg gets the sampler the compose booted with. Where that follows the thinking switch (Qwen3.8: `ENABLE_THINKING` chooses the card row at boot), one leg runs on the other mode's row. rebench now **warns** in that case, and the docs say to boot each leg separately there, as the canonical two-leg recipe already does. `--both-modes` has always had this property.
- **`quality-baseline.sh`:** gates on `--pack-sampling` unless you choose; it's a reproducible regression gate.
- **`rerun-failed-packs.sh`:** re-runs under the *original* result's sampler, including its explicit overrides (and never `max_tokens`).
- **`--both-modes`:** no longer injects `--sampling-from-server`; `--pack-sampling` carries over to both legs.
- **c3 test-console:** the quality toggle keeps its meaning (default on; off adds `--pack-sampling`).

## Behaviour changes to know about

- **Default-run numbers change.** A plain `quality-test.sh` or `rebench-full.sh` run after this merges is `sampling=server`; before, it was `sampling=pack:…`. The `Quality:` stamp from #1583 shows which, but c3 and any stored history will show a step change between pre- and post-merge default runs. Compare only across matching stamps. Under the SemVer note, this is a **minor bump** at the next release.
- **Reporting rules reworded.** The pass@1 section and BENCHMARKS rule said `/150` totals are "pass@1 at pack contract, always". They now say "pass@1 under the stated sampler (`sampling=server` since 2026-10-09; the pack sampler before)".
- **Thinking-off legs are now sampled, not greedy**, so single draws are noisier. `--repeat 3` is already the documented advice for quotable numbers.
- **`presence_penalty`** still can't be applied server-side on vLLM / SGLang. That's unchanged and documented, with the per-request workaround in RUN_EVALS.md.

**Follow-up (not filed):** benchlocal-cli still labels server sampling `⚠ NON-CANONICAL (sampling: server defaults …)` in its run header, and warns that results are "NOT comparable to the default temp=0 baseline". After this PR that contradicts club's meaning on every default run. A benchlocal change to word it neutrally (e.g. "sampling: server defaults") would match; I can open it if wanted.

## Validation

- **New `scripts/tests/test-quality-sampling-default.sh`** (13 cases), asserting on the argv the mock benchlocal receives:
  - the default sends `--sampling-from-server`; `--pack-sampling` and `SAMPLING_FROM_SERVER=0` don't;
  - explicit `--temperature`, `--retry-failed` and `--exit-on-regression` aren't overridden;
  - `--resume` gets no flag, and `--resume` with an explicit flag is refused;
  - `--both-modes` puts both legs on the server sampler, and `--pack-sampling` carries to both;
  - `quality-baseline.sh` dry-run uses `--pack-sampling` and your choice wins;
  - `rerun-failed-packs.sh` re-runs server, pack and explicit-override originals each under their own sampler;
  - rebench defaults and the `=both` warning.
- **Negative control:** on master the test fails at its first assertion, `the default should send --sampling-from-server`.
- **Updated tests:**
  - `test-run-context.sh`: a run with no sampling flag now records the server defaults; `--pack-sampling` doesn't.
  - `test-quality-passthrough.sh`: allowlists `--override-generation-config` (vLLM boot flag) and `--retry-failed` (benchlocal), now named in the docs.
  - test-console: a new toggle case; **84/84** against the worktree's code.
- Tier 0 plus every test touching quality-test / baseline / rerun / rebench / sampling / run-context / the docs: **46/46 pass**.
- No live boot: `--sampling-from-server` itself is long-established; only the default changed, and the argv tests cover that.

Docs: `QUALITY_TEST.md` (sampling section rewritten, recipe, flag tables, pass@1 and reporting rules, stamp lists, limitations) and `RUN_EVALS.md` (recipes, SGLang instruct note, flag table).

body:
Fixes #1590. The last two scripts now follow the container rule from #1587 / #1588. With `URL=` set, the container is the one that publishes that URL on this host (`club_container_for_url`); if nothing publishes it, there's no container.

## `report.sh`

`resolve_stage_endpoint()` honoured `URL` / `ENDPOINT`, but **three** sections picked their own container without looking at it:
- the per-card VRAM attribution;
- the KV-math calibration;
- "Active container" (the stack default, then any of ours).

A bundle for `URL=<another machine>`, or for the second of two local engines, therefore put one server's endpoint next to another's logs, image and boot config.

**Now** the container is resolved **once**, at the top level. The sections that read it run in `{ …; } | redact` subshells, so resolving inside them wouldn't persist. The rule:

| Input | Container |
|---|---|
| `CONTAINER=` set | that one (`none` = host engine build, as before) |
| `URL` / `ENDPOINT` set | the one publishing it here, else `none`, reported as *"No local container serves the endpoint (CONTAINER=none) — a remote server or a host process"* (not as a host engine build) |
| neither | the stack-default ladder, unchanged |

`none` reaches the VRAM attribution as empty, because `docker inspect none` succeeds on Docker's built-in network (#1067). One side effect: the VRAM attribution now also honours an explicit `CONTAINER=`; before, it always took the first of ours.

## `spec-sweep.sh`

The reboot path (vLLM / SGLang / exl3) read an arm's acceptance rate from the first container whose **name** carried the engine family (`grep -m1 "$ENGINE_FAMILY"`). With two engines of a family up, or a remote `URL`, another server's rate landed in the arm's row.

**Now** `_measure_vllm_arm` asks the new top-level `_arm_container`: explicit `CONTAINER=`, else `club_container_for_url "$URL"`, else nothing, which gives an honest `—`. The arms spec-sweep boots publish the slug's port, so the booted container is always the one found. The llama.cpp fast path reads per-request timings and never used this picker.

AGENTS.md: both scripts are now listed as using the rule. c3's `detect.py` is described accurately: it has its own picker, but takes no `URL=` and admits only registry-claimed or engine-named containers. (#1587's PR description claimed otherwise; that was wrong, as noted in #1590.)

## Validation

New `scripts/tests/test-pickers-follow-url.sh`:
- **spec-sweep:** `_arm_container`, extracted from the script and run against a docker stub that lists the wrong `vllm-*` first:
  - picks the container serving `URL`;
  - a remote URL gives nothing;
  - an explicit `CONTAINER=` wins, and `CONTAINER=none` gives nothing.
- **report.sh,** end to end through the report harness. The docker stub lists the stack default (`vllm-qwen36-*`, another port) first, and the URL is served by a second (SGLang) container:
  - the Active container is the SGLang one;
  - `URL=http://remote.invalid:…` reports "No local container serves the endpoint" and names no container;
  - with no URL, the stack default is still picked (positive control).

Follow-up to #1588. With the right container chosen, a remote URL now has **no** local container, but the card still measured this machine.

## Bug

With no container, `concurrency_probe.py` scopes VRAM to every GPU on this host, and the card's GPU field lists them. Pointed at a remote endpoint, the probe printed `2× GeForce RTX 3090` and a VRAM curve of whatever *this* machine was doing, on another server's card.

## Change

A **remote endpoint** is one where no local container serves the URL **and** the URL's host isn't this machine. That second test is the new `url_on_this_host` in `listen-scope.sh`: loopback, this host's own addresses, or a name resolving to either. For a remote endpoint:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| card GPU field | this rig's GPUs | `remote GPUs n/a` |
| `[probe] VRAM measured on:` | `every GPU on the host (rig-wide…)` | `none — remote endpoint; VRAM is not measured from this host` |
| verdict VRAM line | `cold … -> warm … MB` (this host's numbers) | `VRAM: not measured (…)` |
| `RESULT … vram_gpus=` | `all` | `none` |

- VRAM is scoped to an empty selection, which makes it unmeasured (`-1`). That's the same path a host without `nvidia-smi` takes, and the fit verdict already skips it.
- **Unchanged:** a host-process server (no container, localhost URL) is still measured rig-wide, because its GPUs are this rig's. A containerised local server is scoped to its container's GPUs as before (#1502).

## Validation

- Live on the reference rig, with `--sweep --n 1`:
  - `URL=http://remote.invalid:8020`: card `remote GPUs n/a`, `VRAM: not measured`, `vram_gpus=none`;
  - a free local port: `2× GeForce RTX 3090`, VRAM measured rig-wide, `vram_gpus=all`.
- `test-concurrency-probe.sh`, new end-to-end legs:
  - remote (`.invalid` never resolves, RFC 6761, so the sweep finishes in seconds): the three remote assertions;
  - a free local port: not labelled remote, measured rig-wide (positive control).
- `test-preflight-autodetect.sh`: 9 `url_on_this_host` cases (localhost, `0.0.0.0`, `[::1]`, own LAN IP, own hostname, a name resolving to this host, a remote IP, a remote name, an unresolvable name).
- **Negative control:** master's probe fails `a remote endpoint's card should say 'remote GPUs n/a'`.
- Tier 0 plus every test touching concurrency-probe / listen-scope / club-containers / served-slots / rebench, and the stub-lifecycle guard: **41/41 pass**. No `results/` cards left behind.

body:
Follow-up to #1584 / #1587. #1587 listed `concurrency-probe.sh`'s container choice as not covered; this covers it.

## Bug

`concurrency-probe.sh` picked its container in two ways, and both are wrong for a URL on another machine:

1. **Port-only match.** The Python `container_for_url` (#1537) compared the port and ignored the host, so `URL=http://<other host>:8020` bound the local container on :8020.
2. **Name fallback.** When nothing matched, the `vllm-(qwen|gemma)` heuristic bound one anyway.

That container supplies the slot count (`served-slots.sh` reads its `--max-num-seqs` first), the GPU label, the spec label and the KV pool. A remote run therefore reported the local server's values as its own. Reproduced: with a local vLLM on :8020 at `--max-num-seqs 4`, `URL=http://10.9.9.9:8020` announced `CONCURRENCY=4 (detected: container max-num-seqs)`.

## Fix

- The probe now uses `club_container_for_url`, the helper preflight's autodetect and `soak-test.sh` already share since #1587. It returns the container that publishes `URL` on this host through an engine port, respecting the bind address and resolving hostnames, or nothing.
- The Python matcher and its `--container-for-url` flag are removed; nothing else called them.
- **An explicit `CONTAINER=` is trusted.** `CONTAINER=none` (which `rebench-full.sh --url` sets) means host-only: no lookup, passed to the Python helpers as empty, which they already handle (`if not container`). Only an unset `CONTAINER` is resolved.
- **No new output line.** The first line stays the sweep header, which callers and tests read. When there's no container, the slot detector's FATAL already says "no container flag", and the card's GPU scope says "rig-wide: no container to scope to".
- AGENTS.md: `concurrency-probe.sh` moves from "not on this rule" to "asks it too". Still separate, unchanged: `spec-sweep.sh`, `report.sh`, c3's `detect.py`.

**Not changed:** for a remote URL the card still measures VRAM and labels GPUs from *this* host ("rig-wide"). The probe assumes a local server, and changing that is a larger question.

## Validation

`test-concurrency-probe.sh`:
- The container cases now use the shared helper, plus a new negative: another machine's `:8144` gives nothing.
- The checks that the script uses the helper now look for `club_container_for_url` and for the absence of the name heuristic in non-comment lines.
- **New end-to-end slot case.** It uses a docker stub (local vLLM on :8020, `--max-num-seqs 4`) and a curl that never answers:
  - remote URL: no `CONCURRENCY=4 (detected: container …)`, and a loud `FATAL: cannot detect the served slot count`;
  - the container's own URL: `CONCURRENCY=4 (detected: container max-num-seqs)` (positive control).
  - `CONTAINER=none` with a URL the stub publishes: no container flags read.
  - The stub publishes a **free port**, not :8020 (the reference rig's default serving port), so the positive leg can never send load to a live server.
- **Negative control:** master's probe with the static checks disabled fails the end-to-end case with `a remote URL took the LOCAL container's --max-num-seqs as its slot count`.

**Test hygiene (predates this PR).** The test's `--sweep` legs run against a dead URL, and `--sweep` always writes its card to `results/concurrency-<ts>-<model>.{md,json}`. Every run of this test left a card for a run that measured nothing; 264 had piled up in the main checkout since 2026-08-23. The test's EXIT cleanup now removes only the cards this run created. Verified: `results/` is unchanged after a run. The 264 existing files in the main checkout are untouched; deleting them is your call.

Tier 0 plus every test touching concurrency-probe / club-containers / served-slots / rebench, and the stub-lifecycle guard: **39/39 pass**.

body:
Fixes #1584.

Endpoint autodetect (`preflight_autodetect_endpoint`) is used by verify / verify-full / verify-stress / bench / bench-agentic / health / rebench-full / quality-test / power-cap-sweep. It attached serving scripts to containers that weren't the inference server, in three ways:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing set; SearXNG (8088→8080) and Open WebUI up, no engine | picked **SearXNG** as "the inference container", `URL=http://localhost:8088` | nothing bound; the caller's defaults stand |
| `URL=` another machine, a local engine up | bound the local engine: its logs, sampling defaults and `tp` were read as the remote server's | `CONTAINER=none` (host-only), with a notice |
| `URL=` the second local engine's port | bound the **first** engine | binds the one that publishes that URL |
| `CONTAINER=` the second engine, no `URL=` | URL came from the **first** engine's port | URL is the named container's own port |

## How

- **`:8080` needs evidence, like `:5000` already did.** A line counts only for one of our containers by name, or when the image names an engine (`engine_kind_from_image`, the shared classifier). A BYO llama.cpp container (any name, a llama.cpp image) is still found. `docker ps` lines now carry the image (`name|ports|image`); a two-field line gets only the name check.
- **`URL=` → `club_container_for_url`** (new, in `club-containers.sh`). It returns the container that publishes that URL on this host through an engine-internal port. The check is `ports_serve_url` (new, in `listen-scope.sh`). It respects the bind address (a `127.0.0.1` publish isn't reachable on the LAN IP), port ranges, and hostnames (resolved with `getent`, so `URL=http://<rig hostname>:PORT` works). A URL you named needs no evidence, so whatever publishes it on an engine port is the server. If nothing does, `CONTAINER=none`, the host-only value `power-cap-sweep`, `bench`, `soak`, `rebench` and others already honour (and `health.sh` reports "server may be on another machine").
- **`soak-test.sh`** has its own picker and wasn't gated on the URL. It now asks the same `club_container_for_url` for an `ENDPOINT` / `URL` it was given, and falls back to host mode.
- **`rebench-full.sh`'s snapshot** re-picked "the first of ours by name". It now snapshots the container preflight chose and keeps the name heuristic as the fallback.
- **#1583's guard in `quality-test.sh` is removed**, because autodetect now makes that choice for every caller. `container_serves_url` is replaced by `ports_serve_url` and has no other users.

## Behaviour changes to know about

- A `URL=` with no local container behind it (a host-build llama-server, or a remote box) now gets `CONTAINER=none` and a notice. Before, `CONTAINER` stayed unset and verify/bench fell back to the `vllm-qwen36-27b` literal. That's equivalent in practice, since docker calls fail on a missing container either way.
- `URL=` the LiteLLM gateway (`:4000`) gives `CONTAINER=none`, so a gateway-routed run doesn't scrape a local engine's logs, VRAM or spec-decode stats. The documented gateway flow (`docs/QUALITY_TEST.md`, DashScope) targets a cloud model, where that is correct. To route the gateway to a local engine, set `CONTAINER=<engine>`.
- A `URL=` you name binds whatever publishes it on an engine-internal port, with no evidence check: `URL=http://localhost:8088` binds SearXNG, because you pointed at it.
- **`:5000` widened, deliberately.** The evidence rule also admits a BYO TabbyAPI image on 5000. #1360 made 5000 name-only; an engine image is the same evidence the 8080 rule relies on. The drift guard's header now says so.

## Not covered (separate pickers, not on this rule)

- `concurrency-probe.sh` finds the container by URL (#1537), but falls back to a `vllm-(qwen|gemma)` name heuristic when nothing matches, so a remote URL can still bind a local container there.
- `spec-sweep.sh` picks by engine family for its own sweep boots. `report.sh` picks the stack default or any of ours for the local rig bundle; it doesn't use autodetect.
- c3's `tools/tui-core/.../detect.py` still treats 8080 as self-evident.

These are listed in AGENTS.md next to the rule.

## Validation

New `scripts/tests/test-preflight-autodetect.sh`:
- 18 `ports_serve_url` cases;
- 14 autodetect scenarios against a mocked `docker ps`, a fake `hostname -I` and `getent`;
- 3 `club_container_for_url` cases;
- `soak-test.sh` end to end, asserted at the docker layer: a remote URL never inspects the local container, and the container's own URL does (the positive control).

Negative controls:
- master's `preflight.sh` + `club-containers.sh` fail **9 of the 14** scenarios, one for each bug shape, and pass the positive controls and the unchanged cases;
- master's `soak-test.sh` fails the soak leg;
- `test-engine-port-set-drift` (new :8080 controls) and `test-health-container` (new remote-URL case) both fail on master's code and pass on this branch.

Live on the reference rig (no engine up; SearXNG, Open WebUI and LiteLLM running):

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| nothing set | nothing bound (master picks `searxng`) |
| `URL=http://10.9.9.9:8020` | `CONTAINER=none` |
| `URL=http://localhost:4000` | `CONTAINER=none` |
| `CONTAINER=litellm` | "publishes no engine port", `URL` left unset |

`ports_serve_url` against litellm's real publish (`0.0.0.0:4000`) accepts localhost, `[::1]`, the rig's hostname and its LAN IP, and refuses another port and a remote IP.

Tier 0 plus every test touching preflight / club-containers / listen-scope / soak / rebench / quality-test / health: **65/65 pass** on the final tree.

body:
Fixes #1579.

## What was wrong

1. **Override runs were mislabelled as canonical.** The `Quality:` line stamped only `sampling=server`. A run with explicit `--temperature` / `--top-p` overrides printed the same line as a canonical run. Example: a 2026-09-23 result measured with the Qwen3.8 card's instruct sampler (`temperature=0.7/top_p=0.8/top_k=20/min_p=0`, thinking OFF).
2. **Remote `URL=` runs could carry the local rig's facts.** `preflight_autodetect_endpoint` binds the first container on an engine port even when `URL=` points somewhere else. `run_context.py` then read *that* container's boot log, so a run against another machine recorded the local container's server sampling defaults and `tp` as its own. Reproduced on this rig: `URL=http://10.9.9.9:9999` bound `CONTAINER=searxng`.

## What changes

**Every `Quality:` line now names its sampler.** The stamp follows the precedence `runner.build_request` applies to each request:

| Stamp | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sampling=server` | `--sampling-from-server` (unchanged spelling) |
| `sampling=explicit temperature=0.7/top_p=0.8/…` | sampler overrides; they win on both legs |
| `sampling=pack+extra-body …` / `sampling=pack+thinking-sampler …` | the pack contract, modified by those flags |
| `sampling=pack:greedy` / `pack:thinking` / `pack` | canonical OFF / ON / mixed |
| *(none)* | results JSON from before 2026-05-24, when benchlocal didn't record its sampler yet |

- `max_tokens` is a budget, not a sampler. The wrapper's default 4,096 rides in `sampling_overrides` on every run, and it never reads as `explicit`. That case is the negative control in the test.
- The emitter moves from an inline heredoc to `scripts/lib/quality_line.py`, so it can be tested from fixture JSONs.

**An auto-detected container is kept only if it serves `URL`.** It must publish `URL`'s port on this host, where "this host" means loopback, its own addresses, or a hostname resolving to either. Otherwise the wrapper ignores it and prints a notice. An explicit `CONTAINER=` is still trusted.
- Behaviour change: `--thinking-budget` against a truly remote `URL` now refuses ("cannot tell which engine family"). Before, it guessed the engine family from the wrong local container.

**Docs (`docs/QUALITY_TEST.md`).**
- Fixed "the packs sample at temperature 0 by default": that is true for the OFF leg only. The ON leg uses benchlocal's t1.0 / p0.95 / k20 / min_p 0 thinking sampler; hermesagent-20 stays greedy.
- Added the stamp table.
- Noted that `quality-test.sh --both-modes` (server sampler) and `rebench-full.sh --with-8pack-thinking=both` (pack contract) use different samplers.

## ⚠️ Convention decision — yours to veto

I kept the convention as it is: **canonical = the pack contract, so the thinking-OFF leg is greedy.**
- I did not move the OFF leg to the card's sampler.
- I did not align `--both-modes` with rebench `=both`; the stamp now makes the difference visible on every line instead.

There is a tension in the doc that this PR does not resolve. The "⭐ canonical two-leg run" recipe uses `--sampling-from-server`, while "Sampling & temperature" calls the pack contract canonical. Which one is *the* canonical is the issue's open question.

## Known limitation

benchlocal doesn't persist `--thinking-sampler` or `--extra-body` in the results JSON, so the stamp reads those two from the wrapper's own argv. On `--resume` they come back from the journal instead, so a resumed run that used them stamps `pack:*`.

## Follow-ups found (not filed — say which you want)

- **benchlocal-cli header bug.** The header prints `⚠ NON-CANONICAL (sampling: max_tokens=4096)` for budget-only overrides (`cli.py:840`). The Results Card table already filters `max_tokens`, so the header and this Quality line disagree on every default wrapper run.
- **benchlocal-cli persistence gap.** `RunResult.to_dict` doesn't persist `thinking_sampler` / `extra_body`. This causes the limitation above.
- **preflight autodetect.** It treats any container whose internal port is 8080 as llama.cpp, so on this rig with no engine up every serving script picks `searxng` at `:8088`. It also binds a container whenever only one of `URL` / `CONTAINER` is set. This PR guards only `quality-test.sh`.
- **Test-order dependence.** `test-hwdetect` leaves schema-2 captures in `.pull-captures/`, and a later `test-trust-pipeline` reads them as real captures and fails (`manifest schema must be 1, got 2`). It passes in isolation.

## Validation

- New `scripts/tests/test-quality-sampling-stamp.sh`:
  - 17 stamp cases from fixture JSONs;
  - 15 `container_serves_url` cases against a fake `docker port` / `hostname -I` / `getent`;
  - 3 wrapper-level cases with a mocked docker: a remote URL drops the container; an autodetected URL keeps it (positive control); an explicit `CONTAINER=` is trusted.
- Negative controls, each confirmed red:
  - guard removed;
  - notice kept but the container not cleared;
  - `max_tokens` counted as a sampler.
- Live check of `container_serves_url` against real `docker port` output (litellm on :4000): localhost, `[::1]`, the rig's hostname and its LAN IP are accepted; a different port and a remote IP are refused.
- Tier 0 plus every test touching `quality-test.sh` / `listen-scope` / `run_context`: **38/38 pass**.
- `test-quality-passthrough`'s drift guard now allowlists `--thinking-sampler` as a pass-through flag.

body:
Stub HTTP servers started by the test suite were outliving their tests. On the reference rig, ~60 orphaned stub processes were found, some running for 10 days, plus 2 orphaned engine stubs from a different test. They hold ports and memory, and they accumulate with every run.

## Two leak shapes
1. **A function that records `$!` is called inside a command substitution.** The PID is appended to the array inside the substitution's subshell, so the EXIT trap never sees it.
2. **A long-lived server whose only stop is an explicit `kill` after use.** An abort under `set -e`, or an interrupt, between start and kill skips the kill, and the EXIT trap only removed a temp dir.

## Fixes (before → after measured with each test's `master` version vs this branch)
| Test | Shape | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test-served-model-id.sh` | 1 | **6 orphans on every run** (the ~60) | 0. `start_stub` runs in the parent shell and sets a variable |
| `test-concurrency-probe.sh` | 2 | **2 orphaned engine stubs** after an injected abort (the pair found in the wild) | 0. The EXIT trap kills the registered PIDs |
| `test-deep-context-probe.sh` | 2 | **1 orphaned fake engine** after an abort once it is up | 0 |
| `test-verify-stress-salt.sh` | 2 | **1 orphaned mock engine** on SIGTERM | 0 |
| `test-bench-agentic-ramp.sh` | 1 | no orphan observed (the subshell outlives a killed parent and stops the mock itself), but `cleanup()`'s kill of `server_pid` was dead code | `run_bench` runs in the parent and sets `$out`, so the cleanup it already had now works |

The trap kills use `|| true`. The PIDs are usually already gone, and under `set -e` a failing `kill` aborts the trap before its `rm`. Checked: bash runs the EXIT trap on both SIGTERM (what `timeout` sends) and SIGINT, so the interrupt hardening is real.

## Guard
New **`test-tests-stub-lifecycle.sh`**. It's tree-wide and picked up by the Tier 0 derivation, since it greps the tree.
- **Rule 1:** a function that records `$!` must not be called inside a command substitution.
- **Rule 2:** a test that backgrounds a server must set an EXIT trap that kills it (directly, or through the function it names).
- Comments are stripped quote-aware, and functions defined mid-line or one-line are understood.
- **Negative controls:**
  - built-in bad fixtures for both rules, plus a correct fixture that must pass;
  - dropping `master`'s five originals into the tree makes it name each one under the right rule.

## Testing
- **Tier 0:** 26/26, including the new guard.
- **The six affected tests:** all pass, and each leaves **zero** orphaned processes, checked by diffing the process table before and after each run.

body:
Fixes #1578 (reported in #1572).

## Correction to the issue
#1578 proposed adding a container probe. **That probe already exists** (the #960 hermes container-reachability preflight): it runs a throwaway container against `host.docker.internal:<port>` and stops the run with exit 2. What it got wrong is the **diagnosis**. Any failed probe printed "appears bound to loopback only", and its bypass hint was wrong too.

## What was wrong (all reproduced on a real Docker host)
| Server | From a sandbox via `host.docker.internal` | Old message |
|---|---|---|
| bound `127.0.0.1` / published `-p 127.0.0.1:P:…` | unreachable | loopback only ✓ |
| bound `0.0.0.0`, but a host firewall drops docker0 → host | unreachable | "loopback only" ✗, and the suggested fix (bind to 0.0.0.0) is already in place |
| bound to a LAN address only | unreachable | "loopback only" ✗ |
| bound to the bridge address `172.17.0.1` only | reachable, **but `127.0.0.1` stops answering on the host** | n/a |

The bypass hint named `--no-sandbox`, which doesn't exist (the flag is `--no-sandboxed`). It also said "unset `BENCHLOCAL_HERMES_RESOLVE_LOCALHOST`", which doesn't bypass anything: the wrapper sets it again whenever it's empty.

## Change
- **`scripts/lib/listen-scope.sh`** classifies what the port listens on (`ss -ltnH "sport = :P"`): `wildcard` / `bridge` / `loopback` / `specific` / `none` / `unknown`.
- **`quality-test.sh`**: when the probe fails, the preflight names the actual cause and its fix:
  - **loopback only:** `BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1` → back to `0.0.0.0`; `-p P:<port>`, not `-p 127.0.0.1:P:<port>`; `--host 0.0.0.0`;
  - **`0.0.0.0` yet unreachable:** the bind isn't the problem, it's a host firewall (`sudo ufw allow in on docker0 to any port P proto tcp`);
  - **a LAN address only:** run against that address; a non-loopback URL is used as-is.
  - The off-LAN option (bind to the Docker bridge address) now says the URL has to change along with it.
  - The same classifier replaces the old `ss` grep fallback used when no probe image is cached.
- **Bypass hint:** now `--no-sandboxed`, or `BENCHLOCAL_HERMES_RESOLVE_LOCALHOST=0`.
- **`docs/QUALITY_TEST.md`** (Limitations §2): the causes, the fixes and the bypass.

## Testing
- **New `test-hermes-reachability.sh`:**
  - **A:** 12 classifier cases (`ss` stubbed), including IPv6, `*`, mixed listener sets and the `%iface` suffix.
  - **B:** a live leg with the real `ss`. A real server bound to 127.0.0.1 reads `loopback`; one bound to 0.0.0.0 reads `wildcard`.
  - **C:** the real wrapper driven to its preflight (docker / ss / curl / benchlocal-cli stubbed):
    - each cause → exit 2 plus the matching message;
    - a reachable endpoint passes and runs;
    - the no-probe-image fallback, both ways;
    - both bypass hints actually bypass;
    - "unset" does not bypass;
    - a self-check that the container probe really ran, so the assertions aren't vacuous.

body:
Fixes #1577 (reported in #1572).

## Problem
- **SGLang over `--url` fell back to N=1 needlessly.** `rebench-full.sh`'s concurrency step had its own copy of `concurrency-probe.sh`'s slot detector, minus the SGLang sources (`--max-running-requests`, `/get_server_info`). The probe could read an SGLang endpoint's slot count; rebench could not, so it ran only the N=1 control.
- **vLLM over `--url` falls back to N=1, and only the step log said so.** vLLM reports no slot count over HTTP (`/server_info` needs `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`), so the fallback itself is right. But the banner still said `rungs 1 2 4`, and neither the summary nor `REPORT.md` mentioned that the N>1 rungs were skipped.

## Change
- **`scripts/lib/served-slots.sh`** is now the one detector. Same order as the probe's (#818): container `--max-num-seqs`, `-np`, `--max-running-requests`, then SGLang `/get_server_info`, then llama.cpp `/props`. Booleans and `0` don't count as a slot count. It also writes and reads `concurrency-slots.txt` (slots, source, rungs, override).
- **`rebench-full.sh`**:
  - uses the shared detector;
  - the banner says up front that a vLLM endpoint over `--url` runs N=1 unless `CONCURRENCY_RUNGS` is set;
  - the concurrency step writes the marker;
  - the end-of-run summary prints `⚠ concurrency: N=1 only …` with the fix.
- **`concurrency-probe.sh`**: `_detect_slots`, the sweep's slot-source label and the `CONCURRENCY` default all use the shared detector. Its five private helpers are removed. The labels the existing tests assert (`server max_running_requests`, …) are unchanged.
- **`rebench-report.py`**: an N=1-only run is flagged in the TL;DR and in the Concurrency section. Otherwise it states the rungs and where the slot count came from (`N=1/2/4 (served slots 4, from server max_running_requests)`).

## Testing
- **New `test-served-slots.sh`** (hermetic: stub HTTP endpoints plus a `docker` PATH stub). It covers:
  - every source, the precedence order, and the `=`-form flag;
  - that booleans and `0` are rejected;
  - the marker and summary note;
  - `REPORT.md` for undetected, detected and override runs;
  - a guard against private detector copies coming back. Negative control: master's `rebench-full.sh` trips it at both of its old parsers.
- **Existing tests:** `test-concurrency-probe.sh` and `test-concurrency-probe-verdict.sh` pass. The first includes the sweep-header slot-source assertion, which now runs through the shared detector.
- **Tier 0 tree-wide guards:** 25/25. **Tests touching rebench** (bench-capture, default-url-gateway, engine-detection-sglang, measurement-record-resolve, quality-passthrough): all pass.
- **End to end, the real `rebench-full.sh --url …`** against stub endpoints (heavy steps skipped):
  - **vLLM-shaped endpoint:** the banner warns, the marker reads `slots=undetected`, the summary prints the ⚠ line, and `REPORT.md` flags it in both places.
  - **SGLang-shaped endpoint:** `served slots: 4 (detected: server max_running_requests)`, rungs `1 2 4`, no warning anywhere. On master this case ran N=1 only.

body:
## Problem

`quality-test.sh --thinking-budget N` on vLLM checks that the server has a reasoning parser, because vLLM rejects `thinking_token_budget` per request without one. The check only looked at the container's argv (`docker inspect`).

An image that starts vLLM **through its own launcher** adds `--reasoning-parser` inside that script, so the argv shows none. The wrapper then refused with "booted WITHOUT --reasoning-parser", which counts as positive evidence and so can't be overridden with `THINKING_BUDGET_UNVERIFIED=1`.

Seen on bucko's official image. Its `qwen38-serve` adds `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, and the server's boot log shows `'reasoning_parser': 'qwen3'` in `non-default args`. Sending the budget directly worked: `thinking_token_budget: 200` cut reasoning from 1,343 to 548 characters, and the answer was still produced.

## Fix

- `scripts/lib/thinking-budget.sh`: when the argv has no parser, the vLLM branch reads the boot log's `non-default args` line and accepts the parser it reports, naming that source in the evidence. If neither has a parser, it still refuses, and the message now says both were checked.
- `docs/QUALITY_TEST.md`: the verification-table row says so.

## Verification

- `test-quality-thinking-budget`: the docker mock gains `logs`. New cases:
  - **I2:** launcher-started vLLM with the parser only in the boot log → accepted, and the budget is sent as `{"thinking_token_budget": 8192}`.
  - **I3 (negative):** a boot log without a parser → still refused.
- **Negative control:** against the previous `thinking-budget.sh`, I2 fails (refused, no extra-body).
- Tier 0 + thinking tests: **30/30**.
- **Live:** a graceful 16K-budget re-run on bucko Swift-1.5 (4 cli-40 scenarios) went through this path. The verifier reported "vLLM's boot log reports reasoning_parser=qwen3", and the budget took effect, cutting reasoning at 16,383 with an answer produced after it.

Fixes the VRAM misattribution seen in #1537's report.

## Problem

`report.sh` → "Display / desktop state" found **one** running club container and credited it with **every** card that had more than 100 MiB in use. #1537's report said GPUs 0 and 2 were "held by running `sglang-cmp170hx`", but that container could only see GPU 1, and `nvidia-smi` showed another container's `VLLM::Worker_TP0/1` on GPUs 0 and 2.

## Fix

A new `gpu_vram_report_lines` in `scripts/lib/gpu-select.sh`, called by `report.sh`, attributes **per card**:

1. **Host `--query-compute-apps`**: each process on the card is mapped to its container through `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` (falls back to the process name).
2. **The container's own compute-apps view** (existing `gpu_select_container_uuids`), for hosts whose `nvidia-smi` lists no processes.

A card with memory in use and no owner found is **flagged** (`⚠ … — not <container>`) and never credited to the club container. Example output for the #1537 shape:

```
- **GPU 0 idle VRAM:** 20000 MiB (held by `vllm-other` — not `sglang-cmp170hx`)
- **GPU 1 idle VRAM:** 21000 MiB (held by running `sglang-cmp170hx`)
- **GPU 2 idle VRAM:** 20500 MiB (held by `vllm-other` — not `sglang-cmp170hx`)
```

## Verification

- New `test-report-gpu-attribution` (stubbed `nvidia-smi` / `docker` / `/proc`, no GPU) covers:

  - the container-view fallback;

## Problem

`test-compose-flags-accepted` only read a **list** `command:`. A string command, which is the folded `command: >-` every mainline llama.cpp compose uses, was skipped **without being counted**. So the guard checked none of the 10 functional `llama-cpp-local` composes and still printed ok.

## Problem

`test-spec-toggle-contract` has been red on master on any 3090 host since #1540 (65438792, 2026-10-03):

```
⛔ models/qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/single/autoround-int4/mtp.yml: ships --speculative-config but the default resolves to no drafter
```

The compose is fine. The gate runs each entrypoint with the host's `PATH`, and the single-fast entrypoint sizes itself from the card with `nvidia-smi`: under 30 GiB it takes the lean tier, which ships with the drafter off by design. So the verdict depended on the machine running the gate. A 24 GB host failed it; a host with no GPU (no `nvidia-smi`) fell back to the full tier and passed.

## Fix

- The sandbox carries its own `nvidia-smi`, reporting a fixed card. The default contract is checked on an 80 GB card, i.e. the recipe as written.
- For entrypoints that call `nvidia-smi`, the toggle legs repeat on a 24 GB card. The drafter may default off there (a recipe choice), but `SPEC_N=<n>` must turn it on at that depth and `SPEC_N=0` / `SPEC=off` must keep it off. Without this leg the stub would hide the lean tier from the gate entirely.
- A `SIZE_TIER` exported on the host no longer leaks into the sandbox.
- Two self-tests: an auto-sized shape that passes **only** when the stub answers (flagged on any host if the stub stops being used), and one whose small-card branch overwrites `SPEC_N` (flagged).

body:
## What

`catalog.sh register --dry-run` wrote `scripts/lib/profiles-local/engines.d/<engine>.yml` whenever the compose's engine was unknown, even though the run ended with `[promote] dry-run — nothing written.`. A declined confirm left the file behind the same way.

## Why it happened

`catalog.sh` wrote the engine profile itself, in its own Python, *before* handing the spec to `promote.py`, which owns the plan, the `--dry-run` exit and the confirm. Nothing downstream could stop a write that had already happened.

It also hid itself in the tests: `test-catalog-cli.sh` runs several `--dry-run` registers with the same engine before its real round trip. So the round trip's "engine profile written" check passed on the file the dry runs had leaked.

## Fix

- **`catalog.sh`** puts the engine profile in the spec as `local_engine_profile: {id, yaml}` and no longer writes anything itself.
- **`promote.py`** handles it as part of its gated plan:
  - **Validation:** local layer only (the core layer refuses it: a curated engine profile is a PR to `scripts/lib/profiles/engines/`). A safe id. An existing profile is never overwritten; it's planned as `keep`.
  - **Plan:** it lists `write …/engines.d/<id>.yml (new local ENGINE profile)`, or the keep line.
  - **Write:** it's written first among the local artifacts. That puts it after the plan, the `--dry-run` exit and the confirm, and before the post-write `registry-emit` check, whose cross-reference validation needs the engine to exist.

## Validation

- **`test-catalog-cli.sh`:** new check 2d asserts that the dry runs leave no engine profile, that the dry-run plan names it, and that a second dry run still writes nothing. The existing round trip now proves the real register writes it through `promote.py`.
  - **Negative control:** against master's `catalog.sh` + `promote.py`, all three new checks FAIL.
- **`test_promote.py`, `TestLocalEngineProfile`, 5 tests:** a dry run writes no profile but plans it; a real write lands it; an existing profile is not overwritten; an unsafe id is refused before any write; the core layer refuses the key.
  - **Mutation check:** dropping the write, or overwriting existing profiles, turns them red.
- **Suites:** `test-catalog-*`, pytest modules (143 passed), local-slug-shape and the tree-wide guards, 32/32.

body:
## What

`preflight_compose_deps` (run by `switch.sh` before every launch) refused a compose whose model files were present, for two reasons:

1. **`${MODEL_DIR:-/abs/path}/<sub>` volumes resolved to a doubled path.** `_preflight_compose_path_default` substituted every `${VAR:-default}` *before* stripping the `${MODEL_DIR…}/` prefix. So `${MODEL_DIR:-/mnt/models/huggingface}/x/IQ3_S` became `/mnt/models/huggingface/x/IQ3_S`, the strip found nothing, and the caller prefixed `model_dir` again: `/mnt/models/huggingface//mnt/models/huggingface/x/IQ3_S (MODEL_DIR volume path)` reported missing.
2. **The MODEL_DIR volume extractor scanned comment lines.** A header line such as `# downloaded to ${MODEL_DIR}/x/IQ3_S; setup checks it` was checked as a mount, with the `;` included. The vLLM extractor just above already skips comments.

## Fix

- Strip the `${MODEL_DIR…}` prefix first, then resolve defaults.
- Skip comment lines in the MODEL_DIR volume extractor.

## Scope

No curated compose uses either spelling (checked with a grep of `models/`), so shipped slugs are unaffected. A local-layer Strata recipe hit both: it boots with plain `docker compose` but `switch.sh --force` refused it in 4 s. Local-layer users write their own composes, and `${MODEL_DIR:-/abs}/sub` is a natural spelling.

## Validation

- **`test-preflight-compose-deps.sh` gains a case:**
  - a defaulted volume with the folder present passes;
  - with the folder absent (negative control) it's reported missing once, at the single correct path, with no doubled path and no `;`;
  - a header comment mentioning the path is ignored.
- **Mutation check:** reverting either half of the fix turns the test red.
- **Suites:** `test-preflight*` and the tree-wide guards, 35/35.
