body:
## What

Local slugs can now attach to a **core** model instead of inventing a local model id, through a new additive-only file: `scripts/lib/profiles-local/extends.d/<core-model-id>.yml`.

```yaml
schema_version: 1
extends: qwen3.8-flash-next     # a CORE model id; must match the file name
weights:                        # NEW variants only
  ista-iq3s: {path: ..., size_gb: 83.6, format: gguf, ...}
valid_tp_add: [1]               # optional
```

With that file present, `registry.local.json` entries may use `"model": "qwen3.8-flash-next"`, and any number of them may attach. c3 and `switch.sh --list` show them under the curated model.

## Why

- A second engine, quant or fine-tune of a model we already ship (bucko or Strata on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, the Swift fine-tune) had to be registered under a made-up local model id. So it showed up as a separate "model" in c3 and `--list`.
- **The refusal that forced this was also load-bearing in a way nobody wrote down.** `compat.load_profiles` merged `models.d` *after* core, so a `models.d/<core-id>.yml` replaced the curated profile. Only the registry loader's core-collision refusal stopped that, and a profile file without a registry row slipped straight past it.

## How

- **`local_extensions.py`:** one helper for validation and merging. It refuses:
  - a variant key core already has (an extension can only ADD);
  - an `extends:` that isn't a core model, or that doesn't match the file name;
  - any other top-level key;
  - an unknown key inside a variant.
- **All three readers apply it:**
  - `compat.load_profiles` raises on a bad file.
  - `weights.py` warns and skips; its listing must never go down. It now also imports the helper when run as a script, which is how `setup.sh`, `preflight.sh` and c3 call it.
  - `registry-emit.sh`'s weights facet skips a bad file; c3's format and quant columns read it.
- **`compose_registry.load_local_registry`:**
  - It allows a core model id only when `extends.d/<id>.yml` exists, a stdlib file check that keeps the launcher's PyYAML-free table path.
  - Attached slugs may share a model.
  - The one-slug rule still holds for local-only models, and so does the old refusal when no extension exists.
- **`compat`:** core now wins a `models.d` id collision, with a warning that names `extends.d`.
- **`demote`** reports and keeps the extension file. **`export_pr`** refuses an attached slug and explains how to promote it: add the variant to `models/<id>.yml`.
- **`switch.sh --list`** grouped every local slug under a model called `lib`, the 2nd path segment of `scripts/lib/profiles-local/...`. It now takes the local layout's `composes/<model>/` segment, so attached slugs list under the core model. This was pre-existing and is fixed here because it decides where these slugs appear.
- **`profiles-local/README.md`:** a new "Extending a core model" section, and the stale "two local slugs can share a model id" line corrected.

## Validation

- **New tests:**
  - `TestCoreModelExtensions`, 15 tests: the attach path, the refusals, the core-wins collision, and that `weights.py`, `registry-emit`, `demote` and `export_pr` all behave.
  - `test-switch-local-filter.sh` checks 6 and 7: model grouping for curated, local and attached paths, and both listing passes using it.
- **Mutation check:** each of these turns its test red:
  - local `models.d` winning again;
  - the registry ignoring the extension file;
  - dropping the overlap check;
  - `weights.py` or `registry-emit` skipping extensions;
  - breaking the local branch of the `--list` helper.
- **On a copy of a real local layer** (bucko, Strata dual and single, a new Swift slug), migrated with these files:
  - `switch.sh --list --all` shows all nine Flash-Next slugs under `qwen3.8-flash-next`.
  - `registry-emit --json` reports `model=qwen3.8-flash-next` with the right `weights_format` for each.
  - Diagnose is GREEN for the Strata slugs. bucko's is RED only on its local engine profile's empty capability lists, unchanged from before.
- **Suites:**

body:
## What

`switch.sh` now prints a hint when the NVIDIA open driver's system-memory page pool is holding host RAM:

```
[preflight] NOTE: ~10 GB of host RAM is held outside every /proc/meminfo category and
            does not count as available. With no other GPU program running, this is
            usually the NVIDIA driver's page pool, left by a slug that kept host memory
            through CUDA VMM. The kernel can reclaim it; to free it now:
              sync; echo 2 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches
            (drops only reclaimable kernel caches; cached model files stay. Relaunching
            the slug that filled the pool reuses it, so skip it then.)
```

## Why

OpenRM keeps freed system-memory pages in per-NUMA-node pools to speed up reallocation (`NVreg_EnableSystemMemoryPools`, default `0x211`; `kernel-open/nvidia/nv-vm.c`).
- A slug that keeps tens of GB of host memory through CUDA VMM (`cuMemCreate` with `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA`) leaves that much in the pool after it stops.
- Those pages appear in no `/proc/meminfo` category and are not in MemAvailable, so the host-RAM gates read them as used. On the reference rig a ~58 GiB pool made available RAM read 160 GB against ~166 GB needed.
- The pool registers a kernel shrinker, so `drop_caches=2` returns it. It looks like a leak but isn't one, and no module reload is needed.
- Ordinary pinned memory (`cudaHostAlloc`, torch `pin_memory`, the llama.cpp / exl3 offload paths) does not fill the pool. On the reference rig those engines left under 1 GiB.

## How

- **`preflight_nvidia_page_pool` (`scripts/preflight.sh`):**
  - Computes MemTotal minus every meminfo category (hugetlb via `Hugetlb:` or `HugePages_Total` × size, and Zswap included), then subtracts the ZFS ARC.
  - Prints the hint at ≥ 4 GiB, and only when `/proc/driver/nvidia/params` shows pools enabled.
  - Warn-only: it always returns 0.
  - Fixture overrides `NV_POOL_MEMINFO` / `NV_POOL_PARAMS` / `NV_POOL_ARCSTATS` are there for the test.
- **`switch.sh` `up_variant`:** calls it after the teardown, which is when a just-stopped slug's pool appears, and before the LMCache / CPU-offload RAM gates it explains. It also runs under `--force`. `launch.sh` delegates to `switch.sh`, so it's covered too.
- **What the gap does and doesn't mean:** it is not the pool size. A still-running process's VMM host memory sits there too, which is why the message says "with no other GPU program running" and never blocks. Running the hint when nothing can be freed is harmless.

## Validation

- **New `scripts/tests/test-preflight-nv-page-pool.sh`, 16/16:**
  - It warns on a 58 GiB pool, both alone and with a 10 GiB ARC.
  - It stays quiet on a fresh driver, just under the threshold, with pools off, with no pool parameter, with no `/proc/driver/nvidia`, when the ARC explains the gap, and with a 13 GiB hugetlb arena (both accounting forms).
  - It never blocks.
  - The wiring check asserts the call comes before both RAM gates and is `|| true`.
- **Mutation check:** dropping the hugetlb term, the ARC subtraction or the pools gate each turns the test red.
- **Live on the reference rig (open 610.57.04, pools `529`):**

  | Step | Driver-held | Hint |
  |---|--:|---|
  | Empty pool | 1.32 GiB | quiet |
  | 8 GiB `cuMemCreate(HOST_NUMA)` alloc + full release | 9.41 GiB | fires (~10 GB) |
  | After the hinted `drop_caches` | 1.34 GiB | quiet |

- **Guards:** Tier 0 tree-wide guards + `test-preflight-thp`: 27/27. `test-switch*` + `test-preflight*`: 18/18.

## Problem

This is the last wrong label from @xtj7's #1537 cards (follow-up to #1555 and #1556). `_served_ctx` grepped the container's command for `max-model-len N`, so it read `?` for:

- vLLM auto-fit (`--max-model-len -1`), used by the single-fast composes;
- every SGLang compose, which sets `--context-length` from `CONTEXT_LENGTH` inside the entrypoint.

The value isn't only a label. It also sets the sweep planner's context clip and `VALIDATE`'s default fill target. On those composes the sweep never clipped to the real limit, and `VALIDATE` fell back to 32768.

## Fix

- **New `concurrency_probe.py --served-max-len`.** It reads what the engine reports: SGLang's server-info `context_length`, else vLLM's `/v1/models` `max_model_len`, else vLLM's `max_seq_len` boot-log line (read from the log head). `_served_ctx` tries it first; the command grep stays as the fallback.
- **Wording:** on SGLang the recommendation's first line says "served context length", not "max-model-len".

| Live, reference rig | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-single-fast`, lean tier on one 3090 (command says `--max-model-len -1`, engine serves 81920) | `max-len=?`, "compose default" | `max-len=81920`, "80K" |
| `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` (`context_length` 262144) | `max-len=?` | `max-len=262144` |

The new stubbed tests use vLLM and SGLang stand-in servers driving the real dry-sweep header, plus the boot-line fallback past 3,000 log lines. ## Problem

Follow-up to #1555. Three more labels on @xtj7's #1537 cards were wrong:

- **"KV ?" on both engines.** `--detect-kv` only parsed vLLM's `GPU KV cache size` line, and only from the last 2,500 log lines. A container that has been serving for a while has scrolled past it.
- **`slots=4 (undetected)`, with the count right.** The source label skipped the two SGLang paths `_detect_slots` uses: `max-running-requests` in the container command, and `max_running_requests` on the server info.
- **The SGLang recommendation said `MAX_NUM_SEQS` / `MAX_MODEL_LEN`.** SGLang composes ignore both.

## Fix

- **KV pool:** `detect_kv_tokens(container, url)` reads SGLang's `max_total_num_tokens` from `/get_server_info` first. Failing that, it reads the log tail (the latest boot of a restarted container), then the log head. SGLang's `max_total_num_tokens=` boot line now parses too.
- **Slot source:** `slots_src` covers both SGLang sources, in the same order `_detect_slots` tries them. The engine then resolves to `sglang`.
- **Knob names:** for `engine == "sglang"` the recommendation names `MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS` / `CONTEXT_LENGTH`. 25 of the 27 SGLang composes take those two; the other two are experimental EAGLE3 composes. vLLM and llama.cpp output is unchanged.

| Live `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`, reference rig | header `slots=2 (server max_running_requests) KV=547147`, matching the engine's own boot line; card `KV 547147 · slots 2 · MTP n=4`; recommendation uses `MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS` / `CONTEXT_LENGTH` |

body:
## Problem

The concurrency cards @xtj7 posted on #1537 were mislabelled, and both bugs reproduce on the reference rig:

- **vLLM said "spec off" with MTP n=4 running.** `_spec_fp` greps the container's `Cmd` for `--speculative-config`, but the Qwen3.8 vLLM composes build that flag inside their entrypoint script from `SPEC_N`, so it never appears in `Cmd`.
- **SGLang said "spec ?", listed every GPU on the host and measured VRAM rig-wide.** `CONTAINER` came from a `vllm-(qwen|gemma)` name heuristic, so an SGLang container was never found.

## Fix

- **Container:** `CONTAINER` is now the running container that publishes `URL`'s port, for any engine (`concurrency_probe.py --container-for-url`). The name heuristic stays as a fallback.
- **Spec label:** it comes from what the engine reports (`--spec-label`). For SGLang that's `/get_server_info`; for vLLM it's the engine-config line (`speculative_config=…`), read from the head of the log, because a `--tail` window has scrolled past it on a container that has been serving for a while. The `Cmd` grep stays as a fallback. When the entrypoint script itself mentions spec flags, finding no flag in `Cmd` now reads "spec ?" rather than "spec off".
- **Comma-joined GPU pins:** `run_context.visible_gpu_selectors` now splits a comma-joined `DeviceIDs` entry. A compose `device_ids: ["${ESTATE_GPUS}"]` with `0,1` reaches docker as a single entry, `"0,1"`. This only showed up once the probe found the SGLang container: its card then said "? GPU" with no VRAM reading. `quality-test.sh`'s run metadata reads the same helper, so it gets the fix too.

## Validation

| Check | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Live `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` (MTP n=4), one-rung `--sweep` | `spec off` | `MTP n=4` |
| Live `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` (MTP n=4) | `spec ?`, VRAM rig-wide | `MTP n=4 · 2× GeForce RTX 3090`, VRAM scoped to the container, `leak=0` |
| New stubbed tests (container by port; vLLM log head past 3,000 lines; SGLang server info; joined `DeviceIDs`) | fail | pass |
| `test-concurrency-probe`, `-verdict`, `test-run-context`, Tier 0 guards | — | 28/28 pass |

**Not fixed here:** the card's `KV ?` (`--detect-kv` reads only vLLM's KV line, from the last 2,500 log lines) and the sweep header's `slots=N (undetected)`. The slot count itself is right there; only the label naming its source is wrong.

## Problem

Follow-up to #1552. On a 2-GPU rig, c3 still listed every multi4/multi8 slug at startup, so pressing `h` looked necessary.

The needs-more-GPUs filter got the rig's GPU count only from the estate poll, which first arrives about 20 s after launch (docker + host batch). Until then the count was unknown and the filter showed everything. On the reference rig, 42 multi rows stayed visible until t+22 s.

## Fix

- `_known_gpu_count()` falls back to the fast, docker-free nvidia-smi read (`_refresh_gpu_bars`), which now records the count.
- `on_mount` runs one fast GPU read right after `load_catalog()`. It no longer waits for the first 3 s tick.
- New `_sync_catalog_gpu_count()` re-renders the catalog when the count changes. Both the fast read and the estate poll call it, so whichever learns the count first wins.
- `CatalogPane.refresh_enriched()` is now a no-op before the first `populate` and while the catalog shows a load error. Without this, the early sync replaced "Loading catalog…" or the red "Catalog error" status with "0 variants loaded". The existing `test_catalog_error_surfaces` caught it.

| Real data (headless app on the repo's catalog, 2 GPUs), master | `multi_visible=42` until t+22 s |

body:
Two c3 catalogue defaults made the list mostly noise on a real rig.

## 1. Downloaded-only is now the default, and remembered
`[w]` downloaded-only started **off** on every launch (#963 chose "what COULD I run?"), and the choice wasn't saved, so the usual first keystroke was `w`.
- **Default:** on.
- **Remembered:** the choice is saved as `catalog_downloaded_only` in `c3-settings.json`, the same way the `[s]` sort order already is.
- **Fresh-install fallback:** a rig with nothing downloaded would open on an empty list, so it shows everything instead and the status line says "nothing downloaded yet — showing all — w".

## 2. Slugs needing more GPUs than the rig has are hidden by default
On a 2-GPU rig, the catalogue listed every multi4/multi8 slug: **62 of the 134 non-deprecated slugs** on the reference rig. `switch.sh --list` already hides them, and `--list --all` shows them.
- **The fix:** they join the existing `[h]` bucket (deprecated + incompatible-hw). `[h]` now means "show what this rig can't or shouldn't run", so there's no new key.
- **GPU count:** comes from the estate poll (`_known_gpu_count`, already used by the Bring picker). The poll re-renders the catalogue when the count changes, so these rows fold away just after the first poll, as incompatible-hw rows already do.
- **Never on a guess:** an unknown GPU count or topology hides nothing.
- **Visible:** the status line adds "+N need more GPUs"; the help screen and command palette say the same.

The filter, the `[w]` pool and every count now share one `[h]` predicate (`_h_hidden` / `_h_pool`). The pool logic used to be copied in two places, so they could drift.

## Tests
Run against the worktree code; I checked the import path first.
- `test_catalog_downloaded_only_filter`: updated for the on-by-default behaviour.
- **New:**
  - the nothing-on-disk fallback;
  - the save/load round trip (a malformed saved value falls back to on);
  - the GPU bucket: hidden at 2 GPUs, counted once alongside deprecated, revealed by `[h]`, nothing hidden at an unknown count or at 8 GPUs.
- All four fail on master's `app.py` / `__main__.py`.
- The help-screen test also requires the new GPU phrase.

`report.sh`'s shipped-recipe comparison renders the compose with bare defaults. `switch.sh`, though, sizes some knobs for the host before every launch: `resolve_offload_threads` exports `THREADS=nproc/2` for every CPU-offload compose, and compose interpolates it into the entrypoint script. So **every stock CPU-offload launch read as modified**. #1547 (4× 3090 on a 64-thread EPYC) was flagged "Entrypoint differs" plus "`THREADS` 32 vs (unset)" for nothing but `switch.sh`'s own sizing.

## Fix
- **`resolved_config.launcher_host_env`:** re-runs the launcher's host-deterministic resolvers, sourcing `compose-meta.sh` and `preflight.sh` as `switch.sh` does. Today that's just `resolve_offload_threads`.
- **Recipe rendering:** the recipe is rendered with that output, and the section names it: "Compared as the launcher starts it on this host with no user settings: `THREADS=32` …".
- **User values still show:** a `THREADS` the user chose differs and is listed with both values.
- **Deliberately left out:** the residency and CPU-MoE split resolvers. They size from **free** VRAM at boot, which the running model has since used up, so the report can't reproduce them.

## Verified live
`llamacpp-club3090/qwen38-flash-next-dual-q4kxl-moecache`, 2× 3090, 32-thread host, two boots:

| Boot | Comparison |
|---|---|
| `THREADS` left to the launcher (16) | ✅ **Stock recipe**, with the host sizing named (was: "Entrypoint differs" + a `THREADS` row) |
| our saved `THREADS=28` (a real user setting) | ⚠️ `THREADS` `28` vs `16`, correctly flagged |

## Tests
`test-report-resolved-config` gains two legs on #1547's compose, with a fake 64-thread host:
- a launcher-sized `THREADS=32` launch reads stock, names the sizing, and shows no entrypoint or env diff;
- a user `THREADS=7` is not stock and shows `7` vs `32`.

Both legs fail on master's `resolved_config.py`, and when the fake root lacks `preflight.sh` (the helper then can't size `THREADS`). Result: 64 pass, 0 fail. Relevant tests and Tier 0 tree-wide guards: **33 pass / 0 fail**.

Refs #1547.

body:
At the engine's default log verbosity 3, every `[moe-cache]` line is dropped, pool lines included. `bench.sh`'s allocation check counted the pools it could see, found **0 of N**, printed "a cache was REQUESTED but only 0 of N devices hold a pool … HALF-CACHED path", and set `CAP_CACHE_OK=0`, so the run ended **`CACHE_DISABLED`**. Every stock moe-cache boot therefore read as uncached:
- our own 2026-10-02 bench;
- both community multi4 reports, #1543 and #1547. Their cards sat at full-minus-reserve, i.e. the pool had filled.

## Fix
- **`capture.sh`:** the `pooldev` parse now reports the engine's log verbosity (its own `verbosity = N` line). A new `cap_pool_lines_hidden` decides "not visible" when there is **no pool line at all** and verbosity is **below 4**. Verbosity comes from the log, else `LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY`, else llama.cpp's default 3. Any pool line proves the lines were visible, so a partial allocation (#824) is never hidden.
- **`bench.sh`:** in that case the section prints "allocation: NOT VISIBLE at this log verbosity … re-boot with `LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY=4`" and **leaves `CAP_CACHE_OK` alone**. That's the same absence-is-not-data rule the hit-rate branch already follows. A real miss (no pool at verbosity 4) and a partial pool still warn and flip the status.

## Verified live
`llamacpp-club3090/qwen38-flash-next-dual-q4kxl-moecache`, stock verbosity 3, 2× 3090:

```
allocation: devices=0 pool_lines=0 enabled=0 nobudget=0 devlist=- verbosity=3  (GPUs on this host: 2)
allocation: NOT VISIBLE at this log verbosity — the [moe-cache] pool lines print only
            at LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY=4. This is not a sign the cache is off; this run
            cannot see it. To check: re-boot with LLAMA_ARG_LOG_VERBOSITY=4.
status: OK        (was: CACHE_DISABLED)
```

## Tests
`test-bench-capture` gains cases built from the community reports' own log lines:
- verbosity 3 with no pool line → hidden;
- verbosity 4 with "no cache budget" → a real miss;
- the #824 partial log → never hidden;
- env and default-verbosity fallbacks;
- a code-level check that the hidden branch never sets `CAP_CACHE_OK=0` while the real-miss branch still does.

The test fails on master's `capture.sh`/`bench.sh`, and on a copy whose hidden branch flips the status. Relevant tests and Tier 0 tree-wide guards: **34 pass / 0 fail**.

Refs #1543, #1547.

Closes #1545 · supersedes #1544 (same change, re-opened with the corrected commit author)

## Problem

`scripts/lib/capture.sh` sums `memory.used` over **every** card `nvidia-smi` reports. On a box that serves something else on other cards, a bench of one server measures its neighbours too.

Measured 2026-10-03 (4-GPU rig): a one-card vLLM server on GPU 2, next to an SGLang TP=2 server on GPU 0/1:

| | before | `BENCH_GPUS=2` |
|---|---|---|
| VRAM idle / peak / post | 68002 / 68382 / 68382 MiB | **23232 / 23232 / 23232 MiB** |
| per-device | GPU0..GPU3 | GPU2 only |
| PCIe dmon / link | all four cards | GPU2 only |

## Change

- **`capture.sh`**: a new `BENCH_GPUS` knob takes the `nvidia-smi -i` syntax: comma-separated indices or GPU UUIDs. It applies to every read through `cap_smi`: the VRAM sum and peak sampler, per-device VRAM, dmon, PCIe link state and `cap_gpu_count`.
- **Labels keep the real index.** Per-device VRAM and link state now query `index`, so `BENCH_GPUS=2` reports `GPU2`, not a renumbered `GPU0`.
- **An empty selection can't become a number.** For an absent card, `nvidia-smi -i` prints `No devices were found` on **stdout**, and the old `NF{s+=$1}` sum turned that into `0`. The sums now count numeric rows only, so a missing card reads as unavailable.
- **`bench.sh`**:
  - documents the knob;
  - exits 2 with a `Fix:` hint on a malformed or absent selection;
  - adds `GPUs measured` to the config fingerprint;
  - filters the closing `=== GPU state ===` table (`|| true` so a bad `-i` can't trip `set -e` under `CAPTURE=0`).
- **Unset `BENCH_GPUS`** keeps today's all-card behaviour.

**Not covered:** the interconnect block (`p2p-state.sh`) still reports on every card.

## Tests

- `test-bench-capture`: unit cases on three fake cards.
  - Sums for unset, `2`, `0,2` and a UUID.
  - Real-index labels, dmon rows and link state.
  - An absent or malformed selection fails instead of printing `0`.
  - End to end: the fingerprint names the selection, VRAM reads one card, and `BENCH_GPUS=7` stops before measuring.
- The fixture `fake-nvidia-smi` learns `-i` and multi-field `--query-gpu`.
- Green: `test-bench-capture`, `test-bench-card`, `test-offload-matrix-{mocked,static}`, `test-pull`, `test-pullemit-capture`, `test-submit-bench`, `test-measurement-record`, and every Tier 0 tree-wide guard.
- Live on the rig above:
  - `BENCH_GPUS=2` gives `idle=23232 peak=23232 post=23232 MiB` and GPU2-only rows.
  - `BENCH_GPUS=5` exits 2 with `pick from: 0,1,2,3`.

body:
`switch.sh --help` advertises `CLUB3090_GPU` as the "single-card GPU index override … on a hetero rig", and `docs/HARDWARE.md` shows it. But it only took effect inside `preflight_compose_hardware`, which:
- runs for **vLLM** slugs only;
- returns early on a compose **without `Requires-*` metadata**;
- is **skipped under `--force`**, which every 🧪 slug needs.

So on those slugs the override did nothing, and they landed on GPU 0.

**Reproduced on master** (two 3090s, `CLUB3090_GPU=1`):

```
CLUB3090_GPU=1 bash scripts/switch.sh --force sgl/qwen38-27b-single-fast
→ DeviceIDs ["0"]: the container got GPU 0
```

This surfaced while handing the new single-fast slugs to a 64 GB CMP 170HX, which sits at host GPU 1 between two 3090s (#1537).

## Fix
- **`apply_club3090_gpu_pin`** runs once in `switch.sh`, right after the slug is resolved and before anything reads the GPU selection: the arch warning, the engine-pin resolver and the preflights. On a single-card slug it resolves the index to a UUID and exports `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` / `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` through `scripts/lib/gpu-select.sh`, the same path `launch.sh --gpus` takes (#610).
- **Dual/multi slugs** are left alone, with a note pointing at `launch.sh --gpus`.
- **A value that isn't one index** is refused.
- **User-facing docs:** the single-fast compose headers, their registry notes and the HARDWARE.md CMP row now say `CLUB3090_GPU=<index> bash scripts/switch.sh --force <slug>` instead of `launch.sh --gpus`.

## Verified live (reference rig, GPU 1)
| | Before (master) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `CLUB3090_GPU=1 switch.sh --force sgl/qwen38-27b-single-fast` | container on GPU 0 | container sees only GPU 1 |
| `CLUB3090_GPU=1 switch.sh --force vllm/qwen38-27b-single-fast` | (same code path) | CUDA mask = GPU 1's UUID; the auto-size reads that card |

## Tests
New **`test-switch-gpu-pin`** runs the real function against a stub `nvidia-smi`. It checks:
- unset is a no-op;
- a single-card slug gets the UUID in both variables;
- an unresolvable index falls back to the raw index;
- dual and multi4 slugs are untouched;
- `1,2`, `a` and `GPU-x` are refused;
- `switch.sh` calls the function before the arch warning and before `check_variant`.

**Negative controls:** the test fails on master's `switch.sh`, on a copy that drops the multi-card exemption, and on a copy that calls the pin after the teardown.

Targeted guards plus every Tier 0 tree-wide guard: **36 pass / 0 fail**. That covers `switch-gpu-pin`, `gpu-select`, `switch-` and `launch-registry-parity`, `compose-status-drift`, `compose-registry-disk`, `profiles-compat`, `launch-compat`, `docs-slugs-resolve`, `preflight-vram`, `switch-custom-ar-warning` and the Tier 0 set.

Refs #1537.

body:
Adds two experimental slugs. Each runs the `dual-fast` recipe on **one card** and sizes itself to that card's VRAM at boot. They were built for a community 64 GB CMP 170HX (#1537), and they also run in a reduced ("lean") form on a 24 GB card.

| Slug | Port | Engine |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-single-fast` | 8117 | vLLM v0.30.0 |
| `sgl/qwen38-27b-single-fast` | 8144 | SGLang v0.5.21 |

## How the auto-size works
The entrypoint reads the total VRAM of the card the container got, then picks a tier:
- Every value below is only a default; anything the user sets wins.
- `SIZE_TIER=full|lean` forces a tier.
- The boot log prints the choice: `[size] tier lean (24576 MiB, …): W4A8=1 SPEC_N=0 …`.

| | full (≥ 30 GiB) | lean (< 30 GiB) |
|---|---|---|
| W4A8 | on | on |
| MTP drafter | n=4 | off |
| Vision tower | loaded | vLLM: not loaded (`--language-model-only`) · SGLang: loaded (its `--language-model-only` refuses this arch) |
| Memory | vLLM 0.90 · SGLang 0.95 | vLLM 0.95 · SGLang 0.88 |
| Concurrency | vLLM 8 seqs · SGLang 2 requests | 1 |
| Prefill chunk | vLLM 8192 batched tokens | 2048 |
| Context | vLLM auto-fit up to 262144 (keeps 262144 when it fits) · SGLang 262144 | vLLM **81920** · SGLang **32768** |

## Measured — lean tier, one RTX 3090, 2026-10-02 (booted through `switch.sh`)
| | vLLM | SGLang |
|---|---|---|
| KV pool | 89,435 tokens | 36,588 tokens |
| ~30K-token prompt | 14.1 s (~2,117 tok/s) | 14.0 s (~2,128 tok/s) |
| ~80K-token prompt | 79,813 tokens in 53.1 s | — (32K context) |
| verify-full | ✅ | ✅ |
| verify-stress | ✅ 5/5 boundary + 2/2 recall | — |
| bench (3 warm + 5) | 45.2 tok/s narrative and code · prefill 2,621 tok/s @10K · peak 21,651 MiB | — |

Forcing `SIZE_TIER=full` on the 3090 logs the whole full recipe, then fails at load, as it must on 24 GB. **The full tier itself is unmeasured on any card**, because the reference rig has only 3090s. The CMP report will be the first.

### Why the lean tier looks like this
All boots on the same card:
- **W4A8 + MTP doesn't load on 24 GB**, at n=4 or n=2: W4A8's load-time repack plus the drafter's weights. On SGLang, the MTP draft needs a memory fraction ≥ 0.98 even with W4A16.
- **W4A16 + MTP at 0.97:**
  - with 8192 batched tokens, the engine died on the first 30K prompt;
  - with 2048, it served 30K but hung on a 63.6K prompt.
- **vLLM's auto-fit overstates the usable context.** For the lean recipe it reported 89,600 tokens: an 84,942-token prompt passed and an 88,704-token prompt hung until aborted. So the lean context is fixed at 81,920, below that ceiling.

## Pinning the card
These slugs are 🧪, so they boot with `--force`, and `FORCE=1` also skips the preflight that would otherwise pick the largest card. On a mixed rig, pin the card:

```bash
FORCE=1 bash scripts/launch.sh --variant vllm/qwen38-27b-single-fast --gpus <index>
FORCE=1 bash scripts/launch.sh --variant sgl/qwen38-27b-single-fast --gpus <index>
```

The SGLang compose takes `ESTATE_GPUS`, else `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, for its `device_ids`.

## Catalog changes
- Two registry entries: `kvcalc_key: SKIP`, status experimental.
- The reasoning-effort template's `load_bearing_when` lists both slugs.
- Registry/disk counts bumped.
- `test-mamba-ssm-knob`: the vLLM single compose joins the CUDA-graph-estimate allowlist, because its lean tier was sized and validated with the estimate off.
- `test-diagnose-profile`: the vLLM single slug joins the expected-YELLOW register. kv-calc models the full tier on a 24 GB card and can't model a boot-time tier.
- The opt-in KV-offload block was dropped from both composes, since that tier is probed only on the dual MTP composes.

## Tests
Targeted catalog guards plus every Tier 0 tree-wide guard: **37 pass / 0 fail**. That covers `compose-registry-disk`, `compose-status-drift`, `profiles-compat`, `launch-compat`, `launch-knobs`, `switch-` and `launch-registry-parity`, `compose-mounts-resolve`, `model-weights-registry`, `patch-attribution`, `diagnose-profile`, `docs-slugs-resolve`, `baselines`, `kv-offload-knob`, `mamba-ssm-knob` and the Tier 0 set. `migrate_registry_to_yaml.py --check` reports the registry canonical. The full sweep was not run, at the maintainer's call.

Refs #1537. Supersedes #1539 (the TP knob on the dual SGLang compose).

Adds a hardware profile for the NVIDIA CMP 170HX with 64 GB, marked **community-validated**: it has never booted on the reference rig.

The CMP 170HX is a GA100 (sm_8.0) mining board, the A100's chip, so vLLM and SGLang run it through their sm_80 kernels. A community user, xtj7, reported a 64 GB board on a PCIe Gen 2 x4 link, beside two 3090s, and filed a rig report in #1537. In that report, SGLang v0.5.20 serves on the CMP alone at TP=1 with their own config (W4A16 GPTQ checkpoint, DFlash2 drafter, fp8_e4m3 KV, 262K context):
- 510,075-token KV pool;
- decode 58-106 tok/s at ~142K tokens of context;
- board power-capped to 175 W of 250.

Until now the detector had no name for the board. It fell back on sm and VRAM and read a 64 GB CMP as an A100-40GB, a profile that assumes NVLink and a 400 W cap.

## Changes
- **`scripts/lib/profiles/hardware/cmp-170hx-64gb.yml`:**
  - sm 8.0, 64 GB, `ampere-datacenter`, NVLink off, the A100's KV formats, `mem_util_safe` 0.90;
  - power caps unset: the board reports 250 W, and no optimal cap has been measured;
  - the header splits measured facts (name, VRAM, link, SGLang boot) from unmeasured ones (vLLM, club-3090's own recipes).
- **`launch_compat.py`:** maps a CMP 170HX to the new profile only at ≥ 60 GB, ahead of the sm_8.0 A100 fallback. A smaller board gets no profile rather than an inflated one.
- **`switch.sh --explain`:** card detection does the same.
- **`tools/kv-calc.py`:** knows the board's VRAM.
- **`docs/HARDWARE.md`:** a new row covering the measured link, the #1537 result, single-card guidance, and how to pin a 3090 on a mixed rig.

## Tests
- `test-launch-compat` gains three cases:
  - the 64 GB board, in both MiB spellings;
  - a stock 8 GB board, which stays unmapped;
  - xtj7's exact three-GPU spec, which maps to `rtx-3090` / `cmp-170hx-64gb` / `rtx-3090`.

  The 64 GB case fails against the previous detector, which returned `a100-40gb`.
- `test-profiles-compat` now counts 12 hardware profiles.
- Full sweep: `for t in scripts/tests/*.sh` gives **241 pass / 0 fail**. Afterwards, only the notes and the HARDWARE.md row changed (to add the #1537 result), and `test-profiles-compat`, `test-launch-compat` and `test-docs-slugs-resolve` were re-run green.

Refs #1537.

body:
## What

**`scripts/dsh-setup.sh`** sets up dsh (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`, DeepSeek's agent harness) the way `pi-setup.sh` sets up pi. dsh reaches models through pi's model library, so the wiring mirrors pi's.

In each profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (default: `headless` and `web`; `--profile` picks others) it writes one marked block containing:
- **an `llm-pi-ai` `club` provider** on the gateway. It's a snapshot of the routes the gateway serves, with their context windows, plus `qwen3.8-27b`. Thinking and effort travel as `chat_template_kwargs`, the field vLLM and SGLang read.
- **`agent-default-model` set to `club/qwen3.8-27b` at `low`**, but only when the profile names no default model of its own.

The gateway key goes into `$DSH_HOME/.env` as `CLUB3090_GATEWAY_KEY`, with mode `0600` and the file's other lines kept. dsh reads it for the provider's `apiKeyEnv`.

## Why the order matters

dsh's built-in default model is DeepSeek's paid API, so a new profile's first run goes there unless the profile names a model first. While testing, one run did exactly that, using `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` from the shell. To prevent it, the script creates a missing profile with `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config`, which runs no model, and writes the default before dsh ever runs it.

What it never touches:
- **`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`:** left alone, so DeepSeek's models stay in dsh's model menu.
- **The user's own setup:** a profile that names its own default model keeps it, and the script adds only the provider.
- **Refused:** a profile that already configures `llm-pi-ai` itself.
- **Warned about, not touched:** an older `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` that names a default model. dsh would move it into the first profile it boots.

The empty `off` effort is written quoted (`"off":`). A YAML 1.1 parser reads a bare `off` as false, while dsh reads YAML 1.2 and accepts the quoted key; this was verified live.

## Docs

`docs/CODING_AGENTS.md` gets:
- a dsh section: the script, the block it writes, and what was checked;
- a Cautions row for the paid-API first run;
- dsh in the title, the diagram and the Sampling table.

## Live check

Through the gateway: dsh 0.2.0-rc.2, vLLM dual-fast, scratch `DSH_HOME`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `dsh-setup.sh` on a fresh home | profile created with no model run; key read from `~/.dsh/.env` |
| effort `low` | `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: true, reasoning_effort: "low"}` |
| effort `off` | `{enable_thinking: false}`, no thinking |
| session titles | dsh's 64-token title request is sent with thinking off at every effort |
| tools | `glob` + `bash` on a three-file workspace, correct answer |
| continued session | correct follow-ups; system prompt and the 24 tools identical every turn; 13,440 of 13,692 prompt tokens (98%) from the prefix cache |
| sampling | none sent |

## Tests

`test-dsh-setup` runs offline: a stub gateway and a fake `dsh`, plus the real dsh, when installed, composing the generated file via `--dump-config` with no model call. Its 15 checks cover:
- `--print` writes nothing and never shows the key;
- profiles are created without a model run;
- the block and the `0600` key file;
- the Qwen3.8 wiring and the gateway's windows;
- re-runs are idempotent;
- other entries and file modes are kept;
- the user's own default model is kept;
- a foreign `llm-pi-ai` entry is refused;
- `.env` is merged, not overwritten;
- a legacy `settings.yaml` is warned about;
- a profile name can't be a path;
- the Qwen3.8 id list equals `omp-setup.sh`'s;
- the doc block matches the script output.

34/34 green, together with the omp/pi/Hermes setup tests, the doc tests and the Tier 0 tree-wide guards.

body:
## What

`quality-test.sh`, and so `rebench-full.sh`, now defaults the budgets that `docs/RUN_EVALS.md` told every run to pass by hand:

| Default | Was (benchlocal per-pack) | Override |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-tokens 4096` | ~1024 | `--max-tokens N` / `MAX_TOKENS=N` |
| `--thinking-max-tokens 16384` (sent explicitly: once `--max-tokens` is set, benchlocal gives thinking packs that value) | 16384 | `--thinking-max-tokens N` / `THINKING_MAX_TOKENS=N` |
| `BENCHLOCAL_MODEL_TURN_TIMEOUT=900` | 300 s | the env var |
| `BENCHLOCAL_HERMES_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S=600` | 300 s | the env var |

- An explicit flag or env var always wins.
- `--pack-budgets` (or `PACK_BUDGETS=1`) keeps benchlocal's own budgets.
- `--resume` keeps the saved run's budgets.
- Each run prints its budgets (`[quality-test] budgets: …`) and records them with `--run-meta`, because the results JSON keeps none of its own.

## Why

benchlocal's per-pack budgets cut long answers off into `token_limit` rows that read as wrong answers. The recipe passed the flags by hand, but neither script did. A thinking-off A/B on 2026-10-02 lost 5 scenarios per run this way (RM-04/05/06/15 and BF-12), the same ones every run.

## Timeouts: deliberately not defaulted

`--timeout-per-case` stays unset. Left unset, benchlocal scales each scenario's clock with the token budget and the rig's measured speed (benchlocal-cli #103). By benchlocal's formula with the reference rig's measured speed factor (1.2×), that's about 290 s for the quick packs at 4096 tokens and about 1150 s at 16384. These are computed, not timed. A fixed value would:
- switch that scaling off;
- shorten the thinking arm's clock;
- lower aider-polyglot-30's 1800 s.

So the recipe's `--timeout-per-case 600` is dropped from `RUN_EVALS.md` and `QUALITY_TEST.md`. Its one real effect, raising the hermes episode cap to 600 s, is now the hermes default above. This also resolves the contradiction with `AGENTS.md`'s "don't hand-set `--timeout-per-case`".

## Docs

- **`RUN_EVALS.md`:** shorter commands, plus a "Budgets: set for you" table.
- **`QUALITY_TEST.md`:** same commands. Its two-leg block still called instruct "the shipped default", but thinking has been the default since 2026-09-01 (`19e3e823`), so the legs are fixed.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** a dated note that quality results from before this change used whatever budgets their command named.
- **`rebench-full.sh`:** help text updated.

## Tests

`test-quality-thinking` covers:
- the defaults: argv, the env vars benchlocal receives, the printed line and the `--run-meta` record;
- every override: flag, env var, `--pack-budgets` / `PACK_BUDGETS=1`, and an explicit value under `--pack-budgets`;
- that `--timeout-per-case` is never added.

It's hermetic against a shell that exports the knobs, and fails on master's `quality-test.sh`.

`test-quality-thinking-budget`: case A now expects the default cap with no derived budget, and a new case A2 keeps the "argv untouched" check under `--pack-budgets`.

Run on this branch, 37/37 green:
- every `test-quality-*` and `test-rebench*`;
- every test that reads the docs;
- the Tier 0 tree-wide guards.

**Effect on a real run.** The same arm of an ongoing A/B, run with these values passed explicitly: `token_limit` failures went from 5 to 1, and the score from 100/150 to 109/150. Part of that gain is run-to-run noise.

**Live check: done after merge** (main checkout at `72a7a25a`, vLLM dual-fast, TC-01 + HA-01, no flags passed): `[quality-test] budgets: max 4096 · thinking 16384 · model turn 900s · hermes episode 600s (wrapper default: …)`; benchlocal `timeout scaling active: … scale=1.26, token-budget-multiplier=4096/1024=4.00` (per-case clock still auto-scaled); `hermesagent-20 clocks: episode 600s (BENCHLOCAL_HERMES_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S; default 300s)`; the results JSON's `run_meta.budgets` carries the same string. Both scenarios passed.

body:
## What

- **`scripts/omp-setup.sh`** adds `compat.reasoningDisableMode: none-effort` to the `club` provider.
- **`docs/CODING_AGENTS.md`**
  - adds a **Sampling** section;
  - corrects the omp and pi thinking notes.
- **`docs/FAQ.md`** points its sampler answer at the new section for Qwen3.8.

## Why

Gateway request logs (`scripts/litellm-log.sh on`, SGLang dual-fast, 2026-10-02) showed that neither omp nor pi could turn thinking off:

| Agent | `off` as forwarded to the engine | Model reasoned? |
|---|---|---|
| omp 18.4.10, before | `/v1/responses` with **no `reasoning` field** | yes |
| omp 18.4.10, with this change | `reasoning: {effort: "none"}` | no |
| pi 1.0.0, `--thinking off` | `enable_thinking: true, reasoning_effort: "medium"` | yes |
| pi 1.0.0, level set in the session (RPC `set_thinking_level`) | `enable_thinking: false` | no |
| pi 0.99.2 / 0.87.1, `--thinking off` | `enable_thinking: false` | no |

- **omp** talks the Responses API through the gateway and needs the `none-effort` mode for `off`. That is upstream's answer in oh-my-pi#11184. `effort: "none"` gave 0 reasoning tokens:
  - on SGLang, through omp and the gateway;
  - on vLLM dual-fast, sent directly.
- **pi 1.0.0** ignores the thinking level it starts with: `--thinking`, a `:level` suffix and the saved default all leave it at `medium`. 0.99.2 and 0.87.1 don't have this problem. It's an upstream regression; the doc says to use `/thinking` in the session until it's fixed. Not reported upstream yet.

The same capture showed that **no agent sends sampling values** (omp, pi and Claude Code live; Hermes Agent from its source). So every thinking-off turn runs on the thinking row: `presence_penalty` comes out 0.0, where the card's thinking-off row says 1.5. The Sampling section explains:
- why the server can't apply the thinking-off row (it's chosen at boot);
- why `presence_penalty` can't be set server-side on vLLM or SGLang;
- that on SGLang, `TEMP` / `TOP_P` don't reach chat requests (sglang#39096).

## Tests

33 tests:
- `test-omp-setup`, `test-pi-setup` and `test-hermes-setup`;
- every test that reads `docs/`;
- the Tier 0 tree-wide guards.

`report.sh`'s "Recent failed boot attempts" section listed every exited engine container from the last 24 h, whatever its exit code. Fixes #1522.

## What was wrong

`switch.sh` syncs the gateway twice: after teardown (`down_running`, which renders the old route away and restarts the gateway) and after a waited ready. The second sync, and the Open WebUI registration next to it, only ran when `switch.sh` waited for ready. With `--no-wait`, or a boot slower than `READY_TIMEOUT`, the gateway served **no local route** for a model that came up fine minutes later, until someone ran `litellm-sync.sh` by hand.

## Change

- **`scripts/lib/post-ready-sync.sh` (new):** polls the ready URL and, once the server answers, runs the same two steps a waited launch runs: `owui-register.sh <port>` (with `--owui`) and `litellm-sync.sh --quiet`.
  - It exits without syncing when the container has stopped or is gone (exit 2), and after `POST_READY_SYNC_TIMEOUT` (default 3600 s, exit 3).
  - It does **not** run `switch.sh`'s generation probe, and the printed line says so.
- **`switch.sh`:** `schedule_post_ready_sync` starts it detached (`nohup`) in exactly two cases, and logs to `<data dir>/logs/post-ready-sync-<container>.log`:
  - `--no-wait`;
  - the ready timeout firing while the container is still running. The existing timeout line is unchanged, a `still booting` line follows it, and **the exit code stays 1**, since nothing has answered yet.
- **`scripts/tests/test-post-ready-sync.sh` (new), 22 checks:**
  - **The waiter**, with stub curl/docker and stub sync scripts: syncs on answer, with and without `--owui`; no sync when stopped, gone, or past the ceiling; exit 64 on missing args.
  - **`switch.sh`'s own `schedule_post_ready_sync`:** the arguments it passes; with no container it prints the manual command instead.
  - **The real `wait_ready()` timeout branch:** schedules the waiter and still exits 1.
  - **The `--no-wait` wiring.**

  Hard limits (`timeout`, short ceiling) make a stub mistake fail the test rather than hang it. Nothing is launched or left running.

**Not in this PR:** the reporter's option 4, the gateway restart at teardown, which happens even when a launch follows straight away. That restart is what empties the gateway in the first place; it's a separate change.

## Verification

- `test-post-ready-sync.sh`: 22/22. Against master's `switch.sh`: 8 failures (every `switch.sh`-side check).
- Tier 0 tree-wide guards plus `switch-orphan-teardown`, `switch-refuse-before-teardown`, `slug-label`, `switch-registry-parity`, `litellm-sync`: 31/31.

  | `--no-wait` | returned after 17 s, exit 0 | 0 routes on :8122 | answered after 63 s → OWUI registered, route added; chat through :4000 → 200 |
  | `READY_TIMEOUT=10` | timeout line + `still booting`, exit 1 | 0 routes on :8122 | answered after 15 s → route added |

body:
Closes #1520.

## Problem

omp (`discovery: litellm`) talks the Responses API to every gateway route, and LiteLLM turns Claude Code's `/v1/messages` into a Responses call on `openai/` routes. Both are forwarded to the engine's `/v1/responses` as-is. tabbyAPI (exllamav3) doesn't serve that endpoint. It answers `404`, and LiteLLM 1.100.3 then cools the whole model group down for 5 s, so chat completions on the same slug get `429` too. On an exl3 slug, omp can't run at all and Claude Code fails with 404s followed by bursts of 429s.

This is the Responses-side sibling of #1461.

## Fix

- **Runtime view (`litellm_sync.py`):** `serves_responses()` sends an **empty-body** `POST /v1/responses` to each live port, so nothing is generated. An engine with the endpoint rejects the body (SGLang: 400), and one without it 404s the path. Only a 404 marks the endpoint absent, and that route gets `use_chat_completions_api: true`, LiteLLM's Responses → chat-completions bridge. Any other answer, or no answer, keeps today's route, so a flaky probe can't move a native engine off its Responses wire.
- **Catalog view (`litellm-emit.sh`):** the same flag, decided by engine family via `engine-kind.sh` (exllamav3 → bridge), since the catalog has no live server to ask. No catalog route changes today, because no exl3 slug is `gateway=True`.
- **Docs:** `docs/CODING_AGENTS.md` route-key table + wire-format note (which said every engine serves `/v1/responses`).

## What the bridge carries (A/B on a scratch gateway, same pinned image)

Stub upstream with tabbyAPI's endpoint surface, flag off vs on:

| Request | Without | With bridge |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/responses` (omp) | 404 → cooldown | 200 via `/v1/chat/completions` |
| chat completion right after | 429 | 200 |
| `/v1/messages` streaming + thinking (Claude Code) | 404 → cooldown | 200; `thinking` from `reasoning_content`, then `text` |
| past omp reasoning item / past Claude `thinking` block | — | `reasoning_content` on the assistant turn; tool calls → `tool_calls` / `role: tool` |
| `/v1/messages` **non-streaming** | 404 → cooldown | 200, but `content: []` |

**Known gap (LiteLLM, not this PR):** non-streaming `/v1/messages` through the double bridge (Anthropic → Responses → chat) drops the content. Claude Code streams its turns. It's noted in the code comment and docs.

## Rig verification

`tabbyapi/qwen38-flash-next-exl3-4.05bpw` on 2x 5090, gateway `litellm:v1.100.3`, synced from this branch:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| engine `POST /v1/responses` `{}` | 404 → route rendered with `use_chat_completions_api: true` |
| gateway `/v1/responses` | 200, `reasoning` item (tabbyAPI's `reasoning_content`) + `message` "OK" |
| `omp -p --no-tools --no-session --model qwen3.8-flash-next-exl3-4.05bpw "Reply with exactly: OK"` | `OK`, exit 0 (was the gateway 404 before) |
| `/v1/messages` streaming + thinking | `thinking` block, then `text` "42" |
| `docker logs litellm` after the run: 404 / cooldown 429 | 0 |

## Tests

- `test-litellm-sync.sh`: 4 new checks. Seam render with `+noresponses` (combinable with `+messages`), bridged route keeps the common shape, and the real probe against stub servers (404 → bridge; 400/405/422/500/no answer → native). Mutation-checked: breaking the probe or the render fails them.
- `test-litellm-generate.sh`: fixture gains an exllamav3 entry, which is bridged; the vLLM/llama.cpp fixture routes are not.
- Tree-wide guards (incl. `test-engine-kind-resolver`): green.
- `test-litellm-local-config.sh` fails on this rig on `master` too (compose hash differs by path), so it's pre-existing and unrelated.

body:
Fixes #1516.

## What was wrong

The #246 Phase 2 memory-fraction floor (`_mem_util_env`) lowers `GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION` to the minimum `mem_util_safe` over every GPU in the rig. Its commit (47b43f9a) meant it for one card, the DGX Spark, whose LPDDR5X is shared with the CPU and OS. But `rtx-3060-12gb.yml` carries `mem_util_safe: 0.88` too: added with the hardware data layer on 2026-05-14, two months before the floor existed, and never measured as a boot limit. So on a 3090 + 3060 rig every 0.92 slug booted at 0.88, including slugs that never touch the 3060. That's about 1 GiB of KV per 3090 rank, lost without warning, plus a message blaming a "unified-memory card" the rig doesn't have.

## Change

- `HardwareProfile` gains `unified_memory: bool = False`; `dgx-spark.yml` sets it to `true`.
- `_mem_util_env` considers only unified-memory cards. A discrete card's `mem_util_safe` stays a fit-estimate input (`compat.fits`), and the compose's own tuned fraction is what boots.
- The launcher message (`switch.sh`, `launch.sh`) is now accurate by construction, since only a unified-memory card can trigger it, and says how to override.
- `docs/ENGINE_FLAGS.md`: the row claimed the floor fired only on the Spark; it now says why that's true.

**Deliberately not changed:** the GPU set the floor sees (still every card in the rig). With the Spark the only unified-memory profile, that only matters on a host mixing a Spark with discrete cards. `_envelope_env` / `_deepgemm_env` / `_moe_cache_env` still read the whole-rig spec; the report shows no visible effect from them today, so they are a follow-up.

**Trade-off:** a 0.90/0.92 compose run on a 3060 now gets the compose value instead of 0.88. That margin was never measured, and `GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION` still overrides.

## Verification

- `test-launch-compat`: three new cases. A 3090 + 3090 + 3060 rig (`vllm/dual`) and a lone 3060 (`vllm/minimal`) get nothing injected; Spark + 3090 is still lowered to 0.85. A positive control first asserts the spec maps to the `rtx-3060-12gb` profile with a ceiling below the slug default, so "nothing injected" can't pass for an unmapped card. Against master's resolver the test fails with `GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.88`.
- Full suite (profile-schema change): 238/238 on the branch before the rebase.

Fixes #1515.

## What was wrong

Since #1498, every launch brings the container up with two compose files: the slug's compose, then the `club3090.slug` label override. Docker Compose records both in `com.docker.compose.project.config_files` as one comma-joined string. `down_running()` passed that string to `-f` as a single path, compose rejected it as a missing file, and every switch or `--down` fell back to `docker stop`. The old container was left stopped (not removed), and its network and any orphans stayed behind.

## Change

- `scripts/switch.sh` `down_running()`: split the label on `,` and pass one `-f` per file, as `litellm-log.sh`, `resolved_config.py` and c3 already do. A file that no longer exists is dropped: the label override only adds labels, so a data dir that moved must not cost the `down`. With no file left, the `docker stop` fallback stays.
- `scripts/lib/bench-row-formatter.sh`: take the first entry (the slug's compose) before `rel()`, so a bench record's `compose` field is one relative path again.
- `scripts/tests/test-switch-orphan-teardown.sh`: three new scenarios: two-file label → two `-f`, no stop; override gone → `-f` the compose only; no file left → `docker stop`.

## Verification

- `test-switch-orphan-teardown.sh`: 15/15 with the fix; 5 failures with master's `switch.sh`.
- Tier 0 tree-wide guards plus `test-switch-refuse-before-teardown`, `test-slug-label`, `test-submit-bench`, `test-report-resolved-config`, `test-litellm-log`: 31/31.

  | this PR | removed | removed |

## What was wrong

In a git worktree (and a submodule) `.git` is a **file** pointing at the real git dir. Three scripts decided "is this a git checkout?" with `-d`:

| script | from a worktree, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `report.sh` | `club-3090: not a git repo` | `` `v0.12.0-9-g4bee2145` (branch: `fix/report-worktree-git`, SHA `4bee2145`) `` |

| `preflight.sh` (`preflight_repo_drift`) | bailed at the `.git` check | reaches the master-only check, which skips a worktree branch anyway (no behaviour change) |

## The fix

`-e` instead of `-d`. That keeps the old meaning, that the repo root must itself be the checkout. `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` would also say yes for a copy sitting inside some unrelated repo.

Refs #1427 (that issue is a bench report and stays open; this fixes the "odd characters" @alexanderjacuna saw in it).

## What was wrong

`report.sh` writes Markdown for a file or an issue, but the tools it embeds (`verify-full`, `verify-stress`, soak, bench, `nvidia-smi topo`) colour their output even when piped. Every embedded block kept those escape sequences. Pasted reports read as `[32m✓[0m` / `[4mGPU0…[0m`, and the four `--full` reports in #1427, #1431, #1434 and #1452 carried 37-39 sequences each and looked mis-encoded. The file itself was valid UTF-8.

## The fix

- **`strip_ansi()`** drops CSI (colour, cursor), OSC (window titles) and charset escape sequences. `redact()` runs it on every embedded block, redacted or not. `--no-redact` used to pass them through untouched. The studio-logs block's own narrower `sed` goes away in favour of it.
- **It runs under `LC_ALL=C`.** Under a UTF-8 locale GNU sed reads `[@-~]` in collation order, which leaves `m` out, so the first version of this matched no colour code at all. Bytewise matching is safe: every pattern is ASCII, and ✓ — × pass through untouched.

## Verified

- **On the four real reports:** every escape byte is removed (78 → 0, and 100 → 0 for #1452), and the output is otherwise identical to a pure regex removal.
- **A default `report.sh` run on the reference rig:** 4 escape bytes on master (the `nvidia-smi topo` underline), 0 from this branch. The rest of the diff is timestamps and bandwidth readings.
- **New `test-report-ansi`:** it runs the real `strip_ansi` / `redact` under C, C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8, redacted and not, on colour / cursor / OSC / charset sequences, ✓, × and a literal `[32m`. It also guards that every block piped into `details()` goes through `redact()`. Dropping `LC_ALL=C` fails the en_US cases, and routing one embed around `redact()` fails the guard.
- Tier 0 and every `report.sh` test (39 scripts) are green.

Spotted along the way, not changed here: run from a git worktree, the report's Stack version line says "not a git repo".

body:
Fixes #1508 (reported by @paulp83, with the root cause in the issue).

## What was wrong

c3's download progress for a slug whose core weights were already on disk sat at **98-99 %** for the whole tail: the companion transfer and the re-hash of the core. Two bugs fed it:

1. **Each artifact was counted by an `rglob` of its whole subdir.** Variants can share a parent bucket. GLM's core has `subdir=glm-5.3-flash-gguf`, `verify_glob=UD-IQ4_XS/*.gguf`, and the `dflash2/` and `mmproj/` companions live inside that bucket. The core's count therefore included the companions, any other quant in the bucket and hf's staging tree. Summing the set counted the companions twice.
2. **The present core dominated the denominator.** With 157 GB of 158.83 GB already there, the remaining 1.8 GB was ~1.15 % of the bar, so it could move only 1-2 steps before the re-stat flipped it to present.

## The fix (`tools/serve-cockpit`)

- **`weights_files_on_disk(meta)`:** an artifact's own files are its `verify_glob` matches under its subdir, plus their in-flight `*.incomplete` staging. Staging is looked for both under `<subdir>/.cache/huggingface/download/` (what `hf download --local-dir` writes) and beside the file (older layouts). The whole subdir is never counted, and the backup/cruft exclusion is unchanged.
- **`weights_download_progress_set`:** the bytes of the set's **distinct** files over its size, so nothing counts twice.
- **`download_complete_at_start` + `complete_at_start=`:** an artifact already on disk when the download starts (≥ 97 % of its `size_gb`) leaves the percentage, unless a re-fetch of it shows up in staging. For the reported slug, the bar now moves 0 → 99 over the 1.83 GB of companions instead of sitting at 98-99 % of 158.83 GB. The download worker takes the baseline once, at start.

Not changed: once the companions are in, the bar reads 99 while `setup.sh` re-hashes the core. A separate "verifying" state would need the worker to read `setup.sh`'s phase; that's a possible follow-up.

## Verified

- **New `test_services.py` cases, modelled on the report:** the core in a shared bucket with both companions, another quant, an undeclared neighbour and hf staging metadata.
  - The core counts only its own 157 GB, and the companion-only progress reads 0 → 69 %.
  - The same disk without the start baseline reads 99 %, the bug's frozen bar.
  - A re-fetched core rejoins the percentage.
  - A nested companion is counted once.
  - Both cases fail against master's `services.py`.

Fixes #1507. The fix is @simplesisu's diff from the issue (credited as co-author).

## What was wrong

`peer_bandwidth()` in `scripts/lib/p2p_collective_check.py` timed the GPU0→GPU1 copy while GPU1 was still idle. A peer copy only raises the **source** GPU's P-state. The destination stays at P8 with its link at Gen1 and caps the copy at ~2-3 GB/s however long it runs. On a 2× 3090 x8/x8 Gen4 rig the sizing line read **0.49× ("NO peer advantage")** where P2P actually runs at **1.98×** (13.16 GB/s, the x8 line rate).

## The fix

- Wake both GPUs with `warm_s=0.5` of host traffic before anything is timed.
- Sync both devices: a bare `torch.cuda.synchronize()` waits on the current device only, but the copy spans two.
- The printed line says `GPUs woken`. The verdict (ARM A / ARM B) and the return value are unchanged.

## Verified

- **Not reproducible on the reference rig** (2× 3090, x16/x8 Gen4, patched 610.57 P2P driver in a VM). From P8 / Gen1, in a fresh process each time, original and fixed both measure 13.17 GB/s (1.48×) on 3 runs each, so the change is neutral here. The reporter's 3 runs on a 615.71 driver are the evidence for the fix.
- **Real `p2p-validate.sh` from this branch:** ARM A PASS, ARM B PASS; peer 13.18 GB/s vs host-staged 8.91 GB/s.
- **`test-p2p-validate`:** a new arm runs `peer_bandwidth()` under a fake `torch` that records every copy and sync. It asserts both GPUs get host traffic before the first timed peer copy and every sync names both devices. It fails against master's payload.
- Tier 0 and the P2P tests (25 scripts) are green.

body:
Fixes #1502 (reported by @tjengbudi, with both root causes below).

## 1. `--sweep` died at its first skipped cell

A sweep skips a cell when it doesn't fit the KV pool, when the wall budget runs out, or on early-stop. All three paths piped the cell's JSON into `emit_row`, which ran `python3 - <<'PY'`. `python3 -` reads its **program** from stdin, so the heredoc replaced the piped row, `json.loads("")` raised, and `set -e` ended the run before the card, the `=== recommend ===` block or the `results/concurrency-*` files were written. On small cards some cell nearly always overflows the pool, so the sweep never finished there.

**Fix:** the row is an argument (`emit_row "$json"`, read from `sys.argv`).

## 2. VRAM and the GPU label were rig-wide

`vram_used_mb()` summed `memory.used` over every GPU on the host, and `_gpu_fp()` counted every GPU and named them all after GPU 0. The report: a container pinned to one RTX 3060 showed **55,319 MB on "4× GeForce RTX 3090"**, against a real 10,381 MiB. The post-warm leak gate (`vram_ok`) was judged on that sum, so another service could fail a clean run or hide a real leak.

**Fix:** the probe resolves the container's GPUs with `run_context.visible_gpu_selectors` (DeviceRequests, then `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, then `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`), the same reading `quality-test.sh`'s run metadata already uses. It then:
- scopes VRAM, the leak gate and the card's GPU label to those GPUs, with a mixed rig labelled by name (`3× … 3090 + 1× … 3060`);
- prints which GPUs it measured (`[probe] VRAM measured on: GPU 3 (container …)`);
- records each GPU's peak: a verdict line, plus `vram_gpus` / `vram_peak_gpus` on the `RESULT` line;
- falls back to rig-wide, and says so, when the container can't be resolved.

## Verified

`test-concurrency-probe` gains two arms:
- **`emit_row`:** the real function, extracted from the script, records a skipped-cell row, and a guard fails if any call site pipes into it again.
- **GPU scoping:** checked against stub `nvidia-smi` / `docker inspect` shaped like the report (3× 3090 + 1× 3060). Device IDs, UUIDs and `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` each give `1× GeForce RTX 3060` and 10,381 MB. A container that sees every GPU covers all four, and an unknown container falls back.

Both arms fail against master's code. Tier 0 plus the probe and `run_context` tests (30 scripts) are green. `--gpu-label` on the reference rig prints `2× GeForce RTX 3090`.

Not covered by a test: a full live sweep that reaches a skip. The loop needs a live server warm-up, so the arm runs the real `emit_row` instead.

body:
Fixes #1503 (reported by @datanerdie, with the root cause and both fixes below).

## What was wrong

vLLM's OffloadingConnector keeps the KV RAM tier in a file under `/dev/shm`, in both modes our composes use (RAM only, and RAM + disk). The five vLLM composes that read `KV_OFFLOAD_GB` run with `ipc: host`, so the limit is the **host's** `/dev/shm`, by default half of RAM; their `shm_size: "16gb"` does not apply. On a 125 GiB host that is 63 GiB, so `KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64` passed `switch.sh`'s RAM rule, then every worker failed with `Insufficient space in /dev/shm` and the container restarted in a loop.

## The fix

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/launch_settings.py` | `shm_error()` next to `ram_error()`, vLLM only. A tier larger than `/dev/shm`'s **size** is refused before the running slug is torn down, and by `switch.sh --set`, with what fits and how to enlarge `/dev/shm`. A tier that fits but is larger than what is **free** right now is a warning, because the running slug's own tier is released when it stops. SGLang is exempt: HiCache's host pool is ordinary pinned memory. |
| the 5 vLLM dual MTP composes | The entrypoint checks **free** `/dev/shm` after the offload block and fails with the numbers instead of vLLM's generic error. This also covers a raw `docker compose up`. The `KV_OFFLOAD_GB` comment says where the tier lives. |
| `docs/CODING_AGENTS.md`, `scripts/kv-offload-probe.py`, `launch-knobs.json` | No more bare "use 64": the tier must fit in `/dev/shm`, and on a 128 GB host 48 fits and passes the probe (from the report). The knob caveat names the new rule. |

Not changed: the inert `shm_size: "16gb"` lines. They do nothing under `ipc: host` but don't hurt either.

## Verified

- **Live, reference rig** (`/dev/shm` 112.2 GiB, 224 GiB RAM): `KV_OFFLOAD_GB=120 bash scripts/switch.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast --force` → refused, `at most 112 GiB fits`, nothing torn down. Master's resolver accepts the same value.
- `test-launch-settings`: 8 new `/dev/shm` cases through a statvfs seam (refuse, exact fit, warn-only, SGLang exempt, `--force`, unreadable, secrets never echoed, `switch.sh --set`). With the rule disabled, 6 go red.
- `test-kv-offload-knob`: runs each compose's real check line with `os.statvfs` faked. 64 GiB with 62.8 free → refused with the numbers; 48 → passes; a 113 GiB `/dev/shm` with 20 free → refused. Mutating one compose to compare against size instead of free is caught.
- Tier 0 and the touched-area tests (36 scripts) green; c3 `test_launch_settings_form.py` 32/32.
- Not done: a container boot that reaches the in-entrypoint check (the line is the one the test runs).

body:
Follow-up to #1499, which came up while checking whether the probe should simply use nproc/2 threads.

## Why

The probe tries ¼, ½ and all physical cores and reports the best, but the partial runs pinned to the **first** N cores. Two problems follow:
- **Die-by-die numbering** (big EPYC or Threadripper): a half-core run landed on half the CCDs, or on one socket. Each CCD has its own fabric bandwidth ceiling, so the run read low.
- **Interleaved socket numbering** (some dual-socket Intel: even CPUs on socket 0, odd on 1): a plain stride would put every thread on socket 0.

The all-cores run still covered everything, so the reported best was usually close. But when the true optimum is "half the cores, spread over every die", the sweep couldn't find it.

## What changes

`membw_probe.c`:
- orders the physical cores by (package, L3 id = die, core);
- runs thread *i* of *n* on core *i × cores / n*;
- as a result, spreads evenly over sockets and dies whatever the CPU numbering scheme.

The plan output (`MEMBW_PLAN_ONLY=1`) now lists each run's pins.

## Tests

`test-report-membw`, new arms:

| Fake topology | 4 threads | 8 threads |
|---|---|---|
| 2 sockets × 2 dies, numbered socket by socket | `0,4,8,12`: one per die | `0,2,…,14`: both sockets |
| 2 sockets, interleaved even/odd numbering | `0,8,1,9`: 2 per socket | `0,4,8,12,1,5,9,13` |

**Mutation checks:** pinning to the first cores fails 3 checks, and striding without the topology sort fails the interleaved check.

**Reference rig:** packed and spread read the same range, 146–155 vs 152–155 GB/s Triad. That's expected, because this VM hides the host's dies (each vCPU reports its own L3 and the host mapping is invisible). The benefit is on bare-metal multi-die and multi-socket rigs.

Tier 0: all pass.

body:
`report.sh`'s memory-bandwidth line under-read by about 40%, on the reference rig and on users' rigs alike. It came up when Paul asked whether the rig reaches its platform's bandwidth. The old probe couldn't say.

## Why it under-read

Reference rig: EPYC 7543 with 8 channels of DDR4-3200, 204.8 GB/s rated. Each row adds one fix on top of the one above:

| Probe | STREAM Triad |
|---|---|
| old `report.sh` probe | 87–102 GB/s |
| + threads created once, each first-touching its own slice | 107–113 |
| + threads pinned | 117–119 |
| + non-temporal stores | **156–165** (~78% of rated, normal for Milan) |

Compiler flags (`-O3 -march=native`) changed nothing. The biggest loss was the read-for-ownership that a plain store pays and STREAM doesn't count.

## What changes

**`scripts/lib/membw_probe.c`**, still compiled on the rig, handles what differs between rigs:

| Varies across rigs | Handling |
|---|---|
| write-allocate on x86 | non-temporal stores (SSE2/AVX: every x86-64). Plain stores elsewhere, and the report says so. |
| SMT, CCDs, NUMA, sockets, P/E cores | one pinned thread per **physical** core from sysfs topology, each first-touching the slice it streams |
| where bandwidth saturates (a few cores on desktops, most on servers) | tries ¼, ½ and all cores; reports the best and its thread count. Here the best came from 8, 16 or 32 on different runs. |
| large L3 (X3D, V-Cache up to ~1 GB) | arrays of at least 4× total L3, counted per cache `id` as `lscpu` does, capped by free memory |
| noise | threads created once, barrier-timed, best of 5. A read-only figure too (decode is read-heavy). |

**`scripts/lib/membw.sh`** formats the line:
- **Rated peak:** when `dmidecode` names every DIMM's channel and speed, it adds the rated peak (channels × MT/s × 8 B) and the percentage. Otherwise it prints nothing rather than guess, because slots are not channels.
- **Notes:**
  - "measured inside a VM";
  - a warning when the host was busy (load ≥ 1; a load of 2.6 already cost ~10–15% here);
  - "arrays capped by free memory";
  - "Triad used plain stores".

**`report.sh`** hands its `dmidecode` text to it. The old inline probe is removed. `REPORT_NO_BANDWIDTH=1` still skips it.

## Tests

**Live on the reference rig** (quiet, same window): the old probe read 100–102 GB/s; the new one reads 156–165 Triad and 158–166 read. `report.sh` end to end:

```
- Memory bandwidth (measured): 151.7 GB/s STREAM Triad · 154.9 GB/s read (best with 16 thread(s) on 32 physical core(s); 3 × 684 MiB arrays) — this, not the rated MT/s above, …
  - Measured inside a VM (`kvm`): this is what the guest gets; the host itself may measure higher.
```

It shows no percentage here because this VM's firmware reports no channels or speed.

**New `test-report-membw`:**

| Area | Checks |
|---|---|
| Plans on fake `/sys` trees | SMT (one thread per physical core; tries 1, 2, 4); V-Cache-size L3 (1024 MiB arrays); a VM's per-vCPU cache ids (counted per id); no topology files; a memory cap (170 MiB, flagged); low memory (skipped with the reason) |
| Measurement | a real tiny run prints every field, with non-temporal stores on x86-64 |
| `dmidecode` fixtures | AMD desktop, 2 channels → 51.2; Intel desktop with the channel only in `Locator` (`BANK n` is per slot) → 89.6; 8-channel EPYC → 204.8; an empty slot ignored; mixed speeds → the slowest; a VM's virtual DIMM → no peak; channel-less `BANK n` slots → no peak |
| The report line | % of rated; each note (VM, busy host, capped, plain stores); a skip; a failed run (never a zero) |

Tier 0: all pass.

## Not verified yet

Only this rig was available. A check from users with an Intel desktop, a Threadripper or a DGX Spark, against a reference tool such as Intel MLC, would confirm the cross-rig claims.

body:
Follow-up to #1497: every launched container now says which registry slug it runs.

## Why

Two slugs can share one compose file:

| Compose | Slugs |
|---|---|
| `qwen3.6-27b/…/dual/autoround-int4/fp8-mtp.yml` | `vllm/dual`, `vllm/qwen-27b-dual-fast` |
| `qwen3.6-27b/llama-cpp/…/mtp.yml` | `llamacpp/default`, `llamacpp/mtp` |

Per-slug launch settings (#1465) now make the twins run differently. The compose a container came from therefore no longer identifies the slug, and measurement records (#1497) and c3's running-container marker (#1490) fell back to registry order.

## What changes

| | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/slug_label.py` (+ `slug-label.sh`) | Writes a compose override that labels every service `club3090.slug=<slug>`. It lives in `<data dir>/compose-labels/`, the same place for every checkout, and is rewritten only when its content changes. It **refuses** an unknown slug, or a slug whose registered compose isn't the file being launched, so a label never lies. |
| `switch.sh` | Adds the override to `compose up`. This covers `launch.sh` and c3 serves, which go through it. |
| `gpu-mode.sh` | Its model modes pass their slug (`COMPOSE_SLUG=vllm/dual compose_at …`), so a mode and a `switch.sh` launch of the same slug render the same config and neither recreates the other's container. Services get no label. |
| c3 | `containers_for` prefers the label: #1490's form no longer shows `vllm/dual`'s container under `vllm/qwen-27b-dual-fast`. |

`measurement_record.resolve_serving` already trusts the label first (#1497).

## Tests

- **New `test-slug-label`, 12 checks:**
  - the helper, run over all 168 registry slugs;
  - it refuses a mismatched compose or an unknown slug, and doesn't rewrite an unchanged file;
  - a real `docker compose config` render shows the label merged;
  - gpu-mode's `27b` mode, run from a scratch copy with docker and sudo shimmed, hands compose `-f …/vllm-dual.yml`, and services get none;
  - twin slugs resolve to the labelled one; unlabelled containers use registry order, as before.
- **`test-launch-settings`** asserts the rendered container label on the real `switch.sh` path. On master it's `<absent>`.
- **c3:** tests for label-aware matching.
- **Adjusted tests:**
  - four tests that drive a launch (`test-launch-settings`, `test-switch-refuse-before-teardown`, `test-thinking-pin`, `test-default-resolver`) now use temp data and cache dirs; otherwise they'd have written the label into the real `~/.local/share`;
  - `test-engine-cache`'s explicit-`KV_OFFLOAD_DIR` check now asserts "no KV-offload dir" rather than "no data dir at all";
  - `test-shm-cleanup`'s `compose up` regex allows the extra `-f`.
- **Full sweep: 235/235**, with no files written to the real data dir. **Full c3 suite: 1202 passed**, 0 failed.

## Note

A container started before this change has no label, so the first launch of that slug afterwards recreates it once, because its compose config changed.

body:
Fixes #1477. Thanks to @tjengbudi for a precise report: both bugs are confirmed on current master, and the fix follows the suggested approach.

## The two bugs

Every per-rig measurement record (`bench.sh`, `verify-full.sh`, `soak-test.sh`, `quality-test.sh`, … and `rebench-full.sh`'s roll-up) needs to know which slug served the benchmarked URL.

1. **`rebench-full.sh` used its own private lookup.** It checked `COMPOSE_REGISTRY` only, so local-layer slugs never matched; it didn't check that the container publishes the benchmarked port; and the first match won. With two models up, a rebench of one was recorded under the other.
2. **The shared resolver didn't know pods.** `resolve_serving_tag` only matched each compose's default container name. A pod or estate instance runs as `club3090-<name>`, so runs against it left no record, and the fingerprint inspected a container that doesn't exist.

## What changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `measurement_record.py` | `resolve_serving(url)` returns `(slug, container)`. It checks, in order: a `club3090.slug` container label; the default estate file's instances (for pods booted before the label existed); the default container name (core and local layer). The URL port guard applies on every path. `resolve_serving_tag` stays as the slug half. `_detect_serving_fingerprint` now inspects the container that actually matched. |
| `estate_cli.py` | The per-instance compose override labels each service `club3090.slug=<slug>`, so a pod says which slug it runs whatever its container name or estate file. |
| `rebench-full.sh` | The record step calls `resolve_serving`, is now given `URL`, and reads compose paths via `get_registry()`. The private lookup is gone. |

The estate-file fallback needs PyYAML, like the estate CLI itself. Without it, that step is skipped and the label and default-name paths still work.

## Tests

New `test-measurement-record-resolve`, **17 checks**, fully offline: a scratch copy of the tree, a local slug promoted into it with `promote.py`, an estate file under a temp `HOME`, and a `docker` shim for `ps`, `port` and `inspect`.

| Area | Checks |
|---|---|
| Default container names | a core slug; a local-layer slug; the URL port guard (a port the container doesn't publish → not attributed) |
| Pods | by label; by the estate file; the port guard on both; an unknown pod → nothing, not a guess |
| Two models up (the reported rig) | the pod's URL → the pod's slug; the core slug's URL → the core slug |
| Fingerprint | `engine_pin` comes from the pod's own container |
| Estate | the override carries the label |
| `rebench-full.sh` | its **real** record step, extracted and run: the pod's rebench lands in the pod slug's corpus file, and a URL nothing publishes is skipped |

**Against master** the same test reproduces both bugs. The pod resolves to nothing, and a rebench of the pod's URL is **appended to `sgl-thinkingcap38-27b-dual-superfast__….jsonl`**, the other model that was up. That is the exact case in the report.

**Live on the reference rig** (read-only):

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `:8142` | `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`, engine pin `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20` from the running container |
| `:9999` | not attributed |

Tier 0 and the measurement, bench-capture, submit-bench, estate, pod and rebench tests: 33/33.

## Not in this PR

- A container started by `switch.sh` still identifies its slug by the compose's default container name, so two slugs that share one compose file are told apart by registry order, as before. Stamping `club3090.slug` on `switch.sh` launches too would close that. It needs a compose override on the launch path and is left for a follow-up.
- A pod booted before this change is found through the **default** estate file only. A pod booted from a custom `--file` estate needs one re-`up` to get the label.
