`health.sh` answered the wrong question on any rig not serving qwen3.6-27b's default slug.

## Why

1. **Wrong port.** It probed the port of qwen3.6-27b's default slug (`:8020`) whatever was running. On the reference rig, with `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` healthy on `:8142`, it printed `✗ API not reachable at http://localhost:8020`. `verify.sh` and `bench.sh` have autodetected the running container since #310; `health.sh` never did.
2. **Wrong engine.** It named the engine itself: `owned_by llamacpp` meant llama.cpp, and anything else was vLLM. An SGLang server was labelled vLLM and got a vLLM runtime section that looks for log lines SGLang never writes. That was a private engine classifier, the thing `scripts/lib/engine-kind.sh` exists to replace (#1282).

## What changes

| | Change |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `health.sh` calls `preflight_autodetect_endpoint` first, exactly as `verify.sh` does. `URL=` and `CONTAINER=` still win, and `PREFLIGHT_NO_AUTODETECT=1` skips it. The registry default is the fallback when nothing runs. |
| Engine | The container is found first. Then `engine-kind.sh` decides from its image, else its name, else `/v1/models` `owned_by`. Labels: vLLM / llama.cpp / SGLang / ExLlamaV3 / unknown. |
| SGLang runtime section (new) | Built from SGLang's batch log lines: KV from `full token usage`, spec-decode from `accept len` (the engine's own counter), `gen throughput`, running and queued requests. The KV and spec-decode lines keep the shape c3's Doctor read parses. |
| ExLlamaV3 / unknown | Says the runtime details aren't parsed, instead of reading the wrong logs as vLLM. |
| AGENTS.md | The diagnosis row from #1494 no longer needs `URL=`. |

## Tests

**Live on the reference rig** (`sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` on `:8142`, no `URL=`):

```
[autodetect] using running container=sglang-qwen38-27b-mtp-dual url=http://localhost:8142
Endpoint: http://localhost:8142
  ✓ Serving model: qwen3.8-27b  (engine: SGLang)
SGLang runtime (last 200 log lines):
  ✓ KV cache: 0%  (token usage 0.00)
  ✓ MTP/Spec-decode: accept len last 5 = 1.00  (1.00,1.00)
  ✓ Last gen throughput: 1.01 tokens/s
```

Master printed `✗ API not reachable at http://localhost:8020` on the same rig.

**`test-health-container`**, with new arms on mocked docker, curl and logs:
- the autodetected port is the one probed, and `URL=` still wins;
- the engine comes from the image even under a custom container name, then from the name, then `owned_by`, and is "unknown" with no evidence;
- the SGLang section parses a real-format decode line (KV 12%, accept len 3.12, 95.33 tokens/s).

Against master's `health.sh`, 10 of the new checks fail. The ones that pass there held before too: `URL=` wins, and a vLLM image or llama.cpp `owned_by` gets its label.

**Other checks:** Tier 0 guards (including `test-engine-kind-resolver`) plus `test-default-url-gateway`, `test-quality-passthrough` and `test-docs-local-layer`: 28/28. c3's fast files (c3 parses `health.sh` output): 277 passed.

AGENTS.md was a contributor guide with nothing for an agent working on a rig — "make it serve, find out why it doesn't" — and several of its facts had drifted from the code. Checked every path, slug and default it names against the tree and `registry.yaml`.

## What changes

**New section: "Working on a rig — yours or a user's"** (after Hardware truths)
- Change behaviour through settings, never by editing tracked files, in this order: a shell prefix → a per-slug setting (`switch.sh --set`) → a global setting (`settings.sh set`) → the gitignored local layer.
- Where per-machine state lives since #1466, the precedence order, and that values are literal.
- Secrets: never `--show-secrets` in shared output, never `cat secrets.env`, send the gateway key on stdin; `gateway-key.sh status` answers without printing it.
- Raw `docker compose` via `settings.sh compose-env-file`; worktrees share settings and caches.

body:
`test_services.py` + `test_registry_parser.py` are the files AGENTS.md says to run on every c3 change. On master, run on their own with the repo's venv, they give **11 failed, 266 passed**, though the full suite passes.

## Why

`TestScriptsImportable.test_init_puts_repo_root_on_sys_path` builds a `scripts/lib/profiles` package in `tmp_path`, and `CockpitData` puts that root first on `sys.path`. It was never taken off. From then on, every `scripts.lib.profiles.*` import in the process resolved to the empty fake:
- 8 tests failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: scripts.lib.profiles.model_spec` / `.downloader`;
- 3 asserted on empty catalogue data.

The full suite hides it because an earlier test imports the real package first. The leak was found with a small pytest plugin that reported which test changed `sys.modules['scripts']`.

## What changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_services.py` | That test hands `CockpitData` a copy of `sys.path` via `monkeypatch`, so pytest puts the original back. |
| `tests/conftest.py` | After each test's fixtures are torn down, whatever their order, any temp dir the test added to `sys.path` is dropped. The launch-settings form tests leave their temp repo roots there too, because `services.py` inserts a `CockpitData`'s repo root. The real repo root is left alone; later imports need it. |

## Tests

| Run | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_services.py` + `test_registry_parser.py` | 11 failed, 266 passed | **277 passed** |
| `test_services.py` + `test_launch_settings_form.py` | 37 failed | **291 passed** |
| full c3 suite | 1199 passed, 1 failed | 1199 passed, 1 failed (the same unrelated test) |

Each half alone also fixes the 11: the conftest hook without the test change gives 277 passed, and the test change without the hook gives 277 passed. A first version of the hook was a fixture that failed on a leak; it gave false alarms, because fixture teardown order decides whether `monkeypatch` has restored `sys.path` yet. The teardown hook runs after all fixtures.

The one remaining failure, `test_real_registry_reps_are_status_aware` (it expects 10 curated slugs; the registry has 14), fails the same way on master. It's a separate stale count and isn't touched here.

body:
Follow-up to #1466. An install updated with `git pull` keeps its settings in the repo `.env`, and its gateway routes and keys in `services/litellm`. They keep working, but nothing told the user they could move them to `~/.config/club-3090`. The plan promised a one-time notice; only `settings.sh show`, `report.sh` and a plain `litellm-sync` ever mentioned it.

## What changes

| Where | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `club_config.migrate_notice` / `migrate_pending` (new) | Lists what `settings.sh migrate` would still copy: counts and file names, never a value. The notice is shown **once per set of pending items**. A stamp in the config dir holds a hash of the key names. The notice comes back when a new key lands in the checkout and goes quiet after `migrate`. If the stamp can't be written (the config dir can't be created), nothing is shown, because the notice would otherwise repeat on every launch. |
| `switch.sh` | Prints it on a launch, before its refusals, so a refused launch still shows it. |
| `launch.sh` | Prints it after the estate validate/down exits, before preflight. |
| `gpu-mode` | Prints it on the commands that start or stop things. `status`, `--list-modes` and `service-images` stay quiet. |
| c3 | Shows it as a startup toast, alongside the `c3-settings.json` fold-in notices. |
| `setup.sh` | In a terminal, offers the copy (`Copy them now? [Y/n]`), but only when the config dir can be created. End of input counts as "no" and never ends setup. Without a terminal it prints the notice instead. |
| `litellm-sync --quiet` (run by `switch.sh` and gpu-mode) | Leaves the "still read from the checkout" line to this notice, so it isn't said twice. A plain run still says it every time. |
| `docs/FAQ.md` | One line. |

One stamp is shared by all of them, so whichever runs first shows the notice. No silent auto-migrate: that would copy HF tokens and cloud keys into `~/.config` without asking, and some users sync that directory between machines.

## Tests

- **New `test-migrate-notice`, 30 checks.**
  - It drives the real `switch.sh`, `launch.sh`, gpu-mode (docker and sudo shims, checked first on `PATH`) and `setup.sh` through a pty.
  - These run on a scratch copy of the tracked tree with a planted `.env`, so the test never writes the checkout's own `.env`.
  - It covers: shown once, then quiet; one stamp across the launchers; shown again for a new key; quiet after migrate; no stamp → no notice; nothing pending → no config dir created; the gateway files counted; no value anywhere; the setup offer copying (`secrets.env` 0600) and leaving the repo `.env` alone; end of input at the offer.
- **c3 `TestMigrateNotice`:** the toast shows once and shares the launchers' stamp, stays quiet when nothing is pending or after migrate, and a broken notice can't stop c3.
- **`test-litellm-local-config`:** the notice arm is updated for the dedupe.
- **Negative control against master:**
  - `test-migrate-notice` fails 13 checks.
  - The 15 that pass are absence checks (no value, no repeat), which hold trivially when nothing prints; each has a positive counterpart that fails.
  - c3: 2 of 3 fail.
- **Mutation:** dropping the end-of-input fallback in `setup.sh` fails the new arm.
- **Full sweep**, run with a dummy key planted in the worktree's `.env` so the notice fires inside other tests the way it would on a maintainer's checkout:
  - 231/233 on the first run. The 2 failures were real:
    - `test-setup-picker` caught `setup.sh` exiting at a bare `read` under `set -e` when the offer met end of input;
    - `test-tests-never-launch` wanted the `PATH` shim spelled out on the gpu-mode call.
  - Both are fixed. Tier 0, every `test-setup*` and the three affected tests were rerun: 35/35.
- **Full c3 suite:** 1199 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_real_registry_reps_are_status_aware`, which fails on master too.

title: feat(settings): one-time notice while settings live in the checkout (#1466)

body:
Phases **4a** and **4b** of the #1466 settings plan: the compile caches and the KV-offload disk tier move out of the repo tree.

## Why

- The vLLM composes mounted their torch.compile and Triton caches from `models/<model>/vllm/cache/` in the checkout. So every new worktree compiled from cold, the same kernels were stored once per model and again per checkout (22 GB in one checkout on the reference rig), and root-written files sat in the repo tree.
- On the reference rig **every** in-repo `triton/` and `torch_compile/` folder is `root:root 0755`. Docker created them itself, because the bind-mount source didn't exist yet. So even the files the `user: "0:${DOCKER_GID}"` fix made group-writable can't be deleted without sudo.
- The KV disk tier (`KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1`) defaulted to the repo's `kv-offload/`.

## What changes

| | Before | After (through a launcher) | Raw `docker compose up`, nothing set |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compile caches | `models/<model>/<engine>/cache/<subdir>` | `${CLUB3090_CACHE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/club-3090}/<image key>/<subdir>` | unchanged (old in-repo path) |
| KV disk tier | repo `kv-offload/` | `${CLUB3090_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/club-3090}/kv-offload` | unchanged (repo `kv-offload/`) |
| Explicit `KV_OFFLOAD_DIR` | wins | still wins | still wins |

The composes now mount:

```yaml
- ${CLUB3090_ENGINE_CACHE_DIR:-../../../cache}/triton:/root/.triton/cache          # 70 composes, 140 mounts
- ${KV_OFFLOAD_DIR:-${CLUB3090_DATA_DIR:-../../../../../..}/kv-offload}:/kv-offload   # 9 composes
```

The disk tier stays **unbounded by default** (#1419). No cap is added.

### The key

`<image reference, sanitised>-<first 12 hex of the local image ID>`, for example `vllm-vllm-openai-v0.30.0-8a69ffad015f`.

- Same image → same folder, from any checkout and for any model. The caches already key their own entries by config and kernel hash; the 20 Qwen3.8 composes shared one folder this way.
- The ID and not only the tag: a re-pulled tag is different engine code (`gemma4-unified` is a moving tag), so it gets a new folder. The reference is there so people can read `settings.sh caches`.
- The image is whatever `docker compose config` renders in the launch's own environment, so an engine-profile image a launcher injects and a compose default both resolve exactly as they will at `up`. An image that isn't on the machine is pulled first (`up` would pull it anyway).
- The variant subfolders (`triton_int8`, `torch_compile_qatawq`, …) are kept. They came from 160e8fce ("the overlay file set differs"). The 20 Qwen3.8 composes already share one folder across five different overlay sets, so the split doesn't look necessary, but keeping it costs nothing (see the questions).

### Every launch path

| Path | How it gets the folders |
|---|---|
| `switch.sh` (and `launch.sh`, which delegates to it; c3's catalog serves) | `up_variant` calls `club_engine_cache_export` after the engine pin and launch settings, before `compose up` |
| `gpu-mode` model modes | `compose_at_env` computes them **as you**, renders the compose the way `sudo` will see it (`--env-file` plus the `VAR=val` arguments only), and passes both variables through `sudo` as `VAR=val` |
| `launch.sh --estate` | `estate_cli.run_compose` calls the same helper |
| c3 generated / brought composes (raw `docker compose up`) | `serve_generated` adds them to the plan env. It never pulls at plan time, so an image that isn't local keeps the in-repo default for that serve |
| raw `docker compose up` | nothing set → the old in-repo paths. The FAQ says so and shows how to export the helper's two lines by hand |

A brought compose (`pull.sh --apply-swap`, written outside the sibling's folder) has its relative mounts made absolute. `swap_apply` only did that for a whole-string `${VAR:-relpath}`, so the new suffixed and nested fallbacks would have stayed relative. It now rewrites every relative `${VAR:-default}`.

`scripts/lib/engine_cache.py` holds the logic; `scripts/lib/engine-cache.sh` is the bash wrapper. It creates **every mounted folder as the invoking user before compose runs**, so docker never creates one as root. It never fails a launch: on any problem (no compose v2, image not found, a relative `CLUB3090_CACHE_DIR`, an unwritable folder) it prints why, and that launch uses the in-repo default. A compose that mounts neither variable costs one `grep`.

### The old in-repo caches

Nothing is deleted automatically.

- At launch, when the compose's old in-repo folder still holds a cache, one line says so and names the command.
- `bash scripts/settings.sh caches` lists the shared per-image folders, the disk tier with the free space where it lives, and this checkout's old caches with sizes.
- `--remove-legacy` asks first, removes what you own, and prints the exact `sudo rm -rf -- …` line for folders docker created as root (all of them on the reference rig, see Why). It refuses without a terminal unless `--yes`.
- `settings.sh path` now lists the cache and data folders.

## Findings on ownership and free space (4b)

| | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level folders | Docker creates a missing bind-mount source as `root:root 0755`. That is why every in-repo `triton/` and `torch_compile/` needs sudo to remove. | Fixed for the new location: the launchers create them first. The guard checks it. |
| `umask` | 38 of the 70 cache composes set `umask 0002` (the Qwen3.8 family), so their files come out `root:<your group>`, group-writable. The other 32 don't, so their files are `0644` in `0755` folders and can't be deleted without sudo, even with the GID line. | Not changed (32 entrypoints, needs boots). Question below. |
| vLLM disk tier | The 5 vLLM KV composes have the GID line and `umask 0002`, so the tier's folders should be deletable under a launcher-created top folder. | **Not verified live.** It's in the reviewer check. |
| SGLang disk tier | The 4 SGLang KV composes have no `user:` line, so HiCache's files are `root:root`. Flat files in the launcher-created folder are deletable; files in any subfolder SGLang creates would not be. `docs/engines/SGLANG.md` measured about one file per token per GPU. | Not changed. The guard lists these 4 as a list that may only shrink. Question below. |
| Free space | Both folders are on the **home filesystem** by default. One image's compile cache reached 22 GB in one checkout here (21 GB of it `torch_aot_compile`, 85 entries, never pruned). vLLM's disk tier has no cap. SGLang's keeps a 20 GiB free floor, but its file count also costs inodes. On the reference rig home and the repo share one filesystem, so nothing changes there. On a rig with a small home partition and the repo on a data disk, this is a real risk. | Called out in the FAQ with the one-line fix (`settings.sh set CLUB3090_CACHE_DIR=… KV_OFFLOAD_DIR=…`). A launch with the disk tier on prints the free space where it lands. Sharing across checkouts also means one copy per image instead of one per checkout per model. |

## Tests

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test-engine-cache` (new) | 37/37. Drives the **real** `switch.sh`, gpu-mode's real `compose_at_env` and the estate planner with docker/sudo shims and a render-only `docker compose config`: same folder from two worktrees; another image and a re-pulled tag get their own; variant subfolders; folders exist and are yours before `up`; sudo gets both variables; a shell-only `VLLM_IMAGE` is ignored on the sudo path while a saved one is honoured; explicit `KV_OFFLOAD_DIR` wins; XDG defaults; a saved `CLUB3090_CACHE_DIR` with a space; relative path refused; pull-then-key; unpullable image falls back; `COMPOSE_BIN=:`; the legacy notice; `settings.sh caches` report, refusal and `--remove-legacy`. |
| `test-compose-cache-ownership` (Tier 0) | Pass. Keeps the GID and UID checks, scans both mount forms, and now fails on a bare in-repo cache mount, a wrong fallback, a KV mount without the data-dir default, a new GID-less KV compose, or a helper that doesn't create the folders as you. |
| `test-compose-mounts-resolve` | Pass, **710 → 1396 checks**. Its volume splitter cut `${VAR:-x}:/target` at the `:-`, so no `${…:-…}` mount had ever been checked. It now checks them, nested and suffixed defaults included. |
| `test-club-config` | Pass, with cache/data folder parity in bash and Python (8 cases, decoy variables set). |
| `test-kv-offload-knob`, `test-launch-knobs`, `test-diagnose-estate` | Pass. `test-diagnose-estate` now picks the `up` call from its recorded calls, because `run_compose` renders the compose first. |
| Tier 0 guards (24 files) | 24/24 |
| Targeted (config-launchers, gpu-mode ×4, launch-settings, parallel-boot, estate ×3, switch ×4, launch-compat, registry/status/profiles/patch drift, kv-offload-probe, …) | 24/24 |
| c3 (`test_services.py` + `test_registry_parser.py`, venv built inside the worktree) | 266 passed, 11 failed. The same 11 fail on unmodified `origin/master` with the same venv (a `scripts.lib.profiles` import-order problem). The new c3 test passes. The headless `serve_generated` tests: 6/6. |
| Full sweep, `for t in scripts/tests/*.sh` | First run 226 pass / 5 fail, all five caused by this change and fixed in the third commit: three gateway tests run gpu-mode from a partial copy of `scripts/`, `test-settings-cli` counted the `path` rows, and `test-pull-swap` caught the swap absolutizer below. After the fix, the five plus the swap/pull, gpu-mode and Tier 0 tests rerun green (231/231 overall). |

**Negative control** (the new and changed tests run against `origin/master`):

- `test-compose-cache-ownership` fails 4 of its new checks.
- `test-kv-offload-knob` fails 18 checks (the mount line and the data-dir render, on all 9 composes).
- `test-club-config` fails all 8 cache/data parity cases.
- `test-engine-cache` fails at once (no helper). Given the helper but master's composes and launchers, it fails 25 of 37; the 12 that pass are the pure key and report legs.

**Mutation check** on the guard: each mutation below makes it fail, with the matching message, and it passes again after revert.

1. Drop the GID line.
2. Set UID 1000.
3. Put back a bare in-repo mount.
4. Use the wrong fallback depth (`test-compose-mounts-resolve` catches this one too).
5. Put back the old KV mount.
6. Add the GID line to a listed SGLang compose (the list must shrink).
7. Make the helper skip `mkdir`.

## Live check for the reviewer (no boot was done here)

Needs the GPUs free. `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` is experimental, hence `--force`.

```bash
git fetch origin pull/1491/head:pr-1491
git worktree add ../c3090-A pr-1491 && git worktree add ../c3090-B pr-1491

# 1. Boot from A. First boot on this image in the new location compiles cold (a few minutes).
cd ../c3090-A && bash scripts/switch.sh --force vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast 2>&1 | tee ~/a.log
grep -F '[cache]' ~/a.log      # [cache] compile cache: ~/.cache/club-3090/vllm-vllm-openai-v0.30.0-<id12>  (shared by …)
docker inspect vllm-qwen38-27b-dual-fast --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} -> {{.Destination}}{{println}}{{end}}' \
  | grep -E 'triton|torch_compile|kv-offload'   # the ~/.cache/club-3090/<key>/… and ~/.local/share/club-3090/kv-offload sources
docker logs vllm-qwen38-27b-dual-fast 2>&1 | grep -E 'saved AOT compiled function|Directly load'   # cold: "saved AOT compiled function to …"

# 2. Switch from B, a fresh worktree that has never booted anything.
touch ~/marker-before-B
cd ../c3090-B && bash scripts/switch.sh --force vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast 2>&1 | tee ~/b.log
grep -F '[cache] compile cache:' ~/a.log ~/b.log   # the SAME folder in both
docker logs vllm-qwen38-27b-dual-fast 2>&1 | grep -E 'Directly load AOT compilation from path|Directly load the compiled graph'
#   reuse = "Directly load AOT compilation from path /root/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/<hash>"
#   and "Directly load the compiled graph(s) for compile range … from the cache, took N s"; no new "saved AOT compiled function"
find ~/.cache/club-3090/vllm-vllm-openai-v0.30.0-*/torch_compile -newer ~/marker-before-B -type f | wc -l   # expect ~0

# 3. Ownership: nothing under the new folders that only root can clean up.
find ~/.cache/club-3090 ~/.local/share/club-3090 -type d ! -writable | head      # expect nothing
find ~/.cache/club-3090 -printf '%u:%g %m %y\n' | sort | uniq -c

# 4. Optional, the 4b open item: the disk tier's file ownership.
KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64 KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1 bash scripts/switch.sh --force vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast   # prints "[kv-offload] disk tier: … (N free …)"
python3 scripts/kv-offload-probe.py --url http://localhost:8113 --disk
find ~/.local/share/club-3090/kv-offload -printf '%u:%g %m %y\n' | sort | uniq -c
find ~/.local/share/club-3090/kv-offload -type d ! -writable | head   # expect nothing

# 5. Reclaim the old in-repo caches (main checkout).
bash scripts/settings.sh caches; bash scripts/settings.sh caches --remove-legacy
```

## Not in this PR

- **SGLang, llama.cpp and exl3 caches.** No SGLang compose mounts a cache today (flashinfer, Triton and DeepGEMM JIT live inside the container and are lost on `down`). Adding a mount is now a one-line compose change, but it needs a boot.
- **`umask 0002` for the other 32 cache composes**, and a `user:` line for the 4 SGLang KV composes. Both change entrypoints or the runtime group and need boots.
- **Pruning**: the per-image folders and `torch_aot_compile/` are never pruned. `settings.sh caches` shows them; old image folders are safe to delete by hand.
- **Phase 4c** (the gateway's and Open WebUI's config files) is a separate PR.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. **umask**: add `umask 0002` to the 32 cache composes that lack it, so every cache file is deletable by you? The guard could then require it.
2. **SGLang KV composes**: add `user: "0:${DOCKER_GID:-1000}"` (plus `umask 0002`) once someone can boot one?
3. **Variant subfolders** (`triton_int8`, `_qatawq`, `_google_qat_w4a16`): keep, or collapse into `triton/` and `torch_compile/`? The evidence above says the split isn't needed.
4. **GPU arch in the key?** `docs/UPSTREAM.md` records that vLLM's `torch_aot_compile` key ignores the GPU arch. A host with mixed GPU generations now shares one cache folder across checkouts. That was already true within one checkout. Add the compute capability to the key?
5. **`DOCKER_GID`** is never set by the launchers, so files get group 1000, which is only right when your group is 1000. Should the helper export `DOCKER_GID=$(id -g)` when it's unset?
6. **Side finding, not changed:** `switch.sh` replaces a `VLLM_IMAGE` set in the shell with the engine profile's image, although its comment says the resolver leaves shell values alone. The cache key follows whatever compose actually runs, so this PR is right either way.

Refs #1466.

body:
Phase **3d** of the settings plan for #1465: c3 gets a **Launch settings** form, the twin of `switch.sh --explain / --set / --unset`.

## What changes

**Where it lives.** On the Catalog tab, `E` opens the form for the selected slug. `e` already explains a slug, so `E` edits what its next launch uses. It is also in the command palette ("Launch settings…"), the help overlay and the c3 README. It is not in the catalog hint line: at 80×24 that line would wrap onto a row the terminal clips, hiding `[|] columns` (`test_catalog_hint_shows_the_sort_and_columns_keys_at_80` caught this).

**What it shows.** One row per catalogued knob that the slug's compose reads. A slug that reads none says so.

| Column | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| setting | the knob catalogue (plus a `✗` when the next launch would refuse it) |
| next launch | the resolver's value, shown exactly as `--explain` prints it (secrets hidden) |
| from | the resolver's layer name: `shell`, `this slug`, `model pin`, `club3090.env`, `secrets.env`, `repo .env`, `compose default` |
| running | what a running container of the slug was started with: `=` same, `≠` differs, `· can't check` |
| allowed | the slug's catalogued domain in words |

Under the table: the highlighted knob's description, what it overrides, what "unset" means, this slug's own saved value, and each refusal in full. The top of the form says **"Changes apply on the next launch of this slug. A running container keeps the settings it started with."**

**Writes.** `⏎` on a row saves a value **for this slug** (`slugs.json`) and `x` removes it. Both go through the resolver's own save and remove, the same code `switch.sh --set/--unset` now calls. A refusal is shown in the resolver's words and nothing is written. There is no second validator in c3. The value for every slug stays a global setting (`bash scripts/settings.sh set KEY=VALUE`). The form shows it as a source and says where to change it, but doesn't write it. `settings.sh` doesn't know knob domains, so writing global values from the form would skip the checks.

**Same answers as switch.sh.** c3 calls the resolver in-process, the way `settings_store.py` calls the loader. c3 puts one key into its own environment, the saved HF token, and passes it as `loaded` (switch.sh does the same with `CLUB3090_CONFIG_SOURCE`). That way the key counts as coming from its file, not from the shell. c3 serves slugs by running `switch.sh` with its own environment, so a launch from c3 resolves the same way.

**Drift marker.**
- The running container is found by its `com.docker.compose.project.config_files` label, which must end with the slug's `compose_path`. This works from any checkout.
- It is read with `docker ps` and `docker inspect` only. The inspect `--format` template filters inside docker and prints only the slug's knob entries. The rest of the container's environment (tokens included) never reaches c3 or its logs.
- A forwarded knob that was unset shows up as a bare `KNOB` entry. It is compared through the compose default, so "started unset" equals "next launch unset".
- **Only knobs the compose forwards into `environment:` are checked.** A knob that only goes into the command line (for example `${REASONING_EFFORT:-low}` inside `--default-chat-template-kwargs`) can't be read back from the container, and the form shows it as "can't check". On today's catalogue:

| Knob | Checkable | Not checkable (command line only) |
|---|---|---|
| `KV_OFFLOAD_GB`, `KV_OFFLOAD_DISK`, `KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB`, `SPEC_N` | every slug that reads them | — |
| `ENABLE_THINKING` | 60 slugs | 3 (e.g. `vllm/thinkingcap-dual-w4a8`) |
| `REASONING_EFFORT` | the 22 SGLang slugs | 63 vLLM and llama.cpp slugs |

**Resolver additions** (`scripts/lib/launch_settings.py`, `launch_knobs.py`). None of them changes behaviour:
- `--explain --json` knob entries gain `allowed` and `errors` (the refusals about that knob). Both are additive.
- `Resolution.uses` exposes the compose scan per knob.
- `save_values` / `remove_values` are the `--set` / `--unset` logic as functions. `cmd_set` / `cmd_unset` print them, and their output is unchanged.

## Tests

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| c3, new `tests/test_launch_settings_form.py` | 30 passed |
| c3, full suite on this branch | 1193 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed |
| c3, full suite on `origin/master` (baseline) | 1163 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The same test fails on both: `test_real_registry_reps_are_status_aware` expects 10 curated reps and the registry now has 14. That failure is unrelated to this PR. |
| `test-launch-settings` (+1 case for `allowed` / `errors`), `test-slug-settings-store`, `test-launch-knobs`, `test-switch-explain` | all pass |
| Tier 0: the 19 tree-grep guards + `test-script-permissions`, `test-locale-utf8`, `test-no-bare-grep`, `test-config-single-parser`, `test-tests-never-launch` (24 files) | 24/24 pass |

The new c3 tests cover:
- **Parity.** For 5 slugs (SGLang, vLLM, qwen3.6 vLLM, GLM llama.cpp, and one that reads no knob), every layer is in play: shell, this slug, model pin, `club3090.env`, `secrets.env`. The form's rows must equal the real `switch.sh --explain <slug> --json` value for value and source for source, including `detail`, `overrides`, `allowed`, `errors`, `unread`, `warnings`, and the whole `launch_settings` object. A refused value must read exactly like `switch.sh --set` prints it.
- **Writes.** Round trip, out-of-domain values, a knob the slug doesn't read, the host-RAM rule, an unreadable `slugs.json`.
- **Drift.** Label matching, the filtered inspect template, bare/empty/absent env entries, command-line-only knobs, a hidden secret.
- **The form**, through a Textual pilot. It opens with `E`, shows the "next launch" note and the precedence, refuses `high` in the resolver's words and then saves `xhigh`, `x` removes a value, a dependency refusal is shown inline, a running container that differs is marked, a slug with no knobs says so, and `esc` leaves an edit before it closes the form.

The tests use a fixture checkout (symlinks plus an empty `.env`) and the per-test config dir from conftest. Docker comes from a FakeRunner. The only real subprocesses are read-only `switch.sh --explain` and a refused `switch.sh --set`, run with `COMPOSE_BIN=:` and a `docker` shim that exits non-zero if called.

**Negative controls:**
- The new c3 test file run against `origin/master`: **30 of 30 fail** (9 failed and 21 errors, because the module doesn't exist).
- The new c3 code with `origin/master`'s resolver: **23 of 30 fail**. The 7 that pass are pure parsing tests.
- The modified `test-launch-settings.sh` against `origin/master`: **1 failure**, the new `allowed`/`errors` case. The other 59 checks pass.

## Not in this PR

- No live launch. The plan's live check (launch the same slug from c3 and from `switch.sh`, then compare effective values) is left for the maintainer-side review. Steps are below.
- No drift badge in the Catalog or Containers lists. The mark is in the form only.
- No editing of global values from the form (see Writes).
- No drift check for command-line-only knobs.

### Live check (reviewer)

1. In c3, go to Catalog, select a knob-reading slug (e.g. `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`), press `E`, choose `SPEC_N`, then `⏎`, type `2`, `⏎`. Then `bash scripts/switch.sh --explain <slug>` should list `SPEC_N 2 this slug`, matching the form.
2. Serve the slug from c3 (`⏎` on the row). Once it is ready, press `E` again: every checkable row should show `=`. Record the container's knob entries without printing anything else: `docker inspect <container> --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | command grep -E '^(KV_OFFLOAD_GB|KV_OFFLOAD_DISK|KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB|ENABLE_THINKING|REASONING_EFFORT|SPEC_N)(=|$)'`
3. Launch the same slug with `bash scripts/switch.sh <slug>` and run the same `inspect`. The two outputs should be identical, and so should the `[switch] launch setting …` lines (c3's serve log prints them too, because c3 runs switch.sh).
4. Drift: `bash scripts/switch.sh --set <slug> SPEC_N=3` without relaunching. In the form, `SPEC_N` shows `≠ 2` and the banner says one setting differs. Clean up with `--unset <slug> SPEC_N`.
5. On a vLLM Qwen3.8 slug, `REASONING_EFFORT` shows `· can't check`.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. **Key.** Is `E` (next to `e` explain) OK? It is free app-wide and gated to the Catalog tab.
2. **Global values.** Should the form also offer "save for every slug" (`club3090.env`)? I left it out because that path has no per-slug domain check.
3. **Command-line-only knobs.** Should those composes also forward the knob into `environment:` (a compose change) so drift can be read? The alternative is comparing `docker compose config --hash` with the container's `config-hash` label, but that can't say which knob differs, and it also changes when anything else changes.
4. **Pods.** `pod.sh` doesn't apply per-slug launch settings, but a pod started from a slug's compose matches by label. So the form would mark a pod as drifted whenever that slug has saved values. Is that the message you want, or should pods be left out?
5. **Shared composes.** `vllm/dual` and `vllm/qwen-27b-dual-fast` share one compose, so both forms show the same running container.
6. **One-launch toggles.** The serve modal's thinking toggle (`t`) makes a one-launch shell override. Afterwards the form shows `ENABLE_THINKING ≠` until the next plain launch. I think that is accurate. Do you agree?

body:
Phase 4c of the #1466 plan: the gateway's per-rig files move out of the checkout, into the settings directory. Nothing changes for a rig that doesn't migrate.

## Why

This rig's own LiteLLM routes (a cloud endpoint, a private service) and their keys lived in the checkout, gitignored: `services/litellm/config.local.yaml` and `services/litellm/local.env`. So a worktree or a second checkout served different routes, and the keys sat in a checkout-local file instead of the 0600 `secrets.env`, which is where plan decision 2 puts cloud route keys.

## Where things live now

| What | Now | Before (still read) |
|---|---|---|
| This rig's own routes | `~/.config/club-3090/litellm/config.local.yaml` | `services/litellm/config.local.yaml`, read only while the config-dir file doesn't exist |
| Their keys | `secrets.env` (0600), saved with `settings.sh set MY_KEY=…` | `services/litellm/local.env`, still loaded by the compose; a saved key wins over it |
| Rendered `config.runtime.yaml` | unchanged: `services/litellm/` | — |
| Open WebUI `imagegen.env` | unchanged (tracked defaults) | — |

`~/.config/club-3090` is the usual config dir (`CLUB3090_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` move it).

## How the gateway gets the route keys

Not from `secrets.env` itself: that file also holds the HF token, and the gateway needs none of it.

- `scripts/lib/litellm_local.py route-keys-file` writes a 0600 temp file holding only the keys a route names (`os.environ/<NAME>` in the catalog or in this rig's routes; YAML comments ignored; `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` excluded, the compose sets it). Values come from the one loader, so the usual precedence holds (shell > `club3090.env` > `secrets.env` > repo `.env`). It prints only the path.
- The compose loads two optional env files, in this order:
  ```yaml
  env_file:
    - path: ./local.env                                   # older installs
      required: false
    - path: ${CLUB3090_LITELLM_ROUTE_KEYS:-/dev/null}     # the keys from your settings: they win
      required: false
  ```
- Every starter passes the file's path as `CLUB3090_LITELLM_ROUTE_KEYS` and deletes it once compose returns (compose reads an env file only when it creates the container):
  - **gpu-mode** (every mode that starts the gateway, `upgrade`, and `gpu-mode gateway`): through sudo's argv, like the studio paths already are. `sudo` strips the environment, and the path isn't a secret.
  - **c3's Containers tab**: an `env CLUB3090_LITELLM_ROUTE_KEYS=<placeholder>` prefix, filled in when the command runs and removed when it ends, the same way as the settings env file.
  - **`scripts/litellm-log.sh`**: when it recreates the gateway for logging on/off.
- **A plain `docker compose up`** in `services/litellm` passes nothing and loads only `./local.env`. That is exactly today's behaviour, and the compose comment says so.

A value is never printed and never on a command line. The container ends up with the keys in its environment, as it did with `local.env`.

Checked with `docker compose config --hash`: the hash depends on the keys, not on the temp file's path, so an unchanged gateway is not recreated on every mode switch. For an older rig the new compose hashes identically to master's (same directory, same `local.env`), so pulling this doesn't recreate the gateway either.

One behaviour to know: `local.env` handed the container every key in it, and the keys file hands only the ones a route names. So a route added later whose key was not in use yet needs `gpu-mode gateway`, not only the `docker restart` that `litellm-sync` does. `litellm-sync` checks the running gateway's variable names (names only: docker's own template drops the values) and warns with that command when a route's saved key is missing.

## Legacy fallback and notice

- A rig with only the old files is unchanged: same routes, same keys. Section 3 of the new test renders the compose both ways and shows it.
- `litellm-sync` prints a note when either file is still read from the checkout. It prints it once for the quiet runs from `switch.sh` and gpu-mode (a stamp file in the config dir), and on every plain `bash scripts/lib/litellm-sync.sh`. It also warns when the checkout's routes file was edited after the move, since that copy is no longer read.
- `settings.sh show` (and report.sh's Settings section) carry the same note until you migrate. `settings.sh path` lists the routes file, and the old `local.env` while it exists.

## `settings.sh migrate`

It extends the existing command (same rule: copy, never modify or delete the repo files):

- **Routes:** copied byte for byte to `litellm/config.local.yaml` (0600, atomic, never over an existing file). If that file already exists: "same content", or "differs — that one is read".
- **Keys:** each key in `local.env` that a route names goes to `secrets.env`.
  - A key already saved is skipped.
  - A value the writer refuses (`$`, quotes, …) stays in `local.env`, with the reason.
  - A key no route names stays too.
  - No value is ever printed.
- **What you can delete:** it says so per file. `config.local.yaml` can go. `local.env` can go only when every key in it was saved, otherwise it names the keys to keep it for.
- **`--dry-run`** writes nothing, not even the config dir.
- **Effect:** the keys the gateway gets are the same before and after (tested).

## What changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/lib/litellm_local.py` (new) | Where the routes are, which keys the gateway gets, the keys file, migrate, the notice, `path` rows. Stdlib only; reads env files through `club_config`. |
| `scripts/lib/litellm_sync.py` | Reads routes via `litellm_local` (config dir, else legacy; the test seam still wins); names the source in the rendered block; the one-time notice; the missing-key warning. |
| `services/litellm/docker-compose.yml` | The second optional `env_file`, and the comments. |
| `scripts/gpu-mode.sh` | `compose_litellm_up`, used by `start_service litellm` and `gpu-mode gateway`. |
| `scripts/litellm-log.sh` | Passes the keys file on its recreate. |
| `scripts/tests/test-config-single-parser.sh` | The ratchet also flags a private reader of `local.env`; `litellm_local.py` is its one sanctioned reader. |
| `scripts/lib/club_config.py` | `migrate` also runs the gateway part; `show`, `path`, report and `--help` mention it. About 30 lines, all at existing call sites; no loader change. |
| `tools/serve-cockpit/…/services.py`, `settings_store.py` | The route keys placeholder for a gateway start. |
| `services/litellm/*.example`, `config.yaml` (comment), `docs/CODING_AGENTS.md`, `docs/FAQ.md`, `docs/QUALITY_TEST.md` | New locations; the old files described as still read. CODING_AGENTS gets a short *Routes of your own* section. |

Not changed, and why:
- `gateway-key.sh` and `hermes-setup.sh`: they only name `config.local.yaml` in messages, and the file keeps its name.
- `setup.sh`: never touches these files.
- `preflight.sh`: has no gateway check.

## Decisions

- **`config.runtime.yaml` stays in `services/litellm/`.**
  - It is rendered from this checkout's catalog (`config.yaml` + registry), so it is per checkout by nature.
  - The compose mounts it by a relative path. That is what keeps a raw `docker compose up`, c3 and `litellm-log.sh` free of path plumbing. Moving it needs an absolute path in every starter, and a missing bind source makes docker create a directory.
  - The live gateway mounts today's path, and `litellm-sync` (which follows that mount) and `gateway-key.sh init` (which uses its existence as a sign the gateway has run) both key on it.
  - It holds no keys: routes reference them as `os.environ/<NAME>`.
  - A data-dir move can follow once phase 4b's data-dir helper exists. This PR adds no `data_dir()`.
- **`imagegen.env` stays as it is.** It is tracked, shipped defaults, not per-rig secrets. Its values are Open WebUI PersistentConfig: they seed a new volume only, and on an existing volume Admin → Settings → Images wins. An override layer would need the same path plumbing in every starter, for a value that seeds once. Not cheap enough for what it buys.
- **The keys file is a per-start temp file**, not a persistent filtered copy. The alternatives: a copy in the checkout would bring a secret back into the tree this phase empties, and a copy in the config dir would be a second place the keys live, which goes stale when one is changed.

## Tests

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test-litellm-local-config.sh` (new) | 41/41 |
| `test-config-single-parser.sh` (extended: a private reader of the old `local.env` now fails the ratchet; self-test 12 readers / 10 look-alikes) | pass |
| `test-litellm-log.sh` (+ route keys leg; compose assertion now checks both env files in order) | pass |
| c3: `test_settings_store.py` + `test_services.py` (+2 tests, 1 updated), in a venv built inside the worktree (checked it imports the worktree's code) | 282 passed |
| c3 full suite (incl. the headless app tests) | 1165 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed: `test_app_headless.py::TestProfileTemplateDerivation::test_real_registry_reps_are_status_aware` ("expected 10 curated reps, got 14"). It fails the same way on `origin/master`: I ran master's c3 code in a detached worktree, and it is about registry defaults, not this change. |
| Tier 0: the 19 from `command grep -lE "grep -rn\|grep -rE\|grep -rl" scripts/tests/*.sh`, plus `test-script-permissions`, `test-locale-utf8`, `test-no-bare-grep`, `test-config-single-parser`, `test-tests-never-launch` | 24/24 pass |
| Related: `test-litellm-sync`, `test-litellm-generate`, `test-gateway-key`, `-init`, `-apply`, `test-model-weights-registry`, `test-club-config`, `test-config-launchers`, `test-settings-cli`, `test-gpu-mode-compose-env`, `-list`, `-power-cap`, `-service-upgrade`, `test-openwebui-gateway-key`, `test-report-resolved-config`, `test-setup-saved-settings`, `test-litellm-ports-resolve`, `test-default-url-gateway` | 18/18 pass |

What the new test checks, each through the real entry point:

1. **Routes.** `litellm-sync` serves the config-dir routes over the checkout's, and the checkout's when there is no config-dir file. The seam still overrides both. The note prints once when quiet and every time otherwise, never with a value.
2. **Keys file.**
   - It holds only the key a route names: not the HF token, not the gateway key, not a commented or unsaved reference.
   - It is 0600, and the shell wins.
   - With nothing to hand over it prints nothing and writes nothing.
   - The missing-key check reports a saved key the gateway lacks.
3. **Compose**, via `docker compose config` on a scratch copy:
   - With nothing passed you get exactly `local.env`'s keys, as before.
   - With the file, the saved key wins, byte-exact including `$` and `#`, `local.env`'s other keys stay, and there is no HF token.
   - The hash is path-independent.
4. **gpu-mode**, as a scratch clone with docker/sudo/curl shims. For both `gateway` and `upgrade`:
   - compose gets the file (0600, only the route key) via sudo's argv;
   - no key appears on any command line or in the output;
   - the file is removed afterwards.

   With no saved route key, nothing is passed.
5. **Migrate**, through `settings.sh` in a fixture checkout:
   - Dry run: writes nothing and prints the plan.
   - Real run: byte-identical routes copy (0600); the referenced key goes to `secrets.env`; the unreferenced and refused keys stay, with reasons and the "keep local.env for …" line; no secret in the output.
   - The repo files keep the same bytes, mode and mtime.
   - The gateway's keys are identical before and after.
   - It is idempotent. `show` loses its note after the run, then flags a later edit to the old copy. `path` lists both files.

**Negative control:** the final test file, run against `origin/master` (ef39be4c) in a throwaway detached worktree, fails with rc=1: 22 checks fail and 17 pass. The 17 that pass fall in three groups:

- Behaviour this PR keeps, which master already has (9): legacy routes served, the seam override, the legacy-only compose environment, the path-independent hash, nothing passed without a saved key, the repo files left alone, an unreferenced or refused key staying in `local.env`, no gateway note, and a dry run that writes nothing.
- No-leak checks that hold trivially when nothing is written (6).
- "The keys file is removed", which holds trivially when there is none (2).

The extended `test-litellm-log.sh` fails 3 checks on master.

**Mutation checks**, each run and then reverted:

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| keys file holds every resolved setting (no filter) | 5 failures, incl. "keys file holds: COMMENTED_KEY HF_TOKEN LITELLM_MASTER_KEY …" |
| `gpu-mode gateway` recreates through plain `compose_at` | "compose up got no route keys file", "not through sudo" |
| compose loads the keys file before `local.env` | "with keys file: …" (legacy value wins), plus test-litellm-log's compose assertion |
| `litellm-log.sh` doesn't export the variable | 2 failures in test-litellm-log |
| migrate lists `KEY=value` | "migrate --dry-run: no secret value — printed a secret" (and the real run) |
| `gpu-mode.sh` gains a `grep … local.env` | test-config-single-parser: "new private .env parser(s): scripts/gpu-mode.sh" |
| the notice ignores quiet | "a quiet sync notes it once" |
| c3 gateway start without the route keys prefix | 2 failures: `test_compose_up_plan`, `test_gateway_start_gets_only_its_route_keys_and_removes_the_file` |

**Live check** with a throwaway gateway: the real compose file (scratch copy; only the container name, a `127.0.0.1` port and `restart: "no"` changed) on the local `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.3` image, a unique project name, temp config dir and test keys. Its cloud route pointed at a stub upstream in the same throwaway project, which logged the `Authorization` header it received. The real `litellm_sync.py` rendered the routes, with the test seam on so it neither probed nor followed the live gateway's mount; `route-keys-file` and `club_config.py compose-env-file` fed compose the way gpu-mode does. The rig's gateway, Open WebUI and models were not touched. Removed afterwards: 0 containers and 0 networks left.

| Step | Upstream saw | Other checks |
|---|---|---|
| A. Older install: routes and key only in the checkout | `Bearer key-from-legacy-local-env` (HTTP 200) | no `HF_TOKEN` in the gateway env; the sync printed the one-time note |
| B. `settings.sh migrate`, then a different key and a new route saved in the settings | `Bearer key-from-secrets-env` (HTTP 200) | before the recreate the missing-key check reported `NEW_ROUTE_KEY` (the sync's own docker template, names only); after it, nothing missing; still no `HF_TOKEN` |
| C. The checkout's two files deleted | `Bearer key-from-secrets-env` (HTTP 200) | |

A separate throwaway `busybox` container confirmed that a single-quoted `'a#x$y'` in an env file reaches the container as `a#x$y`. (`docker compose config` prints it as `$$`; the test undoes that.)

## What to verify live on the rig's real gateway

This needs a recreate of the live `litellm` (about 10 s; no model is touched):

1. `bash scripts/settings.sh migrate --dry-run`. It should list `services/litellm/config.local.yaml` and the route keys it would copy, with no values.
2. `bash scripts/settings.sh migrate`, then `bash scripts/settings.sh path`. The routes file should exist, and `local.env` be listed as still loaded.
3. `bash scripts/gpu-mode.sh gateway`. It should print no notice, and `gateway-key.sh status` should say "accepts it".
4. Check the gateway has the route keys and not the HF token, without printing values:
   `docker inspect litellm --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{index (split . "=") 0}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}' | sort`
5. Send one request to a cloud route through `:4000`, e.g. the DashScope route benchlocal uses. Expect 200.
6. Optional: move `services/litellm/local.env` aside, run `gpu-mode gateway`, repeat step 5, then move it back or delete it.
7. `bash scripts/lib/litellm-sync.sh`. It should print no WARN about missing keys and no note.

## Not in this PR

- Moving `config.runtime.yaml` to a data dir (see Decisions). It waits for phase 4b's helper.
- An Open WebUI `imagegen.env` override layer (see Decisions).
- `settings.sh unset KEY` clears `club3090.env`, `secrets.env` and the repo `.env`, but not `local.env`. While a key is still in `local.env`, unsetting the saved copy brings the old value back. `migrate` says when `local.env` can be deleted; I didn't widen `unset` into the gateway's file.
- A changed key value can't be detected from outside the container: `litellm-sync` only warns about a key the gateway lacks, not a stale one. The docs say to run `gpu-mode gateway` after changing a key.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. Is `~/.config/club-3090/litellm/config.local.yaml` the layout you want? The alternatives were a flat `litellm-routes.yaml`, or `config.local.yaml` beside `club3090.env`. I kept the file name, so the `.example` and the old file map one-to-one.
2. Should `migrate` also copy `local.env` keys that no route names? It leaves them, because the gateway would no longer get them from `secrets.env`, which hands over only route keys.
3. Should the stale `local.env.example` go entirely? It now only says where keys go instead.

body:
Follow-up to #1466: the hints that still pointed at the old ways of saving a setting.

## What changes

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.sh`, both "no weights under MODEL_DIR" hints | `python3 scripts/lib/club_config.py set MODEL_DIR=…` | `bash scripts/settings.sh set MODEL_DIR=…` |
| `preflight.sh`, the HF_TOKEN warning | "export HF_TOKEN=hf_... in your shell or .env file" | "save it: `bash scripts/settings.sh set HF_TOKEN=hf_...` (goes to secrets.env, 0600)" |
| `promote.py`, the core-gate refusal | "set in the repo-root .env" | "saved with `bash scripts/settings.sh set C3_ALLOW_CORE_PROMOTE=1` (the shell wins)" |
| `launch_settings.py`, the fix hint | `python3 scripts/lib/club_config.py set KNOB=<value>` | `bash scripts/settings.sh set KNOB=<value>` |
| `slug_settings.py`, the "credentials are never per-slug" refusal | `python3 scripts/lib/club_config.py set --file secrets KEY=…` | `bash scripts/settings.sh set KEY=…` (it stores it in secrets.env) |
| `docs/WSL_SETUP.md` | a `vllm/single` row | removed: no such slug exists, and the row above already names `vllm/minimal` as the single-card vLLM path |
| `docs/HARDWARE.md`, WSL2 note | "0.92 for single, 0.95 for `long-text.yml`" (that compose is gone) | any compose defaulting above ~0.94 crashes on WSL2; 24 vLLM composes default to 0.95 |

`settings.sh set` files a credential-looking key (HF_TOKEN included) into `secrets.env` on its own, so one command form covers every hint. Checked: setting `HF_TOKEN` into an empty temp config dir creates `secrets.env` with mode 600. `promote.py` fills unset keys from the loader before the gate check, so a gate saved with `settings.sh` does reach it.

## Tests

- Tier 0 guards plus the tests that cover the edited files (`test-config-launchers`, `test-launch-settings`, `test-slug-settings-store`, `test-pytest-modules`, `test-local-layer-lifecycle`, `test-thinking-pin`, `test-docs-local-layer`, `test-catalog-cli`): 32/32 pass.
- The rendered `launch.sh` hint was checked by running it against a models dir that doesn't exist.

No test asserts these strings, so there is no negative control. The change is text only.
