body:
## What

Makes the LiteLLM gateway usable by coding agents (omp, Claude-style clients) without per-client workarounds:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level `reasoning_effort` | **HTTP 400** at the gateway (`UnsupportedParamsError`) — every request that named an effort failed | forwarded; vLLM and SGLang render it into the template |
| Past `reasoning_content` on assistant turns | dropped on the catalog view's `hosted_vllm/` routes | forwarded untouched |
| `model_info` on runtime routes | none — agents fall back to a generic window | `max_input_tokens` from the booted server, `max_output_tokens`, `supports_function_calling`, `supports_reasoning` / `supports_vision` where the registry knows |
| Gateway timeout / retries | LiteLLM defaults | `request_timeout: 1800`, `num_retries: 0` |
| `switch.sh` run from a worktree | re-rendered the worktree's runtime file; the gateway kept serving the main checkout's stale routes | renders the file the running gateway actually mounts |

## Route shape — why `openai/` + `allowed_openai_params`

Checked against a request-capturing stub (LiteLLM v1.100.3):

| Route | past `reasoning_content` | past `reasoning` | top-level effort | `chat_template_kwargs` / budget / `top_k` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/` (runtime view today) | kept | kept | **400** | kept |
| `openai/` + `drop_params` | kept | kept | silently dropped | kept |
| `hosted_vllm/` (catalog view today, since d63bb8d9) | **dropped** (unconditional `pop`) | kept | passed | kept |
| **`openai/` + `allowed_openai_params: [reasoning_effort]`** | kept | kept | passed | kept |

`hosted_vllm` drops `reasoning_content`, which is the field omp replays, and SGLang answers with it. Qwen3.8's template re-renders past reasoning by default, so the model got an empty think block in place of the reasoning its client kept. (It does **not** cost prefix reuse: on vLLM dual-fast the previous turn's prompt was reused either way — 27,120 tokens after a 2,673-token turn; vLLM doesn't reuse generated tokens.) llama.cpp ignores a top-level `reasoning_effort` (it only rejects `best_of`/`suffix`), so one shape fits every engine and the per-engine provider split, and the emitter's engine-kind shell-out, go away.

⚠️ Side effect worth knowing: omp's `discovery: litellm` talks the **Responses API** to a route whose provider is `openai` (chat completions otherwise). vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp serve `/v1/responses` natively; verified end to end on vLLM and SGLang in the follow-up omp PR.

## Verified live (real gateway, `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`)

- Prompt tokens per effort for "hi", gateway == direct: unset 41 · low 41 · medium 11 · xhigh 53 · high 53 · top-level medium 11 · top-level xhigh 53 · thinking off 13. Top-level effort no longer 400s.
- `/model_group/info`: `qwen3.8-27b` 262144 / 32768 / reasoning true / function calling true.
- Also rendered for `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` (262144 / 32768).
- Anthropic-format `/v1/messages` through the gateway (the Claude Code path) to `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`: tool call returned (`stop_reason: tool_use`); a `thinking.budget_tokens` request reaches the template as an effort (prompt 309 → 283 tokens). Reasoning is not surfaced back as thinking blocks on that path.

## Tests

- `test-litellm-sync`: new cases — route shape on vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp routes, `model_info` from the live server, `supports_reasoning` only where declared, `litellm_settings` survives a render + prune. Negative control: with the allowed-params line removed, the three shape checks go red.
- Green on the stacked tip (this + the omp PR): Tier 0 (15). On this branch alone: `test-litellm-sync`, `test-litellm-generate`, `test-litellm-ports-resolve`, `test-engine-kind-resolver`, `test-docs-slugs-resolve`.

Not live-tested: a llama.cpp route through the gateway (source-checked only).

body:
Follow-up to #1436. A `git pull` that bumps a pinned support-service image changes nothing that's already running. Only `docker compose up -d` recreates a container on the new image, and nothing users routinely run does that:

| After pulling, the user runs… | Picks up a new service pin? |
|---|---|
| `gpu-mode chat` / `gpu-mode 27b-dual-mtp` | yes, since they call `compose up -d` |
| `switch.sh <slug>` | **no:** its LiteLLM sync uses `docker restart` |
| a reboot / `restart: unless-stopped` | **no:** same container, same image |

That's how LiteLLM ran a six-month-old `main-latest` build unnoticed.

## What this adds

- **`gpu-mode status` gets a "Service Images" section.** Each support service is shown as current, drifted (running image ≠ compose pin) or not running. The pin is read through `docker compose config`, so `${VAR:-default}` image lines resolve. If anything drifted, the section ends with *run 'gpu-mode upgrade'*.
- **New `gpu-mode upgrade [--no-backup]`:**
  - It recreates only running services that are behind their pin. Stopped services are left alone, since they pick up the pin the next time a mode starts them.
  - It goes through `start_service`, so LiteLLM's config render still runs first.
  - It backs up Qdrant's volume to `backups/` (gitignored) before recreating it, because Qdrant's storage migrates forward one way.
- **`update.sh` reports drift after pulling.** It calls a new `gpu-mode service-images` and prints the section only when something drifted. It uses `sudo -n`, so it never stops to prompt. `update.sh` still doesn't restart anything itself.
- **`docs/FAQ.md`:** step 5 of the update flow.

## Tests

`test-gpu-mode-service-upgrade.sh` runs offline, with fixture-driven `docker`/`sudo` PATH shims:
- `upgrade` recreates only the drifted running service, not current, stopped or missing ones.
- Qdrant is stopped, backed up, and only then recreated.
- `--no-backup` skips the backup but still upgrades.
- No drift means no stop, backup or recreate.
- `status` shows the drift and the hint.
- The `update.sh` contract holds: the hint appears only when something drifted.

The test fails on master. `test-tests-never-launch` now recognizes the inline shim as a neutralizer. That's verified rather than assumed: the test refuses to run unless the shims resolve, and an unstubbed `gpu-mode` call is still flagged (negative control run). 22 gpu-mode + Tier 0 guards pass. It was also caught and fixed during testing that a never-created container used to end the loop under `set -e`.

**Live on the reference rig:** `status` shows all five services current, and `upgrade` reports "Nothing to upgrade" without touching any container.

body:
Bumps the four support services that had fallen behind, and pins the two that used floating tags.

| Service | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| LiteLLM | `main-latest` (frozen at the 2026-03-22 build, **1.82.6**) | **`v1.100.3`** |
| Qdrant | `latest` (**v1.18.0**, 2026-05-08 build) | **`v1.19.1`** |
| Open WebUI | `v0.11.3` | **`v0.11.4`** |
| SearXNG | `2026.9.20-fdd8525b1` | **`2026.9.25-12f8b6515`** |

spark-dashboard is already on the latest release (`v0.14.0`), so it's unchanged.

**Why pin:** `main-latest` and `latest` were pulled once and never refreshed, so LiteLLM ran a six-month-old build without anyone noticing. A floating tag can also upgrade silently the next time someone re-pulls. The other services already pin exact versions, and this brings these two in line.

## Deployed and checked on the reference rig

- **Qdrant 1.19.1:** both Open WebUI collections are green with unchanged point counts (1 and 741). The storage format migrates forward on first start, so the volume was backed up first.
- **LiteLLM 1.100.3:** `/health/readiness` healthy, `/v1/models` lists the same 3 routes as before, and there are no errors in the log. There's no database; config comes from the generated file.
- **Open WebUI 0.11.4:** `/health` ok, and from inside the container it reaches Qdrant (both collections) and SearXNG.

body:
Addresses discussion #1419 ("What'd help: a real agent workload ... several long conversations, switched between ... attach the output of report.sh").

Adds a probe that interleaves 3 distinct long agentic conversations (15 fixture turns each, real tool-loop turns, switched between turn-by-turn, ~58K tokens each), evicts them (11×100K fillers over the GPU pool, or `docker restart` for the disk tier), revisits each, and PASSes only if every revisit is < 0.5× a fresh cold ref AND a host/storage counter moved AND a planted per-conversation needle is still answered. Reuses the fixture, tool schemas, seed and guards from `bench-agentic.sh` verbatim, and the engine/counter detection pattern from `kv-offload-probe.py`.

- `scripts/kv-offload-agentic-probe.py` (new): the probe; `--url` auto-resolves the running slug's port from the registry (same resolution `bench-agentic.sh` uses), `--disk --container` for the restart leg.
- `scripts/report.sh`: new opt-in `--kv-agentic` section (not in `--full`, like `--agentic`).
- `scripts/tests/test-kv-offload-agentic-probe.sh`: offline test (structure, flags, URL resolution, exit-code contract) — no live endpoint needed.

Measured result on this rig (2×5090, SGLang v0.5.20 dual-fast, `KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64`): the agentic conversations FAIL to come back from the tier in both RAM and disk modes (revisits = cold), while the repo's word-soup probe PASSes (9.22 s → 0.30 s). Root cause: on hybrid MTP slugs a host/disk match is gated by the trailing-page MAMBA sidecar (`TRAILING_PAGES` policy); multi-turn conversations create one request path per turn and overflow the small host mamba pool, so LRU drops their sidecars while the KV stays. Full write-up in the discussion post.

verify-full's [7/10] thinking check failed healthy boots of concise and adaptive thinkers:
- **ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8** scored 9/10 on 41 characters of reasoning (the caveat in #1418).
- **MiMo-V2.6** flaked on empty reasoning.

**Cause.** The check asked "What is 2+2?" and failed any reasoning under 50 characters. Such models rightly answer that with a line of thought, or none. The check exists to prove that thinking engaged and was parsed into its own field. Short reasoning plus an answer already proves that.

**Fix** (`scripts/verify-full.sh`, `check_thinking`):
- **Prompt:** ask a multi-step question (train departure + trip duration). That's the shape MiMo's compose header had already shown to reason reliably (445 characters vs 80 on 2+2). `max_tokens` still bounds the verbose models.
- **Short reasoning:** short but present reasoning, with an answer in `content`, now **passes with a note**.
- **Still hard fails:** empty reasoning, reasoning without an answer (`finish` ≠ `length`), and an unparseable response.
- **Preflight:** its reasoning-effort ladder keeps its 50-character bar, now the stricter of the two, which is the safe direction. Its comment and `test-thinking-control`'s now say so instead of "must match".

**Test:** new `scripts/tests/test-verify-full-thinking-check.sh`.
- It extracts the real `check_thinking`, stubs `curl`, and asserts the verdict for six response shapes plus the prompt.

body:
Two changes across all **38** Qwen3.8-27B and ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B vLLM composes that run a drafter (MTP or DFlash2, dual / multi4 / multi8 / single).

## 1. Probabilistic draft sampling

vLLM defaults `draft_sample_method` to `"greedy"`, which treats every draft as one-hot in the rejection test. `"probabilistic"` samples drafts at the request's temperature and keeps their logits, so a draft is accepted with probability min(1, p/q) instead of p(draft). More tokens are accepted per step whenever temperature > 0, and the output distribution is unchanged because the target model still decides.

- **Where it lives:** each compose passes it in `--speculative-config` from a new `DRAFT_SAMPLE_METHOD` knob, default `probabilistic`.
  - The knob is declared bare in `environment:`, so an unset value stays unset.
  - Anything other than `greedy|probabilistic` refuses to boot, and `greedy` reverts.
- **Supported on our runner:** the v0.30.0 V2 runner implements it for both drafters (MTP via `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.sample_draft`, DFlash2 via its `_cache_draft_logits`), and the V2 rejection sampler consumes the cached logits.
- **Incompatibilities:** stock vLLM rejects it only with `use_heterogeneous_vocab` or `use_local_argmax_reduction`. We set neither.

Measured on the reference rig: 2×3090, **230 W** (the same power as the recorded rows), one boot each, decode-only bench:

| slug | recorded 2026-09-23 (greedy), T 0.6 | this PR, T 0.6 | this PR, T 1.0 (same boot) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-fast` (MTP n=4) | 74.0 / 101.0 | **77.6 / 107.3** (+5% / +6%), AL 3.08 | — |
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-superfast` (DFlash2 n=7) | 80.0 / 157.6 | **85.1 / 163.3** (+6% / +4%), AL 3.58 | 84.8 / 153.9, AL 3.69 |

Caveats:
- **Noise:** these are single boots, and +4–6% is only somewhat above boot-to-boot noise. The superfast code run had CV 7.9%.
- **The served temperature is unmeasured:** there was no greedy run at T 1.0, which is where the larger effect is expected. HyperQwen reports MTP 78→90 and DFlash2 101→122 at T 1.0 on a 3090.

## 2. Drop `vllm-gdn-mtp-async-spec-order` (the #1052 hoist)

Since v0.29.0, vLLM serves MTP and DFlash on the **V2 model runner**; our boot logs say `Using V2 Model Runner`. The hoist patched V1's `gpu_model_runner.py::synchronize_input_prep`, which V2 never calls. So it has been inert since the 2026-09-12 pin bump, while still logging `[gdn-async-order] applied` and passing its anchor drift guard.

- **Removed:** the mounts, the entrypoint installs, the patch directory, and its `patches.yml` entry.
- **Corrected:** compose headers that claimed "✅ PATCHED HERE" or "now fixed by", the `docs/UPSTREAM.md` rows, and three registry status notes.
- **Still active under V2:** `vllm-flashinfer-decode-pin` (it patches the FlashInfer package) and `pr48375` (the shared KV manager).
- ⚠️ **Open question:** whether V2 has the same async race is **untested**. The crash had already stopped reproducing on the shipped Frozenlock checkpoint (2026-08-24); the #1052 reproducer needs the retired Avuja export.

## Validation

- **New guard `scripts/tests/test-compose-draft-sample-method.sh`:**
  - static: all 38 composes carry the key, the bare knob and its guard;
  - every hand-built speculative-config JSON (3 variants) still parses once its shell variables are filled;
  - delivery: an MTP and a DFlash compose are rendered for unset, `greedy` and junk;
  - on master it fails with 158 findings.
- **Other guards:** Tier 0, all `test-compose-*`, patch attribution, caveat/patch ambiguity, registry round-trip, profile/launch compat, switch/launch parity, docs, locale and permissions: **52/52** pass.
- **Live, via `switch.sh`:** ThinkingCap dual-fast and dual-superfast, plus Qwen3.8 dual-ultramax (the DFlash + `attention_backend` JSON variant).
  - All three showed `draft_sample_method: probabilistic` in vLLM's own args, the V2 runner, and zero hoist lines.
  - verify-full was clean on ultramax.
  - ThinkingCap superfast got 9/10: the known concise-thinking false-fail (#1418), a harness issue I'll fix in its own PR.
- **Not booted here:** multi4/multi8 (we have only 2 cards) and single nvfp4 (Blackwell). They're the same edit, covered by the static JSON check.
- **Docs:** `.env.example` documents the knob, and BENCHMARKS gets two dated rows. The per-model CHANGELOG history is left untouched.

body:
One command now fetches everything a launch slug needs:

```bash
bash scripts/setup.sh llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs   # weights + mmproj projector
bash scripts/setup.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultramax      # weights + DFlash2 drafter
```

**Why.** 40 slugs declare `weights_companions`, a drafter or vision projector their compose mounts. Only the serve-cockpit's Download action read them. A CLI download of the model got the core weights and could leave a slug that crash-loops on a missing drafter (#1247; #1379 made preflight catch it at launch, but not at download time).

**How.** An argument containing `/` resolves through the registry:
- `WEIGHT_KEY` = `<model>:<weights_variant>`;
- `WEIGHT_EXTRA_KEYS` = the qualified companions, the same keys `services.py` `run_weights_download` builds.

Explicit env vars still win. `WEIGHT_EXTRA_KEYS= bash scripts/setup.sh <slug>` skips the companions. An unknown slug is refused, with the model list and `switch.sh --list`. `setup.sh <model>` is unchanged.

**No required/optional split, and why.** Every declared companion is fetched:
- **Drafters:** all drafter companions are default-ON in their slugs.
- **Projectors:** 12 slugs pass `--mmproj <path>` unconditionally (iq4xs, MiMo, flash-next ×3, prism ×2, plus 5 deprecated), so the projector is required there.
- **The one exception:** GLM's 18 composes fall back to text-only without the projector. It's 1.13 GB next to 114–157 GB of weights.

Deriving requiredness from the model profile's `setup.vision` would have marked the MiMo / iq4xs / flash-next projectors optional, and those slugs would then fail to boot.

**Also:**
- **Queue before the dump:** companions are queued before `SETUP_DUMP_KEYS`, which now prints `slug=` and `companions=`, so `extras=` shows exactly what downloads.
- **Deduplication:** companions are deduped against the primary and the model's always-fetched drafter (GLM's `dflash2-q4km` is both).
- **Disk estimate:** it now counts queued companions, which the cockpit path missed too (ultramax on an empty dir: 40 → 41 GB).
- **#250 error:** the two-argument error points a stray slug at the slug form.
- **Docs:** a line in GETTING_STARTED; ADDING_MODELS notes what `weights_companions` now drives; the iq4xs compose quick-start uses the one-liner.

**Tests.** New `scripts/tests/test-setup-slug-companions.sh`. For one slug per distinct companion set (20), it checks:
- the model and primary are right, and the companions equal the cockpit's keys;
- every companion is queued and resolves in the weights catalog;
- nothing is queued twice.

Negative controls: `WEIGHT_EXTRA_KEYS=` skips, an explicit `WEIGHT_KEY` wins, a model name doesn't resolve as a slug, and an unknown slug is refused. On master's `setup.sh` it fails at the first slug. The existing `test-setup-*` / `test-preflight-*` guards, Tier 0, docs, compose, locale and permission guards all pass (42/42).

**Live run on the real path**, weights already present: `MODEL_DIR=… bash scripts/setup.sh llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs` resolved the slug and SHA-verified both the GGUF and the projector (rc=0). Disk use was unchanged, so nothing was re-downloaded.

The cockpit is untouched; it already sends these keys.

body:
26 llama.cpp-family composes (9 llama.cpp, 13 ik-llama, 4 beellama) disagreed with themselves about the drafter's default depth.

**The bug.** The entrypoint decides drafter ON/OFF from `_spec_n="$${SPEC_N:-1}"`. The depth flag reads `${SPEC_N:-${MTP_DRAFT_N_MAX:-N}}` host-side (or `DRAFT_N_MAX` / `MTP_N_MAX`). That second variable was never declared in `environment:`, so the entrypoint couldn't see it:
- the banner printed `[spec] drafter ON (SPEC_N=1)` while the server drafted at N (the #1394 rig report showed `SPEC_N=1` on a depth-2 slug);
- `MTP_DRAFT_N_MAX=0`, which the headers document as "disables", kept the drafter loaded at n-max 0. That's the half-off state the toggle exists to avoid.

**The fix.** The entrypoint defaults to `$${SPEC_N:-$${VAR:-N}}`, and `VAR` is declared bare. Default argv is unchanged; only the banner and the `VAR=0` path change. `SPEC_N` still wins when set.

**Guard:** new `scripts/tests/test-compose-spec-n-default-parity.sh`.
- **Static, all 118 composes with the toggle:** the entrypoint default equals every host-side `SPEC_N` default, and any variable the entrypoint reads is declared.
- **Delivery:** renders `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs`'s compose and runs its real entrypoint with the real argv (only the final `exec llama-server` swapped for a printer) for three settings.

| setting | unfixed master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| static parity | ✗ 26 mismatches | ✓ 118 composes |
| unset | ✗ banner `SPEC_N=1` | ✓ `SPEC_N=2`, `--spec-draft-n-max 2` |
| `MTP_DRAFT_N_MAX=0` | ✗ banner ON, `--spec-type` kept | ✓ drafter OFF, flags stripped |
| `SPEC_N=3` (positive control) | ✓ | ✓ |

**Live, through `switch.sh`** on `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs`:

| setting | banner | VRAM | notes |
|---|---|--:|---|
| unset | `drafter ON (SPEC_N=2)` | 22,352 MiB | verify-full rc=0, 0 failures |
| `MTP_DRAFT_N_MAX=0` | `drafter OFF … flags removed` | 20,306 MiB | no draft context created; serves |

**Also in this PR:** `test-compose-mmproj-offload-knob.sh` (from #1424) now exports `PYTHONUTF8`. Without it, `test-locale-utf8` has been red on master since 63175df6.

Guards: Tier 0 + all `test-compose-*` + profiles/launch compat + script permissions + patch attribution + locale: all green.

Makes the #1380 recipe (q8_0 KV @215K on one card, F16 projector in system RAM) a one-liner on `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs`:

```bash
KV_TYPE=q8_0 CTX_SIZE=215000 LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_OFFLOAD=false \
  bash scripts/switch.sh --force llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs
```

**Change.** `q4kv-vision.yml` declares `- LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_OFFLOAD` in `environment:`, bare. llama-server reads the variable natively, and an unset host var stays out of the container, so the default boot is unchanged. Nothing new in `command:`.

**Why the bare form matters.** llama.cpp rejects an empty boolean before it loads the model (`error while handling environment variable "LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_OFFLOAD": invalid boolean value`, checked on both b10920 and b11146). So the usual `- VAR=${VAR:-}` would set it empty and break every default boot. A `--mmproj-offload` / `--no-mmproj-offload` in argv would override the env and make the knob do nothing.

**Guard:** new `scripts/tests/test-compose-mmproj-offload-knob.sh` (modelled on `test-compose-nparallel-knob.sh`):
- **static:** bare declaration, and no `--(no-)mmproj-offload` in argv;
- **delivery path:** `LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_OFFLOAD=false` reaches the container as `false`;
- **negative control:** unset means absent.

| negative control | result |
|---|---|
| `=${LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_OFFLOAD:-}` form | ✗ fails (static + negative control) |
| `--mmproj-offload` added to argv | ✗ fails (static) |
| declaration removed | ✗ fails (search finds nothing) |

**Live, through `switch.sh` (b11146, the compose's pin):**

| | container env | VRAM | new 640×480 image |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| unset (default) | absent | 22,368 MiB | 0.60 s |
| `LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_OFFLOAD=false` | `false` | 21,178 MiB | ~1.5 s, bursts to ~4 s |

`verify-full` on the knob-on boot: rc=0, vision 4/4. Guards: Tier 0 + all `test-compose-*` + profiles/launch compat + script permissions + docs: 43/43. `verify-stress` not run; the default path is unchanged.

**Correction bundled in.** The per-image cost recorded on 2026-09-25 (compose note + #1380 BENCHMARKS row) said 4.01 s on the CPU. Salting the test image per run showed the CPU projector is bimodal on our 32-vCPU VM: mostly ~1.4-1.6 s, in bursts ~4 s, the same on b10920 and b11146. The 09-25 runs happened to sit in the slow mode. CPU steal was 0, and the burst cause isn't isolated. Both places now state the range.

body:
Fix the `test-bench-capture` triad branch so it passes on numpy-less rigs.

Split off from #1412 (SGLang `MAMBA_RADIX_CACHE_STRATEGY` seam) — it's a
standalone test fix with no dependency on the seam, so it can land on its own.

## Root cause (two things, not one)

On a numpy-less rig the test failed with:

```
FAIL: the triad ceiling must state its worker count — a single-threaded number is not a host ceiling
```

1. **numpy isn't installed** on such a rig, so `STREAM_CALIB=1`'s
   `cap_stream_triad_gbps` hits `import numpy` → `ModuleNotFoundError` → rc=3,
   and bench.sh prints its "degrades cleanly" line instead of a ceiling value.
2. **A latent test bug made that degradation branch dead code.** Section 11
   branched on the `========== RAM BANDWIDTH CEILING … ==========` *header* —
   but bench.sh prints that header unconditionally whenever `STREAM_CALIB=1`
   (bench.sh:701), before it knows whether calibration succeeded. The header
   can't distinguish a measured ceiling from a numpy-absent degradation, so the
   test always took the success branch and never reached the else-branch its
   own comment calls "a supported configuration, not a failure."

## Fix (one line)

Branch on the `triad ceiling  :` *value* line (bench.sh prints it only when a
ceiling was actually measured) instead of the header. Numpy-less / failed rigs
now route to the degradation branch the test already declares supported;
numpy-present rigs still assert the worker count on a real ceiling
(reference-rig behavior preserved).

## Verification

- Passes on this rig (exit 0).
- Reference-rig behavior (numpy present) unchanged — still asserts the worker
  count on a real measured ceiling.

body:
## What

**1. `scripts/kv-offload-probe.py`** proves the KV offload tier actually serves hits. A clean boot with offload on proves nothing: vLLM v0.29.0 and today's vLLM DFlash tiers both accept every write and never serve a read. It's stdlib-only and works on vLLM and SGLang:

- **RAM mode:** prompt A cold → A again (GPU) → fillers past the **auto-detected** GPU pool → A again.
- **Disk mode** (`--disk --container <name>`): A → `docker restart` (the GPU and RAM tiers die with the process) → A again.
- **PASS** = A returns in under half a fresh same-length prompt's time **and** the engine's own offload counters moved. A carries a needle, so a hit that returns the wrong state shows up too.

**2. A fix the probe found: the SGLang disk tier threw away its hits on a large directory.**
- SGLang's default `timeout` prefetch policy gives storage `2 s + 0.1 s per 1K tokens`, then **silently re-prefills**. A 40K prompt gets 5.9 s.
- On a tier directory of ~850K files per GPU, reading it back took **7.4 s**, so every disk hit was discarded and the prompt came back cold.
- The knob's disk branch now sets `--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete` on all four SGLang dual MTP composes. Waiting for pages already on disk always beats a re-prefill.

**3. Probe pool detection on vLLM hybrid models.** `num_gpu_blocks × block_size` reads 11,840 against a real 591,422 (the block is a padded page). The probe now reads the `cache_config_info` label `kv_cache_size_tokens`.

## Validation (2× 3090, live)

| run | result |
|---|---|
| SGLang `dual-fast`, RAM | ✅ PASS: 0.46 s vs 28.10 s cold, 40,064 tokens from host |
| vLLM `dual-fast`, RAM | ✅ PASS: 1.68 s vs 26.32 s cold, 1.41 GB loaded from the tier |
| SGLang disk, fresh directory | ✅ PASS: 4.61 s vs 26.38 s cold |
| SGLang disk, ~850K files/GPU, **default policy** | ❌ FAIL: 27.63 s vs 27.99 s (the bug) |
| same directory, **`wait_complete`** | ✅ PASS: 7.38 s vs 28.68 s cold |
| SGLang, **offload off** (negative control) | ❌ FAIL as expected: 26.39 s vs 26.38 s |

**Guards:**
- New `test-kv-offload-probe` covers counter parsing (device-side hits must not count) and pool detection on both engines. Each check has a failing negative control: a too-broad counter pattern, and the old block-product detection.
- `test-kv-offload-knob` now requires `wait_complete` in the SGLang disk branch.
- 18/18 Tier-0 + diff-area guards pass.

It's used by the "Try it yourself" section going into the KV offload announcement (#1419).

body:
## What

The registry repeats two numbers that live in each compose: the concurrency cap (`--max-num-seqs` / `--max-running-requests`) and the memory fraction (`--gpu-memory-utilization` / `--mem-fraction-static`). Nothing kept them in step, so **20 entries had drifted**. Tools that read the registry (c3, kv-calc) were describing configs the composes don't boot.

| entries | field | registry was | compose boots |

## What

**1. Opt-in HiCache host-RAM + disk tier** on the four Qwen3.8-family dual MTP SGLang composes: `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`, `sgl/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-fast`, `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-max` and `sgl/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-max`. It uses the same knob as the vLLM tiers (#1408), off by default:

| env | effect |
|---|---|
| `KV_OFFLOAD_GB=<GiB>` | host-RAM prefix tier, total across both GPUs → `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size <per GPU> --mamba-max-states-per-path 1` (+ `--radix-eviction-policy slru` unless `RADIX_EVICTION_POLICY` is set) |
| `KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1` | HiCache `file` backend below RAM, at `KV_OFFLOAD_DIR` (default: the repo's gitignored `kv-offload/`) |
| `KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB=<GiB>` | SGLang-only cap on the disk tier (LRU, split per GPU); a 20 GiB free-space floor is always set |

**2. dual-fast pair: `MAX_MAMBA_CACHE_SIZE` defaults to 20** (was auto-fit K=63; `=auto` restores it). The pool goes 451,633 → **548,520**, so **two full 262,144-token sessions stay resident at once**. dual-max keeps its pinned K=10.

**3. Stale-doc fix.** The "⛔ NO HiCache knob — sgl#33713" note in the other 19 SGLang composes, `docs/engines/SGLANG.md` and the `docs/UPSTREAM.md` #33713 row are corrected. HiCache works on the v0.5.20 pin; those slugs just aren't probed yet.

## Why HiCache looked broken

Stock SGLang backs up one SSM checkpoint per ~2,048 prompt tokens, and `--hicache-size` is split between host KV and host SSM in proportion to the device pools. At dual-fast's 451K pool, the host held only ~240 checkpoints, about 6 long sessions. Past that, LRU dropped a session's SSM state while its KV stayed on host, so the prefix could never match again. `--mamba-max-states-per-path 1` cuts a session to ~3 checkpoints. Flag set credit: @A1RM4X (#1340). The #39342 patch and `--enable-mixed-chunk` are **not** needed for HiCache.

## Validation (2× 3090, TP=2, v0.5.20)

| test | result |
|---|---|
| dual-fast, 12 × 40K needle sessions pushed off the GPU by 500K of fillers | **12/12 served from host**, 0.3–3.1 s vs 26 s cold, including extended turns and c2 pairs |
| fidelity: host hit vs GPU hit, same prefix | **bit-identical**, 6/6 greedy text + first-token logprobs |
| verify-full (knob on) | ✅ all checks, vision 4/4 |
| bench (knob on vs off) | flat: decode, prefill, MTP accept len 3.17 vs 3.25 |
| host RAM | +74 GiB at `KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64`, fully released on stop, no `/dev/shm` growth |
| disk tier | a session written before `docker restart` came back from disk in **4.74 s** vs 26.7 s cold; the cap held at 1.43 of 1.5 GiB per GPU |
| dual-max (fp8, K=10) | 4/4 host hits, host vs GPU 4/4 identical, 0 errors |
| **K=20, c2 at full context** | two concurrent 261,948 / 261,943-token prompts: both needles ✅. Re-sent with HiCache **off**, both served from the GPU (261,888 cached each), peak pool 96%, 0 errors, 0 retractions |
| K=20 vs K=63 bench | MTP 3.12 vs 3.17, decode/prefill within the boot-to-boot floor, headroom 1.48 vs 1.47 GB, VRAM 23,159 / 22,852 MiB |

Guards: `test-kv-offload-knob` extended to 5 vLLM + 4 SGLang composes (every knob combination, bad inputs refused, K seam, registry ↔ compose sync). 21/21 Tier-0 + diff-area guards pass. Three `tools/serve-cockpit` `test_services.py` cases fail identically on unmodified master in this environment, so they're not caused by this PR.

## Not in this PR

- **ThinkingCap replicas** are mirrored from their siblings (same compose apart from weights, name and port) and not booted separately.
- **DFlash2 (`superfast`) and multi4/multi8:** HiCache not probed; their notes say so.
- **sgl#38147** (share the MTP draft's embed/lm_head) was tested and not vendored. At `MEM_FRACTION` 0.95 the reclaimed memory is the engine's runtime scratch: OOM in graph capture, or on the first prefill's Triton autotune.
- ⚠️ The `file` backend writes about one file per token per GPU, all root-owned (documented).

body:
## Problem

The interconnect diagnostics understood the club `[nvlink]` trail and vLLM vetoes, but not SGLang's runtime evidence. As a result, a healthy SGLang boot could initialize NCCL and its custom all-reduce communicator while `bench.sh` still reported layer 3 as unknown. The config fingerprint also missed SGLang's KV dtype.

Fixes #1414.

## What changed

- add one shared ordered-log normalizer used by both `bench.sh` and `report.sh`
- recognize SGLang's NCCL initialization (`sglang is using nccl==...`)
- treat `All Reduce config:` as proof that CustomAllReduceV2 initialized
- keep `disable_custom_all_reduce=False` as a request only, not engagement proof
- classify SGLang operator disables, P2P failures, and topology vetoes
- slice evidence at the latest normalized SGLang boot marker so restarts cannot leak stale success or veto lines
- read the current SGLang KV dtype from the latest `server_args` dump, with the allocation log as fallback

## Live validation

Against `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20` on the running dual-card Qwen3.8 compose:

```text
KV cache type  : fp8_e4m3 (source: SGLang server_args)
layer 2  NCCL use         : initialized — sglang is using nccl==2.30.7; P2P policy: engine default (no NCCL_P2P*/NVLINK_MODE override)
layer 3  engine custom-AR : custom-AR OFF (operator), P2P LIVE — --disable-custom-all-reduce / DISABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE=1. Peer transfers still go via NCCL. Healthy, deliberate
```

The enabled fixture uses the pinned image's successful runtime line and classifies it as engaged only after:

```text
All Reduce config: symmetric_memory = ...
```

## Tests

- `bash scripts/tests/test-p2p-state.sh`
- `bash scripts/tests/test-bench-capture.sh`
- `bash scripts/tests/test-report-engine-liveness.sh`
- `bash scripts/tests/test-report-exit-code.sh`
- `bash scripts/tests/test-report-resolved-config.sh` — 57/0
- Tier-0 tree-wide guards
- `bash -n` on all edited shell files
- `git diff --check`
- live zero-run `bench.sh` capture against the SGLang container

## Impact / trade-off

No serving flags, request behavior, throughput, VRAM, or compose files change, so verify-full/stress and TPS A/B are N/A. This only improves diagnostics. The parser intentionally keys on runtime strings emitted by the pinned SGLang image and preserves exact fallback output when those strings are absent.

Closes the exposure decision in #1264. One line per SGLang compose, next to its existing `--mamba-ssm-dtype` knob, mirroring that seam's interpolation (`"${MAMBA_RADIX_CACHE_STRATEGY:-auto}"`, single-`$` compose-time form) and delivery:

```
--mamba-ssm-dtype "${MAMBA_SSM_DTYPE:-bfloat16}" \
--mamba-radix-cache-strategy "${MAMBA_RADIX_CACHE_STRATEGY:-auto}" \
```

**All 24 SGLang composes** — the 13 `qwen3.8-27b` + the 11 `thinkingcap-qwen3.8-27b` replicas from #1395, so the replicas don't drift from their siblings. `auto` is the engine default and resolves to `extra_buffer` on both rigs (2×3090 reference — issue thread; 2×5090 WRX80 — this PR's boot test), so the shipped default is a no-op against today's resolved args. The pointer comment sits **above `exec python3`**, not in the arg list: a `#` line inside a backslash-continued command breaks the continuation (verified: the next flag becomes a stray `command not found`, rc=127), and it points at the header k/r note + `docs/engines/SGLANG.md` rather than restating the table.

## `no_buffer` guard (per maintainer review) — `c2410c80`

`no_buffer` is not standalone-reachable on these composes: v0.5.20 `mamba_hook.py` asserts `disable_overlap_schedule` for it, and these composes run overlap schedule ON. Rather than auto-pairing the flag (a throughput trade we haven't measured), the entrypoint now validates the value where these composes already check their knobs — same compose-time form, so it sees exactly what the flag receives:

```bash
case "${MAMBA_RADIX_CACHE_STRATEGY:-auto}" in
  auto|extra_buffer|extra_buffer_lazy) : ;;
  no_buffer) echo "[mrcs] …needs --disable-overlap-schedule, which these composes do not expose; use auto, extra_buffer, or extra_buffer_lazy" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  *) echo "[mrcs] …must be auto, extra_buffer, or extra_buffer_lazy" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
```

`auto`/`extra_buffer`/`extra_buffer_lazy` pass; `no_buffer` and any other value hard-fail with a readable first line (boot-tested the `no_buffer` leg through `switch.sh` → exits 1 with the `[mrcs]` line, not the engine assertion). A genuine `no_buffer` opt-in can set both flags together later.

## `lazy` data point (item 3) — balanced ABBA, 4 fresh boots

Per #1323 the strategy moves both K and the pool; the pool alone can't show slots-vs-bytes, so this captures both. `sgl/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-superfast` dflash2, 2×5090, v0.5.20:

| | `extra_buffer` (default) | `extra_buffer_lazy` |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| `max_mamba_cache_size` (K) | 60 | 51 |
| KV pool (tok) | ~500K | ~509–515K |
| mamba slots / running-req | 4 | 3 |
| code decode TPS | 388.5 | 411.3 (+5.9%) |
| narrative decode TPS | 212.9 | 218.1 (null) |

Per-slot SSM size is identical (~36 MB); the strategy only moves memory between the pools. **Lazy shrinks K (60→51) but drops per-request cost (4→3)** → mamba-dimension concurrency capacity up (15 → 17, derived) and +5.9% code decode (both lazy boots above both extra_buffer boots). Narrative + prefill within the ~2.8% boot noise. Log: `1264-lazy-ab-20260925-0803.log`.

## Verification

- Boot read-backs: unset → `extra_buffer` (no-op), `extra_buffer_lazy` → override lands, `no_buffer` → guard fires (log: `1264-strategy-seam-boot-test.log`; script `tools/1264-strategy-seam-boot-test.sh`, untracked)
- `verify-full.sh` on the restored default container: **PASS**
- Scoped guards green: every re-derived Tier-0 tree-wide guard + `test-compose-registry-disk` + `test-launch-compat` + `test-profiles-compat`

_The `test-bench-capture` fix that surfaced while running the scoped guards has been split to its own PR — **#1422** — a standalone test fix with no dependency on this seam._

body:
Two fixes for RAM that stays resident in the **host `/dev/shm`** after containers stop. Our composes use `ipc: host`, so engine shared memory lands in the host's `/dev/shm`, and files there are held in RAM until they're deleted. With nothing running, the reference rig had **65 GB** resident.

### 1. KV offload disk mode leaked its whole RAM tier ([vllm#57303](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57303))
With `KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1` (#1408), vLLM's `TieringOffloadingSpec` keeps its RAM tier, `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_<engine_id>.mmap`, **named** until a graceful `cleanup()`. `docker restart`, or a `docker stop` whose grace period expires, kills vLLM before cleanup runs, so every such stop leaked `KV_OFFLOAD_GB` (2 × 32 GiB after the #1408 disk test). The RAM-only spec doesn't have this problem: it unlinks the name as soon as every worker has mapped the region.

**Workaround** in the 5 dual MTP composes, disk mode only:
- pin `engine_id=club3090-$HOSTNAME`, so the container knows its own region's path;
- remove that region at start if a previous run of this container left it behind;
- unlink the name once `/health` answers. By then every worker has mapped it, and the mappings stay valid, so the kernel frees the tier however the process exits. This is the same approach vLLM already uses for RAM-only.

vLLM may log one harmless "Failed to unlink" at a graceful shutdown. **Drop trigger:** #57303 fixed in a pinned release. It's recorded in `docs/UPSTREAM.md` on the #1327 row.

### 2. Pre-boot cleanup of orphaned engine segments
`switch.sh` now runs the new `scripts/lib/shm-cleanup.sh` before every `compose up`. It removes leftover `psm_*` / `sgl_*` / `sglang_*` / `torch_*` / `sem.mp-*` / `vllm_offload_*.mmap` files, but only when a file meets **all** of these conditions:
- it is **root-owned**, meaning a container created it;
- it is **older than 5 minutes**, so a peer container that is still booting is never raced;
- **no live process maps it or holds it open**, checked against host `/proc` from a short alpine container with `--pid=host` and `SYS_PTRACE`.

It uses a helper image already present on the machine (pulling `alpine:3` only as a fallback), never fails a boot, and can be disabled with `CLUB3090_SHM_CLEANUP=0`.

### Live validation
dual-fast, `KV_OFFLOAD_GB=32 KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1`, run through `switch.sh`:

| Step | Named regions | Shared RAM |
|---|--:|--:|
| an orphan was planted before boot (root-owned, backdated 30 min) | — | removed by `switch.sh`: `[shm] removed 1 orphaned engine shared-memory segment(s)` |
| boot 1 serving (region unlinked once serving) | 0 | 32 GB (live tier) |
| **right after `docker restart`** | **0** | **0 GB** (previously a 32 GiB leak) |
| boot 2 serving | 0 | 32 GB |
| A after the restart | — | **2.36 s** from disk (81,408 tokens; 2.41 s before the fix) |
| **after `docker stop`** | **0** | **0 GB** |

### Tests
- **New `test-shm-cleanup.sh`** runs the real helper on a scratch directory seeded with one file per rule:
  - removed: 2 genuine orphans;
  - kept: a too-new file, two files held open by a live container process, a user-owned file and a non-engine file;
  - `CLUB3090_SHM_CLEANUP=0` is honoured, and `switch.sh` calls the helper before `compose up`.
- **Negative controls, each red:** the in-use check removed; the root-owner rule removed; the age rule removed; the cleanup moved to after `compose up`.
- **`test-kv-offload-knob`** now also checks that disk mode pins a `club3090-` engine ID and keeps both the stale-region removal and the unlink after `/health`.
- Tier 0 plus the compose, `switch.sh` and knob guards: **29/29 pass**.

The c3 catalog's **act** column showed `16bit` for the SGLang AutoRound tiers, but they have served **int8 activations (W4A8) by default since 2026-09-19**. Their entrypoint reads `"${W4A8:-1}"` ("DEFAULT-ON since 2026-09-19 (was 0)"), while the registry and the compose headers were never updated.

### What was stale
| Where | Said | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `registry.yaml` `act_format` on 12 slugs: `sgl/{qwen38,thinkingcap38}-27b-{dual,multi4,multi8}-{fast,superfast}` | `16bit` | `int8` |
| Header W4A8 paragraph in 13 composes (the 12 above + the unregistered `dual/autoround-int4/dflash2-bf16.yml`) | "OPT-IN … It is OFF by default because…" | **ON BY DEFAULT since 2026-09-19**, `W4A8=0` reverts. It now cites the entrypoint's repeat-boot trade (+49% prefill@10K, −8.4% narrative / −5.5% code decode), which supersedes the 2026-09-11 single-boot read. |
| Entrypoint label in the same 13 files | `# --- W4A8 opt-in (patch …; not vendored here) ---` | `# --- W4A8 (…patch, vendored + mounted; DEFAULT ON, W4A8=0 reverts) ---` |

**Untouched on purpose:** the SGLang **fp8** tiers (`max` / `supermax`) default `W4A8` to 0. Their `16bit` value and "opt-in" wording are correct.

**c3 behaviour:** the SGLang slugs keep `act8_capable: false`, so the serve-confirm int8 toggle stays hidden for them; that toggle drives vLLM's `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE`. Only the column text changes.

### New guard: `test-act-format-drift.sh`
It derives each slug's default activation format from its **compose** and asserts the registry `act_format` matches. It reads the compose in one of four ways:
1. **W4A8 gate** `{W4A8:-N}` (vLLM env line or SGLang entrypoint): 1 → int8, 0 → 16bit.
2. **Hard-coded** `- VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8`: int8.
3. **Bare** `- VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` passthrough (opt-in): 16bit.
4. **No knob**: 16bit.

It also rejects the old "OPT-IN / OFF by default" wording on any gate that defaults ON, and fails if one compose's own W4A8 defaults disagree with each other.

- **On a copy of master:** 48 failures, which is 12 slugs × (the registry value + 3 stale phrases).
- **On this branch:** green across 168 slugs, 40 of them read via a W4A8 gate.
- **Negative controls, all red:** one slug set back to `16bit`; the stale title restored; an SGLang gate flipped to 0; a vLLM gate flipped to 0; a gate disagreeing with itself.

### Gates
- Tier 0 plus the registry, compose, SGLang, parity and knob guards: **30/30 pass**.
- `migrate_registry_to_yaml.py --check`: canonical.
- c3 `test_services` + `test_registry_parser`: 265 passed, with the same 11 pre-existing failures as master.

vLLM **v0.30.0** fixed native KV offload for hybrid GDN models running MTP. On v0.29.0 the RAM tier stored blocks but never served them back ([disc #1327](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/discussions/1327)). This PR adds an **opt-in** knob, off by default, to the five Qwen3.8-family **dual MTP** composes:

| Slug | Compose |
|---|---|
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` | `qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/dual/autoround-int4/mtp.yml` |
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-max` | `qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/dual/fp8/mtp.yml` |
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-nvfp4` | `qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/dual/nvfp4/mtp.yml` |
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-fast` | `thinkingcap-qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/dual/autoround-int4/mtp.yml` |
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-max` | `thinkingcap-qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/dual/fp8/mtp.yml` |

### The knob
```bash
KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64 bash scripts/switch.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast                                   # RAM tier
KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64 KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1 bash scripts/switch.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast                 # + disk tier
KV_OFFLOAD_GB=64 KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1 KV_OFFLOAD_DIR=/mnt/nvme/kv bash scripts/switch.sh ...            # disk elsewhere
```
- **`KV_OFFLOAD_GB`**: GiB of host RAM, **total across both GPUs**. It maps to `--kv-offloading-size` on vLLM's native `OffloadingConnector`. The RAM is pinned at boot. Size it above the GPU pool (~36 KiB/token), or it only mirrors what the GPU already holds.
- **`KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1`**: adds a disk tier below RAM (`TieringOffloadingSpec` + `fs`), mounted at `/kv-offload`. The default host directory is the gitignored `kv-offload/`; override it with **`KV_OFFLOAD_DIR`** in `.env`. The tier survives restarts and model swaps. ⚠️ vLLM's `fs` tier has **no size cap** and writes root-owned files.
- vLLM rejects any KV connector while `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` is set, so the entrypoint drops that setting when offload is on. **Side effect:** the GPU pool also grew in both offload boots: 549,063 → 591,422 on dual-fast and 345,075 → 365,766 on superfast. The cause isn't isolated, so no claim is made here.
- The tier **never enlarges the GPU pool or concurrency**. Prompt blocks are copied down as they're computed, and a returning prefix the GPU has dropped reloads instead of being re-prefilled.

### Measured (2×3090, TP=2, 32 GiB, forced-eviction probe)
| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `dual-fast`, RAM | 80K prompt **59.4 s cold → 1.51 s** after 700K tokens of fillers evicted it from the GPU. 78,864 tokens loaded from RAM (`external_prefix_cache_hits`). |
| `dual-fast`, RAM + disk | **61.9 s cold → 2.41 s** after a container restart, which empties the GPU and RAM tiers. 2,816 MiB read from disk. |
| `dual-fast`, verify-full | 9/9 checks pass with offload on (Genesis check skipped as usual); MTP acceptance length 2.65. |
| `dual-superfast` (DFlash2) | **Write-only:** stores everything, 0 external hits, 58.8 s after eviction, the same as a fresh cold prompt (58.7 s). |

### Deliberately excluded
- **DFlash tiers:** closest upstream match is [vllm#47890](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47890). That's the re-test trigger, now recorded in `docs/UPSTREAM.md`.
- **`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`:** open TP=2 engine-wedge report, [vllm#53868](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53868).
- **LMCache:** planned as a separate container service later, so its KV survives model swaps.
- **multi4 / multi8:** their GPU pools are already large.

### c3
A new registry facet, `kv_offload` (`null` / `"opt-in"`), is carried through `registry-emit.sh --json`. The catalog **offload** column shows **`kv opt`** when a slug's weights stay on the GPU but the compose has the knob. Weight placement (`static` / `dynamic`) still takes priority.

### Guards
- New **`test-kv-offload-knob.sh`** checks:
  - the entrypoint block resolves correctly in each case: off, RAM, RAM + disk;
  - 5 malformed inputs fail the boot;
  - the default and override mount paths render;
  - no DFlash compose carries the knob;
  - the registry `kv_offload` matches the compose knob exactly.
- **Negative controls:** six deliberate breakages each turned the guard red:
  - `OFFLOAD_ARGS` dropped from a second exec branch;
  - a broken passthrough;
  - the knob leaking onto a DFlash compose;
  - a bad value being accepted;
  - offload on by default;
  - the disk tier pointed at the wrong directory.
- **Other guards:** Tier 0 plus the compose, registry and emit guards all pass, 32 in total, including `test-registry-json` (key set updated), `test-registry-yaml-roundtrip`, `test-pytest-modules` and the switch/launch parity tests.
- **c3:** `test_services` + `test_registry_parser` give 265 passed. The 11 failures are identical on untouched master; this PR adds one passing test.

Follow-up to #1406. Extends the `MAMBA_SSM_CACHE_DTYPE` knob (default `bfloat16`) to the **24 Qwen3.8 / ThinkingCap DFlash composes**: dual, multi4 and multi8 × autoround-int4 and fp8 × `dflash2` and `dflash2-fp8`.

### Why
For Qwen3.5-family models, vLLM copies the HF config's `mamba_ssm_dtype` (float32) into `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` whenever that is `auto`. The DFlash composes had no SSM knob, so their SSM state was fp32. DFlash keeps more SSM snapshots per request than MTP (spec depth 7), so the saving is larger than on the MTP tiers.

### Measured: `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-superfast`, vLLM v0.30.0

| SSM state | KV pool | ÷ 262K | attention block |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| fp32 (master) | 284,010 tok | 1.08× | 1,648 |
| **bf16 (this PR)** | **345,075 tok** | **1.32×** | 880 |

**+21.5% pool.** For comparison, dual-fast (MTP) gained 5.3% from bf16 SSM alone in #1406. The boot log confirms the override took effect: `mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' in its config, but --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype='bfloat16' was passed`.

**verify-full on bf16: all checks pass.** Tool calls, streaming and streaming tool calls, thinking, the 2K-token quality/cascade check, vision 4/4, and DFlash acceptance length 3.73.

### Changes
- Each of the 24 composes gets:
  - `MAMBA_SSM_CACHE_DTYPE` declared in `environment:`;
  - a `MAMBA_ARGS` block, the same shape as the MTP composes, that echoes `[mamba] ssm cache dtype <dt>`;
  - `"${MAMBA_ARGS[@]}"` added to **every** `exec vllm serve` line. 10 composes have two exec branches, and both carry it.
- `test-mamba-ssm-knob.sh` now:
  - covers all 38 non-archive Qwen3.8-family vLLM composes (was 14);
  - adds a delivery check that every exec line count equals the `MAMBA_ARGS` count.

  Negative controls, each red then restored:
  - drop `MAMBA_ARGS` from a second exec branch;
  - remove the env passthrough;
  - revert the default to `:-auto`.
- Revert with `MAMBA_SSM_CACHE_DTYPE=float32` or `auto`.

### Not in this PR (flagged, not edited)
The `dual/autoround-int4/dflash2.yml` headers (Qwen3.8 + ThinkingCap) quote `fp8 KV pool 421,970 tok = 1.61×`, which was measured with fp32 SSM. The bf16 default should raise it, but it was not re-measured here.

### Gates
Tier 0 plus compose-area guards: 25/25 pass, including `test-mamba-ssm-knob`, `test-compose-status-drift`, `test-launch-compat`, `test-profiles-compat` and `test-compose-mounts-resolve`.

body:
## The bug
`bench.sh`'s last command was the #1076 restart check:

```bash
[[ "${_RESTART_RC:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 90
```

As the script's **final** command, that `&&` list's status becomes bench.sh's exit code, and it's **1 whenever the engine did not restart**. Since `39343b46` (2026-09-20) two cases have exited 1:
- **every clean bench**;
- **every bench against a container-less endpoint** (the guard can't check, so it reports "unavailable").

**Impact:** `report.sh --bench/--full` passes that exit code to `stage_record`. So every clean bench in a community rig report rendered **FAIL**, and the whole report escalated to exit 1 ("hard failure"). `rebench-full.sh` hid it with `|| true`.

Found during today's llama.cpp v0.5.0 boot test: the bench completed with every section populated and still exited 1.

## The fix
The check is now an `if` block, the shape `quality-test.sh` already uses for the same guard.

## Tests
Nothing caught this because the `BENCH_MOCK` path skips the whole block.

`test-engine-restart-guard` gains **leg 8**. It extracts bench.sh's **real** tail (from the #1076 marker to EOF) and runs it under bench.sh's own `set -euo pipefail`, with the guard stubbed to each verdict:

| guard verdict | this PR | master (negative control) |
|---|---|---|
| clean (0) | exit **0** | exit 1 ✗ |
| unavailable (2) | exit **0** | exit 1 ✗ |
| restarted (1) | exit **90** | exit 90 |

**Live check:** on the same booted engine (`llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs`), `bench.sh --quick` exits **1 from master** and **0 with this change**.

**Guards:** the Tier 0 set, the 3 bench tests, `test-engine-restart-guard`, `test-locale-utf8` and `test-script-permissions`: **17/17**.

## Summary

Serve Agents-A1 using its checkpoint-native BF16 dtype instead of casting it to FP16.

Under vLLM v0.30.0, this model boots normally and returns HTTP 200 with FP16, but its logits are corrupted: deterministic chat and raw completion repeat `duct`, while sampled prose repeats `!` until the token limit. Changing only the dtype to BF16 restores coherent output.

This is intentionally scoped to the confirmed Agents-A1 compose. It does not modify the unverified Qwen3.6 candidates discussed in #1393.

## Diagnosis

- Verified the 37.7 GB checkpoint against Hugging Face SHA-256.
- Reproduced corruption through both chat and raw completion APIs.
- Ruled out the NVLink custom-all-reduce interaction: FP16 remains corrupted with `DISABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE=1`.
- Restored BF16 with custom all-reduce enabled; deterministic chat returns `Paris` with `finish_reason=stop`.

Full reproduction and the custom-all-reduce split test are in #1393.

## Validation

On 2x RTX 3090 with vLLM v0.30.0:

- `scripts/verify.sh`: 4/4 passed
- `scripts/verify-full.sh`: 10/10 passed
- `scripts/verify-stress.sh`: 8/8 passed
  - ceiling ladder passed through 240,660 tokens (91% of 262,144)
- Targeted compose/catalog compatibility guards passed
- Mandatory tree-wide guards passed

Addresses the confirmed Agents-A1 portion of #1393; the broader audit remains separate.

## Why
The Step-Audio-EditX node's `requirements.txt` pins only `transformers` (4.53.3, since 4.54+ produces silent audio) and `gradio`, and floors everything else. The Dockerfile's extra install line floors nothing. So every fresh build of the voice image silently resolved **newer** dependencies than the image we validated. The no-cache rebuild for #1400 differed from it in **32 packages**: `onnxruntime` 1.26→1.30, `accelerate` 1.14→1.15, `numba` 0.65→0.67, and more.

- **Both `pip install` steps now pass `-c constraints.txt`.** That fixes versions and installs nothing extra.
- **Base-image packages aren't listed.** The `FROM` tag fixes them, and some freeze as `@ file://` paths a constraints file can't express. Today's base tag still matches the June image package for package.

|---|---|
| no-cache build **without** constraints (for #1400) | **32 packages differ** |

body:
Closes #1394.

The **`Saganaki22` GitHub account is gone**: the user and both of its repos return 404. Two AI Studio lanes cloned from it, and both break on a **fresh** install:

| Lane | Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🎙️ Voice (Step-Audio-EditX) | `services/studio/step-voice/Dockerfile` | image build fails at the clone | tries 2 forks in order, checks out the **same pinned SHA** `d8eddc66`, fails loudly if none has it |
| 🖼️ HiDream-O1 image | `services/comfyui/entrypoint.sh` | `git clone` of a dead URL under `set -e`, so **all of ComfyUI** stops | new `clone_pinned`: pinned to the last upstream commit `1f1dd545` (it used to track the tip), fetched from forks only when missing, warns and continues if unreachable |

A commit SHA names exact content, so any fork that still carries the pin yields byte-identical source. Existing installs were unaffected. On the maintainer rig the break was invisible, because a rebuild reused the cached clone layer.

## Verification
- **Forks, clone-verified.** Step: `FloyoAI` and `mrlzla`, tree `b66262a6`, the same tree as the image we validated. HiDream: `d01` and `yuanjun55`, tree `dcef1f00`, the same as this rig's clone.
- **Voice lane, real delivery path.**
  - `docker build --no-cache` cloned from FloyoAI and landed on HEAD `d8eddc66`, tree `b66262a6`.
  - In a throwaway container on GPU1, the model loaded in 20 s. `/clone` produced **4.2 s of 24 kHz speech** (RMS 0.15, peak 0.91), so it's not the silent-audio failure mode. `transformers` is still 4.53.3.
  - ⚠️ The Dockerfile's unpinned pip deps have drifted since the original build: `onnxruntime` 1.26→1.30, `accelerate` 1.14→1.15, `numba` and others. That's pre-existing, not from this PR, and the smoke test shows it still works.
- **HiDream lane, `clone_pinned` run live against the forks.**
  - Fresh install → tree `dcef1f00`.
  - A **copy** of this rig's existing clone keeps its HEAD and gets its origin repointed to the fork. After the entrypoint's compat-patch step, its working tree is **byte-identical** to the rig's live tree.
- **New guard `test-comfyui-clone-pinned`** (offline; runs the real function text extracted from the entrypoint, under its own `set -euo pipefail`). It covers five cases:
  1. fresh install past a dead mirror and one that lacks the SHA;
  2. already at the pin with every mirror dead: no network needed, and the local patch is reset;
  3. a shallow clone at an older commit moves to the pin;
  4. no mirror has it: WARN and continue;
  5. a pre-existing non-git directory is never deleted.

  **Negative controls** each turned it red: a fatal exit, `rm -rf` on a failed clone, and skipping the reset on the fast path.
- **Guards:** Tier 0 plus `test-comfyui-paths`, `test-script-permissions`, `test-locale-utf8`: **16/16**.

Credit stays with the original author in the entrypoint comment, `download_hidream_o1.sh` and `docs/ai-studio/image.md`. Both nodes are open-licensed (HiDream MIT, Step Apache-2.0).

body:
Follow-up to #1396 / #1398, found while building `run_context.py`.

## The bug
`report.sh`'s **Engine-resolved values** section shortens SGLang's one-line startup dump to a list of keys. The pattern it used only understood the `server_args=ServerArgs(key=value, ...)` shape that SGLang ≤ v0.5.19 logs. **v0.5.20 logs a Python dict**, `server_args={'key': value, ...}`, so nothing matched. Every SGLang v0.5.20 rig report therefore showed `server_args (elided to 0 keys; …)`, an empty block that reads like a successful capture. No test ever fed a boot log, so nothing noticed.

## The fix
- `resolved_config.py` now parses the dict shape exactly: a quote-aware balanced-brace scan plus `ast.literal_eval`, never `eval`. Because it doesn't pattern-match, a nested dict that reuses a key name can't be mistaken for the top-level value. The older `ServerArgs(...)` shape still uses the existing pattern.
- The parser (`dict_after`) moves here from `run_context.py` (#1398), which now imports it. That leaves **one** parser for the SGLang and vLLM dumps instead of two copies that could drift.

## Tests
New leg **2h** in `test-report-resolved-config.sh` feeds both dump shapes through the real `docker logs` read path. The v0.5.20 fixture plants a nested `tp_size: 99` **before** the top-level `tp_size: 2`.

| Arm | Result |
|---|---|
| this PR | **57/57** |
| negative control: master's parser | 5 failures, all on the dict assertions (`elided to 0 keys`); the `ServerArgs` assertions stay green |
| negative control: a naive regex over the dict text | 2 failures: it reports the nested `tp_size=99` |

Pending: a parse of a real v0.5.20 boot log, `test-run-context`, and the Tier 0 guards. I'll post the results here.

Part of #1396, item 1 (sampling and topology in the report format). The benchlocal-cli side is noonghunna/benchlocal-cli#165, which also fixes item 2 (HermesAgent token counts).

## What changes
`quality-test.sh` now records the rig and the sampling in effect with every run, whenever it can see the serving container:

```
[quality-test] rig (vllm): engine=vllm 0.30.0 · tp=2 · pp=1 · quant=auto_round · kv=fp8_e4m3 · max_ctx=262144 · spec=dflash n=7 · gpus=2x RTX 3090 · power_cap=230 W · pcie=gen4 x16 / gen4 x8 · nvlink=no
[quality-test] sampling: server defaults resolved from the vllm boot log (recorded with the results)
```

- **Results JSON:** gains `run_meta` and `server_defaults_source`.
- **Summary header and Results Card:** gain `Rig:` and `Sampling:` lines, for example `Sampling: server defaults — temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, repetition_penalty=1.0, presence_penalty=0.0, frequency_penalty=0.0 (supplied: vLLM effective defaults (generation_config.json + --override-generation-config))`.
- **The compose `Quality:` one-liner:** gains a `tp=N` stamp.

## It reports what the engine applies, not what we told it
The obvious implementation reads the flags we pass. That would be wrong on both engines:

| Engine | Read from | Why not the flag |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `Default vLLM sampling parameters have been overridden by …` | vLLM filters `--override-generation-config` to `repetition_penalty/temperature/top_k/top_p/min_p` first, so a compose's `presence_penalty` never applies |
| SGLang | `Using default chat sampling params from model generation config:` plus the chat adapter's fallbacks | `--preferred-sampling-params` is inert on `/v1/chat/completions` (sglang#39096): the adapter fills every key before the merge. Checked against v0.5.20's own classes; our SGLang composes already note it |
| both | `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` = 0.0 | both chat adapters hard-default them, so only a client can change them |
| llama.cpp | not touched | benchlocal-cli reads `GET /props` |

How it's wired:
- The engine family comes from `engine-kind.sh` (#1282). `run_context.py` takes it as `--engine` and never classifies.
- On `--resume`, nothing is re-read, because the journal keeps the first session's values.
- With a benchlocal-cli older than #165, the wrapper prints a one-line upgrade warning and runs exactly as before.

## Validation
- `test-run-context` (new) has 8 legs. Every fixture makes the flag differ from what the engine applies. **Negative controls** each turned it red:
  - reading the vLLM override;
  - honouring SGLang's preferred params;
  - treating `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` as host indices;
  - dropping the `--resume` guard;
  - not passing the args.
  One control first exposed a leg that couldn't discriminate (the override and the effective line agreed); I fixed the fixture before trusting it.
- `test-quality-card` has a new `tp=4` case, also negative-controlled.
- **Real engines:** parsed real boot logs from vLLM v0.30.0 (TP=2 DFlash) and SGLang v0.5.20 (TP=2 DFLASH). Fed the arguments emitted from the real vLLM container to the benchlocal-cli #165 branch; it accepted all 24, and the header, `rig:` line and card came out as above.
- **Guards:** Tier 0 tree-wide set plus `test-locale-utf8`, `test-script-permissions`, `test-report-resolved-config`, `test-quality-card`, `test-run-context`: 17/17 green.

Merge after benchlocal-cli#165. Until then the wrapper just prints the upgrade warning.

> ⚠️ **Pinned without a live boot.** Both GPUs are busy and the image wasn't pulled, so this deliberately breaks the engine's own "pin validated builds" rule. What was checked and what's still pending are both listed below. Don't read "merged" as "validated" for these slugs.

## What changed

- **Engine profile** (`engines/llama-cpp-mainline.yml`): `install.spec` points at the new digest. The notes gain the pin history, the unbooted warning, and the fact that upstream publishes versioned images again (`server-cuda-v0.5.0`, `server-cuda13-v0.5.0`). The pin stays a digest, because a tag can be re-pushed.
- **10 functional composes**: the image default moves to the new digest (`engine-pin-bump.sh`). The 19 deprecated composes keep their pins.
- **The same 10 composes' `Engine:` header lines**: these were already stale before this PR (they still said b10236 or b9570 after the b10920 bump). They now point at the engine profile instead of restating a build number.
- **`patches.yml`**: MiMo's Qwen3-Coder template workaround (#1387) now meets its drop condition, because v0.5.0 carries `bfd73a876` (ggml-org#29257). It **stays wired** until the CLI-21 first-turn probe runs on v0.5.0 without it.
- **`docs/UPSTREAM.md`**: engine-pin row.

## Patches

There's nothing to re-validate:
- The engine is overlay-free (`vendored_overlays: []`).
- MiMo's template is the only compose-level patch on it.
- `arch_patches.yml` has no llama.cpp `engine_pin` rows (that gate is vLLM-only), and `resolve-variant-pin` accepts all 10 slugs on the new pin.

## Dry run (no GPU, no image pull)

- All 10 composes render (`docker compose config`) with the new digest.
- The resolver accepts all 10 slugs; none are refused.
- Guard suite: **187/187 passed**, which is the full `for t in scripts/tests/*.sh` sweep minus two tests. Those two are skipped because they run containers: `test-compose-flags-accepted` runs `llama-server --help` inside the pinned image, and `test-p2p-validate`.

## Pending before trusting it

1. Run `test-compose-flags-accepted` on the pulled image. It catches any flag our composes pass that v0.5.0 renamed or removed.
2. Boot, verify-full and bench each of these at the **same 230 W cap as its baseline**, one fresh boot per bench:
   - `llamacpp/deckard40B-dual-mtp` and `llamacpp/tess-dual-mtp` (production);
   - `llamacpp/mimo9b-single-vision`: the CLI-21 probe without the patch should end `finish=tool_calls`; if it does, drop the patch;
   - `llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs`: #28549 turns on CUDA graphs for MTP drafting, which can change decode speed and VRAM on this slug's tight 215K ceiling.
3. DeepSeek offload ×3: the 2026-08-09 drafter-placement note applies. None of these composes sets `-devd`, and ggml-org#26475 is still open.

## Inherited from v0.5.0 (worth measuring)

- The MiMo tool-call fix.
- #28549, CUDA graphs for MTP drafting.
- Qwen3-Coder parser fixes.
- #27380, sampler environment variables. None of them collide with the `LLAMA_ARG_*` names our composes set.

Not included: DFlash2 (#27342 was merged into a feature branch only) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MTP (#27836 and #28243 are still open).

body:
Adds **ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B**, bottlecapai's reasoning fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B (released 2026-09-23), as a new model with **29 🧪 experimental slugs**. Each is a one-to-one copy of an existing Qwen3.8 slug.

Its `text_config` and chat template are identical to Qwen3.8-27B's, so the existing Qwen3.8 composes serve it with only a weights swap.

## Weights

| Variant | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `autoround-int4` | **[wasifb/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-AutoRound-W4A16](https://huggingface.co/wasifb/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-AutoRound-W4A16)** (ours, gated auto-approve) | Upstream has no INT4 AutoRound, and the W4A8 fast/superfast/ultrafast tiers need one. Built with the Tess shot-2 recipe: W4A16 int4 g128 sym, `mtp.fc` BF16, 200 iterations, 512 samples, alg_ext. Its packed layout matches Frozenlock's Qwen3.8 INT4 tensor for tensor. |
| `fp8` | [bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-FP8](https://huggingface.co/bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) (gated) | Same format as the official Qwen FP8, except the whole MTP head stays BF16 (+0.37 GB; all 21 differing tensors are `mtp.*`). |
| `dflash2` / `dflash2-zlab` | the Qwen3.8 drafters | Same `local_subdir`, so they're shared on disk. |

## Slugs: `thinkingcap38-27b-<topology>-<tier>`, one per `qwen38-27b` sibling

- **15 on `autoround-int4`**: vLLM fast, superfast and ultrafast, plus SGLang fast and superfast, each on dual, multi4 and multi8.
- **14 on `fp8`**: vLLM max, supermax and ultramax on dual, multi4 and multi8; SGLang max on all three; SGLang supermax on multi4 and multi8.

**What changes from each sibling compose:**
- the weights path;
- the served name (`thinkingcap38-27b`, plus the `-fp8` alias);
- the service and container names;
- the port (8155–8179 and 8184–8187, inside the 8010–8199 product space);
- the three-level patch mounts, re-pointed at the `qwen3.8-27b` tree.

**The header's `Model` / `Status` / `Caveats` blocks are rewritten.** A replica banner says the rest of the header is the sibling's text and describes base Qwen3.8. Every slug ships 🧪 experimental, the same status as its Qwen3.8 sibling, with the gateway off and `kvcalc_key: SKIP` (the model id isn't wired into kv-calc yet).

## Catalog plumbing

- **`models/thinkingcap-qwen3.8-27b.yml`**: the architecture is copied verbatim from `qwen3.8-27b.yml`, since the `text_config` is identical. `kv_calc_supported` is false, and the setup primary is `autoround-int4`.
- **Drafters**: `qwen-mtp-builtin`, `syvai-qwen38-dflash2` and `zlab-qwen38-dflash2` add the model to `model_compat` (constraint C8).
- **Guard counts**:
  - registry entries 139 → 168;
  - compose files 142 → 171;
  - models 22 → 23;
  - the `sampler_profiles` prefix allowlist.
- **Docs**: regenerated DUAL_CARD / MULTI_CARD slug tables, a BENCHMARKS section and `models/thinkingcap-qwen3.8-27b/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Validation

2× 3090 PCIe at a 230 W cap, vLLM v0.30.0. Each arm is paired with a Frozenlock (base Qwen3.8) reference taken the same day:

| Slug | ThinkingCap narr / code | Frozenlock narr / code | Checks |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-fast` | 74.0 / 101.0 | 75.5 / 106.5 | MTP accept 3.6–5.0; a 20K-token forced generation held accept 2.7–4.0; through `switch.sh`, verify-full scored 9/10 (see below) |
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-superfast` | 80.0 / 157.6 | 84.0 / 154.0 (control) | verify-full passed through `switch.sh`; the base-trained DFlash2 drafter converts on the fine-tune |
| `vllm/thinkingcap38-27b-dual-ultrafast` | 108.3 / 198.9 | 108.8 / 191.5 · 111.1 / 196.6 | booted through `switch.sh`; verify-full passed; the FA2 fp8-KV plugin verified |

- **`diagnose-profile`**: valid on all three, 15/16. The 16th is the skipped kv-calc projection.
- **The `dual-fast` 9/10**: the one failure is verify-full's 2+2 reasoning-length heuristic. ThinkingCap reasoned *"The user wants a one-line answer to 2+2."*, which is 41 characters, under the check's 50-character floor. Thinking engaged and was extracted correctly; this is the fine-tune's token efficiency. At temperature 1.0 the check is a coin flip, and the equivalent scratch boot passed 10/10. Frozenlock's own slug records the same class of failure.
- **Guard suite**: the full `for t in scripts/tests/*.sh` sweep passed, **189/189**, on idle GPUs.

**Not covered:** the other 26 slugs (FP8 tiers, SGLang, multi-card) are unbooted, and the 8-pack quality run is pending. That's why everything stays 🧪 experimental.

## Also in this PR

- **Attribution fix for ThinkingCap on Qwen3.6:** the profile comment, model README and BENCHMARKS called it "LeaderboardModel1's". LeaderboardModel1 made the AutoRound quant; its card names `bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B` as the base.
- **Status:** by maintainer call, the slugs ship 🧪 experimental instead of the 🐣-first default for new models. The status-affected guards were re-run green.

## License

PolyForm Small Business 1.0.0 plus BottleCap's personal-use grant. This is **not** Apache-2.0, unlike ThinkingCap on Qwen3.6. Commercial use by an organization that isn't a small business needs a license from BottleCap. Every compose's `Caveats` line and the model profile say so.

Bumps the `vllm-stable` engine from `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` to **v0.30.0**.

This is a maintenance bump. It keeps the pin current so the vendored patches can be dropped as their upstream fixes land. **v0.30.0 inherits no fix we track:** #48375, #51581, #40756, #48904, #48905, #50021 and #51599 are all still open, so every vendored patch and every MTP caveat stays.

## What changed

- `engines/vllm-stable.yml`: `install.spec` and `display_name` set to v0.30.0. The 43 vllm-stable compose `:-` defaults are bumped to match (`engine-pin-bump.sh`). The Gemma and DiffusionGemma engines have their own profiles and are untouched.
- `arch_patches.yml`: adds `vllm-stable@v0.30.0 loads:true` ×18. The v0.29.0 rows stay as history.
- `test-launch-compat`: the pin assertions now expect v0.30.0.
- **Corrected a wrong note in the engine profile.** It said "VLLM_IMAGE override still works". That's true only for a direct `docker compose`. `switch.sh` and `launch.sh` re-resolve the image from `install.spec` and export it over any user-set `VLLM_IMAGE`. That is why the first A/B round for this bump silently ran v0.29.0 on every arm.
- Docs: the UPSTREAM engine-pin and engine-table rows, the ENGINE_FLAGS current pin plus a presence re-check, and BENCHMARKS rows.
- **Deliberately not rewritten:** v0.29.0 mentions that record where a measurement or citation came from (`baselines.yml`, `[vllm-help 0.29]`, the FA2 plugin's VALIDATION docs).

## Validation

**Patches.** Every load-bearing patch ran inside the real v0.30.0 image, and its anchors held:
- `qwen-w4a8-int8-act` (both files)
- `vllm-pr48375-mamba-drop-eagle-block`, which logs `applied`, so the bug is still in upstream's code
- `vllm-gdn-mtp-async-spec-order`
- `vllm-51581-dflash-dense-kv`
- `vllm-flashinfer-decode-pin` (flashinfer 0.6.18 → 0.6.18.post1; all 4 sites still present)

**FA2 fp8-KV plugin.** No rebuild is needed. torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0 and cp312 are identical in both images, and the plugin's metadata and KV-layout interface gate passes.

**Flags and env vars.** Every `--flag` and `VLLM_*` name the 43 composes use resolves in v0.30.0 (checked against `vllm serve --help=all` and `vllm.envs`). The only flag v0.30.0 removed, `--enable-bf16x3-router-gemm`, has no users. This checks presence only; defaults were not diffed.

**Live boots.** Each boot went through `switch.sh` from a bumped worktree. Every arm asserted both `docker inspect` (image) and the engine's `LLM engine (v0.30.0)` log line. One fresh boot per bench, on 2× 3090 PCIe at a 230 W cap:

| Slug | v0.29.0 narr / code | v0.30.0 narr / code | Prefill @10K / @90K |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast` | 110.0 / 199.9 · 110.3 / 200.8 | 108.8 / 191.5 · 111.1 / 196.6 | level (1,788–1,814 / 1,380–1,394 vs 1,798–1,801 / 1,371–1,383) |
| `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` | 76.2 / 101.9 | 75.5 / 106.5 | 1,710 / 1,266 vs 1,729 / 1,232 |

Code decode fell 3.2% on ultrafast (two-boot means) and rose 4.4% on dual-fast. The signs are opposite and both are inside this rig's boot-to-boot noise, so I read neither as a real change. The boots were not alternated. verify-full passed on every arm, with 0 restarts.

**Guard suite:** `for t in scripts/tests/*.sh` → **189 passed, 0 failed**.

## Not covered

Only the Qwen3-Next hybrid arch was booted. The Gemma-12B dual, 35B-A3B, AgentWorld, Nemotron, ThinkingCap and Tess composes were not. The other 17 `loads:true` rows are untested assertions, the same partial-validation call as #682 and #1272.

## Worth trying on this pin later (opt-in, not claimed)

- `disable_eagle_block_drop` (vllm#53388) and the new `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` flag, for prefix-cache hit rates on the MTP and DFlash2 slugs.
- FlashInfer all-reduce over PCIe (vllm#53576). A rig has to pass `p2p-validate.sh` first.

Promotes `llamacpp/mimo9b-single-vision` from 🧪 Experimental to **⚠️ Production w/ caveats**.

## Gates, all on the shipped config

The shipped config is Q8_0, q8_0 KV, `-ub 4096`, 262144 ctx and vision, with the vendored tool-call template (#1387).

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| verify-full | 7 pass, 2 N/A (vLLM-only checks), 1 known harness false-fail. `[7/10]` asserts reasoning on a trivial prompt, which is repo-wide for adaptive-thinking models. |
| verify-stress | ceiling ladder **6/6 to 240,785 tok (91% of 262,144)**, 6,629 MiB free and flat; boundary 5/5, recall 3/3 |
| bench | BENCHMARKS row: 53.69 / 50.88 decode, prefill 2359.7 @10K |
| soak-continuous | **PASS** on its own fresh boot: 25/25 turns, 0 MiB growth, retention 100% |
| 8-pack | thinking ON: **79/150 p@1, 94/150 p@3** (IF/SO packs v2.0.0) |

## Why "w/ caveats" and not ✅

These four are on the compose's new `Caveats:` line:
1. **Tool calls depend on the vendored chat template** until the llama.cpp pin passes ggml-org/llama.cpp#29257.
2. **With no tools offered, it answers in tool-call XML instead of a requested `<solution>` block:** cli-40 one-shot 0/25, bugfind 2/15. That's a model trait; agentic tool use itself is fine (toolcall 15/15, cli-40 multi-round 14/15, hermes 13/20 p@3).
3. **verify-full `[7/10]`** is a known harness false-fail.
4. **Thinking is adaptive.** With thinking on, three packs reasoned on only 1–4 of 15 responses.

## Changes

- **Compose header:** the `Status:` line, plus new `Caveats:` and `Quality:` lines.
- **`registry.yaml`:** `status: caveats` and an updated `status_note`, re-canonicalised with `migrate_registry_to_yaml.py` (`--check` passes).
- **`services/litellm/config.yaml`:** the generated block drops its `# status: experimental` tag.

Effect: `mimo-v2.6-9b/default` now resolves to this slug (it resolved to nothing on master, since experimental slugs are skipped), and launching no longer needs `--force`. The `DEFAULTS` row already pointed here.

## Validation

- **84 related guards pass:** registry, resolver, status drift, compose, LiteLLM, profiles, launch/switch, setup, preflight and docs. `test-litellm-sync` only failed while the `config.yaml` edit was uncommitted, which is what that test checks; it passes on the commit.
