body:
Fixes the SearXNG failure reported in #1342, though not by the mechanism that issue proposes.

## What was wrong here

Our instance had the **opposite** config to the one described in #1342 — `google`, `duckduckgo`, `startpage`, `brave` and `wikipedia` all `enabled: true`, 93 of 249 engines on — and was nonetheless returning **zero results for every query**:

```
q="rtx 3090"                  -> results=0
q="dlss 5 rtx 3090"           -> results=0
q="python list comprehension" -> results=0

unresponsive_engines: [
  ["brave",       "Suspended: too many requests"],
  ["duckduckgo",  "CAPTCHA"],
  ["karmasearch", "Suspended: access denied"],
  ["startpage",   "Suspended: CAPTCHA"]
]
```

`google` and `wikipedia` were the interesting part: queried, returning nothing, raising **no error at all** — absent even from `unresponsive_engines`. `!go rtx 3090` and `!wp rtx 3090` both gave `results=0` with an empty error list. That is a broken result parser, not a blocked request. Egress was fine (`wget https://www.google.com/` from inside the container returned a page), and `!bi` returned 10 results despite bing shipping `enabled: false`.

## Cause

`image: searxng/searxng:latest` is never re-pulled under `restart: unless-stopped`, so the running container was a **2026-05-10** build — four months stale, while `latest` on Docker Hub had moved that same day. SearXNG ships frequent releases largely *because* engine scrapers break when providers change markup or anti-bot behaviour.

## Fix and verification

Pinning to `2026.9.20-fdd8525b1` fixes it outright, with no engine changes:

```
q="dlss 5 rtx 3090" -> 41 results  (brave, google cse)
    DLSS 5 Supported Cards & GPU Compatibility Checker
    Is it possible to run DLSS 5 on RTX 3000-series GPUs ...
q="python list comprehension" -> 36 results
q="rtx 3090"                  -> 41 results
```

Only `duckduckgo` (CAPTCHA) and `wikidata` (timeout) remain unresponsive.

## Why no engine block

#1342 proposes enabling `google, bing, duckduckgo, startpage, brave, yandex`. That would not have helped: brave, duckduckgo and startpage were **already enabled** here and still failed. Enablement was never the problem — image vintage was. duckduckgo still CAPTCHAs from this network, which no config change fixes.

An explicit pin also makes behaviour reproducible. With `latest`, which engines work depends on when the image happened to be pulled — which is precisely how two deployments of the same compose end up behaving differently, as #1342 and this rig did.

## Note on the reporter's specific example

The Habr / Playground results #1342 expects are a **locale** matter, not an engine one. Same query, same instance:

| query | Habr/Playground hits |
|---|--:|
| `dlss 5 rtx 3090` | 0 |
| `dlss 5 rtx 3090` + `language=ru` | **2** (`habr.com/ru/news/…`, `playground.ru/…`) |

So Russian-language sources need `language=ru` on the query (or a `default_lang` in settings), independent of this fix.

body:
## What this adds

A **drafted** tier for the ternary Bonsai artifact: `llama-cpp-prism-mtp/qwen38-27b-single-ternary-mtp` (port 8183).

The existing `prism-ternary-pq2` slug is **un-drafted**, because prism-ml's ternary conversion dropped the `blk.64.nextn.*` MTP head. ProCreations re-bundled target+head into one GGUF (`…-PQ2_0-MTP-Q8_0.gguf`, 7.66 GB vs the plain target's 7.21 GB), same `qwen3_5` arch, so it loads with `-m` and **no `-md`**. Sharing the target's `token_embd`/`output` is what makes MTP profitable here — a separate `-md` sidecar duplicates the vocabulary (~92% of its bytes) and turns even 40% acceptance into a net loss.

## Measured

`bench.sh`, **shipped sampler** (`temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20`), fresh boot per arm, single 3090:

| metric | spec-off | MTP n=4 | delta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| decode — code | 41.19 | **66.27** | **1.61x** |
| decode — narrative | 41.28 | **51.40** | **1.25x** |
| prefill @10K | 902.84 | 862.67 | **−4.4%** |
| TTFT | 139 / 137 ms | 142 / 138 ms | — |
| VRAM (peak) | 8,379 MiB | 9,682 MiB | +1,303 |

Both arms are the **same image** (`b10709-series-multi`), same `-c 32768`, KV `q8_0`, `-b 512 -ub 512`, `--reasoning off`; 3 warm + 5 measured. ⚠️ An earlier draft of this table differenced against the *stock b10685* image and so reported prefill as **+3.6%** — that was #216's prefill gain leaking in from the build change. On a matched build MTP **costs** ~4% of prefill, which is the expected direction: drafting cannot help a compute-bound prefill, and the verify step widens the query.

⚠️ A **1.84x** figure also exists for this slug and is **not** what users get — it was taken at `temp 0 / top_k 1`, the single most favourable sampling for a drafter. It is quoted only as a greedy-decoding ceiling.

### Draft depth — `SPEC_N=4`

`--spec-draft-n-max` sweep, greedy, same build:

| n | median t/s | speedup | acceptance |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| off | 48.70 | 1.00x | — |
| 2 | 79.78 | 1.64x | 86% |
| 3 | 82.57 | 1.70x | 82% |
| **4** | **89.58** | **1.84x** | 77% |
| 5 | 73.21 | 1.50x | 61% |

Sharp cliff past the peak (−18% for one extra draft token), so this is not a safe plateau — the default is pinned, not left to drift. ⚠️ The optimum is workload-dependent: code/format peak at n=4, **prose peaks at n=2** and by n=5 is within 2% of spec-off. Shipping n=4 favours structured/code work. `SPEC_N` and `SPEC=off` are both overridable in the compose.

### Batch geometry

`-b`/`-ub` re-swept **decoupled** (the compose previously bound both to one var, so no prior sweep actually tested ubatch):

| `-b` | ub 512 | ub 1024 | ub 2048 | ub 4096 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 512 | **1047.6** | — | — | — |
| 1024 | 1039.2 | **1042.0** | — | — |
| 2048 | 1015.5 | 1037.7 | 992.9 | — |
| 4096 | 998.1 | 1019.8 | | 932.6 |

512/512 and 1024/1024 tie at the top; shipping 512/512. `-ub` costs VRAM (+122 MiB per step), `-b` does not. Our `-b 512` beats llama.cpp's own default (`-b 2048 -ub 512`) by 3.6%.

## The engine

`--spec-type draft-mtp` **cannot start** on a Hadamard-folded target on stock prism, so this slug needs a source-built engine. Three upstream PRs are vendored as diffs and **baked at build time** (`image_baked: true`), not mounted:

| patch | upstream | size | why |
|---|---|--:|---|
| `pr205.diff` | PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp#205 (open) | +14/−0 | the Hadamard inverse on the MTP token-embedding lookup. **The reason this engine exists.** |
| `pr216.diff` | #216 (open) | +5/−2 | GDN `cols_per_warp` 1→4 was gated to GB10; widening to Ampere+ measured **+8.6% prefill** on sm_86 |
| `pr189.diff` | #189 (open) | +6/−0 | guards a CUDA illegal-access in short-query MMA FA with quantized V (Q 3–4). **Inert at the shipped `SPEC_N=4`** (Q=5) |

Image is **digest-pinned**. Build recipe, the stock-matching arch list (`86;89;120`), and three build traps that each cost a build are in `patches/prism-mtp-b10709/README.md`.

⛔ Drop trigger for all three: when the PR merges **and** ships in a prism release tarball, drop the patch and re-point at the stock image. If all three drop, delete this engine profile and fold the slug back onto `llama-cpp-prism`.

## Quality

8-pack at `reasoning_effort=xhigh`, full 262144 context, `--thinking-max-tokens 65536`, `--timeout-per-case 900`.

⚠️ **This run booted the container directly, so `--reasoning-budget` was NOT applied** — server-side thinking was unbounded and only the client-side 65,536 cap and the wall clock bound it. The compose ships `--reasoning-budget ${REASONING_BUDGET:-32768}`; these numbers were taken without it. Observed generation lengths bear that out: median 401 tokens, p90 7,235, p99 37,876, max 48,016 — three generations past 32,768, which a budgeted run would have truncated.

| pack | ternary+MTP p@1 | ternary+MTP p@3 | fp8 ref p@1 | fp8 ref p@3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| toolcall-15 | 13/15 | **14/15** | 13/15 | 13/15 |
| instructfollow-15 | 15/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| structoutput-15 | 15/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| dataextract-15 | 14/15 | 14/15 | 14/15 | 14/15 |
| reasonmath-15 | 13/15 | 14/15 | **15/15** | **15/15** |
| bugfind-15 | 9/15 | 14/15 | **13/15** | **15/15** |
| hermesagent-20 | 14/20 | 15/20 | **17/20** | **17/20** |
| cli-40 | 31/40 | 33/40 | **35/40** | **35/40** |
| **TOTAL** | **124/150 (83%)** | **134/150 (89%)** | **137/150** | **139/150** |

Reference column is [#1027](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/issues/1027): same base model at **fp8 on vLLM**, same effort, same budgets, same 300 s hermes cap. Run took 3.98 h.

**pass@3 is within 5 of the fp8 reference (134 vs 139); pass@1 is 13 behind.** That gap is the signature of a 2.13 bpw quant — capability retained, first-attempt reliability reduced — and the failure detail bears it out rather than just asserting it:

- **8 of 26 failures are output-format, not reasoning.** Five bugfind cases are the identical error (*"Expected exactly one `<solution>` block"*) and all five recover on attempt 2; `CLI-20`/`CLI-33` are *"Missing solution block"* with `commandCount=0`; `RM-01` solved the problem (trace axis 2/2) and mis-formatted the answer line.
- **3 are safety refusals, not capability** — `CLI-31`, `CLI-32`, `CLI-34`: the model complied with destructive requests it was supposed to refuse or narrow.
- **4 are harness, not model** — `HA-13`/`HA-14` at the 300 s inner cap, `CLI-08` at the 900 s clock, `CLI-26` a sandbox `server_error` that passed on retry.


All 14 failures so far are `verifier_fail` — **0 `token_limit`, 0 `timeout`**. The first 8-pack on this artifact was budget-starved (default 16384 / 300 s cap) and produced timeouts and `finish_reason=length`; at 32768 + 65536 + 900 s those are gone, so what is left is the model being wrong, not the harness starving it.

Reference: #1027 ran the **same base model at fp8 on vLLM** and scored 137/150 pass@1 at xhigh.

## Not in scope

**DFlash2 is parked.** No upstream PR adds the conv/selector head to prism (searched every PR in any state and every issue; the six tensor families are absent tree-wide at our pin), and the merged #172 DFly PR — already in our base — rewrote the exact four files an extracted port conflicts on. Re-test triggers are recorded in the stack tracker.

## Gates

Full `scripts/tests/*.sh` sweep — a catalog-shape change touches the registry, resolver, parity and pull-gate paths. Exact-count assertions updated: `test-compose-registry-disk` 137→138 / 140→141, `test-profiles-compat` engines 20→21, drafters 19→20.

body:
## What
Raises the bonsai-ternary reasoning budget **8192 → 32768**.

> **Changed from this PR's earlier revision.** It first proposed **16384**, picked as "roughly double". That turns out to be the *worst* of the candidates — see below. The number is now derived rather than chosen.

## The binding constraint is the house timeout, not a round number

A budget must be emittable inside the **900 s per-case timeout** ([#1027](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/issues/1027)) at this model's measured **52.2 tok/s** decode — otherwise the wall clock kills the scenario before the budget can fire, and a guard you cannot reach is decoration.

| budget | time to emit | vs 900 s timeout |
|--:|--:|---|
| 8192 | 157 s | fits, but **below** the legitimate trace range |
| 16384 | 314 s | fits, but **inside** it |
| **32768** | **628 s** | ✅ **fits, ~30% headroom**; clears observed max by 73% |
| 65536 | 1256 s | ⛔ **exceeds it — can never fire** |

## ⚠️ Why 16384 was the worst option

The same enumeration prompt drew **18,895** and **13,013** tokens on two draws at temp 1.0. 16384 falls *between* them, so it truncates **nondeterministically** — the same prompt sometimes completing and sometimes not, which is the hardest failure to diagnose. A budget belongs clearly above the distribution or clearly below it, never inside.

## ⭐ Why not lower

| | observed |
|---|--:|
| legitimate long reasoning | 13,013 / 18,895 tok |
| runaway (user report, #1027) | ~170,000 tok |

Two orders of magnitude apart, so any budget in the ~20k–100k gap separates them: it cuts pathology while letting real work finish. **8192 sits below the legitimate range**, so it fires on ordinary enumeration rather than only on runaways — a constant quality tax to catch a rare event.

## Measured behaviour

- ⚠️⚠️ **Ships with `--reasoning-budget-message`, always.** At 8192 the truncated run returned `finish_reason=stop` and a confident **1,264-token answer** — the marker was the *only* evidence the chain had been cut. Upstream defaults that message to empty.
- The budget is **graceful**, unlike `max_tokens`: it closes the thinking block and lets the model answer from a partial chain rather than cutting the stream dead. But the model does **not** know the budget in advance, so it cannot pace itself — it concludes at exhaustion.
- ✅ Validated as the default, not as an override: booted with no `REASONING_BUDGET` env set and read the live `llama-server` argv.

## What this does NOT establish

- ⚠️ **Evidence base is two draws of one prompt.** An unbounded xhigh 8-pack at the shipped 262144 context is running; if its trace p99 exceeds 32768, this number should be revisited.
- ⚠️ 32768 does **not** guarantee no truncation at xhigh — the 170k report is on this model. What makes a non-binding guard safe is that truncation stays visible.
- The same change is applied to the MTP sibling on `feat/prism-mtp-ternary-slug`, which inherited the same too-small 8192 from #1349.

body:
## What
Makes every `--reasoning-*` flag reachable and overridable on the three qwen3.8-27b llama.cpp-family composes. All six exist on **both** engines (prism fork and mainline ggml-org — verified by reading each binary's `--help`), so every gap was a choice never made, not a capability limit. Three knobs were unreachable in **every** compose on the stack.

| knob | default | override |
|---|---|---|
| `--reasoning-budget` | **8192** prism / **−1** siblings | `REASONING_BUDGET` |
| `--reasoning-budget-message` | `[reasoning budget exhausted]` | `REASONING_BUDGET_MESSAGE` |
| `--reasoning-preserve` | *unset* → template default | `REASONING_PRESERVE=on\|off` |
| `--reasoning-format` | `deepseek` (**added** to prism) | `REASONING_FORMAT` |
| `reasoning_effort` | `low` → **`medium`** on 2 siblings | `REASONING_EFFORT` |

## Two deliberate behaviour changes
1. **`reasoning_effort` `low` → `medium`** on both llama-cpp composes. Upstream's card: `low` *"is not supported and when selected the model will behave close to xhigh"* — so `low` bought **full xhigh cost while the config claimed the cheapest tier**. The prism sibling already defaulted to `medium` and documented this exact trap; the other two shipped the bug. Same base model.
2. **prism gains `--reasoning-format`.** It was the only one of the six llama.cpp-family composes without it, running at `auto` while every sibling pinned `deepseek` — which decides whether thoughts reach `message.reasoning_content` or stay inline in `message.content`, i.e. what OpenWebUI / LiteLLM / benchlocal actually see.

Everything else preserves current behaviour. `--reasoning-preserve` is emitted **only when set**, so unset keeps the template default rather than silently overriding it.

## Boot-validated — 5 arms, asserted against the LIVE `llama-server` argv

| arm | budget | message | format | preserve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prism default | 8192 | ✅ | deepseek | absent |
| prism `REASONING_BUDGET=4096` | **4096** | ✅ | deepseek | absent |
| prism `REASONING_PRESERVE=on` | 8192 | ✅ | deepseek | **emitted** |
| lc-single | −1 | ✅ | deepseek | absent |
| lc-dual | −1 | ✅ | deepseek | absent |

Plus a real request on each: thoughts land in `message.reasoning_content`.

> ### ⚠️ The positive-control arm is load-bearing, not ceremony
> Two earlier probe versions read the **wrong process** — one streamed the *host's* `/proc/1/cmdline`, the other assumed PID 1 == `llama-server`, which is true for the llama-cpp composes and **false for prism** (`init: true` → PID 1 is `docker-init`, and the shell's *script text* sits in its cmdline; that text names every flag, so grep "found" them all). Both produced confident wrong answers in **both** directions. "Flag absent" means nothing until the same probe has been shown to see it present.

## Still unvalidated
Whether **8192 is enough headroom** for this model's traces. The budget is proven to *apply*; it is not proven to be the right number. A headroom test (uncapped vs capped, long-reasoning prompts, truncation detected via the marker) is running separately.

body:
## What
`test-soak-decode-basis` and `test-soak-vram-baseline` have both been **RED on master**. This fixes them.

## Root cause
Both gates compare the working tree's `soak-test.sh` against `origin/master`'s by extracting the base script into a temp tree — but extracted only two files:

```bash
for f in soak-test.sh soak-helper.py; do
```

`soak-test.sh:265` sources `lib/club-containers.sh` (added by the registry-derived container-discovery work). The base copy therefore could not start, produced no `summary.md`, and the gate died on:

```
cat: /tmp/tmp.XXXX/run-ar-base-ok/summary.md: No such file or directory
```

which names neither the cause nor the fix. The existing `have_base` guard did not catch it — it only tests whether `git show` **succeeded**, which it did, for the two files it knew about. That a third dependency existed was never checked.

## Three changes
1. **Extract `lib/club-containers.sh`** (+ `mkdir scripts/lib`). This alone turns both gates green.
2. **A coverage check** that re-derives the base script's own `BASH_SOURCE`-relative dependencies and asserts each was extracted — so the next `source` added to `soak-test.sh` fails *here*, naming the file, instead of surfacing three steps later as a missing summary.
3. **`require_base_summary()`** — a baseline run that could not start now says so, instead of `cat`-ing a file that was never written.

## ⚠️ The coverage miss FAILS, it does not SKIP
"origin/master unavailable" stays a **SKIP** — that's an environment condition and skipping is honest. An incomplete extraction list is **our bug**, fixable in-repo; skipping it would silently retire the byte-identity leg while the gate stayed green, which is precisely the failure this guard exists to prevent.

## Negative control, both directions
A green gate proves nothing on its own, so:

| | result |
|---|---|
| with `lib/club-containers.sh` listed | both gates **rc=0** |
| with it removed again | **rc=1**, `FAIL: base tree INCOMPLETE — origin/master's soak-test.sh sources scripts/lib/club-containers.sh, which this gate does not extract.` |

The guard fires, names the exact file, and no longer dies on `cat:`.

**Full sweep on this branch: 0 failures / 179.**

body:
## What

Flip `W4A8` from `${W4A8:-0}` to `${W4A8:-1}` on the **7 `autoround-int4/` SGLang composes** for `qwen3.8-27b`. The vendored AutoRound-Marlin W4A8 patch has been in the tree and working, but behind an opt-in nobody sets — so on this rig it was effectively dead code.

## Why — measured, `dual-fast` (MTP), sglang v0.5.20

**Two fresh boots per arm, interleaved, single-variable** (one pin, W4A8 the only thing changing). `bench.sh` 3 warm-up + 5 measured.

| metric | W4A16 | W4A8 | Δ | boot floor | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| prefill @10K | 1128.1 | **1682.5** | **+49.1%** | 1.9% | REAL |
| prefill @90K | 898.7 | **1234.7** | **+37.4%** | 2.0% | REAL |
| decode narrative | 83.91 | 76.88 | **−8.4%** | 2.9% | REAL |
| decode code | 110.70 | 104.63 | **−5.5%** | 4.7% | REAL |

Prefill is the documented pain point for these slugs, which is what makes the trade worth taking.

> ### ⚠️ This PR's original numbers were wrong and are corrected above
> It first claimed −4.7% narrative / −2.4% code. **The real decode cost is roughly double that.** Those figures came from single boots that also crossed two variables (pin *and* quantisation). This is the first W4A8 measurement on the stack that is single-variable **and** repeat-boot — which is why it is also the first where decode deltas clear the noise floor at all.
>
> Also withdrawn: the claim that **decode changes sign by drafter**. It rested on a single-boot DFlash2 reading of code **+3.3%**, which sat inside the boot-to-boot floor. DFlash2 still has no repeat-boot measurement; its composes now say so and carry the MTP numbers as the best available estimate instead of a per-slug table that was never really measured. Prefill is the one axis that reproduced across both drafters (+47/+48%).
>
> And retired: the **"v0.5.20 regresses this path ~10% decode"** warning. Arm a measured narrative 82.45 then **75.11** on the same image, env and VRAM — a 9% swing between identical boots. The pin bump is a measured null.

## Scope — 7 of 13, deliberately

The patch adds an **AutoRound** W4A8 Marlin kernel. The 6 `fp8/` composes serve `--quantization fp8`, so the patched path is never selected there: `W4A8=1` would apply a patch that does nothing while logging a misleading `[w4a8] applying…`. Those keep `:-0` **plus a comment stating why**, so the asymmetry doesn't later read as an oversight and get "fixed".

## Validation

- `dual-superfast` booted with **no `W4A8` env set at all** — what was tested is the compose default itself, not an override. Serves; `[w4a8] applying…` fires; `[w4a8] verifying…` passes.
- All 13 YAMLs parse; the relevant gates are green.

## Caveats

- ⚠️⚠️ **Quality on the W4A8 path is UNVALIDATED.** No 8-pack, no verify-stress. int8 activations are a real numerical change, not a kernel swap. This PR takes the throughput trade with that stated, not hidden.
- ⚠️ **DFlash2 and `dflash2-bf16` inherit the default without their own repeat-boot measurement.** Flagged in-file.
- Numbers were taken on **v0.5.20**; the v0.5.19→v0.5.20 bump is a measured null (narrative −2.4%, code +0.4%, prefill −0.3%, all inside noise over 2 boots/arm), so they transfer to either pin.
- **Revert is one env var:** `W4A8=0`.

body:
Started as "four c3 catalog columns are wrong for one slug". Each column turned out to have
a different cause, and chasing the last one surfaced a test that was booting a 27B model on
every suite run.

## The c3 columns

| column | was | now | cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| provider · GB | `—` | `albucino` · `129G` | join miss |
| weights | `w4a16` | `int4·AR` | label matcher ordering |
| host RAM | `128 GB` | `135 GB` | never measured |
| spec | `mtp` | `MTP` | drafter-less token vocabulary |

**`_weights_meta` read one registry layer.** It globbed only `scripts/lib/profiles/models/*.yml`,
so every LOCAL-layer slug resolved to `(None, None)` and rendered its weights facts blank —
1 of 138 emit rows, the only local entry. `get_registry()` merges core + local, so the emit
feeding the cockpit must read both.

**`_spec_token` spelled one method two ways.** A built-in speculation head needs no external
drafter artifact, so its slug keeps `drafter: null` and the method arrives on `spec_method`.
That branch returned the raw registry token, so three rows printed lowercase `mtp` against
~130 printing `MTP`. Now shares the drafter branch's vocabulary, with a regression test.

**Two Bonsai weights entries shared one `verify_glob`.** Same `subdir` *and* `*.gguf`, so each
matched the other's file — delete the 0.63 GB projector and it still reports PRESENT because
the 7.21 GB pack satisfies its glob.

## The test that booted a model

`test-engine-kind-resolver.sh` drives the real `spec-sweep.sh` to check engine classification.
Its comment said it ran "against a dead URL so it prints its classification and exits before
touching a server". It did not — the banner prints *before* the dry-run check, so for every
non-llamacpp family it went on to `switch.sh --force <slug>` per arm. Three invocations per
suite run, so **every sweep booted models on both GPUs**.

Three things that looked like protection and were not: `timeout 120` TERMs `spec-sweep` only
(the `switch.sh` grandchild survives — observed exceeding its timeout threefold with the model
still serving); `| head -40` never fires SIGPIPE while the child is quiet; and the dead `URL=`
is *why* it boots. The test passed either way, so the suite went green while the rig lost both
GPUs and later GPU-sensitive tests flaked. `SWEEP_DRY=1` fixes it: 120s+ hanging → **0.185s**.

`test-tests-never-launch.sh` gates the class. ⚠️ Its first version was **false-clean** — it
reported "no test can boot a model" with a deliberately unguarded test present, because the
exec regex stepped over env assignments with `\w+=\S*` and `SWEEP_N="0 1"` broke the walk.
Only the negative control caught it. Now verified three ways.

## Open WebUI

Launching a slug did not make it reachable. `owui-register.sh` was append-only and opt-in:
**7 registered connections, every one refusing**, while the running slug was absent and
LiteLLM wasn't registered at all. Now a sync — prunes dead connections, but only registry-owned
ports (derived, never hand-listed, degrades open so a failed read prunes nothing); probes from
*inside* the container on the path OWUI uses; drops `keys` with `urls` since they're positionally
paired. `switch.sh` syncs by default (`--no-owui` opts out) and prunes on `--down`.

Also `test-diagnose-profile.sh`: exit codes are a contract (GREEN=0/YELLOW=1/RED=2), not a
boolean. `vllm/qwen38-27b-single-nvfp4` is yellow by design — its note says "on a 3090 expect an
OOM at KV init, which is the config being honest rather than broken". Now exit-code aware with a
register that can't rot.

## Not here / flagged

- **host RAM was measured, not derived**: cgroup `anon` 57.64 GB + `shmem` 77.37 GB (the UVA
  expert offload — anonymous *shared* memory, `/dev/shm` held 21 MB) = **135.00 GB**, corroborated
  by the system `free` delta. Not `memory.current` (231 GB — mostly reclaimable page cache from a
  129 GB checkpoint). An earlier *derived* 121 landed further from truth than the unsourced 128.
- **Unit trap, deliberately not compensated for**: `preflight_cpu_offload_ram()` compares its
  header against `MemTotal_kB/1024/1024` — GiB — under a key named `-GB`. Every sibling carries it.
- **Nine `size_gb` values look like GiB read off `du -sh`** (`exl3-3.05bpw` 80→85, `unsloth-ud-q4kxl`
  105→111, `devquasar-q3km` 140→149, …). Each verified with a glob unique to its variant.
- **Four more shared `(subdir, verify_glob)` pairs** in core. That pair must be unique per variant.
- The LiteLLM gateway is still static and port-pinned (9 of 138 slugs, 13 models with no route).

Local-layer (gitignored) changes for the bucko slug are not in this PR by design.

body:
Adds two engines and three 🐣 Incubating slugs, plus the harness fixes they exposed.
Everything here was booted and measured on the reference rig (2× RTX 3090).

## 1. Engines and slugs

**exl3 — ExLlamaV3 1.5.0 + TabbyAPI, zero patches** (stock upstream @ `53da791`)

| slug | ctx | KV | decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `…-exl3-305-cpumoe` | 204800 | Q4 | 50.5 T/s |
| `…-exl3-405-cpumoe` | 204800 | Q4 | 39.3 T/s |

⭐ The reason this engine is interesting: **offloaded MoE experts are computed on
the CPU** — expert weights never cross PCIe. Decode is therefore set by the
CPU-resident expert fraction and almost nothing else (25% → 57.4, 44% → 48.5,
80% → 10.9 T/s; GPU util 5–8% at the bottom of that range). GLM-5.3-Flash was
evaluated on this engine and **rejected** on exactly that basis.

⚠️ Two counter-intuitive results are baked into the configs: **Q8 caps 3.05 at
65536 — less context than Q4 buys**, and reaching 204800 needs a deeper CPU split
(144 / 256), which is why context and throughput trade against each other here.
Validated to 100K-token prompts with zero OOM.

**llama-cpp-prism — PrismML ternary fork** (upstream release binary + `libgomp1`)

`qwen3.8-27b` "Bonsai 2 27B" PQ2_0: a 27B at 2.13 bpw in 7.21 GB, so the **full
262144 context runs on ONE 3090** at 17.1 GB with q8_0 KV. bench.sh 42.76
narrative / 41.01 code / 834.8 prefill@10K, TTFT 141 ms. verify-full 8 PASS /
2 skip / 0 fail, vision 4/4.

⚠️⚠️ **Stock llama.cpp cannot run these files and fails silently** — it rejects
`PQ2_0`/`PTQ1_0` and loads `Q2_0` with no warning while producing garbage, having
no Hadamard activation runtime. Verified from the GGUF before downloading:
`file_type 141`, 402 of 851 tensors type `142`, against a mainline enum ending at
`TQ2_0`=35. Never repoint these slugs at another engine.

⚠️ This quant **drops the MTP head** the unsloth GGUFs carry at `blk.64.nextn.*`,
so every throughput figure for it is un-drafted and not comparable to the drafted
dual rows.

## 2. Harness — per-engine acceptance parsing

**The serious fix is for vLLM, not the new engines.** Current vLLM emits
`SpecDecoding metrics: … Avg Draft acceptance rate: 78.9%`, which matched none of
the patterns in `capture.sh` — the form it did match is *old* vLLM. So every bench
on current vLLM reported "no acceptance data" while the log carried it. Caught on
a log holding 26 such lines against a bench saying there were none.

Also: `/props` is no longer llama.cpp-exclusive (TabbyAPI serves a compatible one
and emits no `system_fingerprint`), so exl3 classified as `llamacpp` and
verify-full's step 9 **skipped**, reading as "no drafter" while MTP ran at ~0.69
acceptance. Step 9 is now a real check, not a skip — the same failure mode the
SGLang branch already documents.

Verified against real fixtures captured from live containers, with regression
fixtures for SGLang and llama.cpp and a no-drafter negative control.

## 3. New gate — declared-but-dead env vars

The mirror of `test-compose-entrypoint-env-declared`. That one catches a knob
docker never forwards; this catches a knob docker forwards that nothing reads.
Both end the same way: the user sets it, nothing errors, nothing changes.

Proven in both directions — an injected dead knob **fails** the gate, and an
engine-consumed `LLAMA_ARG_*` var is correctly allowed. The allowlist is measured,
not guessed: 33 declared-but-unreferenced names across 140 composes, of which
exactly one was a real defect.

## Ports

All three slugs are on **8180–8182, deliberately outside 8147–8167** —
`test-bench-capture` allocates fixture servers across that span, so a slug parked
there fails the guard whenever the model serves. A first attempt at 8163/8164 was
still inside it. ⚠️ Eight `sgl/qwen38-27b-multi*` slugs remain on 8147–8154 with
the same latent problem — pre-existing, not addressed here.

## What is NOT validated

⛔ **No quality 8-pack, no verify-stress, no soak on any of the three slugs.** That
is why they ship 🐣 Incubating and not 🧪 — quality is deliberately left to
community validation. For the exl3 pair specifically, 3.05bpw is low enough that
part of its speed advantage is simply that it is smaller, and nobody has priced
that. Q4 KV is also below this stack's q8-grade serving floor, making these
capacity exhibits rather than serving tiers.

Also unmeasured: concurrency beyond C=1, and any context above what is stated.

## Gates

Full suite **173 pass / 2 fail**; both failures pre-existing
(`test-diagnose-profile`, `test-setup-primary-slug-backed`), confirmed against a
clean tree. `preflight-add-model` 11/11 on each slug; registry canonical.

`AGENTS.md` and `docs/UPSTREAM.md` carry another session's in-flight edits
(engine-patch provenance policy; a club-3090#1327 tracker row), included at the
maintainer's request rather than authored here.

body:
## Summary

Self-hosted vLLM routes in the generated LOCAL block currently use the generic `openai/` provider prefix. For vLLM backends this drops `reasoning_effort` / `thinking` from litellm's param whitelist, so clients that send them get a `400` (or a silent downgrade). The dedicated `hosted_vllm` provider includes those params and passes them through.

## Changes

- `scripts/lib/litellm-emit.sh`: when a gateway entry's engine is vLLM, emit `hosted_vllm/<name>` instead of `openai/<name>`. llama.cpp backends keep `openai/<name>` because they do not parse `reasoning_effort` and rely on `drop_params` to discard it safely (the backend would otherwise reject it).
- `services/litellm/config.yaml`: regenerated LOCAL block -- all vLLM routes now use `hosted_vllm/`; the non-vLLM routes (deepseek-v4-flash, glm-5.3-flash, deckard-40b, qwen3.8-flash-next) stay `openai/`.

## Root cause

litellm maps `openai/qwen3.8-27b` to a vLLM `/v1/chat/completions` call but strips `reasoning_effort` before forwarding. A client requesting `reasoning_effort: medium` is therefore rejected with `400`. Switching the provider to `hosted_vllm` restores correct passthrough.

## Verification

- Before: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `reasoning_effort: medium` through the gateway -> `400`.
- After: same request -> `200`, reasoning content returned.
- `litellm-emit.sh --check` passes (generated block matches the registry).

## Scope

Only the registry-emitted LOCAL block is changed. The hand-maintained `agents-a1` route and the cloud (DashScope) block are untouched.
title: litellm: emit hosted_vllm provider for local vLLM routes (fix reasoning_effort 400)

## What this fixes

`models/qwen3.8-27b/vllm/compose/dual/autoround-int4/dflash2.yml` (`vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast`) tells three different stories after the 2026-09-14 #1274 change:

1. The at-a-glance header still says `KV: bf16 — MANDATORY here` / `Max ctx: 204800 (~200K)` — the pre-plugin tier.
2. The file's own 2026-09-14 W4A8 comment says "the shipped default is 262144".
3. The command block actually ships `MAX_MODEL_LEN:-204800` — a bf16-era leftover, so a bare launch today silently takes the *old* config (and a 262K user has to know to override).

Meanwhile the registry entry for the same slug already says `max_ctx: 262144` with a fully current `status_note`, and the BENCHMARKS 2026-09-14 row labels the 262144 config "SHIPPED CONFIG". So the compose file was the one surface still describing the world before #1274.

## Changes (one file, 35+/25-)

- **at-a-glance**: `KV:` → fp8 e4m3 via the #1274 FA2 plugin (with the before/after decode numbers kept in-line); `Max ctx:` → 262144 as the shipped default, with the 204800 bf16-era ceiling preserved as history; `Drafter:` notes the DFlash2 model classes have been native since v0.29.0 (vllm#52816), not a vendored backport; `Best for:` now quotes the shipped fp8 numbers (~220 code / ~123 narr) instead of the bf16-era 227/132.
- The "⭐ WHY bf16 KV + FLASH_ATTN (and why 200K, not 262K)" section is re-cast as a **dated HISTORY block** (2026-08-20 → 2026-09-14) — same facts, correctly framed, ending on what dissolved the trade.
- The **VALIDATED block** gains the 2026-09-14 line (four alternating boots, each arm within 1%: 122.7/219.5 @262144, pool 421,970 tok / 1.61×); the 2026-08-20 bf16 results are kept verbatim under their date.
- **Command block**: `MAX_MODEL_LEN` default `204800` → `262144` — the only non-comment change.

## Why the default flip is safe

- It's not a new config: 262144 + fp8 KV + FA2 plugin is exactly the 2026-09-14 measured/validated configuration on the reference rig, and it's what the registry already advertises. The flip only makes the bare launch match what the file, the registry, and BENCHMARKS all already call "shipped".
- Anyone pinning `MAX_MODEL_LEN` explicitly is unaffected.
- I couldn't run verify-full from the box this PR was authored on (no GPU); the 262144 config is the one the reference rig validated on 2026-09-14, so the gate question is only whether you want a fresh verify-full/soak pass on the reference rig before merge.
- Community cross-check (not part of the gate, just context): this exact config, including the new 262144 default, has been the daily-driver config on a 2× 3090 rig **with an NVLink bridge** (custom all-reduce engaged) since 2026-09-17 — 141 narr / 267 code TPS, prefill 3075 tok/s @10K (vs 1862 on the PCIe reference rig: the NVLink long-ctx win from the #698 notes materializing).

## Deliberately not touched

- `dual/autoround-int4/dflash2-fp8.yml`'s "fp8 KV can't use FLASH_ATTN on Ampere" line is *accurate for that file* — it's the no-plugin FlashInfer sibling, so it reads as the contrast case, not a stale claim.
- The multi4/multi8 ultrafast `status_note`s still carry the "bf16 KV + FLASH_ATTN is mandatory" pre-#1274 framing (their composes still default to bf16 KV, which at TP=4/8 fits 262K legitimately). Extending the plugin to those tiers is a config change, not a header fix — happy to do that as a follow-up if you agree the direction is right.

body:
Two related changes to the qwen3.8-27b DFlash2 tiers, both prompted by measurement.

## 1. `fa2-fp8kv-sm86` on multi4/multi8 (closes a reported gap)

@foureight84 reported in [#1076](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/discussions/1076) that only the two **dual** DFlash2 composes mounted the plugin — the four multi4/multi8 siblings had `fa2=0`, so `KV_CACHE_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3` there either fell back to FlashInfer or silently didn't give the expected pool. Reproduced here.

Transplants the same seven pieces into all four (`fa2=0` → `fa2=7`): `depends_on` gate, kernels-artifact volume, patch mount, `FA2_ARTIFACT_ID`, **`TP`**, the `install.sh` + `source fa2-runtime.env` hook, and the one-shot kernels service with its named volume.

⚠️ **`TP` is the easy-to-miss one.** `install.sh` reads it from the *container* environment (`${TP:-2}`), so without it the installer validates only the first two ranks for homogeneity on a 4- or 8-GPU box. Set to 4 / 8 per topology.

**Validation status — read this before merging.** This rig has exactly two 3090s, so none of these are boot-validated here. `multi4/fp8` is the variant @foureight84 booted by hand, with receipts: `[fa2] verified artifact=731d1942…`, `FLASH_ATTN backend`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`, **1,051,045 tokens = 4.01× concurrency at the full 262,144**. The other three are the same transplant at different TP and container names. Community-validated by design, as the multi-N slugs already are.

⚠️ The installer is deliberately **fail-closed**: on a rig outside sm86/89/120 (or sm90/100 native) the kernels service exits non-zero and `depends_on: service_completed_successfully` blocks the boot. Acceptable for slugs that already require that hardware — and the reason this was **not** extended blanket-wide across all vLLM composes, which would brick A100 (sm80) and DGX Spark (sm121).

## 2. kv-calc: TP clamp + qwen3.8-27b registration

vLLM shards KV heads across TP ranks but clamps at one per rank — `num_kv_heads = max(1, total // tp_size)` (`qwen3_next.py:296`, plus 72 other model files in v0.29.0), with its own comment: *"Number of KV heads is less than TP size, so we replicate the KV heads across multiple tensor parallel GPUs."* Past that point per-card KV stops shrinking, so dividing by `tp` over-predicts the pool by `tp / num_kv_heads` — **predicting PASS where reality is FAIL**.

Adds `_kv_tp_divisor() = max(1, min(tp, kv_heads))` across the five attention-KV branches. GDN/recurrent terms are deliberately **not** clamped — vLLM genuinely shards those (`mamba_utils.py:274-277`).

**The clamp is a proven no-op today:** `--calibration` output is byte-identical pre/post, because every currently-priced model has `max(valid_tp) <= num_kv_heads`. It becomes load-bearing only with qwen3.8-27b, the first priced model to exceed it (4 KV heads, `valid_tp` includes 8).

Registration rides the `qwen3-next-hybrid` KV math since the geometry is byte-identical to qwen3.6-27b; `model_family` is that internal KV tag rather than the ModelProfile family, per the gemma-4-12b precedent. 17 of 18 vLLM slugs priceable — `dual-ultramax` stays `SKIP` because it pins `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` and has no `mem_util` for a utilization model to use.

**multi4/multi8 rows are PROJECTIONS**, not measurements. They're emitted so a 4- or 8-card `report.sh` run validates them automatically via its `## KV math calibration` section — turning them into falsifiable predictions rather than unverifiable table entries.

First TP=4 datapoint, from @foureight84's numbers: **KV pool predicts within ~6%** of their measured 1,051,045 tokens; **per-card overhead under-predicts by ~3 GB** (partly the DFlash2 drafter, which that invocation didn't include). Tracked as a calibration gap.

## Docs

`KV_MATH.md` gains the clamp and a correction worth knowing independently: vLLM's reported token count is **block accounting**, not `bytes ÷ per-token`. It's `int(num_blocks / blocks_per_request × max_model_len)` after hybrid group padding, mamba snapshot blocks and window-bounded drafter SWA layers. That's why vLLM measures MTP at **−13.9%** where the 17/16 layer ratio predicts −6.25%, and why `GPU KV cache size:` **is not comparable across different `max-model-len` values**.

## Testing

`--calibration` 8/8 · four `test-kv-calc-*` gates · `test-profiles-compat` · `test-patch-attribution` · `test-compose-mounts-resolve` · `test-compose-status-drift` · `test-compose-registry-disk` · `test-switch-registry-parity` · `test-launch-registry-parity` · `test-registry-yaml-roundtrip` · all four composes valid under `docker compose config`.

⛔ **No verify-full / verify-stress / bench on the multi composes** — structurally impossible on two cards.

⚠️ `test-setup-primary-slug-backed` fails on this branch **and on master** (pre-existing: `qwen3.8-flash-next-ple` is a LOCAL-layer model with no core registry entries).

body:
Three review rounds found the same defect class three times, so this replaces the mechanism rather than patching it a fourth time.

## The problem

`p2p_classify_engagement` determined machine state by grepping English sentences out of a container log — some of them ours. Any line anyone added could collide with a key, and nothing made that visible at the time of writing.

It is not hypothetical. A boot warning added in this series ended *"vs turning P2P off entirely"*, and `*"P2P off"*` is the classifier's transport-off key:

```
veto alone        -> nccl_only_degraded   (correct: peer path broken)
veto + warning    -> off                  ("P2P is off, set NVLINK_MODE=force_off")
```

Wrong diagnosis and wrong remedy, on the exact rig shape the warning exists to protect.

## The change

`detect_nvlink.sh` emits one machine-readable line per boot:

```
[nvlink] STATE v=1 transport=… kernel=… cause=… verified=… gate=… mode=… world=…
```

The classifier parses that for our configuration. Prose matching survives only for **vLLM's** messages, which we do not control, and on the legacy path — containers predating this, plus SGLang and llama.cpp, which never emit a STATE line. That path is permanent and documented as such.

Four properties, each with a negative control:

| property | why |
|---|---|
| **Boot epoch** | `restart: unless-stopped` leaves several boots in one `docker logs`. Combining our state from one boot with vLLM's veto from another silently reports the wrong rig. Last STATE wins; only engine lines after it count. |
| **Veto catch-all** | vLLM has more veto reasons than we enumerate. An unenumerated one must not read as "engine said nothing" → our configured `kernel=on`. |
| **`kernel=` is a fact** | It records what we passed, never a prediction. The prediction lives in `gate=`, derived from the TP world size — vLLM's actual rule — not the visible GPU count. |
| **Engine argv wins** | A compose may pass the flag itself, and `dual/fp8/dflash2.yml` does on every non-NVLink rig. |

`head -8` and `grep -m1` are gone from both callers, and `report.sh` classifies from one ordered stream instead of reassembled display variables, which defeated the epoch entirely.

## The knob, now universal

`_NVLINK_ENABLED` has always meant *"fast interconnect → custom all-reduce ON"*, so it now carries the **kernel** decision. `DISABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE=1` is therefore honoured by every gate shape ever shipped — the `_archive` composes, forks, hand-edits — **by construction**.

That replaces an opt-in marker plus a boot-time refusal, which could only cover files we had edited (it was inert on 33 of 45 composes, including the tier both #922 reporters run) and fired on host-side probes besides. The transport moved to `_P2P_TRANSPORT`; `lmcache`'s allocator check and `launch.sh`'s probe read `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE`.

Also adds a boot warning on the risky shape — verified PCIe peer path, kernel live, TP=2 — so the affected population hears about the knob before the crash rather than after. Deliberately **not** narrowed to x8 links: the platform correlation is confounded with speculative decoding and the mechanism is unestablished, so narrowing on an unproven mechanism would silence it for someone it should reach.

## On the tests

Every fixture standing for real output is now **derived from the thing it describes**. Each hand-written one was weaker than the line it represented and passed while the feature behind it was broken or absent — a `transport=off` fixture for a line the decider never emitted, a veto fixture missing the clause that makes ordering matter, a `#688` control that tested the reader and not the writer.

Mutation results: gate-on-GPU-count, version-match relaxed, unknown-cause-to-healthy, alias-transport, verified-mapping-removed, operator-arm-removed, operator-arm-misordered, `_NVLINK_FOUND` dropped or over-set, and the `force_on` over-claim are all caught. Survivors are `-tp=` parsing and the non-numeric warning, both of which fail safe — they suppress a warning rather than produce a wrong verdict.

Guards: 58/59 of the targeted set; the one failure is a pre-existing untracked patch artifact unrelated to this change.

body:
Three doc changes from [#1332](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/issues/1332), a 2× 3090 report of a **hard machine reset** under sustained decode over a patched PCIe peer path.

## §7a — a fourth failure mode, and the first that passes every check we ship

§7a carried three ways a live peer path fails: the #873 init hang, the clique-granted collective hang, and #922's fast-but-wrong output. This one announces itself least of all — kernel log ends mid-line, no panic, no oops, no MCE, **no Xid**, kdump produces nothing, filesystem needs orphan cleanup on the next boot.

Isolated in one sitting at identical clocks and power limits: P2P + kernel **resets**, P2P off **clean**, P2P + kernel off **clean and faster** (+10.7% prefill @10K, −8.6% TTFT). The two working arms rule out the PSU and the overclock without argument.

Mechanism recorded as **unestablished** — nothing is logged and there is no dump, so what is on record is the correlation. The reporter's `iommu=pt` hypothesis is noted as a hypothesis, alongside a PCIe fatal error resetting a consumer board, which fits the same silence.

## §7a — the correctness ladder gains a tier, and the discriminator is not what it looks like

The ladder ran grant → transfer test → `verify-full` → quality pack / needle. This report passes **all of it**: verify-full 10/10 including the 2000-token lexical-variety scan that catches #922, and correct needle recall at every depth to 240,660 tokens — immediately before each reset.

The fault needs a sustained *rate* of small all-reduces, and every tier above is either prefill-shaped or a single bounded generation. So a 240K needle test is not the stress it looks like: one enormous all-reduce is a different load than a hundred thousand tiny ones.

**The discriminator is continuity, not length.** `verify-full`'s own 2000-token essay was not enough, while `bench.sh` — 3 warm-ups plus 5 measured generations back to back — reset the box within seconds. So the detector already ships; the ladder simply never named it as a correctness gate. That is what the new tier says.

## §0c — transport and kernel are two switches

The engine table now shows the custom all-reduce kernel as its own row, with `DISABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE=1` as the narrow escape hatch and an explicit note that `NVLINK_MODE=force_off` turns off both. The #922 row's fix column is repointed from the raw flag to the supported knob.

## §5 — the DKMS initramfs trap

Generalises to every DKMS user of the patched module, and currently costs people a working build. After DKMS installs the patched module, **the initramfs still contains the stock `nvidia` module and loads it first** — peer access looks unavailable and the patch reads as a failed build.

The tell is a `srcversion` disagreement *between* the NVIDIA modules: the satellite modules load patched from disk while core `nvidia` comes from the initramfs. Fix is `update-initramfs -u`, and it must be redone after every driver or kernel upgrade — a routine `apt upgrade` silently reverts you with no symptom but P2P quietly stopping.

Its verification is also a false-clean, which is why it is written up rather than just fixed: `lsinitramfs` needs root, and as a normal user the permission error goes to stderr while a counting grep prints `0` — indistinguishable from "clean".

Reported by @leo-3889; the initramfs findings are theirs and credited in the doc.

body:
`--disable-custom-all-reduce` is the documented mitigation for a custom-AR kernel misbehaving over a patched PCIe peer path ([#922](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/issues/922)) — but there has been no supported way to reach it. `NVLINK_MODE=force_off` drops the **transport** as well, discarding the NCCL prefill win, so the only route was editing a shipped compose. That is exactly what the #1332 reporter had to do to stop his machine hard-resetting.

```bash
DISABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE=1 bash scripts/launch.sh <slug>     # or put it in .env
```

`NCCL_P2P_LEVEL` stays as auto-detect resolved it, `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE` stays unset. Only vLLM's own kernel goes.

## Why there was no knob: two decisions in one variable

`_NVLINK_ENABLED` answered both "is the peer transport up?" and "does vLLM run its custom all-reduce on top?", and the composes gated the flag on it. Nothing could express one without the other.

Split into `_CUSTOM_AR_ENABLED`, which defaults to `_NVLINK_ENABLED` — so **behaviour with the knob unset is unchanged**, asserted directly by the test. The 12 composes carrying the gate now read `${_CUSTOM_AR_ENABLED:-${_NVLINK_ENABLED:-0}}`, correct even against a `detect_nvlink.sh` that predates the split.

An invalid value is a hard error, not a silent fallback: a typo must not resolve to "kernel stays on", which is the arm that resets machines.

## Two things the test caught that reading did not

1. **The 2-GPU branches of `detect_nvlink.sh` hardcoded the string `custom all-reduce ON`** instead of calling `_ar_claim()` — which the `>2`-GPU branches did correctly. On exactly the affected rig shape the boot trail would have asserted the kernel was on while the knob had turned it off: the #924 false-verdict bug again, one layer down.
2. **`p2p_classify_engagement` had no pattern for the knob.** It keys on vLLM's `disable_custom_all_reduce=True` and the raw flag, but `detect_nvlink.sh` resolves this one itself, so the trail needed teaching. Without it the trail would classify `on` while the kernel was off.

## Delivery path verified, not assumed

Docker forwards nothing that is not declared, so the var is added to each compose's `environment:` block and checked through `docker compose config` rather than by inspecting the YAML — unset renders `"0"`, set renders `"1"`. Interpolated rather than bare so it resolves from `.env` too, and so the container never sees the empty string that the `{0,1}` validator would reject.

`expandable_segments` is deliberately left stripped on this path even though the IPC clash that motivated stripping it does not apply without the kernel — that keeps the shipped config byte-identical to the arm validated on the reporting rig.

## Scope

This is the knob only. **The default is unchanged** — the kernel still comes on with the transport when peer access is detected. Three rigs run it cleanly over the same patched path and the evidence on the other side is confounded between platform class and speculative decoding; see #1332.

body:
On a 2-GPU rig, `report.sh`'s interconnect verdict attributed an operator-disabled custom all-reduce to vLLM's own `world>2` gate — telling the one person who deliberately turned the kernel off that it was automatic and expected.

Found in the `report.sh` paste on #1332, whose reporter had just disabled the kernel to stop his machine hard-resetting, and was reading the verdict to confirm it had taken.

## The bug

`p2p_verdict` renders `pcie_p2p:nccl_only` with a single hardcoded explanation:

> vLLM auto-disabled its custom all-reduce kernel — **expected at >2 PCIe-only GPUs** (its gate checks NVLink, not peer access; #786), NOT a misconfiguration.

That gate cannot fire at world_size 2. Read straight out of the pinned image, `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py` (v0.29.0):

```python
236:  if same_node and world_size > 2 and not fully_connected:
238:      "Custom allreduce is disabled because it's not supported on"
239:      " more than two PCIe-only GPUs. ..."
```

`world_size > 2` is a hard precondition on the only branch that emits that message. And two lines further down the *enabling* condition at world 2 is peer access, not NVLink:

```python
250:  and not _can_p2p(rank, world_size)
```

So at 2 GPUs `nccl_only` has exactly one possible cause: an operator-supplied `--disable-custom-all-reduce` — the #922 mitigation. (It also confirms the other half: at 2 GPUs a P2P grant is sufficient to turn the kernel **on**, which is how #1332's rig ended up in the crashing arm without opting in.)

`p2p_verdict` already takes `<gpu_count>` as its first argument; it just never branched on it.

The layer-3 line in `bench.sh` is unaffected — #924 made that one cause-neutral. This is only the verdict line.

## Fix

At `count <= 2`, both `pcie_p2p:nccl_only` and `nvlink:nccl_only` now attribute to the operator flag and say plainly that it is a healthy, deliberate state that keeps the NCCL transport.

## Why it survived

`test-p2p-state.sh` exercised `p2p_verdict 4 pcie_p2p nccl_only` and `p2p_verdict 1 …` and `p2p_verdict 2 none …`, but never `p2p_verdict 2 <capability> nccl_only` — the one combination where the card count changes the meaning. Added, for both capabilities.

Verified with a negative control: reverting the fix fails the new assertions on the exact wrong string.

body:
Raises `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-max` from **131,072 → 163,840** context by pinning the mamba cache at **K=10**.

```
CONTEXT_LENGTH        131072 -> 163840
max-mamba-cache-size  (unset, auto-fit -> 21) -> 10
MAX_MAMBA_CACHE_SIZE  new env seam (bare passthrough)
MEM_FRACTION          unchanged (0.92 — already at its measured ceiling)
```

## Why K, and why now

`mem_util` on this tier is **already maxed**: the registry has long recorded 0.92 as the practical ceiling, because above it the prefill cudagraph capture OOMs as a PyTorch `num_active_captures_` assert rather than a clean CUDA OOM. So the mamba pool was the only lever left.

Auto-fit gives **K=21** and spends the surplus slots on *breadth* — which this slug does not use. It ships `--max-running-requests 1` and its role is a single-stream fidelity reference on official Qwen weights.

## Measured

ctx held constant so K was the only variable:

| K | `max_total_num_tokens` | avail mem |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 | 158,116 | 1.67 GB |
| **10** | **182,901** | 1.66 GB |

The **+24,785** delta is exactly **11 × 2,253.2** — the same KV-tokens-per-mamba-slot exchange rate measured on the int4 tier. Predicted 182,901; measured 182,901.

⭐ **That rate is quant-independent.** Per-slot SSM bytes and per-token KV bytes (fp8_e4m3 over 17 KV-bearing layers including the MTP head) are identical across the int4 and fp8 tiers — only the *budget* differs. This PR is the second tier it has been validated on.

⚠️ **It is NOT drafter-independent.** DFlash2 tiers carry 5 extra sliding-attention layers at a different geometry (~+31% per-token KV), so a freed slot buys fewer tokens there. Do not reuse 2,253.2 outside built-in-MTP tiers.

## Gate

The shipped pair (K=10 **and** ctx 163,840) had never booted — K=10 was measured at the old ctx — so it was gated rather than inferred:

| | |
|---|---|
| pool / ctx | 182,901 / 163,840 = **1.116×**, headroom 19,061 |
| verify-full | **10/10** — incl. vision 4/4 and MTP acceptance **3.446** |
| OOM / capture asserts | **0 / 0** |
| peak VRAM | 22,809 / 22,502 MiB |

Targeted gates green: `test-compose-status-drift`, `test-compose-registry-disk`, `test-profiles-compat`, `test-launch-compat`. (Catalog *data* change — no slug added, no status or schema change — so the full 174-test sweep was not run.)

## Why 163,840 and not 180,224

180,224 fits arithmetically at ~1.01×. It is deliberately not chosen: this tier has the **slowest prefill on the rig** (sm_86 has no native fp8 compute, so weights serve weight-only through Marlin), and zero radix headroom repays every cache miss at full price. 163,840 keeps 19,061 tokens of headroom, comparable to the ~27K the tier had before.

## Cost

**Usable warm-prefix slots drop 18 → 7** (`K − 3 × max_running_requests`). Depth is unaffected — one long conversation occupies one slot — but **breadth** shrinks. If many distinct conversations are kept warm, raise `MAX_MAMBA_CACHE_SIZE` back toward 21 and lower `CONTEXT_LENGTH` to match; the new seam exists for exactly that.

K=5 was considered and rejected: it clears the hard floor (K ≥ 5) but buys only ~11K more tokens (~6%) while leaving 2 usable prefix slots.

## Not claimed

**Decode throughput at K=10 vs K=21 was not benched.** The drafter is alive (acceptance 3.446 ≥ 2.0), but that is a health check, not a throughput comparison. This PR asserts pool, context and correctness — not that decode is unchanged.

Single boot. Memory-side numbers are boot-stable on this rig, so the pool figure is solid; anything throughput-shaped would need repeat boots.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

`sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`'s registry note still warns that verify-full step 9 is blind on SGLang (it greps for vLLM's `SpecDecoding metrics` line). It scored natively today — `acceptance length 3.446 >= 2.0 (SGLang)`. Different slug, so it is left for a separate change; it matters because a silent SKIP once hid a dead drafter for a full bench cycle.

Detail: `learnings/qwen3.8-27b.md`, 2026-09-15.

title: sgl/dual-max: pin K=10 and raise context to 163840

body:
**Gated 2026-09-15 — all blocking gates run.** verify-full 10/10 · verify-stress ceiling ladder 6/6 to 240,660 tok (91%) · bench 74.00/101.58 decode TPS · soak-continuous PASS (0/200 MiB growth) · quality cli-40 29/40. One amber flag (VRAM margin 949 MB vs a 1,024 MB threshold) is analysed in the [gate-results comment](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/pull/1329#issuecomment-5685539349).

Changes `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` from **one deep session to two**.

```
MEM_FRACTION          0.90 -> 0.95
MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS  1    -> 2
SPEC_N                unchanged (MTP stays on)
max-mamba-cache-size  stays UNSET (auto-fit) — no new flag, no seam
```

## Measured at the new default

| | value |
|---|---|
| `max_total_num_tokens` | **451,633** (was 409,552) |
| sessions × context | **2 × 225,817** — 86% of the 262,144 ceiling |
| `max_mamba_cache_size` | 63 (auto) → clamp allows C=12 |
| **accept len / rate** | **3.25 / 0.56** — above the 2.86 recorded at the old 1-session default |
| post-boot headroom | 1.47 GB |
| errors / OOM | 0 / 0 |

## Why auto-fit rather than forcing K down

Fewer state slots leave less slack for speculation, so forcing K buys context and costs draft efficiency:

| K | ctx/session | accept len |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 63 (auto) | 225,817 | **3.25** measured |
| 35 | 257,361 | 3.02 measured |
| 20 | 274,260 | ~2.6 interpolated, **not booted** |
| 10 | 285,526 | **2.27** measured |

A full `2 × 262,144` needs K ≤ ~30, costing ~20% of accept length. **86% of the ceiling is a soft limit** — a longer session evicts rather than failing — so throughput is worth more than the last 14% of context.

## The underlying waste

The old default provisioned **K=55 (capable of C=11) to serve a single request** — ~101,000 tokens given to concurrency it was configured never to use. Auto-fit sizes K to available memory, not to the workload.

## ✅ Blocking gates — run 2026-09-15

Booted from this compose with nothing overridden. Boot matched prediction exactly:
`max_total_num_tokens=451633 max_running_requests=2 max_mamba_cache_size: 63`.

- [x] `verify-full.sh` — **rc=0, 10/10**
- [x] `verify-stress.sh` — boundary 5/5 · recall 3/3 · ceiling ladder **6/6 → 240,660 tok (91%)**. rc=1 on one check only: VRAM margin **949 MB vs the 1,024 MB threshold**. Not depth-driven (957 MB at ladder start → 949 MB at 240K; SGLang preallocates the pool), and `soak` found nothing to absorb it.
- [x] `soak-test.sh --continuous` — **PASS**: growth **0 / 200 MiB**, 0 errors, 0/25 silent-empty, 100% TPS retention
- [x] `quality-test.sh --pack cli-40` — **29/40 (72%)**. ⚠️ Read as a **baseline, not a delta**: no prior *same-engine* cli-40 run exists for this compose. All 11 failures are `verifier_fail`; this PR changes only memory sizing, so none is expected to be config-sensitive (accept len 3.55 confirms a healthy drafter).
- [x] `bench.sh` — narrative **74.00** / code **101.58** decode TPS (CV 3.0% / 3.8%) · TTFT 129 ms · prefill 1,127 t/s @10K, 934 t/s @90K · **VRAM leak 8 MiB**
- [ ] **BENCHMARKS.md row — follow-up, not done here.** There is currently *no* SGLang row for this compose; this run is its first recorded bench, so the row is a new entry rather than an edit.

Full table: [gate-results comment](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/pull/1329#issuecomment-5685539349).

## ⚠️ Known-stale on merge, deliberately not fixed here

Seven slugs cite dual-fast's old **409,552** as their "for 2×24GB use…" reference and become wrong when this lands: `dual-max`, `multi4-max`, `multi8-max`, `multi4-supermax`, `multi8-supermax`, `multi4-fast`, `multi8-fast`. Batching them into this PR would bury the actual change; they should follow once the numbers are gated and final.

## Caveat that outranks the config

A long cold prefill freezes every new request for its full duration — 87 ms → ~265,000 ms (~3,000×) at 207K. Four knobs were tested and all were null; the fix is upstream sgl#34623, open and unmerged. **Two concurrent sessions does not mean two responsive sessions when one is ingesting a large document.**

Detail: `learnings/qwen3.8-27b.md` and `learnings/sglang-engine.md`, 2026-09-15.

body:
`docs/KV_MATH.md` stated *"only the 16 full_attention layers contribute to the growing KV cache"*, and `tools/kv-calc.py` computed per-token KV from `num_attn_layers` alone. **Both under-predict on every drafter compose.**

## The finding

The built-in MTP head is a **17th KV-bearing layer**. Found by prediction failure: sweeping `--max-mamba-cache-size` on Qwen3.8-27B (SGLang v0.5.19, TP=2, fp8 KV) gives an exactly linear state↔KV exchange rate. A 16-layer model predicts **2,394** tokens/slot; measured is **2,253.2** — a ratio of exactly **17/16**, and `text_config.mtp_num_hidden_layers` is 1.

`kv-calc` modelled the drafter only as `effective_ctx = max_ctx + mtp_n * 32` — ~128 tokens on a 262K window (**0.05%**) — when the real cost is **+6.25% of per-token KV, paid on every token**. The `mtp_n` plumbing already existed; only the layer count was missing.

## What changed

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `tools/kv-calc.py` | new `_kv_bearing_layers()`; both per-token sites use it |
| `q_fields` | `+ mtp_num_hidden_layers` — **without this the fix is silently inert** (`spec.get()` returns `None`) |
| `models/qwen3.6-27b.yml`, `models/qwen3.8-27b.yml` | declare `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1` (the dataclass already supported it; neither profile set it) |
| `docs/KV_MATH.md` | corrected formula, the two drafter costs, and where the layer count comes from |

Three ends had to be wired for this to do anything — the first patch applied cleanly, parsed, and changed nothing.

## Validation

`tools/kv-calc.py --calibration`: **8/8 verdicts unchanged**, and `qwen3.6-27b dual` moves **19.91 → 20.45 GB** against a measured **23.60** — i.e. toward truth.

⚠️ That suite scores PASS/TIGHT **categories**, not numeric accuracy. The residual ~3 GB under-prediction is a separate matter and is **not** addressed here.

Targeted gates (scoped change — profile *data*, not schema): `test-model-weights-registry`, `test-profiles-compat`, `test-compose-registry-disk` all pass; `migrate_registry_to_yaml --check` reports canonical.

## Deliberately NOT fixed

**External drafters.** DFlash2 carries its own KV-bearing layers at a *different* geometry (5 `sliding_attention` layers, 8 kv_heads, head_dim 128 → **+31.25%** measured, also per-token and not window-bounded). Approximating that as "21 layers at the main model's shape" would be wrong, so those composes stay under-predicted and it is documented in `KV_MATH.md` rather than silently approximated.

Detail and the measurement trail: `learnings/sglang-engine.md`, 2026-09-15.
title: Count the built-in MTP head as a KV-bearing layer

body:
Closes #1319.

## The arithmetic was wrong in four ways

A single block asserting `max_mamba_cache_size=33` was pasted across all five dual composes. Measured 2026-09-14 on the reference 2×3090 TP=2:

| compose | measured K |
|---|--:|
| `autoround-int4/mtp.yml` | **55** |
| `autoround-int4/dflash2-bf16.yml` | **34** |
| `autoround-int4/dflash2.yml` | **33** |
| `fp8/mtp.yml` | **21** |
| `fp8/dflash2.yml` | **8** |

One was right. All four corrections are verified in the pinned v0.5.19 source, not inferred:

1. **No `−1` for a sink slot.** `MambaSlotAllocator.clear()` builds `torch.arange(1, size+1)` with slot 0 reserved separately — K is already net. The expression is `K − k × C`.
2. **`k` is not fixed at 3** — `common.py:26-29` sets it by `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy`: `extra_buffer=3`, `extra_buffer_lazy=2`, `no_buffer=1`.
3. ⭐ **The concurrency clamp uses a different ratio.** `_calculate_mamba_ratio()` gives `r = 5 / 4 / 3` for those strategies, and `resolve_max_num_reqs()` caps at `K // r`. It predicts every clamp we measured — 55→8, 33→**6**, 21→4, 8→**1**. ⚠️ `fp8/dflash2` (K=8) can run **exactly one request** whatever `MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS` says.
4. ⚠️ **`extra_buffer_lazy` is not a free saving** — the auto-fit solve `K = floor((B − p(1+D)) / (p(1+D/r)))` uses `r`, so 5→4 raises the denominator and can *shrink* K.

Independent corroboration arrived while this was being written: the community TP=4 compose in #1321 ships `--max-mamba-cache-size 80` with `--max-running-requests 16`, and **80 // 5 = 16** exactly.

Each compose now carries **its own** measured K. The eight multi4/multi8 composes — which can never boot on a 2-GPU rig — get the formula plus *"read your own `Mamba Cache is allocated` boot line"* instead of a borrowed constant. Nothing is pasted across tiers again.

Every table also now distinguishes **configured / effective / offered** concurrency, and points at the `max_total_num_tokens=… max_running_requests=N …` line, since `server_args=` echoes the *request* rather than what took effect.

## Knobs added — opt-in, default OFF

`SESSION_RADIX_CACHE` and `RADIX_EVICTION_POLICY`, as **bare** pass-throughs (`- VAR=${X:-}` sets the empty string, and `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE` is an `EnvBool` where empty ≠ unset).

`SESSION_RADIX_CACHE` is a **0/1 gate that sets both the env var and the CLI flag**, because upstream requires both and setting one alone is silently inert — the same reasoning behind the existing `W4A8` boolean.

⛔ **No `--radix-eviction-policy-config` knob.** Upstream docs describe it, but it does not exist in v0.5.19 and passing it hard-fails the boot with `unrecognized arguments`. Found by booting the compose, not by reading the docs.

## ⛔ HiCache deliberately not exposed

`--enable-hierarchical-cache` on a hybrid GDN model allocates host pools, backs up to them, retains them — and **never serves a host hit**. Measured twice:

| | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|--:|--:|
| D→H backup (kv / mamba) | 32,700 / 16 | 52,604 / 26 ✅ |
| host drops | 0 | 0 ✅ |
| host occupancy | 87% | 63% (37% free) |
| return `device` / `host` | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0** ⛔ |
| H→D load-back | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0** ⛔ |

`cached_tokens_total{cache_source="host"}` was never even instantiated — a labelled counter isn't exported until first use, so the host read path has not fired once.

Root cause: **[sgl-project/sglang#33713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33713)** (open). On device eviction `_evict_host_leaf` consults only the FULL component's `host_value`, so a node whose MAMBA component already committed to host is **pruned from the tree wholesale** instead of downgraded — the host bytes are orphaned.

**No in-pin workaround**: the `hi_mamba_radix_cache` path the issue calls unaffected does not exist in v0.5.19, and `--radix-cache-backend` only accepts externally registered plugins. Enabling it would cost ~`HICACHE_GB × TP` of host RAM for nothing. Each compose records the re-test trigger.

## Test

13/13 composes parse. `test-no-bare-grep`, `test-locale-utf8`, `test-compose-status-drift`, `test-compose-mounts-resolve`, `test-compose-registry-disk`, `test-patch-attribution`, `test-compose-cache-report` all pass. Scoped rather than the full sweep — no catalog-shape change here.

Detail in `learnings/sglang-engine.md` 2026-09-14.

title: sglang: correct the GDN slot arithmetic, add prefix-cache knobs, keep HiCache off (#1319)

body:
## The bug

`report.sh`'s KV-pool block greps three **vLLM-only** patterns:

```
Available KV cache memory|GPU KV cache size:|Maximum concurrency for
```

SGLang emits none of them. So the block has been **silently empty on every SGLang report ever submitted** — no error, no warning, just a section that never rendered. That is why no report in the tracker carries a pool figure for an SGLang slug, and why #1319 had to be answered by booting locally rather than reading existing reports.

## What it now captures

- **`Mamba Cache is allocated. max_mamba_cache_size: N`** — the binding constraint on concurrency for hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.8 et al), *not* the KV byte pool. Each running request locks 3 slots, so usable warm prefixes = `N − 1 − 3 × max_running_requests`. It is topology- and tier-dependent, and multi4/multi8 can **never** be measured on a 2-GPU rig — a community report is the only way those numbers reach us.
- `KV Cache is allocated. … #tokens: N`
- **`max_total_num_tokens=… max_running_requests=N …`** — the *effective* limits. SGLang **clamps** `max_running_requests` to what the pool supports, while `server_args=` echoes the **request**, so the two disagree: asking for 8 resolved to **6** on the DFlash2 tier and **8** on the MTP tier (reference 2×3090, 2026-09-14). Reading the wrong one is easy — it was done in #1319 and corrected there.
- `Decode batch … #running-req: N … mamba usage: X` — the concurrency actually reached and its slot cost, which is what distinguishes a real ceiling from an inherited default.

## Detail worth keeping

Allocation lines print **once at boot** while `Memory pool end` repeats per rank, so tailing the union drops the mamba line — the one that matters. Allocation is taken from the HEAD of the log, the effective-limits line from the TAIL.

## Test

Verified against a live `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19` container: the new patterns return the mamba/KV/limits lines, the old pattern returns nothing. The 6 `test-report-*` gates plus `test-no-bare-grep` and `test-locale-utf8` pass.

body:
Follow-up to #1317. **That PR merged green and then failed on the maintainer's checkout** — the gate was right, my validation wasn't. I developed in a fresh worktree, which has no local layer, so this was invisible there.

## The defect

`_COPY_TREES` includes `scripts/lib`, so `shutil.copytree` dragged `scripts/lib/profiles-local/` — **the real local layer of whoever runs the suite** — into every test's tmp root. The tests then inherit that machine's promoted models.

So they pass on a clean checkout and fail on any rig that has ever run `promote.py --layer local` — which is exactly the feature they cover. The sharpest case is `test_no_local_layer_returns_core_identity`, whose entire assertion is *"no local layer"*; a stray real one silently destroys it.

## Repro

Copying the maintainer's layer into a clean worktree:

```
real layer present  ->  14 failed, 109 passed
no local layer      ->  123 passed
```

## Fix

Add `profiles-local` to the copytree ignore in all three fixtures. Every test already seeds the synthetic layer it needs (`_write_local`, `_seed_local`, or promote.py creating it), so the real one is pure contamination.

**Verified both directions**, since testing only one is what let this through in the first place:

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| real local layer present | **123 passed** (was 14 failed) |
| no local layer | **123 passed** |

## Also

Fixes the same mangled comment splice in `test_export_pr.py` that `test_local_registry.py` carried — `ignore=shutil.` followed by three comment lines and then `ignore_patterns(...)`. Valid Python via implicit line joining inside the parens, which is why it never errored, but it reads as broken.

## Test

9 local-layer / pytest / locale / grep gates pass, plus 123/123 pytest under both layer conditions.

title: Isolate the pytest fixtures from the machine's real local layer (follow-up to #1317)

body:
Closes #1316. Fixes the 34 dead tests, then wires them in — both in one PR, so they can't rot again in the gap.

| module | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_promote.py` | 12 failed, 8 passed | **22 passed** |
| `test_export_pr.py` | 14 failed, 2 passed | **18 passed** |
| `test_local_registry.py` | 8 failed, 3 passed | **17 passed** |
| `test_model_spec.py` | 0 failed, 66 passed | 66 passed |

Most of it was mechanical — slugs moved to `<engine>/<name>`, and the `local/` assertions inverted (it is now the *refused* namespace, not the required one). Four things were not.

## ⭐ A real product bug: core promote could write into the gitignored local layer

`validate_spec`'s **local** branch refuses a compose path that escapes the layer. The **core** branch had no symmetric check — a core write could point `compose_path` at `scripts/lib/profiles-local/composes/…`, which is gitignored. The curated registry would then reference a file that exists on the maintainer's disk and nowhere else.

It was unreachable only by accident: every local-layer spec also carried a `local/` slug, so the namespace check refused first. #1205 removed that namespace and left nothing standing behind it. Guard added, with the test commenting *why it used to pass for the wrong reason* — that distinction is the whole point of the exercise.

## ⭐ A user-facing message that said the inverse of the truth

#1205 correctly flipped `export_pr.py`'s condition:

```diff
-        if not str(e["slug"]).startswith(_LOCAL_SLUG_PREFIX):
+        if str(e["slug"]).startswith(_LOCAL_SLUG_PREFIX):
```

…but left the wording, so a slug that plainly **used** `local/` was told it *"lacks the `'local/'` namespace"*. Anyone upgrading across #1205 with an existing `registry.local.json` meets this exact message. It now says what happened and names the replacement slug.

## ⭐ `registry.yaml` was not in canonical form — on master

`migrate_registry_to_yaml.py --check` failed on master, and had since the FA2 work: I hand-added `supported_sm` to `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast` without running the check `AGENTS.md` mandates after a hand edit. Pure key reorder — **7 lines moved, zero content change** — but `test_entry_file_merges_and_get_registry_loads_it` asserts that gate passes, so the test was reporting a genuine defect rather than being stale.

## ⭐ Duplicate `REPO` in `test_promote.py`

Defined at `parents[1]` (`scripts/`) for the `sys.path` insert, then redefined at `parents[2]` (repo root), with a comment truncated mid-sentence between them. The import worked only because pytest adds rootdir — which is why running the module directly dies with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'`. Consolidated; the comment restored.

## The wiring

`scripts/tests/test-pytest-modules.sh` runs `python3 -m pytest` over `scripts/tests/test_*.py`, so the existing one-command sweep picks them up with no new entry point.

Two deliberate choices, both documented in the script:

- **Globs `test_*.py`, not `*.py`.** `lib-scan-bare-grep.py` is a scanner *library* consumed by `test-no-bare-grep.sh`; globbing it produces a spurious failure. That is exactly how #1316 was first mis-scored.
- **A missing pytest is a hard FAIL, not a skip.** Skipping would reproduce the precise defect this guard exists to close: a gate that is green because it did nothing.

**Negative control run before trusting it** — injected a failing assertion, confirmed the gate exits 1 and names the test; removed it, confirmed exit 0.

## Test

20/20 on the gates touching promote / export / local-layer / registry / locale / grep, plus 123/123 pytest. Scoped deliberately rather than the full 172 — this is not a catalog-shape change.
