body:
Two commits: the measurement, then the default change it justifies.

---

## 1. `docs`: measured W4A8 on vLLM ultrafast; corrected SGLang W4A8 provenance

### vLLM `dual-ultrafast` — the "unvalidated" caveat was stale

The compose and registry note both carried `W4A8=1 unvalidated with this drafter on FA2`. That predates the #1274 FA2 fp8-KV plugin, so it was re-tested on the **shipped post-#1274 config** (fp8_e4m3 KV + `FLASH_ATTN` + DFlash2 n=7, vLLM 0.29.0), `MAX_MODEL_LEN` pinned to 204800 on both arms so activation dtype is the only variable.

| Metric | W4A8=1 | W4A16 | delta | CV (A / B) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| prefill @10K tok/s (n=3) | **1862.9** | 1276.3 | **+46.0%** | 0.1% / 0.0% |
| prefill @90K tok/s (n=1) | **1441.3** | 1051.1 | **+37.1%** | n=1 |
| decode narrative TPS (n=5) | 117.9 | **125.4** | −6.0% | 4.1% / 4.3% |
| decode code TPS (n=5) | 226.9 | 226.2 | +0.3% | 5.3% / 6.5% |

**The caveat is retired.** W4A8 does not harm the DFlash2 drafter: decode-window acceptance was 6.37/6.33 (W4A8) vs 6.65/6.40 (W4A16) against n=7, 76–81% per-position. A lone `Mean acceptance length: 2.00` window appears in **both** arms with identical shape (`Accepted: 1, Drafted: 7`, ~0.01 tok/s) — a single draft step in an otherwise idle 60 s metrics window during the 60–80 s 90K prefill. Metric artifact, not a drafter fault, and not arm-specific.

**Three stale artifacts fixed in the same file.** `dflash2.yml` (ultrafast) was copied from `dflash2-fp8.yml` (superfast, which ships `W4A8=1`) and the default was flipped to `0` without adjusting the prose: the env block read `⭐ W4A8 (int8 activations) SHIPS ON` directly above `- W4A8=${W4A8:-0}`, and the entrypoint kept superfast's `$${W4A8:-1}` unset-fallbacks in two places. Unreachable through the compose (the env line always sets the var) but wrong for a bare `docker run`.

### SGLang (13 composes) — the W4A8 block was two weeks out of date

It still said the patch was **NOT vendored here** and that `W4A8=1` **hard-fails until #1226 merges**. It was vendored via #1248 on 2026-09-11 and is mounted by default. Replaced with the current state, keeping the hard-fail-not-silent-fallback guarantee (still true if the installer is missing) and the reason the re-cut is carried rather than referenced (the `K%128==0 / N%64==0` shape guard `prepare_w4a8` hard-asserts).

Two accuracy fixes on top of that rewrite:

- the `+44% / −11%` figures **were** measured on the reference rig 2026-09-11 — the table sits directly below them — so they are attributed to it rather than described as inherited and unmeasured
- **−11% is the MTP tier**; the DFlash2 tier measured ~flat. The two variants now say which is which instead of applying −11% blanket

No vLLM figures went into the SGLang composes and no SGLang figures into the vLLM one — different engines, different drafters.

---

## 2. `feat`: ship W4A8 ON by default on the ultrafast slugs

`W4A8` 0 → 1 on `{dual,multi4,multi8}/autoround-int4/dflash2.yml`, plus `act_format: int8` on the three registry slugs.

The tier exists for **code** decode and W4A8 does not move it (+0.3%), so +46% prefill is close to free for this tier's purpose.

⚠️ **Stated plainly because it matters:** the decode arms were **one boot each** against a ~2.8% boot-to-boot spread, so the −6.0% narrative is ~2σ and is **not** boot-confirmed. Four alternating boots were recommended before flipping; the maintainer's call was that the dual test is sufficient. Every file carrying the number still says it is single-boot, and `learnings/` records that the default was flipped with that uncertainty known — and that this is the first thing to re-test if a narrative regression ever appears on the tier. `W4A8=0` restores W4A16 and is documented as the arm to try for narrative-heavy serving.

This also removes a catalog inconsistency: ultrafast was the **only** slug marked `act8_capable: true` while serving `act_format: 16bit`. All nine fast-family slugs are now uniformly `int8`.

⚠️ `multi4`/`multi8` were flipped for tier consistency (fast and superfast are uniformly `W4A8=1` across all three topologies), but **neither has ever booted on the 2-GPU reference rig**. The measurement is the dual's; their comments and status notes say it transfers on TOPOLOGY ONLY, as every other number on those slugs does.

## Also

`BENCHMARKS.md` gains the two W4A8 rows plus the A/B explainer. The existing 2026-09-14 fp8/bf16 rows were two columns short of the table header — completed them.

## Test

`scripts/tests/*.sh` gate suite green on the final tree.

`exec_indices()` never stopped at a shell comment, so a comment could be reported
as executed code — contradicting the scanner's own stated scope ("EXECUTED greps
only") and its failure message ("A hit here IS in code").

It blocked #1313, a correct contributor PR, on this explanatory comment:

    # entirely (grep -m1 = first match). ENGINE_FAMILY is a global set at engine

The scanner flags `grep` when the preceding character is one of `|;&(`, and the
`(` put the word in apparent command position. Their actual code used
`command grep` and was right all along.

Scanning now stops at an unquoted `#` that starts a comment — line start or after
whitespace, top level only. `${VAR#prefix}` and `$#` are deliberately untouched
(their `#` follows a non-space character), as are comments inside `$( )`.

Gate: the existing planted-violation control stays, plus a negative control
feeding five non-executable lines (the comment above, an indented comment, a
trailing comment after valid code, `${VAR#prefix}`, advice in a string) requiring
zero hits — and a positive control on the same pass requiring a real
`ps | grep thing` to still be caught, so the negative control cannot pass by the
scanner silently breaking.

Verified: fails against the unfixed scanner (2 hits), passes after, and #1313
passes unchanged with this in place.

Full suite green.

## Summary

`spec-sweep.sh`'s acceptance scrape (`_measure_vllm_arm`) found its container with `grep -m1 -E 'vllm'`. On an `sglang-*` container `cn` comes back empty, so the `[[ -n "$cn" ]]` gate at line 211 kept the SGLang fallback (214) unreachable and every SGLang arm printed `—` for acceptance — the sweep could not find an acceptance knee on that engine at all. When more than one engine container is up, `grep -m1` also picked whichever came first, which could be the wrong engine entirely. The fix matches the container to the engine already resolved once via the canonical resolver into `ENGINE_FAMILY` (#1282); container names carry that token, so the scrape targets the right container. Seventh site in the #1282 family. One concern per PR: the `/metrics` `sglang:spec_accept_rate` source and the `READY_TIMEOUT` hint are deferred to their own PR/issue per the maintainer's call.

## Type of change

- [ ] New compose variant
- [ ] New patch / sidecar
- [ ] New script or tool
- [ ] New model
- [ ] Doc-only / typo
- [x] Other — one-line fix to existing `scripts/spec-sweep.sh` (container-name lookup in `_measure_vllm_arm`)

## Verification

Offline, all green:
- `bash -n scripts/spec-sweep.sh` — clean
- `test-spec-sweep.sh` — full hermetic run (docker stubbed, nothing booted), all 8 checks pass; the SLUG-guard assertion is untouched
- `test-engine-kind-resolver.sh` arm 4 — the "seventh site" private-classifier guard stays green (the change is a container-name match on the already-resolved global, not a re-classification)
- Container-name alignment (the fix depends on it), confirmed against master: `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` → `sglang` → `sglang-qwen38-27b-mtp-dual`; `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` → `vllm` → `vllm-qwen38-27b-dual-fast`

Live, before/after on the SGLang slug — the `accept` column is the proof. Before the fix, the `sglang-*` container left `cn` empty, so the SGLang arms printed `—`; after (this branch) the same arms populate:

```
=== spec-sweep summary (model=qwen3.8-27b) ===
  n     decode     accept
  0     131.59     —        <- drafter off on baseline arm; honest blank, not a bug
  2     170.75     0.57
  4     160.87     0.42
  sweet spot: n=2 (170.75 tok/s)
```

The `accept` column now reads on SGLang: MTP is net-positive (+29.8% at n=2 over the n=0 baseline), peaks at n=2, and acceptance falls 0.57 → 0.42 going n=2 → n=4 — a real knee. The vLLM path is unchanged (`ENGINE_FAMILY=vllm`, so the new grep equals the old).

The fix is in a measurement helper that runs only during a sweep; `verify-full.sh` exercises the serve/boot path, which this change does not touch, so a 35-min rig report would not exercise the changed line. body:
Three defects found by reproducing a Discord user's failure on a clean install. They are separate bugs but sit on one user journey — `setup.sh` then `switch.sh` for a gemma slug — and a new user hits all three in order. One commit each.

Fixes #1303
Fixes #1304
Fixes #1305

---

### 1. `setup.sh gemma-4-26b-a4b` downloaded 16 GB no slug can serve (#1303)

`profiles/models/gemma-4-26b-a4b.yml` carried `default_weight_variant: awq` against `setup: primary: autoround-int4-mixed`. That tier's composes had been moved to `_archive/` and no registry entry references the variant, but the setup block was never repointed — so the obvious path downloaded the wrong 16 GB, skipped the 17 GB both slugs need, and failed at `switch.sh` time.

Dropped the override so setup falls back to the profile default. The weights entry itself stays registered (kv-calc and the `arch_patches` / `profile_runtime` evidence rows still name it).

`setup.primary` is a deliberate override mechanism, so the new gate is **not** "primary == default_weight_variant" — that would red the two models that override it correctly (`qwen3.8-27b` → fp8, `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` → unsloth-iq2-xxs). It asserts the weaker invariant true of all three: whatever setup fetches, some registry entry must serve it. It is also status-agnostic — a deprecated entry still pins its variant, and three models' primaries are referenced only by deprecated slugs today, which is a different question.

### 2. The MTP drafter was opt-in behind a flag with no user-facing surface (#1304)

`WITH_ASSISTANT_DRAFT=1` existed in the model profile, in `setup.sh`'s implementation and in a test — and nowhere a user would look, while its siblings `WITH_DFLASH_DRAFT` and `WITH_VISION` were at least in the header comment. `vllm/gemma-26ba4b-single` defaults to `SPEC_N=4`, so a user who did not set it got a bare missing-`config.json` naming neither the cause nor either fix. The working escape hatch (`SPEC_N=0`, standardised across every vLLM compose by #1048) was not surfaced in the failure path either.

Three surfaces, working outward from the failure:

- The compose now refuses to boot when `SPEC_N>0` and the drafter has no `config.json`, naming **both** routes — same fail-loud contract the deepseek moecache composes carry for their external GGUF (#1054). Its header's `Drafter:` line now says how to obtain the file.
- `setup.sh --help` grows an "Optional extra downloads" section. The header comment was never the right surface: reading it means already having opened the script.
- The header comment gains the two flags it was missing.

`WITH_PRISM_EAGLE3` turned out to be undocumented in both places too — the new gate found it, so it is documented here as well.

`test-spec-toggle-contract` needed one change to be able to see any of this: it runs entrypoints in a sandbox, and a fail-loud check on a path embedded in the *entrypoint* (rather than in `command:`, which it already stubs) made the compose exit before emitting argv. It now redirects the container HF cache into the sandbox. Confirmed load-bearing, not cosmetic: the old gate reds against the new compose.

### 3. One transient stall aborted a 17 GB download with a traceback (#1305)

`_hf_download_repo` called the hub CLI once. Under `set -euo pipefail` a single `httpx.ConnectTimeout` mid-transfer aborted the whole run with a ~40-line unhandled traceback. Re-running resumed cleanly — nothing said so.

Bounded retry (4 attempts, 8s doubling to 120s, both env-tunable), and a give-up message that is an instruction rather than a traceback. The env hardening was already correct and is untouched; no external wrapper is introduced, since a shipped `setup.sh` cannot depend on anything outside the repo.

**Not implemented:** the stall watchdog the issue raises as a third option. An idle-but-not-erroring transfer is a different failure than a non-zero exit and a plain retry will not catch it — left for a follow-up rather than half-built.

---

## Validation

`for t in scripts/tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` — **172 pass / 0 fail** (master baseline was 168/0; four new test files).

Every new assertion was negative-controlled against the unfixed state first:

| Gate | Against the unfixed tree |
|---|---|
| `test-setup-primary-slug-backed` | FAILS, naming `gemma-4-26b-a4b` and nothing else — the two legitimate overrides are not flagged |
| `test-setup-optin-flags-documented` | FAILS on all four `WITH_*` flags as undocumented in `--help` |
| `test-compose-drafter-preflight` | FAILS showing `--speculative-config` reaching vLLM pointed at a directory that does not exist |
| `test-setup-download-retry` | FAILS on case 2 with the reported shape — one attempt, a traceback, rc=1 |
| `test-spec-toggle-contract` (edit) | The pre-change gate reds against the new compose, so the sandbox change is load-bearing |

Each also has an in-test positive control, so a scanner that quietly matched nothing cannot pass.

**Not verified:** nothing was boot-tested. There are no `gemma-4-26b-a4b` weights on the rig that produced this, and no container was started. The compose entrypoint was exercised with a stubbed `vllm`, not in an image — so what is proven is the shell logic and the messages, not engine behaviour. Likewise the retry was driven against a stubbed CLI: the loop and the give-up message are tested, but not that a real stalled 17 GB transfer resumes (#1305 verified that half independently, 1.1 GB → 6.4 GB with three `.incomplete` markers).

One hardening found while testing rather than from the issues: a mistyped `HF_DOWNLOAD_RETRIES` used to die with `foo: unbound variable`, because `(( attempt >= max ))` resolves a non-numeric value as a variable name — a crash inside the code that handles crashes. It now errors clearly, and case 5 covers it.

body:
Stage 1 of #1308. #1274 landed @AntonProkopyev's FA2 fp8-KV kernel on
`dual-ultramax`; this extends it to `dual-ultrafast` — the one other ultra slug
the reference rig can genuinely validate (TP=2, SM 8.6, and a KV/decode change
rather than a prefill one, so the rig's missing PCIe P2P is not in the way).

## Measured on 2×3090, 2026-09-14

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| KV | bf16 | **fp8_e4m3** |
| max_model_len | 204,800 | **262,144** |
| KV pool | 212,977 tok | **421,970 tok** (1.61× concurrency) |
| attention backend | FLASH_ATTN | FLASH_ATTN (unchanged) |

```
[fa2] verified artifact=731d1942...; FLASH_ATTN plugin; runtime vLLM=0.29.0
kv_cache_dtype: 'fp8_e4m3'   attention_backend: 'FLASH_ATTN'
[spec] DFlash2 EXTERNAL drafter ON - n=7
request -> "Paris"   (thinking on and off)
```

## Three open questions from #1308, now answered

1. **Is the kernel weight-agnostic?** Yes. It is an *attention* kernel, so
   autoround-int4 weights look no different to it than fp8. The issue reasoned
   this; it is now measured.
2. **Does `flashinfer-decode-pin` (#1089) conflict?** No. `ultrafast` installs
   that patch and `ultramax` does not, so this was the real interaction risk.
   They coexist.
3. **Was the 204,800 ceiling caused by bf16 KV?** Yes. Halving bytes per token
   lifted it to the same 262,144 its sibling runs, with headroom left over.

## The stale rationale

The slug's `status_note` carried the justification for the old configuration:

> fp8 KV would force FlashInfer and cost ~40% decode (measured 74/138)

That is precisely the constraint the plugin removes — it registers an fp8
extension *through* the FLASH_ATTN API, so fp8 KV and FLASH_ATTN now coexist on
sm_86. Rewritten to record what changed and when, rather than left contradicting
the config it describes.

## Decode IS measured now — and it is a trade, not a free win

Four boots, **alternating A,B,A,B**, `MAX_MODEL_LEN` pinned to 204800 on both arms
so only the KV dtype varies:

| KV | narrative | code | boot spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp8_e4m3 | 122.7 | 219.5 | 1.0% / 0.9% |
| bfloat16 | **126.9** | **249.6** | 0.2% / 0.5% |
| **fp8 vs bf16** | **-3.3%** | **-12.1%** | |

Both arms reproduce to within 1% across boots, so -12.1% on code decode is well
outside noise. Alternating boots mattered: a single pair per arm cannot separate a
real delta from the ~2.8% boot-to-boot spread, which has produced a false result
on this rig before.

**So fp8 KV buys +28% context (204,800 -> 262,144) and costs -12% code decode.**

### Why fp8 is still the right default *here*

This slug is 2-card. On bf16 it cannot reach the architecture maximum — 204,800 is
a VRAM ceiling, not a choice. fp8 is how a dual rig gets the full 262,144, and the
throughput cost is the price of that.

That reasoning does **not** extend to `multi4` / `multi8`, which already reach
262,144 on bf16 because they have the aggregate VRAM. Converting those would cost
-12% decode for zero context gain, so stage 2 of #1308 is withdrawn — see the
issue.

`KV_CACHE_DTYPE` remains the documented knob, so anyone who wants the old
behaviour has it one env var away:

```bash
KV_CACHE_DTYPE=bfloat16 MAX_MODEL_LEN=204800 bash scripts/switch.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast --force
```

### Still not measured

Quality at the new ceiling — no NIAH at 262K on this config, and the slug's note
already carried that caveat for 204800. Unchanged by this PR.

Stage 2 of #1308 — multi4/multi8 — is deliberately **not** in this PR. Those four
slugs cannot be booted on a 2-card rig, and the plugin is validated at TP=2 only.

Full suite green: **168 pass, 0 fail**.

Refs #1308.

---

body:
## The problem

32 live vLLM composes bind-mount a cache directory **into the repo tree** and run
the container as plain root, so every file vLLM writes there is root-owned on the
host and cannot be removed by the person who made the checkout.

Measured, not hypothetical — three worktrees on the reference rig after ordinary
boots:

| worktree | size | removable as the owner? |
|---|---|---|
| `club-3090-wt-fa2test` | 406 MB | no |
| `club-3090-wt-align` | 373 MB | no |
| `club-3090-wt-pf` | 164 MB | no |

`rm -rf` as the owner cleared everything except the cache dirs, leaving ~50 KB
root-owned skeletons. **779 MB needed `sudo`**, and every worktree used for a boot
reproduces it.

## The fix already existed

20 composes already carry this line; 32 never got it:

```yaml
user: "0:${DOCKER_GID:-1000}"
```

UID stays **0** — the vLLM images need root — while the GID becomes the invoking
user's, so files land group-writable and clean up normally. This applies the same
line to the remaining 32, placed after `container_name:` to match the existing
ones. No other behaviour changes.

## ⚠️ Why it looked fixed

`TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/root/.triton/cache` reads like a fix. It is not: the same
compose bind-mounts that exact container path straight back into the tree, so the
env var has no bearing on where the files land. A `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` passthrough
(`a9061d96`) is the real relocation hatch, but is wired in only 2 of 53 composes.

The cache dirs *are* gitignored — that half of the hygiene was done, the
ownership half was not.

## Scope

| | count |
|---|---|
| live composes bind-mounting a cache path | 52 |
| already setting the host GID | 20 |
| **fixed here** | **32** |
| `_archive/` composes | 21, deliberately untouched (historical records) |

## Gate

`scripts/tests/test-compose-cache-ownership.sh` asserts every live
cache-mounting compose sets the host GID, **and** that UID stays 0 — a
well-meaning `user: "1000:1000"` would break the container rather than the
cleanup, so the guard pins both halves.

Verified as a negative control: it fails against the unfixed tree naming all 52,
and passes after.

Fixes #1309.

body:
## The bug

`preflight.sh` refused to boot **every gemma slug with an external assistant
drafter**, reporting a file that is present on disk as missing:

```
[preflight] ERROR: compose '.../gemma-4-26b-a4b/vllm/compose/single/awq/int8.yml'
            expects model files that aren't on host.
[preflight]   missing: /mnt/models/huggingface/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-assistant\/config.json
```

Note `assistant\/config.json`. Exit 1, boot never starts, and nothing the user
does can satisfy it — the path it wants cannot exist.

## Cause

The in-container path extractor excluded `"` `'` whitespace and `,` but **not
backslash**. These composes write the drafter path inside escaped JSON:

```
--speculative-config "{\"model\":\"/root/.cache/huggingface/<dir>\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":$$_spec_n}"
```

so the match ran past the directory name, consumed the trailing `\` and stopped
at the quote, capturing `<dir>\`.

The comment above that line explains why the class was deliberately narrowed — so
`${MODEL_SUBDIR:-default}` is not truncated before the `:-default` resolver runs.
That reasoning is right; backslash just was not considered alongside it. One
character:

```diff
-  command grep -oE '/root/\.cache/huggingface/[^"'\''[:space:],]+'
+  command grep -oE '/root/\.cache/huggingface/[^"'\''\\[:space:],]+'
```

## Scope

8 composes, all gemma: `gemma-4-12b` ×2, `gemma-4-26b-a4b` ×1, `gemma-4-31b` ×5.

`qwen3.8-27b` is unaffected — its MTP drafter is built-in, so no external path
appears in the speculative config. Confirmed by booting
`vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` on the same rig the same day.

## Boot-verified, not just reasoned about

Same tree, same weights, with the fix:

```
[switch] 180s — Application startup complete
[spec] drafter ON - draft-model gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-assistant n=4
[speculative.py:882] Overriding draft model max model len from 262144 to 176000
request -> "Paris"   (20 prompt / 2 completion tokens)
```

Without it, the same tree refuses at preflight.

## Gate

New `scripts/tests/test-preflight-model-path-extract.sh`, four assertions:

1. preflight's own character class excludes backslash
2. no captured subdir across all **137** non-archived composes contains a
   character that cannot survive into a directory name
3. **negative control** — the pre-fix class captures **8** unusable paths on this
   same corpus. Without this, (2) could pass by matching nothing
4. the extractor still resolves **34** real paths

`}` is deliberately not treated as dirty: `${VAR:-default}` is resolved
downstream, which is the case the original narrowing existed to protect.

Verified the guard fails against unfixed `preflight.sh` and passes with it.

Fixes #1306. Found while reproducing a Discord report; the same user also hits
#1303 and #1304, and this one would block them even after those are solved.

## What this adds

`MODE=concurrent` — the case the other two modes miss. `depth` is one session,
`breadth` is many shallow ones. Both open reports turn on what a **second long
session** does, and on what happens at a **compaction**, which one user named as
their trigger ("when I compact I suddenly see the live TPS drop to around 25 and
stay there").

Five labelled phases, so every claim is attributable to a phase rather than
inferred from a curve:

```
grow            all sessions, round robin, to TARGET_CTX
baseline        reuse for every session before anything compacts
COMPACT A       A's history replaced by a summary, same session continues
after-compact   the others, immediately — did A's compaction cost them?
A regrow        A rebuilds; the compaction is cheap, rebuilding is not
after-regrow    the others again — did A's rebuild evict them?
```

Turns are interleaved **round-robin, never in parallel**. Only one request is
ever in flight, so `max_running_requests` stays 1 and the ACTIVE side of both
pools is held constant while warm-prefix state accumulates — which is the
variable under test. Running them in parallel would move both at once.

## Result of the first live run

`SESSIONS=2 TARGET_CTX=100000` on `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`, two sessions to
~107K each:

| phase | B cached / prompt | reuse |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 100,032 / 106,718 | 94% |
| after A compacts | 106,688 / 113,391 | **94%** |
| after A rebuilds 3 turns | 113,408 / 120,064 | **94%** |

**A compaction in one session does not disrupt a concurrent one**, nor does that
session rebuilding afterwards. The compaction itself is free — 48 tokens, 0.08 s.

It also **falsified the prediction it was built to test.** From a single-session
run ("49 of 55 mamba slots, ~2 per turn") I predicted two deep sessions would
need ~68 slots and could not coexist. Observed: 49/55 with both alive, pinned
there for the whole run. Slots are recycled within a session; the plateau in the
earlier run was the real behaviour, not the rising portion. Recorded in the
per-model learnings so the extrapolation is not repeated.

## Gate

Two contracts against the fake engine: one asserting every phase appears with
both sessions and an explicit neighbour verdict, one asserting that a server
which cannot report reuse yields "unobservable" rather than a survival claim —
the same absence-vs-zero discipline as the rest of the probe. Both verified as
negative controls: they fail against the pre-concurrent probe.

Full suite green.

Refs #1259.

body:
Three compose defects that share one blast radius, fixed in issue order as three commits. Each ships a guard that **fails against the pre-fix tree** — all three negative controls were run, and what they named is recorded below.

| # | Defect | Composes | New guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1297 | `--enable-cache-report` missing → `prompt_tokens_details: null` on every response | 15 SGLang | `test-compose-cache-report` |
| #1295 | healthcheck probes loopback from inside the container → cannot fail | 13 SGLang | `test-compose-healthcheck-reachability` |
| #1293 | `ESTATE_PORT` ignored → estate relocation silently binds the default | 12 vLLM + 2 SGLang | `test-compose-estate-port` |

---

## 1. `--enable-cache-report` — #1297

SGLang gates the whole `usage.prompt_tokens_details` block on this flag (`entrypoints/openai/usage_processor.py`, `enable_cache_report: bool = False`), so without it every response carries `prompt_tokens_details: null` — streaming and non-streaming alike — and `null` is indistinguishable from "nothing was reused". 0/15 SGLang composes passed it while 20 vLLM composes passed the counterpart `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` (#1246): the same probe answered on one engine and returned nothing on the other, with no error either way.

All 15 now pass it, beside `--enable-metrics` where the compose has one.

**The asymmetry that outlives the fix is documented, because it is the same misreading one layer up:** on SGLang **absent is not zero**. Even with the flag on, SGLang omits `cached_tokens` when the value is genuinely 0; vLLM sends `cached_tokens: 0` explicitly. A consumer that reads a missing field as "no reuse" still cannot tell no-reuse from reporting-off. Recorded in each compose and in `docs/INFERENCE_ENGINES.md`.

The guard ignores a flag that appears only in a **comment** — the #1292 lesson that a flag present in the file is not a flag present in the process.

## 2. Healthcheck reachability — #1295

Filed against SGLang, then corrected by the maintainer: the bind failure was ours (#1292, fixed in #1296). **This commit implements the part that survived the rescope** — the healthcheck itself.

```yaml
test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:30000/health || exit 1"]
```

runs *inside* the container against 127.0.0.1 — the one path that stays up when the bind address is wrong. While the server was bound to loopback, `docker ps` read `Up 27 minutes (healthy)` and the engine log showed repeated `200 OK` (its own probes) while every external client got an instant connection reset. It would have passed identically with the port mapping deleted outright. It tested liveness and read as reachability.

The 13 SGLang healthchecks now probe `${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}` — the address docker's port forward actually targets — with **no loopback fallback**, because degrading to the old probe would restore the silent pass. Nothing in this repo gates on container health (no `depends_on: service_healthy`; `switch.sh`'s ready probe curls the endpoint from the host), so an unhealthy mark is a visible signal rather than a boot blocker.

⚠️ **31 llama.cpp-family composes carry the identical probe.** They are out of scope here and could not be validated without booting, so the guard carries them as a named `KNOWN_LOOPBACK` debt register rather than a silent exemption. The gate fails **both** ways — on any unregistered loopback probe, and on a registered entry that no longer has one — so the register cannot rot. Both directions were exercised.

## 3. `ESTATE_PORT` — #1293

`${ESTATE_PORT:-${PORT:-NNNN}}` is already mandatory per `docs/ADDING_MODELS.md` ("Env hooks mandatory … estate mode breaks without them") and is what `generate_compose.py` emits — but nothing enforced it, and 14 hand-written composes had drifted off it: 12 bound `${PORT:-…}` with no `ESTATE_PORT` level at all, and 2 bound `${ESTATE_PORT:-…}` with no `PORT` fallback, leaving users without the plain knob the other 156 have.

The symptom is not "wrong port": a probe against the relocated port returns `Connection refused` against a perfectly healthy container with a clean log, which reads as a dead server.

Reproduced and fixed statically, rendering through `docker compose config`:

| file | env | published |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix | `ESTATE_PORT=8199` | **8101** ← the reported incident |
| fixed | `ESTATE_PORT=8199` | 8199 |
| fixed | `PORT=8222` | 8222 |
| fixed | both set | 8199 (ESTATE_PORT wins) |
| fixed | neither | 8101 (default unchanged) |

**No default port changed** and `registry.yaml` `default_port` values are untouched. The guard also asserts the generator still emits the chain, so a newly generated compose cannot regress silently.

ⓘ Nuance worth recording, because it explains the long survival: `estate_cli.compose_env()` sets **both** `ESTATE_PORT` and `PORT` to the instance port, so the estate CLI's own path was masked on the 12. Any other producer of `ESTATE_PORT` — a user following the documented contract, an override file, a tool that sets only that variable — hit the bug.

---

## Validation

**Full guard suite** — `for t in scripts/tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done`

| run | result |
|---|---|
| baseline, before any change | **161 pass / 0 fail** |
| after all three commits | **164 pass / 0 fail** |

(161 → 164 is the three new guards.)

**Negative controls.** Each new guard was run against the *unfixed* tree before its fix landed and had to fail. A gate that passes both before and after proves nothing.

| guard | vs unfixed tree | what it named |
|---|---|---|
| `test-compose-cache-report` | ❌ exit 1 | exactly the 15 SGLang composes |
| `test-compose-healthcheck-reachability` | ❌ exit 1 | exactly the 13 SGLang healthchecks; the 31 registered llama.cpp entries correctly not flagged |
| `test-compose-estate-port` | ❌ exit 1 | exactly the 12 `PORT`-only + 2 `ESTATE_PORT`-only |

Each guard also runs its **own positive control first**, on planted fixtures, through the *same* scanner as the real run — so a scan that silently matched nothing could not read as a clean tree.

### Verified vs assumed

**Verified:**
- Full guard suite green, against a green 161/0 baseline taken on the same tree beforehand.
- `docker compose config` renders every edited compose; the port-precedence table above is measured output, including the pre-fix reproduction.
- The healthcheck's `$$` escaping is the same convention the `command:` block in these same files already relies on in production, and `docker compose config` round-trips it identically to that block. The raw YAML parses to the intended string with real quotes.
- `${HOSTNAME:-$(hostname)}` executed under POSIX `sh` with `HOSTNAME` set and unset — resolves the container-routable name both ways, never loopback.

**NOT verified — no container was started.** Both GPUs were busy with a live measurement run, so nothing here was booted. Specifically **not** shown at runtime:
- that SGLang actually emits `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` on a repeated prompt;
- that the new healthcheck reports *healthy* against a correctly-bound server (it is designed to fail against a loopback-bound one, but neither direction was observed live);
- that `--enable-cache-report` is accepted by `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12`, the pin on the two **PARKED** `qwen3.6-27b` eagle3 composes. The 13 live composes are on `v0.5.19`, where the issue author read the flag out of the installed source.

Those are the acceptance checks that still need the rig.

Fixes #1297
Fixes #1295
Fixes #1293

body:
## What this adds

`scripts/deep-context-probe.sh` — the first instrument here that reaches the
context range users actually run in. Every existing bench stops at ~35K
accumulated context (`bench-agentic.sh` caps at 15 turns, `bench.sh` is
single-turn, `soak-test.sh` measures *generated* tokens), so everything above
that was unmeasured rather than known-good. Filed as #1259.

Two modes:

- **`MODE=depth`** — one conversation grown turn by turn to a target context,
  recording per-turn TTFT, decode rate, prefix reuse, drafter acceptance,
  preemptions and pool residency.
- **`MODE=breadth`** — many concurrent-ish sessions against a sized KV pool, to
  test whether re-querying an older session still reuses its prefix.

Runs against both engines; counter names and semantics were verified against a
running SGLang v0.5.19 and the vLLM v0.29.0 package source, not inferred.

## Validated live, both engines

Run end-to-end on `vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-fast` and `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-fast`
(matched pair: same compose family, drafter, KV format, TP and ceiling), to
141,714 accumulated tokens each. Neither engine collapses on prompt depth —
vLLM decode -6.4%, SGLang -22.7%, converging within 1 tok/s.

## The probe was wrong before the engines were — four times

This is most of the diff, and each fix carries a negative control that fails
against the previous implementation.

1. **Decode measurable on one basis only.** Timing needed two differing usage
   chunks, and a sub-100ms window dead-ended at `n/a` rather than falling
   through. Now four bases in descending fidelity, the one used named per row,
   and an `n/a` carries the stream shape that caused it.
2. **The probe taught the model to be terse.** Feeding its own replies back made
   any downward drift self-reinforce: 48 → 4 tokens, decode `n/a` from 104K.
   Truncation was only the trigger — with an ask that fit the cap it still went
   40 → 2 by 98K. Two same-boot controls isolated it: single-turn held 48/48 at
   190,670 tokens, fixed-history multi-turn showed no trend to 144,521. Only the
   fed-back arm collapsed. The history is now a fixed turn.
3. **A verdict named a mechanism it could not observe** (#1299). Breadth printed
   "CLEAN eviction" with no pressure input at all, so the same string appeared
   whether or not eviction was possible — and the pressure model itself was
   wrong, since eviction was measured at ~66% of the nominal pool.
4. **A zero gauge read as a dead drafter.** SGLang leaves `spec_accept_rate` at 0
   until a speculation step completes, so early turns read 0.00 and the probe
   cried "ACCEPTANCE LOW" at a healthy drafter.

Common shape: an instrument stating a **conclusion** where it holds only an
**observation**. Worth applying to any new column.

## Gate

New `scripts/tests/test-deep-context-probe.sh`, 16 contracts against a fake
engine reproducing shapes measured on real servers. Full suite green on the
merged tree.

Known gaps, deliberately not closed here: context still grows from synthetic
filler rather than tool calls and file reads, and there is no concurrent or
compaction mode. Both are named in #1259 and are the next increment.

Refs #1259. Closes #1299.

---

body:
**Regression introduced by #1292 (`cfa2df09`) and merged.** All 5 SGLang dual composes have been shipping with speculative decoding silently disabled and the server unreachable from the host.

## What happened

The documentation block #1292 added landed immediately after a line continuation:

```
--mem-fraction-static "${MEM_FRACTION:-0.82}" \
# ⭐ MAMBA STATE SLOTS vs CONCURRENCY — measured 2026-09-13 …
```

The `\` splices the comment onto the command, the `#` comments out the remainder of that logical line, and because the command is an `exec` the shell is replaced immediately — so **every flag after that point never reached the server**.

| flag | effect of losing it |
|---|---|
| `--host 0.0.0.0` | bound `127.0.0.1` — **unreachable from the host** |
| `--enable-metrics` | `/metrics` 404 |
| `--served-model-name` | fell back to the raw model path |
| `--reasoning-parser` / `--tool-call-parser` | parsers unset |
| the `SPEC` array | **`speculative_algorithm: None`** |

That last row is the serious one: **DFlash2 was off on slugs whose entire purpose is the drafter.** `dual-superfast` was serving with no speculative decoding at all.

## Verified on-rig, same compose before and after

```
host                   '127.0.0.1'  ->  '0.0.0.0'
enable_metrics         False        ->  True
served_model_name      <model path> ->  'qwen3.8-27b'
speculative_algorithm  None         ->  'DFLASH'
```

The fix moves the note **above the `exec`**, where no continuation is active. The content is unchanged — it's good documentation in the wrong place.

## ⛔ Why nothing caught it

The entire compose suite was green on the broken tree. The YAML parses, every flag is present in the file, the container starts, and its healthcheck passes — because that healthcheck curls loopback **from inside the container**, which is the one path that cannot fail here. Only the engine's own resolved `server_args` disagreed with the compose text, and nothing compared them.

It also cost real diagnostic time: the unreachable server was investigated as a crash, then as IPv6 resolution, then as a docker-proxy fault, before `/proc/net/tcp` showed the bind address. #1295 was filed blaming SGLang for ignoring `--host` — **that diagnosis was wrong** and I'll correct it.

## New gate

`test-compose-continuation-comments.sh` — scans for a **code** line ending in `\` followed by a comment.

```
negative control  pre-fix : exit 1, flags exactly the 5 broken composes
                  post-fix: exit 0
positive control  plants a violation in a temp tree and requires the scanner to find it
```

⚠️ Deliberately narrowed to **code** continuations. A first pass flagged 46 lines inside doc blocks — pasted shell that legitimately wraps across comment lines — and a gate with that false-positive rate is one maintainers learn to ignore.

title: fix(sglang): a doc comment after a line continuation silently dropped every flag after it

body:
Refs #1264 (item 5). **Docs only — no flag defaults changed.**

## The question

The cookbook's rtx5090 cell warns that *"on this 32GB card the GDN state pool, not KV, is what runs out first"*. #1264 asked whether that holds on 24 GB Ampere, since it could move `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` across the tier.

## Measured answer: it's breadth-dependent, and inverted for our shipped shape

**Depth is nearly free.** A 14-turn / ~33K-token conversation never evicted at 14 slots — TTFT flat at 1.56 s → 1.81 s, no discontinuity.

**Breadth costs one slot per distinct prefix:**

| | 14 slots (`ratio 0.3`) | 29 slots (`ratio 0.9`) |
|---|--:|--:|
| conv 1 re-query after 20 conversations | **1.558 s** — evicted | **0.362 s** — survived |
| conv 20 re-query | 0.086 s | 0.086 s |
| conv 1 cold first visit | 1.540 s | 2.158 s |

At 14 slots, conversation 1's re-query cost matched its *cold* first visit — a full re-prefill. At 29 slots the same 20 conversations didn't evict it. The 0.362 s is a partial hit rather than the 0.086 s of the newest conversation, consistent with interior radix nodes being trimmed while the tail is preserved.

## The arithmetic worth having next to the flag

From SGLang's own bs=1 floor comment — each running request locks 1 active + 2 radix checkpoints, plus a global sink:

```
usable warm-prefix slots = max_mamba_cache_size - 1 - 3 x max_running_requests
```

At the 33 slots this shape gets by default:

| `--max-running-requests` | usable |
|--:|--:|
| 1 | 29 |
| 4 | 20 |
| 8 | 8 |
| 10 | 2 |
| 11 | **infeasible** |

**Raising concurrency spends the prefix cache twice** — 3 slots per stream, and more distinct conversations competing for what remains. That's the part that wasn't written down anywhere.

## The ratio trade

Within a **fixed** budget — VRAM was identical across arms to within 10 MiB:

```
ratio 0.9 (default) -> 33 slots, 279,595 KV tokens
ratio 0.3           -> 14 slots, 314,251 KV tokens   (+12.4% KV)
```

**Deliberately not changed.** Lowering it suits single-stream work, where few distinct prefixes stay warm and KV is the real constraint. For a multi-conversation estate the cookbook's warning applies and 0.9 is correct. It's a per-tier call, so the composes document the trade rather than pick for the operator.

## Scope

Note added to the 5 `dual` composes — the shape actually measured. `multi4`/`multi8` get a different `max_mamba_cache_size` (more VRAM), so the specific numbers don't transfer and the note isn't copied there.

Compose gates green: `no-rig-paths`, `status-drift`, `args-array-scope`, `sampler-profiles`, `registry-disk`, `docs-slugs-resolve`.

title: docs(sglang): record the measured mamba-state-slot / concurrency arithmetic in the dual composes

body:
Closes #1290.

## The defect

`soak-helper.py` filtered every decode rate through `0 < t <= 500`. That ceiling guards a real artifact — a **client-timed** turn where `ttft ≈ wall` divides by a tiny window and yields an absurd rate — and the comment above it says exactly that.

It does not transfer to an engine counter. #1268 added engine-reported rates (`prom-tpot` / `sglang-log` / `llamacpp-log`), computed by the **engine** over its own decode steps, which structurally cannot divide by a tiny window. But `measured_rows` is every non-wall row, so engine rows inherited the same ceiling and correct measurements above 500 tok/s were **silently deleted** from `p50_decode_tps` and `tps_retention`.

## Worse than the issue described

When the over-ceiling rows are the only measured ones, the reported p50 isn't merely low — it is **`0.00`**. A fast rig's soak would report *zero decode throughput*. That's what the negative control shows.

**500 is reachable, not theoretical.** A passing soak on the reference rig reported `p50 269.84` on an instrument that reads 2–3× `bench.sh`, and 2× RTX 5090 with spec-decode clears it comfortably — which is the hardware sending us most of our community bench reports.

## Changes

- **The ceiling is basis-aware** (`CLIENT_RATE_CEILING`), applied to client-inferred bases only. `realistic()` is retained for wall-derived (canvas) rows, which *are* client-inferred.
- **A filtered row no longer vanishes.** A client-timed exclusion is reported with the offending value; an over-ceiling **engine** row is counted *and* disclosed, so the reader knows the figure includes rates that previously disappeared. The summary already owed a per-basis denominator (#1267) — a silent drop contradicted it.

## Negative control

```
pre-fix   exit 1
          FAIL: engine rows >500 counted — expected non-zero p50, got 0.00
          FAIL: over-ceiling disclosure — absent
          FAIL: client exclusion disclosure — absent
          ✓    client-timed artifact still excluded (p50=250.00)

post-fix  exit 0   (p50 650.00 over rows of 640/660)
```

The client-artifact arm passes in **both** states by design — it is the regression guard proving the original protection survives. The other three fail pre-fix.

Gates: `test-soak-engine-rate-ceiling`, `test-soak-decode-source`, `test-soak-decode-basis`, `test-soak-vram-baseline`, `test-locale-utf8`, `test-script-permissions`, `test-measurement-record` — all green.

title: fix(soak): stop the client-timing ceiling deleting engine-reported decode rates

`test-bench-capture` went red on master after #1283. **The red was the fix being correct** — the test had been passing through a shell syntax error, not through the code path it asserts.

## The chain

The offload-matrix fixture's `fake-nvidia-smi` implements *"exactly the two invocations the sweep makes"*, and `-L` is not one of them. So `p2p_gpu_count()` saw no `^GPU ` lines and returned 0 in that test.

The **old** `p2p_gpu_count` returned the two-line string `"0\n0"` (`grep -c` prints `0` *and* exits 1, so `|| echo 0` also fired). And `[[ "0\n0" -lt 2 ]]` is a **syntax error** — so bench.sh's single-card `if` went false, execution fell through into the multi-GPU branch, `CONTAINER=none` printed `custom-AR n/a`, and the assertion matched.

So the test exercised the **single-card** path while asserting the **multi-GPU llama.cpp** one. #1279 made `p2p_gpu_count` return one line, the guard started working, and the accident stopped.

## Two changes

**Fixture** — add an `-L` arm honouring the existing `FAKE_NGPU` knob, so `p2p_gpu_count` returns 2 and the test finally reaches the branch it asserts.

**Test** — assert the **precondition** before the assertion: fail loudly if the interconnect block took the single-card path, because a green custom-AR check means nothing there.

⚠️ Relaxing the assertion to accept either `n/a` wording would have made master green while preserving the hole. That was the tempting fix and it is the wrong one.

## Verification

```
with the -L arm      test-bench-capture  exit 0
with it reverted     exit 1 — "took the SINGLE-CARD path — the custom-AR
                     assertion below would pass vacuously"
```

All nine suites that own this fixture still pass: `offload-matrix-mocked`, `offload-matrix-static`, `p2p-state`, `p2p-validate`, `detect-nvlink-autop2p`, `detect-nvlink-alloc-conf`, `compose-nvlink-escape`, `compose-offload-drift`, `preflight-cpu-offload`.

The guard is an explicit `if` rather than `cmd && fail` — the latter is safe under `set -e` only because bash exempts the left operand of `&&`, and a test guard shouldn't depend on knowing that.

body:
Closes #1280.

## The gap

`test-bench-capture.sh` already gates this — for **one file**. 119 executed bare greps sat unguarded across 27 others.

Where it actually matters is **sourced** files: a sourced script runs inside the *caller's* shell, which is exactly where a shell-function shim reaches. An executed script gets `/usr/bin/grep` regardless. `preflight.sh` held 24 of the 119 and is sourced by 20 scripts.

## What changed

**119 occurrences converted across 27 files.** **11 left alone deliberately** — those sit inside `echo`/`printf` strings, i.e. commands we *print for a user to type*:

```
echo "      docker logs <container> 2>&1 | grep -oE 'accept len: [0-9.]+' | tail"
```

Rewriting user-facing advice to `command grep` would be wrong, and a gate that flags it is one maintainers learn to ignore.

## Why the gate is quote-aware, not a regex

A naive scanner gets two cases wrong in **opposite** directions:

| case | naive result | reality |
|---|---|---|
| `"$( … \| grep … )"` | skipped as "quoted text" | it is **code** — 17 of the 119, six in `preflight.sh` |
| heredoc body (`python3 <<'PY'`) | converted | may be another language where `grep` is an identifier |

That second one is not hypothetical. An earlier pass of this change rewrote a Python variable assignment into

```python
command grep = subprocess.run(...)
```

`test-engine-pin-bump` caught it. The scanner now skips heredoc bodies, and I verified afterwards that **zero** of the remaining conversions landed inside one.

⚠️ **Known limitation, deliberate:** skipping heredocs means shell-inside-a-heredoc is not guarded. That is the price of not corrupting embedded python/yaml, and it is documented in the gate rather than left implied.

## Controls

The gate runs a **positive control before its assertion** — it plants a violation in a temp tree and requires the scanner to find exactly one, and to ignore planted echo advice. A scan that silently finds nothing is otherwise indistinguishable from a clean tree, which is the failure mode this class keeps producing.

```
negative control   pre-fix : exit 1, exactly 119 violations reported
                   post-fix: exit 0
full sweep         157 passed, 0 failed
```

`test-locale-utf8` also caught the new gate shelling out to `python3` without `PYTHONUTF8` (#779) — fixed.

## ⚠️ Stacked PR

Base is `feat/report-resolved-config`. Merge order: **#1285 → #1286 → this**. Retarget downstream before merging a parent, and do not use `--delete-branch` on a parent (it closes the child).

body:
Closes #1265.

> ⚠️ **Stacked PR — targets `fix/centralise-engine-kind` (#1285), not `master`.**
> It is rebased onto that branch and must merge after it. #1285 introduces
> `scripts/lib/engine-kind.sh` and already edits `scripts/report.sh`; this branch
> builds on the `ENGINE_KIND` that resolver produces rather than re-deriving it.

## The gap

`report.sh --full` profiled the rig exhaustively — CPU, STREAM, THP, GPUs, PCIe,
P2P, disk, container state, kv-calc calibration — and captured **nothing about
the engine's configuration**. Eight `docker inspect` calls, never for
`Config.Cmd`, `Config.Entrypoint` or `Config.Env`. So an unexpected number in a
community report was unattributable: we could not tell a shipped recipe from a
modified one.

#1261 is the worked example. A clean `--full` report, and the three findings that
mattered — `--mem-fraction-static 0.82` (recipe 0.91), `--chunked-prefill-size
2048` (recipe 1024), and the drafter identity — came only from a boot log the
reporter happened to paste into a comment.

## Why this is not a compose dump

The obvious implementation is wrong, not merely incomplete:

1. **A compose is a template, not a configuration.** Ours are almost entirely
   `${VAR:-default}`, so the text shows *defaults*. A user who exports
   `MEM_FRACTION=0.82` changes not one byte of the file — the exact case this
   feature exists to detect stays invisible.
2. **The launchers override the compose.** `switch.sh`/`launch.sh` resolve the
   engine image from `scripts/lib/profiles/engines/<engine>.yml` `install.spec`
   and **inject** it over the compose's own `image:` default. A compose dump
   would report the *wrong engine image* in every report, institutionalising a
   trap this repo already documents.
3. It is also the single largest thing we could paste: 28 KB of YAML for one
   slug, into reports that already bump issue-body limits.

### Measured, not assumed

The diff relies on three docker/compose behaviours, so they were verified on a
throwaway two-line compose rather than taken from the docs:

| compose text | `docker compose config` (clean env) | real `.Config.Cmd` |
|---|---|---|
| `${MEM_FRACTION:-0.91}` | `host-sub=0.91` | `host-sub=0.82` |
| `$${MEM_FRACTION:-…}` | `$${MEM_FRACTION:-…}` | `${MEM_FRACTION:-…}` |

i.e. single-`$` interpolation happens **on the host at launch**, so `.Config.Cmd`
carries the resolved value; rendering the recipe in a clean environment
reproduces the shipped defaults; and `$$` survives into `config` output but
reaches the container unescaped — which is why the recipe side is normalised
before comparison. A bare `- VAR` passthrough was confirmed to land in
`.Config.Env`.

## What it captures

**(a) What the container received** — `.Config.{Image,Entrypoint,Cmd,Env}`. An
inline launch script (11 KB on the SGLang slugs) is identified by line count +
sha256 rather than printed; a flat argv is printed one flag per line.

**(b) What the engine resolved** — its own startup dump, where an `auto` becomes
concrete. Elided by default to the keys that matter (SGLang's `server_args` is
~8 KB on one line); the full dump is behind a new opt-in **`--engine-args`**,
deliberately *not* folded into `--full`.

**(c) ⭐ A diff against the shipped recipe.** Resolve the slug from the compose
project label (exact path, then path suffix for a different checkout, then the
compose's own `container_name`), re-render that recipe with `docker compose
config` in a clean environment, and print only the delta.

Three things a flag diff alone would miss, all covered:

* **an env knob read inside the container.** llama.cpp's composes consume
  `SPEC` via `$$SPEC`, so `SPEC=off` disables the drafter with a byte-identical
  `Cmd`. A flags-only verdict would call that launch stock. It is now caught and
  labelled as invisible to argv.
* **non-flag launch-script edits**, via a residual line check (a changed model
  path, a deleted guard).
* **the entrypoint**, which needs the same `$$` normalisation as the command —
  without it every stock vLLM slug reported a phantom entrypoint difference.
  Found by running the vLLM path, not by reading the code.

## Sample output, as rendered on the reference rig

Stock:

```
## Engine configuration (resolved)

### Shipped-recipe comparison

- **Slug:** `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-superfast` — recipe `models/qwen3.8-27b/sglang/compose/dual/autoround-int4/dflash2.yml`
- **Matched by:** compose project label (exact path)
- ✅ **Stock recipe** — launch flags, entrypoint, launch script and every allowlisted env knob are identical to the shipped recipe rendered with its own defaults.
- **Engine image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19` — matches the engine profile `sglang-stable` (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19`)
```

Same slug launched with `MEM_FRACTION=0.91 CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=1024 SPEC_N=0`:

```
### Shipped-recipe comparison

- **Slug:** `sgl/qwen38-27b-dual-superfast` — recipe `models/qwen3.8-27b/sglang/compose/dual/autoround-int4/dflash2.yml`
- **Matched by:** compose project label (exact path)
- ⚠️ **2 flag(s) differ from the shipped recipe:**

| flag | running | recipe |
|---|---|---|
| `--chunked-prefill-size` | `1024` | `2048` |
| `--mem-fraction-static` | `0.91` | `0.82` |

- ⚠️ **1 env knob(s) differ from the shipped recipe and do not appear in the flags above** — they are read inside the container, so argv alone would have reported this launch as stock:

| env var | running | recipe |
|---|---|---|
| `SPEC_N` | `0` | _(unset)_ |

- ⚠️ **1 further launch-script line(s) differ** (flag changes already listed above are excluded):

```
_n="0"
```
- **Engine image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19` — matches the engine profile `sglang-stable` (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19`)

### Container config (`docker inspect`)

- **Container:** `sglang-qwen38-27b-dflash2-dual` (state: created, engine kind: `sglang`)
- **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19`
- **Entrypoint:** `/bin/bash -c`
- **Cmd:** `inline script` — 187 lines, 11327 bytes, sha256 `251fb2a7ac40117c` — not printed; the recipe diff above is the readable form
- **Env (allowlist — 9 shown, 16 set-but-empty, 45 withheld):** an env var must MATCH the allowlist to print; this holds under `--no-redact` too.
```

Hand-rolled compose:

```
- ⚠️ **Unrecognised — not a shipped recipe.** compose file is not a shipped recipe: …/docker-compose.yml
- There is nothing to diff against, so the flags are reported raw. Every value here is the reporter's own configuration, not a club-3090 default.
- **Launch flags extracted from `.Config.Cmd`** (3):

```
--mem-fraction-static 0.72
--model-path /models/x
--tp-size 2
```
```

Printing the flags in that branch is the point: for an unrecognised launch argv
is the only evidence there is, and #1261 is precisely that case.

## Secrets — an allowlist, and two notes on its shape

A name must **match the allowlist** to print at all.

* It is **not** derived from the composes' own `environment:` lists, even though
  that would self-maintain — **75 shipped composes declare
  `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` there**, so a compose-derived allowlist would leak the
  token by construction. The list is curated exact names plus a few bulk
  engine-tuning prefix families.
* Each allowed prefix family contains a real credential var upstream —
  llama-server reads `LLAMA_ARG_API_KEY`, vLLM reads `VLLM_API_KEY`. A name veto
  removes those shapes from *within* an allowed family. It is a **second gate,
  not the mechanism**: a name outside the allowlist never prints regardless.
* A value-shape scrub (`hf_…`, `sk-…`, `gh[pousr]_…`, …) runs last, and now runs
  on the recipe-diff table too — it originally printed raw values there, so an
  allowlisted var holding a token-shaped value would have been scrubbed in one
  block and verbatim in the other. Found by the negative control below.
* Enforced **regardless of `--no-redact`**, which is documented as disabling
  path/host/user redaction. No report has ever carried engine env, so this
  regresses nothing.

## Size

Bounded by construction, not by the compose. Measured on a stock SGLang slug:

| | bytes |
|---|---|
| report before | 17,290 |
| report after | 18,713 (**+1,423**) |
| the compose it diffs against | 27,990 |

`--engine-args` moved a synthetic SGLang `server_args` capture from 1,430 to
5,906 bytes, which is why it is opt-in.

## Tests, and why the assertions discriminate

`scripts/tests/test-report-resolved-config.sh` — 47 assertions covering stock,
modified, env-only override, hand-rolled, the env allowlist as a unit, bounded
size, and the four no-capture paths (no container / missing container / daemon
down / no docker) each as a **distinct** sentence, so an empty capture can never
read like a clean one.

Two traps this file is written around:

1. **"the report mentions X" can pass pre-fix** — `report.sh` has carried a
   per-GPU wattage since its first commit. Every assertion here keys on content
   that exists only if the feature ran: the literal verdict strings, the slug,
   and a flag's *both* values.
2. **"no token appears in the report" also passes pre-fix**, trivially, because a
   pre-fix report never reads `.Config.Env`. A leak assertion alone proves
   nothing. So the redaction case asserts, against the same fixture and in the
   same run: the env block **is** present, it **does** carry a known allowlisted
   knob with its value, **and** the planted token is absent.

### Negative control

Same test, run against the tree with the feature reverted (the test and its
harness helper kept, so it fails on the feature's absence rather than on a
missing function):

```
pre-fix   PASS: 20  FAIL: 28   exit 1
post-fix  PASS: 47  FAIL:  0   exit 0
```

The 20 that pass pre-fix are exactly the "must not contain" assertions — which is
the trap above, demonstrated: their paired positive assertions (`--no-redact: env
block IS rendered`, `--no-redact: a real allowlisted value IS shown`) are among
the 28 failures, so leg 2e as a whole discriminates.

### Proving the leak assertion can fail

A second, live control neuters `env_allowed` in a throwaway copy of the module
and **requires** a plant to leak. Its probe is a shapeless secret, not the
`hf_…` one, and that choice is the point: `hf_…` and `sk-…` are also caught
downstream by the value-shape scrub, so probing with one would test the scrub and
leave the allowlist unexercised. Observed:

```
real module      MY_COMPANY_SECRET  -> withheld     (0 plants in any rendered section)
neutered module  MY_COMPANY_SECRET  -> club3090-planted-bare-secret-value   LEAKED
```

That is also how the raw-value leak in the recipe-diff table was found, and it is
the concrete argument for the allowlist: a shape-matcher cannot recognise the
next secret.

## Gates run

Relevant gates only (report / engine / harness), not the full sweep:

`test-report-resolved-config` · `test-engine-kind-resolver` ·
`test-engine-detection-sglang` · `test-report-exit-code` ·
`test-report-engine-liveness` · `test-report-power-state` · `test-report-calib` ·
`test-script-permissions` · `test-locale-utf8` · `test-registry-emit-no-yaml` ·
`test-p2p-state` · `test-docs-slugs-resolve` — all green.

## Deliberately out of scope

* **(b) is elided by default** and the full dump is behind `--engine-args`, per
  the size argument in the issue. `--full` does not enable it.
* The renderer is **python3 stdlib-only** and reads the catalog through
  `compose_registry.py`, *not* `registry-emit.sh --json` — the emit path may need
  PyYAML, and a community rig without it is exactly the rig whose report we most
  need.
* No `report.sh` refactor beyond the new section and the flag.
title: feat(report): capture the engine's RESOLVED config + diff it against the shipped recipe

body:
Fixes #1282, and does it the way the issue actually asks — one resolver, not a sixth arm.

## The defect

`scripts/spec-sweep.sh` carried a private two-valued classifier:

```python
print("vllm" if eng.startswith("vllm") else "llamacpp")
```

so every SGLang slug fell through to `llamacpp`. Without a SLUG that's the hard exit @paulp83 hit in #1251. **With** a SLUG it was worse than a crash: it took llama.cpp's per-request `speculative.n_max` fast path against an SGLang endpoint, the capability probe failed, and it fell back to reboot-per-arm *by accident via the wrong branch* — never reading SGLang's own acceptance lines.

This was the **sixth** site of a defect closed at five the same morning (#1263) — and that five-site fix was itself five more private arms. @paulp83's deeper point is the right one, and it lands on our own patch.

## The fix

`scripts/lib/engine-kind.sh` is now the single source of truth, with five entry points — one per **evidence form**, because scripts genuinely differ in what evidence they have:

| entry point | evidence | used by |
|---|---|---|
| `engine_kind_from_engine_id` | registry `engine:` value | slug path |
| `engine_kind_from_container` | container name | verify-full, verify-stress, report, bench, report_calib |
| `engine_kind_from_image` | docker image ref | report, bench |
| `engine_kind_from_fingerprint` | OpenAI `system_fingerprint` | verify-full, verify-stress |
| `engine_kind_from_slug` | catalog slug → registry | spec-sweep |

What is centralised is the **rules**; each script keeps its own evidence-gathering. All six previous classifier sites now delegate.

**Routing is written as `!= "llamacpp"` rather than `== "vllm"`,** so a newly added engine inherits the safe reboot-per-arm path instead of silently taking llama.cpp's per-request one. SGLang consequently lands in the branch where `_measure_vllm_arm` reads its `accept rate:` / `accept len:` lines (#1249/#1252).

## Behaviour change, deliberate

A slug whose engine id is **unrecognised** now refuses, instead of being silently called `llamacpp` and swept down the wrong path. That is the point of the fix, but it is a behaviour change rather than a pure refactor.

## Negative control

```
pre-fix   exit 1 — 3 real failures:
            resolver missing
            spec-sweep classification: expected engine=sglang, got llamacpp
            private classifier re-implementation present
post-fix  exit 0
```

The guard also has an arm that **fails if a private classifier reappears** anywhere under `scripts/` — that is the part meant to stop a seventh site.

## Two tests changed, and why

Both asserted **implementation shape** that centralisation legitimately invalidates, so both were converted to assert behaviour:

- `test-engine-detection-sglang` grepped `bench.sh` for a literal `sglang` arm — it now asserts bench sources the resolver and that the resolver answers `sglang` for both evidence forms bench actually has.
- `test-spec-sweep` grepped for the old vLLM-specific guard wording — it now asserts the widened condition, and fails if it is ever narrowed back to `== vllm`.

## A real bug the gates caught

`test-locale-utf8` failed on the first sweep: the new lib's `python3` call was missing `PYTHONUTF8`, so a UTF-8 slug under `LC_ALL=C` would have raised and the caller would have silently read `"unknown"` (#779). Fixed — and it is exactly the failure mode this resolver exists to prevent.

## Verification

Full sweep on this branch, plus targeted re-runs of both initially-red gates after fixing them: `test-spec-sweep`, `test-locale-utf8`, `test-engine-kind-resolver`, `test-engine-detection-sglang` all pass. ⚠️ The sweep ran while other work was in flight on this machine and this suite is known to flake under contention, so a clean quiescent sweep is worth one more run before merge.

body:
Closes #1267
Closes #1268

Both issues sit on the same measurement path in `soak-test.sh` / `soak-helper.py`, so they are fixed together.

## #1267 — an unmeasurable turn and a silent-empty turn rendered identically

`decode_tps=0.0` meant two opposite things: "fine, this turn decoded in 49 ms" and "HTTP 200 with zero tokens, the failure soak exists to catch". The per-turn lines were byte-identical; separating them meant redoing `wall - ttft` by hand.

Now every turn states its provenance, and an unmeasurable turn is not rendered as a number at all:

```
turn 1/3: ... decode_tps=266.131 vram=31900MiB (client-timed: 150 ms decode window)
turn 2/3: ... decode_tps=n/a     vram=31900MiB (no decode figure: 80 ms decode window is under the 100 ms client-timing floor and no engine counter was available)
turn 3/3: ... decode_tps=0.0     vram=31900MiB (SILENT-EMPTY: 0 completion tokens)
```

This is the convention `bench.sh` and `bench-agentic.sh` already use — `n/a` plus the reason, exclusions stated (`docs/BENCH_CARD.md`) — rather than a fourth format.

The `Decode-window basis:` summary line is no longer gated on a canvas turn existing, so a run with unmeasurable turns finally reports its own counts and p50 gets a stated denominator:

```
- Decode-window basis: 2 engine-reported (prom-tpot) / 1 silent-empty of 3 turn(s). The decode
  percentiles and retention below are computed over the 2 turn(s) carrying a decode figure — that
  is the denominator; turns without one are excluded rather than counted as zero.
```

The silent-empty discriminator is untouched — it keys on `completion_tokens`, never on `decode_tps` — and the label appears **after** `vram=`, so the existing downstream turn-line parser still matches every numeric turn (and now matches canvas turns too, which it did not before).

## #1268 — design decision, and it is overrulable

**Implemented the issue's first-ranked option: read the engine's own counter; keep client-side SSE timing and the 100 ms floor as the fallback.** Sources, tried in order:

| Source | Where |
|---|---|
| `prom-tpot` | `<engine>:time_per_output_token_seconds` histogram on `<endpoint>/metrics` (vLLM always; SGLang with `--enable-metrics`). The `(_sum, _count)` **delta** across one turn is that turn's mean seconds per output token — decode steps only, prefill excluded by construction. Single-turn attribution is valid because soak is single-stream. |
| `sglang-log` | `gen throughput (token/s): N` on SGLang's decode-batch lines |
| `llamacpp-log` | llama.cpp's per-request `eval time = … (N tokens per second)` — never `prompt eval time`, which is prefill |

An engine counter is computed over real decode steps, so it does not care how narrow the wall-clock window is. The floor stays exactly where it is useful: on the inference path, where it is genuinely suppressing noise.

Motivating evidence — three turns from a **passing** 25-turn run on the reference rig, all reported as `0.0`:

```
wall=656ms    ttft=557ms    -> decode window  99 ms
wall=650ms    ttft=550ms    -> decode window 100 ms
wall=10606ms  ttft=10531ms  -> decode window  75 ms
```

Plus the two sightings in the issue: #849 at 82-83 ms and #1261 at 49 / 65 / 97 ms on 3 of 5 turns.

**This is overrulable cheaply.** `SOAK_ENGINE_COUNTER=off` pins a whole run to client-side timing plus the floor — pre-change behaviour, one env var, no code edit. Reverting the preference entirely is a one-line change to the branch order in `cmd_run`. If the counters turn out to disagree with the SSE window in a way we do not like, the switch is the A/B.

Two notes on what this deliberately does **not** do:

- It does not become a fourth incomparable TPS number by accident. The source is named on every line and in the summary, so an engine-reported figure is never silently diffed against a client-timed one.
- It does not classify the engine. It probes what the endpoint and container can answer and matches signatures, so it does not pre-empt the canonical resolver landing in #1282; when that lands the probe can key off it instead.

Canvas-granularity turns are deliberately excluded from the engine-counter path — per-output-token accounting is not meaningful for a model that denoises a whole canvas per step — so #809's behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

`scripts/tests/test-soak-decode-source.sh` (new) asserts distinguishability itself, not merely that a run completes: it compares the rendered decode figure of an unmeasurable turn against a silent-empty turn and fails if they match. It also covers all three counter sources, the `prompt eval time` vs `eval time` negative control (reading the wrong line yields a plausible, wrong, unfalsifiable number), the `--since` bound on the log scrape, that engine logs are read from **stderr**, and the off switch.

Negative control, run before trusting the green: against the pre-fix tree **34 assertions fail across all five legs**, starting with

```
FAIL: unmeasurable and silent-empty turns render identically — the #1267 defect:
  unmeasurable: [soak]   turn 3/4: status=200 wall=99ms   ttft=19ms   decode_tps=0.0 vram=31900MiB
  silent-empty: [soak]   turn 4/4: status=200 wall=1219ms ttft=1219ms decode_tps=0.0 vram=31900MiB
```

`test-soak-decode-basis.sh` keeps its byte-identity-with-master leg for the measurable-window shape; the narrow shape now asserts the new rendering, and the header records which two of its expectations were superseded and why. No base-vs-new difference is asserted anywhere — an assertion that master still prints the defect would pass today and fail the moment this lands.

Gates run (soak-relevant only, suite not swept): `test-soak-decode-source` PASS · `test-soak-decode-basis` PASS · `test-soak-vram-baseline` PASS · `test-locale-utf8` PASS · `test-script-permissions` PASS · `test-measurement-record` PASS. No GPU, no engine boot — the harness stub serves `/metrics` and a fake `docker logs` supplies the engine log fixtures.

Adjacent, **not** fixed here: `cmd_summary`'s `realistic()` filter still drops any rate above 500 tok/s silently. Engine-reported rates on fast hardware with spec-decode can legitimately exceed that, so it is more reachable now than it was.

body:
Closes #1279
Closes #1281

Two rig-state correctness defects. Both are silent, and both end up inside an artifact someone then trusts — one in a diagnostic report we ask users to paste, the other in the power envelope a benchmark was taken under.

---

## #1279 — `p2p_gpu_count()` returns the two-line string `"0\n0"`

**Mechanism.** `grep -c` **prints `0` and exits 1** when it matches nothing, so the trailing `|| echo 0` was not a fallback — both sides fired:

```bash
p2p_gpu_count() {
  nvidia-smi -L 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^GPU ' || echo 0    # -> "0\n0"
}
```

Five call sites do arithmetic on the result. `report.sh`'s `[[ "$(p2p_gpu_count)" -ge 2 ]]` therefore printed a **shell syntax error into the report body** on any rig where the driver query fails. The caller-side `|| echo 0` in `bench.sh` cannot rescue it: the function already exited 0, its last command having been the `echo`.

**Change** (`scripts/lib/p2p-state.sh` only — `report.sh` untouched): capture the count, keep the no-match exit off `set -e`/`pipefail`, print exactly one integer line. `command grep`, per the repo convention.

## #1281 — `power-cap on` applies a wattage the script invented

**Mechanism.** The script called `nvidia-power-cap.service` "the single source of truth for the 250W value" but never read the unit. The number lived in comments and in an **executed** fallback that fires whenever `systemctl restart` fails:

```bash
# Fallback: service missing/disabled — apply 250W directly.
if ! { sudo nvidia-smi -i 0 -pl 250 && sudo nvidia-smi -i 1 -pl 250; }; then
```

The installed unit's ExecStart lines say `-pl 230`. So the two halves of one command disagreed about what "on" means, and both reported success. That is the condition behind the −40% reading on this class of rig that looked exactly like an upstream speculative-decoding regression (identical TPS at spec_n=1 and n=2, healthy draft acceptance) and was nearly filed as an engine bug. It was the cap.

**Change** (`scripts/gpu-mode.sh`):

- `powercap_service_plan()` parses `systemctl cat nvidia-power-cap.service` into `<gpu-index|all> <watts>` rows (handles `-i N … -pl W`, `--id=`, `--power-limit=`).
- `power-cap on` resolves that **before touching anything**. Missing / unreadable / no parseable `-pl` ⇒ **refuse**, non-zero exit, nothing applied — an unverified cap is worse than none, because the benchmark it suppresses still looks valid. The refusal names `systemctl cat …` and the explicit `power-cap <WATTS>` escape hatch.
- The fallback now **replays exactly the pairs the unit defines**, so it can no longer disagree with the service it stands in for.
- **No power-limit wattage literal survives in any executed path**, messages included; the ones that cannot resolve the unit (`off` / custom-wattage session-scope notes) degrade to a number-free phrase rather than inventing one. Comment block reconciled. The `off` path is unchanged — it already read each card's own default.

---

## Negative controls

Both tests were written to fail against the pre-fix tree first. No power limit was changed on any rig: `nvidia-smi`, `sudo` and `systemctl` are recording stubs, and the power-cap harness **refuses to run unless it has verified it shadowed the real binaries** (otherwise a broken `PATH` stub would let the assertions "pass" while the real `nvidia-smi -pl` ran).

**#1279 — `scripts/tests/test-p2p-state.sh` §10.** Asserts the function emits *exactly one line* that is a valid integer under a failing `nvidia-smi`, that `[[ "$(p2p_gpu_count)" -ge 2 ]]` leaves stderr clean, and that it survives a `pipefail` caller. "Contains 0" would have passed against the broken version, so the assertion is on the line count.

```
# pre-fix (p2p-state.sh restored from master)
$ bash scripts/tests/test-p2p-state.sh        ; echo "EXIT=$?"
FAIL: failing nvidia-smi: expected ONE line, got 2: $'0\n0'
EXIT=1

# post-fix
$ bash scripts/tests/test-p2p-state.sh        ; echo "EXIT=$?"
  ✓ p2p_gpu_count: exactly one integer line, driver up or down; arithmetic-safe
test-p2p-state: ok
EXIT=0
```

End-to-end, through the repo's own report harness (whose default `nvidia-smi` stub exits 1 — the "driver query fails" rig), running the **real** `report.sh`:

```
# pre-fix — inside the generated report body, right after a </details>
syntax-error lines in the generated report: 1
  57  scripts/report.sh: line 665: [[: 0
  58  0: syntax error in expression (error token is "0")

# post-fix
syntax-error lines in the generated report: 0
```

**#1281 — `scripts/tests/test-gpu-mode-power-cap.sh`** (new, 31 assertions). Drives the real script: unit-missing, unit-present-with-no-`-pl`, restart-OK, restart-FAILS, long-form `--power-limit=`, `off`, custom wattage, plus a comment-stripped static scan for wattage literals in executed code.

```
# pre-fix (gpu-mode.sh restored from master)
$ bash scripts/tests/test-gpu-mode-power-cap.sh ; echo "EXIT=$?"
FAIL: unit missing: expected non-zero exit, got 0
FAIL: unit missing: says it is refusing: missing 'Refusing to re-apply a power cap'
FAIL: unit missing: NOTHING applied: expected '', got '-i 0 -pl 250
-i 1 -pl 250'
FAIL: fallback: replays exactly the unit's ExecStart caps: expected '-i 0 -pl 230
-i 1 -pl 230', got '-i 0 -pl 250
-i 1 -pl 250'
FAIL: restart ok: banner quotes the unit's value: missing '230W'
FAIL: no -pl literal in executed code: expected '', got '776: … nvidia-smi -pl 250 …
777:                if ! { sudo nvidia-smi -i 0 -pl 250 && sudo nvidia-smi -i 1 -pl 250; }; then'
… (22 of 31 failed)
test-gpu-mode-power-cap: 9 passed, 22 failed
EXIT=1

# post-fix
$ bash scripts/tests/test-gpu-mode-power-cap.sh ; echo "EXIT=$?"
test-gpu-mode-power-cap: 31 passed, 0 failed
EXIT=0
```

Behaviour under the stubs, post-fix (unit = `-pl 230`):

```
### on (systemd restart OK)
═══ Re-applying GPU power cap (230W, per nvidia-power-cap.service) ═══
Power cap re-applied via systemd.                       # no direct -pl at all

### on (restart FAILS -> fallback)
systemctl restart failed; replaying the unit's own ExecStart caps directly (230W).
                                                        # applies -i 0 -pl 230, -i 1 -pl 230

### on (unit absent -> refuse, exit 1, nothing applied)
✗ Refusing to re-apply a power cap: cannot resolve one from nvidia-power-cap.service.
